summary: The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 127 - 108, at Wells Fargo Center on Thursday evening. Both teams came out strong in the first quarter but the Bulls held the advantage, leading 41 - 38, heading into the second. However, the Sixers bounced back in the second, where they outscored the Bulls, 27 - 17, to take a 65 - 58 lead heading into halftime. The Sixers came out in domination mode in the third and outscored the Bulls, 37 - 18, to take a 102 - 76 lead heading into the fourth. The Bulls put up a fight in the fourth but the 76ers were able to cruise to their first win of the season without a problem. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 30 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting, in 33 minutes of action. Ben Simmons put up big numbers with 13 points, 13 rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and one steal, in 34 minutes. Robert Covington finished with 20 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block, in 29 minutes. The Sixers shot 48 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 30 points on 11 - of - 20 shooting, six rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes of action. Bobby Portis followed up with 20 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Antonio Blakeney added 15 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Bulls shot 44 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 33 from long range. The Bulls (0 - 1) look to bounce back as they play host to the Pistons on Saturday. The Sixers (1 - 1) play host to the 76ers on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 116 - 115, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The Magic jumped out to a quick 90 lead and went ahead to push it to a 26 - 10 advantage with 4:55 left in the first. However, the Sixers battled back and cut the gap to just two points, trailing, 32 - 30, after one. The 76ers pulled ahead in the second carried the lead for most of the quarter, before taking a 63 - 52 lead into halftime. The tides turned again in the third quarter, as the Magic outscored the 76ers by eight, to cut the deficit to three points, heading into the final frame. The Sixers maintained their edge and pushed the lead back to 10, with five minutes to go in the game, but the Magic used an 18 - 9 run to make it a one - point game with 5 seconds left and possession. The Magic were not able to convert on the final play and dropped their second game in as many nights. On the other hand, the Sixers earned their second straight win. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 32 points, 10 rebounds and three assists, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick came up huge in 32 minutes off the bench, with 31 points, four rebounds and four assists. Dario Saric finished with 13 points, nine rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal, while Robert Covington added 12 points, four rebounds, two steals, one block and one assist. The Sixers shot 48 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Evan Fournier was the high - point man for the Magic with 31 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Nikola Vucevic had a big night with 27 points, 13 rebounds, 12 assists and two steals, in 37 minutes of action, while Aaron Gordon finished with 20 points, 12 rebounds three assists, three blocks and one steal. The Magic shot 46 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 29 from distance. The Magic (1 - 2) take on the Celtics in Boston on Monday, while the 76ers, head to Detroit to challenge the Pistons on Tuesday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 105 - 103, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The battle of two evenly matched teams was as good as expected, as neither club gave an inch through four quarters. A see - saw first half saw the 76ers (3 - 3) enter halftime holding a slim 63 - 62 advantage. Ultimately, a standout defensive effort by Philadelphia that saw them limit the Hornets (3 - 4) to 18 points in the final period helped key the hard - fought win. Both teams scuffled from the field with Charlotte's 39 percent success rate only slightly exceeding the Sixers' 38 percent figure. However, the home squad enjoyed a strong rebounding advantage, winning the battle of the boards by a 56 - 48 margin. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with a game - high 37 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal. Miles Bridges followed with a bench - leading 14 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds and one steal. Cody Zeller produced 12 points, six boards and one steal, while Jeremy Lamb matched his point total and added three rebounds and one assist. Joel Embiid led the way for the Sixers with a 27 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and two blocks. Robert Covington generated an 18 - point, 10 - rebound double - double of his own. J.J. Redick poured in 15 point to lead the second unit. Ben Simmons supplied 14 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dario Saric contributed 11 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Markelle Fultz turned in 10 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Hornets head back home and await a visit from the Miami Heat on Tuesday night, while the 76ers remain home to take on the Atlanta Hawks on Monday evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 113 - 92, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday night. The 76ers (4 - 3) kept their undefeated run at home alive with a convincing win over the Hawks (2 - 4), as Atlanta fought hard but ultimately didn't have enough in them to battle with Philadelphia. In fact, Atlanta won the first quarter 25 - 20, but Philadelphia evened things up with a 27 - 22 second quarter that kept the score tied at 47 after the first two quarters. Philadelphia showed a bit of their playoff form last season with an impressive 31 - 13 third quarter, and they later closed things out with a 35 - 32 fourth quarter. Without a doubt, it was a strong showing from the Sixers and now they move up to 40 at home. Ben Simmons was the star of the game for Philadelphia and he came one assist short of a triple - double thanks to a 21 - point, 12 - rebound, nine - assist stat line, while Joel Embiid registered 10 points, six rebounds, six assists and two blocks. Markelle Fultz chipped in with 16 points and seven assists, Robert Covington added 11 points with six rebounds, and three bench players reached the 10 - point mark: J.J. Redick (14), Mike Muscala (14) and Landry Shamet (13). Kent Bazemore had 18 points to led all players for the Hawks, while rookie point guard Trae Young contributed with 11 points and eight assists. Dewayne Dedmon and Omari Spellman each chipped in with 11 points coming off the bench for the Hawks. All 13 Atlanta players scored, but only four reached the 10 - point mark.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 122 - 113, at Wells Fargo Center on Thursday evening. The Sixers got out to a solid start at home, as they held the upper hand for the entire first quarter, before taking a 34 - 30 lead into the second. They took off in the second, as they quickly pushed their lead to 10, and went on to outscore the Clippers by 11 in the quarter, to take a 72 - 57 lead into halftime. However, the Clippers came out strong in the third, as they kicked off the quarter with an 11 - 4 run, to cut the gap to eight. They kept battling and managed to trim the deficit to just four points, as they trailed 90 - 86 heading into the final frame. Despite the Clippers' strong push, the Sixers kept it together and managed to push their lead back to 11, less two minutes into the quarter. From there, the Clippers were only able to get within three points, as the 76ers went on to their fifth home win of the season. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 41 points, 13 rebounds, four blocks and one assist, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick followed up with 18 points, in 34 minutes off the bench, while Ben Simmons tallied 14 points, 11 assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Sixers shot 47 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, Lou Williams led the Clippers with 26 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting, in 24 minutes off the bench. Danilo Gallinari followed up with 25 points, eight rebounds and one assist, in 35 minutes, while Tobias Harris added 24 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block. The Clippers shot 44 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 23 from long range. The Clippers (4 - 4) will be right back in action, as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Friday. The 76ers (5 - 4) play host to the Pistons on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 109 - 99, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. Wire-to-wire wins are rare in today's NBA but that's just what the Sixers did here. In fact, Philly led by 24 points at times, as a 22 - point halftime lead was too much for the Clippers to overcome. Three-point shooting was key to victory, with Philly hitting 9 - of - 29 of their three's while holding Detroit to just 5 - of - 30 from long range. The free - throw shooting was also critical, as the Pistons connected on just 28 - of - 41 while the Sixers hit 44 - of - 51. Defense really carried Philly too, as they forced 17 turnovers from Detroit while holding them to under 40 percent from the field. The Pistons (4 - 4) had just one starter reach double figures in scoring, as Blake Griffin continued his magical season. In fact, he finished with 38 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and two steals on 12 - of - 21 shooting. Andre Drummond totaled eight points and nine boards. Langston Galloway led the bench with 13 points. The Sixers (6 - 4) got a spectacular performance out of Joel Embiid, as he tallied 39 points, 17 rebounds and two blocks on 10 - of - 18 from the field. Ben Simmons was second among starters, collecting nine points, five rebounds, five assists and five steals. J.J. Redick led the bench with 16 points and four assists. On deck for Philly is a road matchup versus the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday. As for Detroit, they host the Miami Heat on Monday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 133 - 132, in overtime at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (8 - 5) found themselves at the scene of the majority of their successes Friday, as they'd come into the contest with a perfect 60 record at home. After a nip - and - tuck first quarter, Philadelphia seemingly turned the game in their favor with a 32 - 17 advantage in the second period. To their credit, the Hornets (6 - 6) wouldn't go away, chipping away at their deficit until overcoming it in the fourth quarter. However after holding a five - point lead as late as the 1:18 mark of the final period, Charlotte allowed Philadelphia a 7 - 2 run at the end of regulation to force overtime. In a tightly contested extra period, a free throw apiece from Ben Simmons and Joel Embiid in the closing seconds helped create just enough cushion for the win. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with 30 points and added nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal. Jeremy Lamb provided 17 points, three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Dwayne Bacon supplied 15 points, one rebound, one assist and one steal. Willy Hernangomez delivered 14 points and four boards. Cody Zeller matched Hernangomez's scoring and rebounding totals, while Michael Kidd-Gilchrist generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double off the bench. Embiid led the Sixers with a 42 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Ben Simmons tallied a 22 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included eight boards, three blocks and two steals. Dario Saric contributed 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. J.J. Redick finished with 17 points, four assists and two rebounds. Markelle Fultz and Robert Covington started but only had seven points each. The Hornets remain on the road and take on the Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the 76ers pay a visit to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Utah Jazz, 113 - 107, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. It was a tale of two quarters in the first half for the 76ers (10 - 7), which exploded out of the gates for a 38 - point haul over the first 12 minutes. However, as prolific as Philadelphia was in the first quarter, they had as much trouble finding the net in the second. posting only 16 points. That was the extent of their scoring drought, though, as the home squad was able to outpace the Jazz (7 - 8) by a 59 - 55 margin in the second half. The game was not won without several scares in the final period, as Utah held a 107 - 105 lead as late as the 1:37 mark of the fourth quarter before the Big Three of Ben Simmons, Jimmy Butler and Joel Embiid notched the final six points to seal the win. Donovan Mitchell paced the Jazz with 31 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds, four steals and one block. Joe Ingles provided 14 points, two rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block. Ricky Rubio and Derrick Favors generated matching 13 - point efforts. Rudy Gobert contributed a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Butler paced the Sixers with 28 points, a total he supplemented with seven assists, three rebounds and two steals. Embiid delivered 23 points, seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks and two steals. J.J. Redick poured in 16 points. Simmons pitched in a full stat line of 10 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block. Amir Johnson led the second unit with 11 points. The Jazz remain on the road and pay a visit to the Boston Celtics on Saturday evening. The Sixers also hit the road and tangle with the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday night as well.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 119 - 114, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday evening. The 76ers (12 - 7) likely walked into Monday's home game feeling pretty good about themselves, and more specifically, their chances of cruising through an interconference contest against the struggling Suns (3 - 13), which had failed to win a road game in six tries. Philadelphia got an early wake - up call, as Phoenix jumped out to a 36 - 26 first - quarter lead. The visitors still held an advantage at halftime, albeit by just five points. The Sixers were able to eradicate their deficit in convincing fashion in the third and entered the final 12 minutes with a 92 - 86 edge. That would prove to be enough, although the Suns got as close 117 - 114 with 6 seconds remaining after a Mikal Bridges three - pointer. Phoenix kept the pressure on their hosts with a 51 percent success rate from the field, but they were outrebounded by a 53 - 31 margin. Devin Booker paced the Suns with 37 points, a total he supplemented with eight assists and three rebounds. T.J. Warren followed with 21 points, four rebounds, four assists and one block. Deandre Ayton posted 17 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. Bridges finished with 13 points, while Trevor Ariza filled out the stat sheet with 10 points, seven rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block. Richaun Holmes matched Ariza's point total while leading the bench. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with a 33 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, three steals and one block. Ben Simmons had a near triple - double with 19 points, 11 rebounds, nine assists and one steal. Mike Muscala matched Simmons' point total to lead the second unit. J.J. Redick poured in 17 points and added four rebounds and three assists. Jimmy Butler contributed 16 points, three rebounds, one assist and two steals. The Suns remain on the road and visit the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday'night, while the Sixers remain home and face the New Orleans Pelicans on that same evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 121 - 120, at Wells Fargo Center on Wednesday evening. The 76ers got out to a great start at home, as they outscored the Pelicans, 38 - 23, in the first quarter. The Pelicans made a push to start the second and quickly cut the gap to just three points. However, the home team was able to withstand, as the Sixers built their lead back up to double digits, and took a 67 - 57 lead into halftime. The third quarter was evenly matched, as neither team gave up any ground. The Pelicans led 96 - 87 heading into the final frame. The 76ers pushed their lead to 15 early in the fourth, but the Pelicans did not break, as the rallied back to make it a one - point game, with one minute remaining. Despite the visitor's best effort, the 76ers managed to stay one step ahead in crunch time, to pull off the impressive, 121 - 120, home win. This marks the fourth straight win for Philly. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 31 points, 19 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, in 32 minutes. Ben Simmons followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and one steal, in 35 minutes. Jimmy Butler and J.J. Redick chipped in 13 points each. The Sixers shot 45 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Jrue Holiday and E'Twaun Moore poured in 30 points each for the Pelicans. Julius Randle came up large as well, with 22 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and one block, in 28 minutes off the bench. The Pelicans (10 - 8) will look to bounce back as they take on the Knicks in New York on Friday. The 76ers (13 - 7) play host to the Cavs on Friday.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the host Philadelphia 76ers, 121 - 112, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The Cavs got down to business right away, as they outscored the home team, 31 - 23, in the first quarter. The 76ers picked up the slack in the second and outscored the Cavs, 31 - 23, in the quarter, to tie the game at 54 heading into halftime. However, the Cavaliers would not back down, as they came out tough in the third and matched the Sixers bucket for bucket, before they emerged with a one - point lead heading into the final frame. The Cavs continued to play one step ahead of the home team 76ers, and managed to build an 11 - point lead with 4:37 left in the game. The Cavs held on from there to earn their first road win of the season, and hand the 76ers their first home loss of the season. Rodney Hood led the Cavs with 25 points on 10 - of - 20 shooting, four rebounds and one assist, in 39 minutes. Collin Sexton followed up with 23 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, while Tristan Thompson added 18 points, 13 rebounds and two steals, in 35 minutes. The Cavs shot 53 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 22 from long range. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 24 points, 12 rebounds and three assists, in 32 minutes. J.J. Redick tallied 23 points of his own, on 5 - of - 11 shooting, while Ben Simmons and Jimmy Butler tallied 22 points each. The Sixers shot 53 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 33 from long range. The 76ers (13 - 8) will look to bounce back as they take on the Nets in Brooklyn on Sunday. The Cavs (3 - 14) play host to the Rockets on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Washington Wizards, 123 - 98, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (16 - 8) set the tone early for what would be a comfortable victory, establishing a 31 - 19 first - quarter lead that had grown to 68 - 46 by halftime. Philadelphia had no trouble maintaining a sizable advantage in the second half over the reeling Wizards (8 - 14), who were playing without Otto Porter, Jr. (personal). The Sixers limited Washington to 40 percent shooting (including 29 percent from three - point range) while winning the rebounding battle by a 58 - 42 margin. Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 19 points. Austin Rivers followed with a bench - leading 15 points and also offered two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Thomas Bryant drew a start at center and posted 12 points, seven rebounds. one steal and one block. John Wall got off to a slow start and never recovered, tallying 11 points, seven assists, three rebounds and three steals. Philadelphia saw seven players hit double digits in the scoring column, with Joel Embiid leading the way. The big man posted a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks. T.J. McConnell was next with a bench - leading 15 points. J.J. Redick poured in 14 points. Ben Simmons managed a 13 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included eight rebounds. Furkan Korkmaz supplied 13 points, five assists, two rebounds and one steal. Landry Shamet turned in 12 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Mike Muscala matched Shamet's scoring total and pulled down 10 rebounds. Jimmy Butler collected 11 points, seven rebounds, four assists and four steals. The Wizards head back home and face the Brooklyn Nets on Saturday evening, while the Sixers remain home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Sunday evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 103 - 95, at Wells Fargo Center on Sunday evening. The Sixers got out to a quick, 10 - 3, lead but the Grizzlies stuck with it, leading to a, 26 - 25, advantage for the home team, after one quarter. The 76ers stayed on top in the second, where they outscored the Grizzlies, 28 - 19, to take a, 54 - 44, lead by halftime. Things tightened up again in the second half, as both teams matched each other for 24 points in the third quarter, leaving the Sixers ahead by 10 heading into the fourth. The Grizzlies started the fourth quarter with a quick 9 - 1 run, to make it a two - point game. However, the 76ers answered right back, pushing their lead back to nine, with five minutes left. The Grizzlies cut it as close as a four - point deficit, but could not do better than that, as the 76ers held on to earn their fourth straight win. J.J. Redick led Philly with 24 points on 9 - of - 17 shooting, in 30 minutes. Jimmy Butler tallied 21 points, three rebounds, two assists and a block. Ben Simmons finished with 19 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and two steals, while Joel Embiid added 15 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Meanwhile, Mike Conley led the Grizzlies with 21 points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Jaren Jackson Jr. followed up with 17 points, three rebounds, three blocks and a steal, while JaMychal Green tallied 14 points, seven rebounds and four steals. The Grizzlies (13 - 9) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Clippers on Tuesday. The 76ers (17 - 8) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Wednesday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 116 - 102, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday evening. The Pistons jumped to an early, 7 - 4, lead but the 76ers came back to tie it at 11, four minutes into the first quarter. The Sixers did not look back from there, as they used a quick, 90, run to create some separation, and held on to take a, 38 - 29, lead into the second quarter. The game slowed down in the second, as the Sixers and Pistons matched each other with 18 points in the quarter. Things picked up again in the third, where the Sixers held their nine - point lead for most of the quarter, until the Pistons finally made a run to cut the deficit to three, with under two minutes remaining. However, the 76ers charged back with a, 11 - 3, run to bring a, 87 - 76, lead into the final frame. The Pistons kept fighting and cut the gap to six early in the quarter, but the home team responded one final time, pushing the lead to 17 points with three minutes left in the contest. The 76ers cruised from there to their second win in a row, while the Pistons dropped their fifth in a row. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 24 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 32 minutes. Ben Simmons followed up with 18 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block, while T.J. McConnell added 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 28 minutes off the bench. Luke Kennard had a big night for the Pistons, with 28 points, eight rebounds and three assists, in 36 minutes. Blake Griffin (rest) did not suit up, but Andre Drummond finished with 21 points, 17 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal. The Pistons (13 - 12) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Wednesday. The 76ers (19 - 9) play host to the Nets on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 127 - 124, at Wells Fargo Center on Wednesday. The game was certainly not as close as the final score suggests, as the Nets were in control for nearly all of Wednesday's contest before the 76ers' second unit, led by rookie Landry Shamet scoring 10 points in the final minute of the game, made a late push but ultimately just ran out of time. The main reason Brooklyn found itself in full control of the outing was the stellar play of Spencer Dinwiddie, who scored a career - high 39 points in just 30 minutes off the bench. The point guard shot 4 - of - 6 from three and a11 - of - 18 from the field overall, but he did most of his damage from the free throw line, where he was 13 - of - 14. It was the fifth time this season the breakout 25 - year - old scored at least 25 points in a game. As for the rest of the Nets, Allen Crabbe was the high scorer out of the starters, posting 20 points while shooting 50 percent from the field. Joe Harris was 2 - of - 3 from behind the arc en route to scoring 14 points, while rookie Rodions Kurucs scored 13 points off the bench. As a team, the Nets were on fire from behind the arc, going 14 - of - 28 from deep. The 76ers had to play Wednesday's game without star guard Jimmy Butler (groin), and their star players certainly picked up some of the slack. Joel Embiid was a force down low, postig another massive double - double of 33 points and 17 rebounds in 38 minutes, while Ben Simmons had a terrific all - around performance with 22 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, four steals and two blocks. Lastly, Furkan Korkmaz, who started in Butler's absence, scored 18 points for the second straight night. Offensive production, however, wasn't the problem, as the 127 points the team gave up was the most Philadelphia allowed in nearly a month.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 113 - 101, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The Pacers (19 - 10) fell behind by 10 points at the end of the first quarter, and given that the 76ers (19 - 11) had lost only twice all season on their home floor, things looked bleak for Indiana early. The visitors still trailed by 10 at halftime, but a prolific third quarter where they outscored Philadelphia by a 31 - 18 margin. The Pacers then kept the heat on in the fourth by adding nine points to their advantage and sealing a hard - fought road victory. Thaddeus Young led the Pacers by touching up one of his old squads for a 26 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and one block. Bojan Bogdanovic provided 18 points, five rebounds and two assists. Victor Oladipo, Domantas Sabonis and Cory Joseph generated matching 14 - point tallies. Oladipo added nine assists and three steals, Sabonis also pulled down 16 rebounds, Darren Collison mustered eight points but also dished out 10 assists. Joel Embiid paced the Sixers with a 40 - point, 21 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, one steal and one block. J.J. Redick contributed 22 points. Ben Simmons managed 18 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block. Furkan Korkmaz started for Jimmy Butler (groin) once again but only totaled six points and two rebounds. The Pacers head back home to face the New York Knicks on Sunday afternoon, while the Sixers pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Sunday afternoon as well.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the New York Knicks, 131 - 109, at Wells Fargo Center. The 76ers (21 - 12) entered this game losing three of their past four outings, but they bounced back in a huge way thanks to a 22 - point win playing in front of their crowd against a struggling Knicks (7 - 25) side that was unable to get things going from start to finish. As a result, New York have now lost 10 of their last 12 games. Philly established their terms early and jumped to a 38 - 33 lead after the first quarter. They would never looked back, though, and they actually won all quarters here. The final score per each quarter was: 38 - 33, 31 - 28, 30 - 24 and 32 - 24, respectively. Ben Simmons paved the way for the Sixers thanks to a triple - double of 13 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Joel Embiid was the top scorer with 24 points and he also added 10 rebounds. Jimmy Butler had a solid outing as well since he finished with 20 points, four rebounds and four assists. J. J. Redick had 14 points, and Landry Shamet delivered 17 points off the bench. Every Sixers player that saw action scored at least two points. Tim Hardaway Jr. was New York's top scorer with 27 points and he also added five assists. Kevin Knox had one of his best games as a pro and finished with 21 points and six rebounds, while Enes Kanter chipped in with 15 points and six boards. Emmanuel Mudiay filled the stat sheet thanks to 11 points, five assists and three boards. Damyean Dotson contributed 14 points off the bench.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 126 - 101, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. While there were 13 ties and 13 lead changes in the first half, Philadelphia held the lead for the entirety of the second half. In fact, the Sixers outscored the Raptors, 97 - 71, across the final three quarters to take control. The shooting disparity was key, with Philadelphia hitting 54 percent from the field and 33 percent from three - point range while holding Toronto to 39 percent from the field and 25 percent from long range. Ball movement played a huge factor in that, with the Sixers out - assisting the Raptors, 33 - 17. Defensive rebounding was also decisive, with Philly winning that battle, 49 - 33 The Raptors (25 - 10) decided to rest Kawhi Leonard for this game and it clearly hampered them in this defeat. Pascal Siakam was their best player, as he led the way with 26 points, six rebounds and two assists. Kyle Lowry accumulated 20 points, six rebounds and five assists. Norman Powell led their bench with 13 points and four boards. The Sixers (22 - 12) got a spectacular performance from Joel Embiid, as he collected 27 points and 11 rebounds on 10 - of - 15 from the field. Ben Simmons was just as good, tallying 26 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists on 11 - of - 13 shooting. J.J. Redick amassed 22 points, three rebounds and five assists while Jimmy Butler finished with 12 points, seven rebounds, seven assists and three steals. On deck for Philly is a Christmas Day showdown against the Boston Celtics on Tuesday. As for Toronto, they travel to face the Miami Heat on Wednesday for their next fixture.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 106 - 100, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. This final scoreline makes this game look closer than it actually was, as Philly dominated throughout. In fact, the Sixers won each of the first three quarters by at least three points apiece, as they led by 17 heading into the fourth quarter. Dallas did respond with a 30 - 19 fourth quarter, as that got the lead down to four points with less than a minute remaining. Defense was critical for the Sixers, as they held the Mavericks to 43 percent from the field, 29 percent from three - point range and 65 percent from the free - throw line. Philadelphia did a ton of work down low too, outscoring the Mavericks in the paint, 62 - 52. Philly's starters really dominated Dallas's starters, outscoring them, 83 - 49. The Mavericks (18 - 21) are now 3 - 18 on the road this season, as this marks their 10th loss in their last 13 games in total. Wesley Matthews was their leading scorer in this game, as he finished with 18 points and two rebounds. Luka Doncic tallied 14 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Jalen Brunson was huge off the bench, providing 13 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists. The Sixers (26 - 14) were led by Joel Embiid, as he collected 25 points, 12 rebounds and five assists. J.J. Redick amassed 20 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Ben Simmons accumulated 20 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists en route to a triple - double. Jonah Bolden got a rare start and accrued 11 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks. On deck for Dallas is a home matchup versus the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday. As for Philly, they play host to the Washington Wizards on Tuesday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Washington Wizards, 132 - 115, at Wells Fargo Center on Tuesday evening. The Bulls did not have much to offer in the third, as they were outscored by 13 in the quarter and trailed by 33, entering the final frame. However, they pulled together in the fourth with a massive rally, outscoring the Sixers 45 - 28 in the quarter, but it was too little, too late, as the Bulls closed out their season with a third straight loss. The Sixers were able to come through with a win despite Joel Embiid (knee) and the rest of the usual starters (rest) sidelined. Jonathan Simmons led the 76ers with 20 points, seven rebounds, five assists and one block, in 29 minutes. Boban Marjanovic added 18 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two blocks, while T.J. McConnell finished with 18 points, six assists, two rebounds and a block. The 76ers shot 56 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 26 from long range. Meanwhile, seven players scored in double digits for the Bulls, led by Walter Lemon Jr., who finished with 20 points, six rebounds and four assists, in 28 minutes. Ryan Arcidiacono finished with 14 points, six rebounds, six assists and one steal, while Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot tallied 14 points, four rebounds and two assists. The 76ers will begin their playoff run against the Nets in the first round.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 118 - 101, at Fiserv Forum on Friday evening. The Pacers jumped out to a quick 80 lead, but the Bucks answered back with a 13 - 2 run to take the upper hand. The Bucks did not look back from there, as they pushed the lead to nine before settling on a 30 - 25 lead heading into the second. They kept their foot on the gas and quickly pushed their lead to 11, and although the Pacers made a push, the Bucks maintained their cushion and took a 62 - 53 lead into halftime. The third quarter once again belonged to Milwaukee, as the Buck outscored the Pacers 31 - 23 in the quarter, to take a 93 - 76 lead into the final frame. The Pacers battled hard but the Bucks matched them point for point in the fourth, to walk away with their second straight win. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way for Milwaukee, with 26 points, 15 rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, in 31 minutes. Khris Middleton followed up with 23 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal, while Malcolm Brogdon tallied 15 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. The Bucks shot 47 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 47 from long range. Meanwhile, Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 25 points, five rebounds, one assist and one block, in 31 minutes. Doug McDermott chipped in 14 points on 5 - of - 8 shooting, in 20 minutes off the bench, while Myles Turner added 11 points, four rebounds and one block. The Pacers shot 44 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 18 from long range. The Pacers (1 - 1) will be right back in action as they play host to the Nets on Saturday. The Bucks (20) play host to the Knicks on Monday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the New York Knicks, 124 - 113, at Fiserv Forum on Monday night. The Bucks (30) and the Knicks (1 - 3) delivered an intense game in the second half, as Milwaukee looked totally in control of the game in the first half (71 - 52) but the Knicks flipped the script and a 35 - 17 third - quarter gave Milwaukee a one - point advantage heading into the final 12 minutes of action. At one point the game was tied at 100 - 100, but the Bucks pulled away late for good and ended winning by a relatively comfortable margin thanks to good execution on offense and an improvement on the defensive end down the stretch. Giannis Antetokounmpo was the best player for the Bucks and once again filled the stat sheet admirably with 31 points, 15 rebounds, four assists and two blocks, but he wasn't the only Milwaukee player who stood out offensively. Khris Middleton contributed with 30 points and seven rebounds, while Eric Bledsoe chipped in with a double - double with 16 points and 13 assists. Brook Lopez added 13 points with four rebounds. Tim Hardaway Jr. led the way for the Knicks with 24 points but he only shot 10 - of - 23 from the field and 3 - of - 9 from three - point range. Enes Kanter contributed with a double - double of 14 points and 13 rebounds, while Trey Burke had 19 points, five boards and four assists. Mario Hezonja had a strong game off the bench with 18 points, four rebounds, three assists and two blocks.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 123 - 108, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday. The hot start of the regular season from the Bucks (40) hit a bump in the road in Wednesday's first quarter, as Milwaukee scored just 22 points in the first 12 minutes and found itself down by 12 points to the visiting 76ers (2 - 3). The Bucks' struggles, however, would end there, as they would go on to score 49 points in the second quarter and took a seven - point lead into the locker room. They'd never let go of that lead thanks in large part to the stellar play from Giannis Antetokounmpo, who finished with a triple - double of a game - high 32 points, 18 rebounds and 10 assists in 37 minutes. Khris Middleton added 25 points of his own on 6 - of - 18 shooting from the field, while starting center Brook Lopez made five three - pointers in one quarter on his way to scoring 21 points in 32 minutes. As a team, it wasn't a great shooting performance for the Bucks, who hit just 30 percent of their threes and shot 41 percent from the field overall, but they managed to make a living at the free throw line and shot a very impressive 28 - of - 30 from the charity strip Wednesday night. For the 76ers, Joel Embiid had another monster night, posting 30 points, 19 rebounds and six assists in 36 minutes, but he shot just 9 - of - 24 from the field. Fellow young star Ben Simmons also didn't shoot great, going just 6 - of - 15, but he still managed to post a triple - double of 14 points, 13 rebounds and 11 assists in his return from a back injury. Overall, it was just a poor shooting night from the 76ers, as while 32 percent from behind the arc is a decent mark, they hit just 41 percent of their shots overall and 70 percent of their attempts from the free throw line en route to their second straight loss.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Orlando Magic, 113 - 91, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Saturday evening. The Bucks (60) started their quest to keep preserve their perfect record strong, building a 65 - 51 halftime lead. They essentially then put the game away in the third quarter, tacking on another 28 points while limiting the Magic (2 - 4) to just 17. That sealed Milwaukee's fourth home win of the season, one in which they limited Orlando to 33 percent shooting while draining 50 percent of their own attempts. Additionally, the home squad was once again dominant on the boards, winning the rebounding battle by a 57 - 42 margin. Nikola Vucevic paced the Magic with 16 points, a total he supplemented with nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. D.J. Augustin produced 11 points, four assists and one rebound. Evan Fournier managed 10 points and one assist. Jonathon Simmons matched Fournier's scoring total to lead the bench. Aaron Gordon shot just 3 - for - 15 on his way to a nine - point, five - rebound effort. Giannis Antetokunmpo's 21 points led the Bucks. He added seven rebounds, one assist and one block. Khris Middleton turned in 18 points, seven rebounds, four assists and one steal. Malcolm Brogdon went for 16 points, four boards and two assists. Donte DiVincenzo led the bench with 15 points and also hauled in three rebounds. Brook Lopez generated 11 points. The Magic head back home to face the Sacramento Kings on Tuesday night, while the Bucks remain home for a Monday ninght showdown against the Toronto Raptors.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 124 - 109, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Monday evening. The Bucks and the Raptors each entered the contest with 60 records, making it the first time in NBA history for such an occurrence. Unfortunately, both team's star players were sidelined from the contest, as Giannis Antetokounmpo sat out on concussion protocol, while Kawhi Leonard sat out for rest, as it was the first night of a back - to - back for Toronto. The first quarter was tight, resulting in the Bucks taking a 30 - 29 lead into the second. They took control in the second quarter, outscoring the Raptors by eight, to take a 62 - 53 lead into the half. The Bucks continued to build on their lead through the third quarter, pushing the gap to 15 heading into the fourth. The Raptors could not get their shots to fall in the fourth and took their first loss of the season, while the Bucks remain the only undefeated team in the league. Ersan Ilyasova led the Bucks with 19 points, 10 rebounds and two assists, in 23 minutes of action. Malcolm Brogdon and Eric Bledsoe tallied 17 points each, while Khris Middleton finished with 14 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals. The Bucks shot 49 percent from the field, including 19 - of - 45 from long range. Meanwhile, Serge Ibaka led the Raptors with 30 points on 12 - of - 21 shooting, in 28 minutes. Pascal Siakam followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, four steals, two assists and one block, while Jonas Valanciunas was the only other player to score in double digits, with 10 points. Kyle Lowry tallied nine points, 15 assists, six rebounds, two steals and two blocks, in 34 minutes. The Raptors shot 39 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 44 from long range. The Raptors (6 - 1) will be right back in action as they play host to the 76ers on Tuesday. The Bucks (70) take on the Celtics in Boston on Thursday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Sacramento Kings, 144 - 109, at Fiserv Forum on Sunday afternoon. A high - scoring affair in Milwaukee ended going towards the home team, as the Bucks (8 - 1) didn't have problems to dismantle the Kings (6 - 4) who entered this game as one of the most surprising teams in The Association during the young 2018 - 19 season. Milwaukee quickly jumped to a 39 - 30 lead in the first quarter, and they never let it go since they also won the remaining three quarters: 33 - 20, 36 - 32 and 36 - 27, respectively. The fact that the Bucks scored at least 30 points in every quarter certainly stands out, but they were effective on both ends of the court on their way to a huge 35 - point win. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way for the Bucks since he finished with a triple - double of 26 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists, but in the end eight different Bucks scored over 10 points. Eric Bledsoe had 17 points with six rebounds, Malcolm Brogdon contributed with 13 points, and Khris Middleton added 12 of this own. Four bench players topped the 10 - point mark as well: Ersan Ilyasova (15 pts), Pat Connaughton (13 pts), Tony Snell (12 pts) and John Henson (10 pts, 6 rebs). The Kings enjoyed solid efforts from De'Aaron Fox, who had 15 points, six rebounds and six assists, and Buddy Hield, who chipped in with 19 points in only 24 minutes of action. But most of the scoring contributions came from second - unit players who took advantage of the opportunity, such as Justin Jackson, who had 22 points, and rookie Marvin Bagley III, who finished with 11 points and six rebounds.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the host Milwaukee Bucks, 116 - 113, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday. This game was full of monster swings in the second half, as Memphis made the run that mattered most. In fact, Milwaukee went on a 27 - 4 run when they trailed by 15 points in the third quarter to take an eight - point lead early in the fourth. Memphis then responded with a 23 - 7 run to take an eight - point lead with two minutes remaining. The Bucks then ended the game on a 12 - 7 run but that simply wasn't enough to make up their deficit. Those small spurts by Milwaukee was the only time Memphis wasn't in control, as they led for 40 minutes of this game. Three-point shooting was huge for the Grizzlies, as they went 14 - of - 36 from long range while the Bucks hit just 9 - of - 35. Taking care of the ball was also critical, with Memphis recording two more assists than Milwaukee while committing four fewer turnovers. The Grizzlies (8 - 5) were led by Marc Gasol, as he tallied 29 points, five rebounds and two assists. Mike Conley accrued 26 points, two rebounds, four assists and two steals. Kyle Anderson collected six points, eight rebounds and five assists. Shelvin Mack led the bench with 15 points, six rebounds and five assists. The Bucks (10 - 4) got another gen out of Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he accumulated 31 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two blocks on 10 - of - 14 from the field. Khris Middleton finished with 25 points, five rebounds and three assists. Eric Bledsoe totaled 15 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Pat Connaughton led the bench with 16 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals. Both teams play home games on Friday for their next outings, with Milwaukee welcoming the Chicago Bulls and Memphis playing the Sacramento Kings.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 123 - 104, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Friday evening. The Bulls jumped out and stunned the Bucks, as they built a 16 - 6 lead just five minutes into the game, and went on to outscore the home team, 40 - 27, in the first quarter. The Bulls stayed in control, as they maintained a double - digit lead through the second quarter and took a 63 - 45 lead into halftime. The Bucks turned the tables in the third, as they kicked the quarter off with a 17 - 6 run, to cut the deficit to just seven. They carried on to outscore the Bulls by 29 in the quarter, to take a 91 - 80 lead into the fourth. The Bulls were not able to recover from the devastating third quarter, where they were outscored 46 - 17, as they were not even able to get back within 10 points of the Bucks for the remainder of the contest. Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 25 points, six assists, four rebounds, three steals and one block, in 30 minutes. Giannis Antetokounmpo followed up with 23 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and three blocks, while Khris Middleton added 23 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists and two steals. The Bucks shot 50 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 43 from long range. Meanwhile, Jabari Parker led the Bulls with 21 points, eight rebounds and three assists, in 33 minutes. Justin Holiday followed up with 20 points, four assists, three rebounds and three steals, while Antonio Blakeney tallied 18 points on 8 - of - 14 shooting, in 20 minutes off the bench. The Bulls shot 44 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 33 from long range. The Bulls (4 - 12) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Raptors on Saturday. The Bucks (11 - 4) play host to the Nuggets on Monday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 104 - 98, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Monday evening. The contest got out to a very competitive start, as there were multiple lead changes and ties through the first quarter, until the Nuggets emerged with a 29 - 25 lead, heading into the second. The Nuggets continued with the momentum, as they pushed their lead to 11, just two minutes into the quarter. They continued their push until they carried a 10 - point lead into halftime. The home team turned the tide in the third, as the Bucks chipped away at the lead, which the Nuggets continued to push ahead, until they finally broke ahead in the final minutes of the third quarter. The Bucks led 78 - 77, heading into the fourth. The contest continued with the score tied at 89, with five minutes left. The Bucks took the lead with a three - pointer and did not look back. Despite a continued effort from the Nuggets, the Bucks held on with clutch shooting down the stretch. Giannis Antetokounmpo led Milwaukee with 29 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and two steals, in 39 minutes. Eric Bledsoe followed up with 23 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals, in 35 minutes. Khris Middleton came up clutch with a crucial three - pointer, capping off a solid night, with 13 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Meanwhile, Nikola Jokic led the Nuggets with 20 points, five rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 32 minutes. Jamal Murray had a good game, with 17 points, nine assists, eight rebounds and one block. Gary Harris added 14 points, six assists and one steal, in 34 minutes. The Nuggets (10 - 7) will look to bounce back as they take on the Timberwolves in Minnesota, on Wednesday. The Bucks (12 - 4) play host to the trail Blazers on Wednesday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 143 - 100, at Fiserve Forum on Wednesday evening. The Bucks (13 - 4) had recently pledged to start playing sharper basketball from the opening quarter, in order to eliminate some of the last - minute comebacks that had somewhat become their trademark in recent games. They can consider Wednesday's effort mission accomplished in that regard, as the Milwaukee built a commanding 72 - 50 halftime lead. That would prove to be more than enough, as the home squad rained down another 71 points on the Trail Blazers (12 - 6), who were a bit road weary after having already played four away games over the previous seven days coming into Wednesday. Damian Lillard and C.J. McCollum paced the Trail Blazers with matching 22 - point tallies. Lillard added five assists and four rebounds, while McCollum provided a rebound, an assist and two steals. Jusuf Nurkic was the only other double - digit scorer with 16 points, and he also hauled in six boards. Al-Farouq Aminu totaled just four points but added nine rebounds, Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with 33 points and also contributed 16 rebounds, nine assists and three steals. Khris Middleton followed with 21 points, seven rebounds, four assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe and Malcolm Brogdon generated matching 16 - point efforts. Christian Wood and Thon Maker both chipped in 11 points off the bench, while pulling down five and eight rebounds, respectively. The Trail Blazers will remain on the road for one more game, facing off with the Golden State Warriors on Friday. The Bucks remain home and welcome the Phoenix Suns on Friday evening as well.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 116 - 114, at Fiserv Forum on Friday evening. The Suns (4 - 14) came into Saturday's contest still seeking their first road win of the season, and facing quite the uphill battle versus a Bucks (13 - 5) squad that had only dropped one home game. However, Phoenix made a statement by taking a 64 - 61 halftime lead, and they proved it wasn't a fluke by essentially hanging with Milwaukee basket for basket in the second half. The game was deadlocked at 114 - 114 when Jamal Crawford drained 17 - foot jumper with 1 seconds remaining to give the Suns an upset win. Devin Booker led the way with 29 points, a total he supplemented with seven assists, four rebounds and three steals. T.J. Warren provided 19 points, five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Deandre Ayton managed 17 points, seven rebounds and three assists. Trevor Ariza totaled 13 points, 11 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Richaun Holmes led the bench with 12 points, Josh Jackson and Crawford each pitched in 11 points. Giannis Antetokounmpo paced the Bucks with 35 points and added 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Malcolm Brogdon totaled 22 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal. Khris Middleton collected 15 points, six rebounds, four assists and one steal. Eric Bledsoe filled out the stat sheet with 12 points, seven assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Ersan Ilyasova led the bench with nine points, four rebounds and three assists. The Suns next pay a visit to the Detroit Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the Bucks remain home and take on the San Antonio Spurs in a Saturday night showdown.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting San Antonio Spurs, 135 - 129, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Saturday evening. The game got out to a very competitive start, as the Bucks outscored the Spurs, 37 - 36, in the first quarter. The back and forth battle continued through the second, this time with the Spurs taking the advantage, as they outscored the Bucks by two in the quarter, to take a 68 - 67 lead into halftime. The Spurs came out strong in the third, while the Bucks did not fall too far behind. However, the Spurs kept the pressure on and pushed their lead to seven, heading into the fourth. They stayed on top to start the fourth, quickly pushing their lead to 10, but the Bucks did not give up, as they made it a two - point game within just a couple of minutes. The Bucks reclaimed the lead for the first time in the quarter, with 3:13 to go. They went on to outscore the Spurs, 14 - 9, in the final minutes to secure the solid home win. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with 34 points, 18 rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Khris Middleton tallied 21 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal, while Eric Bledsoe finished with 20 points, 10 assists, four rebounds and two steals. The bucks shot 57 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 39 from long range. Meanwhile, DeMar DeRozan led San Antonio with 34 points, seven assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 34 minutes. Bryn Forbes followed up with 18 points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Davis Bertans chipped in 17 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Spurs (9 - 10) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bulls in Chicago on Monday. The Bucks (14 - 5) take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Monday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Chicago Bulls, 116 - 113, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday night. The Bucks (15 - 6) came in with a sparkling 10 - 2 home record, but with a feisty divisional rival on tap. The Bulls (5 - 17) made it clear they weren't fazed by Milwaukee's home - floor dominance in the first quarter, taking a quick 40 - 30 lead. The home squad had erased that advantage by halftime, but the game remained hotly contested into the closing seconds. Khris Middleton then drained a 27 - foot three - point jumper with 5 seconds remaining to snap a 113 - 113 tie, and Justin Holiday's desperation game - tying attempt with a second left couldn't find the net. Jabari Parker and Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with matching 24 - point efforts. They added eight and nine rebounds, respectively. Ryan Arcidiacono netted 22 points and also supplied five rebounds, four assists and five steals. Robin Lopez led the bench with 17 points and also hauled in five rebounds. Holiday finished with eight points, six rebounds, four assists and two steals. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with a 36 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists, two steals and one block. Malcolm Brogdon poured in 24 points and added six assists, five rebounds and one block. Middleton delivered 17 points, six rebounds and four assists. Brook Lopez totaled 12 points, five boards, two assists and two blocks. The Bulls next head to Motown, where they'll battle the Detroit Pistons on Friday night. The Bucks next take on the New York Knicks in the Big Apple on Saturday afternoon.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Detroit Pistons, 115 - 92, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday evening. The Bucks (16 - 7) came in well - rested, last having taken the court Saturday. That energy was evident in the first half, as Milwaukee had forged a 56 - 45 lead over the Pistons (13 - 9) by intermission. The home squad would keep the pressure on in the second half, compiling another 59 points while limiting Detroit to 47. The Bucks put on a stellar offensive show, holding the visitors to 36 percent shooting and forcing 20 turnovers. Blake Griffin's 31 points, which he supplemented with seven rebounds, four assists and one block, led the Pistons. Reggie Jackson provided 15 points, seven rebounds, five assists and one steal. Andre Drummond continued a string of quiet games with 10 points, eight boards, one assist and one steal. No other Detroit player hit double digits in the scoring column, with Zaza Pachuilia coming the closest with eight points off the bench. Eric Bledsoe paced the Bucks with 27 points, adding four assists, three rebounds and four steals. Giannis Antetokounmpo managed 15 points, eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Malcolm Brogdon poured in 14 points and also supplied six rebounds and two assists. Tony Snell drew a start for Khris Middleton (personal) and netted 11 points, seven rebounds, one assist and two steals. Thon Maker and Sterling Brown delivered matching 11 - point tallies off the bench. The Pistons head back home and tangle with the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night, while the Bucks remain home for a Friday night showdown against the Golden State Warriors.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 105 - 95, at Fiserv Forum on Friday evening. The Warriors (18 - 9) were looking for a little retribution after having been walloped by the Bucks back on Nov. 8 in their one previous meeting. This time they had the advantage of attacking the Bucks (16 - 8) with a fully healthy Stephen Curry, who'd exited that contest with a groin injury that would ultimately force him to miss the subsequent 11 games. Golden State forged a 57 - 51 halftime lead, but the game was ultimately won on defense in the fourth quarter. The visitors held Milwaukee to just 19 points over the final 12 minutes, a fitting finish to a strong effort on that end of the floor overall. The Warriors limited their hosts to 39 percent shooting, including 18 percent from three - point range, while also forcing 18 turnovers. Curry and Klay Thompson paced the Warriors with matching 20 - point tallies. Curry added eight assists, four rebounds and one steal, while Thompson supplied six assists, five rebounds, four steals and two blocks. Andre Iguodala turned in 15 points, eight boards, two assists, one steal and one block. Kevin Durant struggled through a 3 - for - 14 shooting night to finish with a modest 11 points, but he added eight boards, six assists and one steal. Giannis Antetokoumpo led the Bucks with a 22 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, two steals and two blocks. Malcolm Brogdon followed with 15 points, seven rebounds and three assists. Brook Lopez and Eric Bledsoe generated matching 14 - point contributions. Khris Middleton posted 10 points, eight rebounds and one steal, although he drained only four of 14 attempts. The Warriors head back home to take on the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday night, while the Bucks pay a visit to the Toronto Raptors on on Sunday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 108 - 92, at Fiserv Forum on Monday. This was an extremely lopsided matchup, as Milwaukee won this game in wire - to - wire fashion. A 31 - 18 first quarter really set the tone, as the Bucks held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Rebounding was huge for Milwaukee, as they out - rebounded Cleveland, 58 - 46. The shooting disparity was critical as well, with the Bucks shooting 44 percent from the field and 42 percent from three - point range while holding the Cavaliers to 37 percent from the field and 33 percent from long range. The Cavaliers (6 - 21) were led by Larry Nance Jr., as he provided 16 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two steals off the bench. Collin Sexton led the starters, as he accrued 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. Jaron Blossomgame recorded a double - double off the bench, amassing 11 points and 10 boards. The Bucks (18 - 8) played this game without Giannis Antetokounmpo (neck) but that clearly didn't affect them in this dominating victory. Eric Bledsoe led the way, as he collected 20 points, 12 rebounds and five assists. Malcolm Brogdon accumulated 18 points, five rebounds and five assists. Khris Middleton finished with 16 points seven rebounds and three assists. Sterling Brown led the bench with 12 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Both these teams return to action on Wednesday, with Milwaukee traveling to play the Indiana Pacers and Cleveland welcoming the New York Knicks to Quicken Loans Arena.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123 - 115, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday. The Bucks came into Wednesday's contest down several key bench players, but some unexpected names showed up when the team needed them to and the home team was able to hold off an undermanned New Orleans squad. Giannis Antetokounmpo still led the way for Milwaukee, posting 25 points, eight rebounds and eight assists in 34 minutes. With the other starters being less effective, however, the second unit stepped up in a major way, as Milwaukee got 49 points from its bench. Tony Snell and newcomer George Hill led the way with 13 and 11 points, respectively, but the surprise performance of the night came from D.J. Wilson, who had the best game of his short career as a Buck with nine points and 10 rebounds. As for the Pelicans, they were without Julius Randle and Nikola Mirotic due to ankle injuries, and they lost Anthony Davis to an illness for all of the second quarter and some of the third. But, despite being without their three key frontcourt players, they still managed to keep the game close and even had the lead going into halftime. This was thanks in large part to the performance out of Jahlil Okafor, who came off the bench in Davis' absence to score an impressive 17 points in just 13 minutes. Okafor shot 6 - of - 8 from the field and 5 - of - 7 from the free throw line. Even though he played just 29 minutes, Davis still managed to finish with a game - high 27 points and 11 rebounds, while Jrue Holiday finished with 25 points and 12 assists.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 112 - 96, at Fiserv Forum on Thursday Milwaukee came into this game as a sizable favorite and this 16 - point victory show just why, The Bucks did all their damage after the first quarter, as they won each of the final three quarters by at least five points apiece. That allowed them to hold the lead for the entirety of the second half while leading by at least five points for the final 16 minutes of action. Milwaukee's defense was critical, as they held New York to 37 percent shooting while winning the defensive rebounding differential, 46 - 33. The Bucks did a ton of damage down low on the offensive end too, outscoring the Knicks in the paint, 52 - 28. The Knicks (9 - 27) got a rare start from Luke Kornet, as he led the team with 23 points, three rebounds and five assists. Noah Vonleh accrued 15 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and three blocks. Emmanuel Mudiay finished with 13 points, three rebounds and six assists. Kevin Knox amassed 12 points and six boards. The Bucks (24 - 10) were led by Giannis Antetokoumpo, as he accumulated 31 points, 14 rebounds, eight assists and four blocks. Khris Middleton broke his shooting slump by totaling 25 points, six rebounds and five assists. Brook Lopez generated 17 points and three boards while D.J. Wilson led the bench with 10 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Milwaukee playing host to the Brooklyn Nets and New York traveling to Salt Lake City to face the Utah Jazz.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 129 - 115, at Fiserv Forum on Saturday afternoon. The Bucks (25 - 10) already had a sizable advantage going into the contest given their past body of work on their home floor this season. However, the news that D'Angelo Russell would be rested for Saturday's game brightened their prospects even further. The disparity between the two clubs was vividly illustrated in the first half, as Milwaukee jumped out to a 71 - 52 halftime lead. The Nets (17 - 21) were much more competitive in the second half, but Giannis Antetokounmpo's 31 - point, 10 - rebound, 10 - assist triple - double spearheaded the home squad's efforts and helped keep Brooklyn at bay. Shabazz Napier paced the Nets off the bench in Russell's absence, posting 32 points, seven assists, four rebounds and one steal. Kenneth Faried followed with a 21 - point, 10 - rebound double - double in 27 minutes off the bench after Rondae Hollis-Jefferson left the game with an adductor strain after logging just three minutes. DeMarre Carroll furnished 18 points. five rebounds and four assists. Joe Harris poured in 15 points, while Spencer Dinwiddie drew the start in Russell's place and provided 10 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal. Khris Middleton was right behind Antetokounmpo with 29 points, seven assists, four rebounds and one steal. Brook Lopez registered 24 points, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Malcolm Brogdon managed 18 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. D.J. Wilson pitched in seven points, seven rebounds and one assist. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Detroit Pistons, 121 - 98, at Fiserv Forum on Tuesday evening. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 124 - 86, at Fiserv Forum on Tuesday. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 116 - 106, at Fiserv Forum on Tuesday. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 140 - 128, at Fiserv Forum on Saturday evening. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 131 - 114, at Fiserv Forum on Saturday evening. The Bucks (59 - 21) were led by Eric Bledsoe, as he collected 33 points, four rebounds, 11 assists and two steals. Khris Middleton generated 24 points, four rebounds and three assists. Both teams have to play again on Sunday, with Brooklyn traveling to face the fading Indiana Pacers and Milwaukee playing host to the surging Atlanta Hawks.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 115 - 107, at Fiserv Forum on Sunday evening. The Bucks got out to a good start at home, with a 28 - 21 lead after one quarter. They stayed in control in the second and pushed their lead to 15, with five minutes left in the quarter, while the Hawks managed to trim it to a nine - point deficit by halftime. The Bucks retained control through the third, with a double - digit lead most of the way, until they took a 13 - point lead into the fourth. The Hawks kept fighting and chipped away though the quarter, and managed to make it a three - point game with four minutes left. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with 30 points, nine rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal, in 24 minutes. Khris Middleton followed up with 21 points, five rebounds, three assists and a block, while Sterling Brown and D.J. Wilson tallied 10 points each. The Bucks shot 44 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 41 from deep. Meanwhile, Alex Len led the Hawks with 33 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks, in 34 minutes. DeAndre' Bembry added 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal, while Kent Bazemore added 12 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Hawks shot 40 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 45 from deep. The Hawks (29 - 52) play host to the Pacers on Wednesday. The Bucks (60 - 21) play host to the Thunder on Wednesday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 127 - 116, at Fiserve Forum on Wednesday evening. The Thunder (49 - 33) came into the contest looking to enter the postseason on a strong note, but knew they'd be missing star forward Paul George due to the latter's shoulder injury. However, the Bucks were without Brook Lopez and Giannis Antetokounmpo for rest as well. Courtesy of a big second quarter, OKC took a 68 - 58 halftime lead. The two teams played a highly competitive second half as well, but the visitors' cushion served them well and allowed them to eventually secure an 11 - point victory to close out the campaign. Dennis Schroder led the way for the Thunder with 32 points, adding five rebounds, three assists and four steals. Jerami Grant provided 28 points, five rebounds and one assist. Russell Westbrook supplied a 15 - point, 17 - assist, 11 - rebound triple - double that included one steal and one block. Markief Morris and Raymond Felton generated matching 12 - point tallies while hauling in 10 rebounds and dishing out seven assists, respectively. Terrance Ferguson and Abdel Nader furnished 11 points apiece. Tim Frazier paced the Bucks with 29 points and supplemented them with 13 assists, six rebounds and one block. Bonzie Colson and Khris Middleton posted 21 points each, with Colson also bringing down 10 rebounds. D.J. Wilson posted an 18 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal. Patrick Connaughton poured in 12 points and added five rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Thunder now face the Houston Rockets in the first round of the Western Conference playoffs, while the Bucks face off against the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 118 - 116, at United Center on Saturday evening. The first quarter featured a few lead swings, with the Pistons up by as many as eight, however, it was the Bulls that led 27 - 25 heading into the second quarter. The Pistons pushed ahead again in the second, this time amassing a 10 - point lead, with 6:21 left in the half. The contest went right down to the wire, where Blake Griffin and Zach LaVine exchanged clutch three - points, but ultimate the Pistons survived to earn their second straight win and remain undefeated. The Bulls dropped to 0 - 2 on the season. Blake Griffin led the Pistons with 33 points, 12 rebounds, five assists and two block, in 35 minutes of action. Reggie Jackson followed up with 18 points, six assists and one rebound, while Andre Drummond tallied 10 points, 13 rebounds and one block, in 24 minutes. The Pistons shot 41 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 40 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 33 points, four rebounds and three assists, in 37 minutes. Justin Holiday followed up with 19 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Cameron Payne contributed 17 points, four assists and three rebounds. The Bulls shot 51 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 22 from long range. The Bulls (0 - 2) will be looking for their first win of the season, as they take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday. The Pistons (20) play host to the 76ers on Tuesday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 112 - 110, at United Center on Wednesday. Chicago was looking for their first win of the season in this competitive matchup, as it wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, there were 12 ties and 21 lead changes in total, as neither club led by more than 11 points. The Bulls actually scored the final four points of this game in the final 80 seconds, as that turned a two - point deficit into a two - point victory. The Hornets (2 - 3) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 23 points, three rebounds and six assists. Cody Zeller totaled 14 points, six rebounds and two assists. Nicolas Batum accrued 13 points, three rebounds and four assists while Jeremy Lamb amassed 12 points, three rebounds and three assists. The Bulls (1 - 3) got another gem out of Zach LaVine, as he led the way with 32 points, four rebounds and five assists. Cameron Payne was the only other starter in double figures, as he accumulated 21 points, five rebounds and four assists. Jabari Parker was huge off the bench, providing 11 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. These teams will have a rematch on Friday, but that will be played in Charlotte.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Chicago Bulls, 149 - 124, at United Center on Monday night. Things looked grim from the opening tip for the Bulls (2 - 5), which saw the Warriors (7 - 1) put up 12 quick points before three minutes were off the clock. It was all downhill from there, with one Klay Thompson largely responsible for their night of misery. Mired in a rather ordinary start, by his standards, to the new season, Thompson exploded for a trademark 52 - point performance that included an NBA-record 14 made three - pointers. As the final score and Thompson's final line both implied, the visitors shot extremely well, draining 55 percent of their attempts, including 53 percent from distance. Thompson added five rebounds and one steal to his game - high scoring haul. Stephen Curry was overshadowed for a change, but he still posted a solid 23 points eight rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block. Alfonzo McKinnie saw extended playing time off the bench and parlayed it into a 19 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one assist and one block. Quinn Cook collected 16 points, two rebounds and one assist. Kevin Durant generated 14 points and handed out eight assists in 28 minutes. Zach LaVine and Andrew Blakeney co - led the Bulls with matching 21 - point tallies. Rookie Wendell Carter, Jr. followed with 18 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Cameron Payne went for 15 points, three rebounds, two assists and one block. Jabari Parker matched Payne's scoring total off the bench and also hauled in nine rebounds, dished out six assists and recorded one block. The Warriors return home and face off with the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night, while the Bulls host the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday evening as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 108 - 107, in overtime at United Center on Wednesday. While these teams are on the opposite spectrum of wins and losses, it took an extra session to determine a winner. Denver ended regulation strong, as they went on an 8 - 2 run across the final three minutes to send the game into overtime. Despite the fact that Denver didn't score in the final 2:10 of overtime, Paul Millsap hit a putback with 0 seconds left to take the lead and win the game. That marked the 16th lead change of the game, as there were also 11 ties. Rebounding really carried Denver, as they outrebounded Chicago, 56 - 43. The Nuggets dominated down low through scoring as well, as they won the points in the paint battle, 62 - 40. The Nuggets (6 - 1) got a near triple - double out of Nikola Jokic, as he collected 22 points, 12 rebounds, nine assists, two steals and three blocks. Millsap finished with 19 points, six rebounds and three blocks to go along with his game - winner. Gary Harris accrued 16 points, five rebounds and two assists. Trey Lyles was huge off the bench, providing nine points, 10 rebounds and three assists. The Bulls (2 - 6) were led by Zach LaVine, as he accumulated 28 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Wendell Carter Jr. totaled 25 points, eight rebounds, five assists, three steals and three blocks. Justin Holiday amassed 15 points, five rebounds and five assists. Antonio Blakeney led the bench with 15 points and three boards. On deck for Denver is a road matchup versus the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday. As for Chicago, they return to action on Friday when they play host to the Indiana Pacers.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 107 - 105, at United Center on Friday evening. The Pacers (6 - 3) came into the contest at full health, which is much more than the host Bulls (2 - 7) could say. Chicago came in missing a quartet of key players, but they didn't let that stop them from giving Indiana everything it could handle. The hosts jumped out to a 37 - 22 first - quarter lead, but the visitors flipped the game in the second quarter to head into halftime with a slim two - point edge. The two teams then traded the lead back and forth throughout the second half, and Chicago boasted a 99 - 92 advantage as late as the 5:55 mark of the fourth quarter. However, Indiana went on a 15 - 6 run to finish the game, with a Darren Collison 19 - foot jumper with 18 seconds remaining ultimately serving as the game - winning bucket.
