Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 25 points, which he supplemented with 14 rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block. Turner supplied 18 points, three rebounds, three assists and six blocks. Collison provided 14 points overall, while Tyreke Evans led the bench with 13. Blakeney paced the Bulls with 22 points and three rebounds off the bench. Zach LaVine registered 20 points, six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Justin Holiday turned in 19 points, two assists and one rebound. Wendell Carter, Jr. and Jabari Parker provided matching 11 - point tallies, along with eight and seven rebounds, respectively. The Pacers head back home to take on the Boston Celtics on Saturday night, while the Bulls remain home and tangle with the Houston Rockets on Saturday evening as well.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 96 - 88, at United Center on Saturday evening. Despite a strong start from the Rockets, the Bulls kept it together and managed to pull ahead with a 28 - 27 lead after one. The second quarter was very similar, in that Houston started out strong and kept up a consistent attack, however, the Bulls were able to stay focused and once again outscore Houston by one in the quarter, to take a 56 - 54 lead into halftime. The third quarter started out very slow, with the Rockets outscoring the Bulls just 6 - 3, halfway through the quarter. The Rockets were able to pull themselves together, and outscored the Bulls 15 - 4 through the second half of the quarter, to take a 75 - 63 lead into the final frame. The Rockets pushed their lead to 17 early in the fourth and were able to ride it out from there. This marks the second win in a row for the Rockets, while the Bulls took their fourth straight loss. James Harden led the way for Houston with 25 points, seven assists, four steals and one rebound, in 33 minutes. Clint Capela was solid, with 12 points, 12 rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one rebound, while Carmelo Anthony tallied 17 points on 8 - of - 14 shooting, in 32 minutes off the bench. The Rockets shot 43 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 42 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 21 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 38 minutes. Wendell Carter Jr. had a big night with 14 points, 13 rebounds, four blocks, two steals and one assist, while Jabari Parker added 15 points, three rebounds and one steal. The Bulls shot 39 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 24 from long range. The Bulls (2 - 8) will look to bounce back as they take on the Knicks in New York on Monday. The Rockets (3 - 5) head to Indiana to take on the Pacers on Monday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 99 - 98, at United Center on Saturday evening. The Bulls got out to a great start at home, as they outscored the Cavs by 14 in the first quarter, to take a 37 - 23 lead into the second. The Cavs answered back in the second quarter though, as they evened things up, by outscoring the Bulls 30 - 16 in the quarter, making it a tie game at 53, by halftime. Neither team could rebuild their lead, as the game went back - and - forth through the third, until the Bulls emerged with a two - point lead heading into the final frame. The Bulls stayed one step ahead through the fourth, but the Cavs would not go away and fought their way to make it a one - point game with 1:13 left in the game. However, that was the last point that either team would score, as either team failed to execute down the stretch, leaving the Bulls to walk away with the one - point win. Zach LaVine led Chicago with 24 points, eight rebounds, five assists and two steals, in 39 minutes. Wendell Carter Jr. and Ryan Arcidiacono tallied 15 points each, while Jabari Parker finished with 13 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Chicago Bulls, 103 - 98, at United Center on Monday evening. The Mavericks (5 - 8) seem to be turning their season around following a negative start and now they have won three of their last four; that's quite an impressive achievement considering they began the year with a 2 - 7 record. Dallas jumped ahead 25 - 20 after the first quarter, and they further increased their lead to 56 - 49 at the break. The Bulls (4 - 10) fought back and made it things closer with a 26 - 22 win in the third quarter, to make it a three - point game entering the final 12 minutes of action. But the Mavs closed things out and with a 25 - 23 win in the fourth, they cruised their way towards a huge win that also represented Dallas' first W on the road during the 2018 - 19 season. Six Dallas players scored in double - digits in this game, including three players coming off the bench. Harrison Barnes led the way with 23 points, five rebounds and four steals, while young guards Dennis Smith Jr. and Luka Doncic contributed with 11 points each; Doncic also chipped in with six rebounds and three assists. J.J. Barea had 14 points off the bench, while Maximilian Kleber (12 points) and Dwight Powell (11 points) looked solid off the bench as well. Zach LaVine was the best player for the Bulls since he finished with 26 points, five rebounds, five assists and four steals. Justin Holiday contributed with 14 points, and Jabari Parker added 16 points, six rebounds and two assists for the losing cause. Wendell Carter Jr. only scored seven points, but chipped in with 10 rebounds and two blocks.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Chicago Bulls, 122 - 83, at United Center on Saturday evening. The Raptors (12 - 4) came into the contest likely smarting from their overtime loss to the Boston Celtics on Friday night, a game in which they blew a fourth - quarter lead. Toronto also came into Saturday's game short - handed, as they were without Kawhi Leonard (rest), OG Anunoby (wrist) and C.J. Miles (groin). However, the visitors set the tone early by jumping out to a 57 - 44 halftime lead. They then put any doubts about the outcome to rest in a dominant third period in which they racked up 32 points while limiting the Bulls (4 - 13) to just 12. Kyle Lowry eventually exited the game for the Raptors with victory firmly in hand during the second half, as he was hampered by a sore ankle. The game was a turnover fest, with Toronto actually outpacing Chicago in that department, 24 - 23. However, the Raptors drained 54 percent of their attempts while holding the Bulls to a 35 percent figure. Fred VanVleet drew the start for Leonard and led the Raptors with 18 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Danny Green turned in 17 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. Serge Ibaka produced 16 points, four rebounds, one assist, four blocks and two steals. Pascal Siakam collected 12 points, eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Lowry finished with eight points, eight assists, seven rebounds and three steals in 29 minutes before his exit. The Bulls had only three double - digit scorers, with Antonio Blakeney leading the way with 13 points off the bench. Jabari Parker and Justin Holiday followed with matching 12 - point efforts. Parker added six rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Holiday had four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Chandler Hutchinson and Robin Lopez posted nine points apiece on the second unit. The Raptors remain on the road and visit the Orlando Magic on Tuesday evening, while the Bulls remain home and take on the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday night.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 124 - 116, at United Center on Wednesday evening. The Suns got out to a good start on the road, as they outscored the Bulls, 28 - 25, in the first quarter. The second quarter picked up as a high - scoring period, where the Suns managed to maintain the upper hand by outscoring the Bulls, 41 - 39, in the quarter, to take a 69 - 64 lead into halftime. The Bulls picked it up in the third, as they snuck up on the Suns and took 91 - 85 lead, with just under five minutes left in the quarter. The Bulls stayed strong and kept the edge, with a 94 - 93 advantage heading into the final frame. The Suns kept it competitive right down to the wire, as they trailed, 119 - 116, with 1:27 to go. Nonetheless, the Bulls remained in control, as they held the Suns scoreless for the remainder of the contest. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 29 points, six assists, one rebound and one steal, in 37 minutes. The Bulls shot 57 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 25 from long range. Meanwhile, Devin Booker led the Suns with 23 points, six assists, three steals and two rebounds, in 33 minutes. Deandre Ayton followed up with 18 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, one steal and a block, while T.J. Warren added 21 points on 8 - of - 15 shooting. The Suns shot 49 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 34 from long range. The Suns (3 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bucks on Friday. The Bulls (5 - 13) play host to the Heat on Friday.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 103 - 96, at United Center on Friday evening. The Bulls got out to a good start at home, with an early 10 - 4 lead, but the Heat came back to take a 28 - 26 lead into the second. The Heat continued their push into the second quarter, where they outscored the Bulls 32 - 13, to take a convincing 60 - 39 lead by halftime. However, the Bulls were not finished, as they came out strong in the third and carried on to outscore the Heat, 30 - 18, in the quarter, to cut the deficit to nine entering the fourth quarter. They continued the push and cut the gap to just four points, but the Heat were able to keep the edge and regain a double - digit lead, en route to the much - needed win, ending a three - game slide. Josh Richardson led the way for Miami with 27 points on 10 - of - 16 shooting, three assists, two rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 33 minutes. Hassan Whiteside finished with 18 points, 10 rebounds, four blocks, one assist and one steal, while Bam Adebayo added 14 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and one block, in 26 minutes. The Heat shot 42 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Justin Holiday led the Bulls with 27 points on 9 - of - 16 shooting, 13 rebounds, three steals, two assists and one block, in 39 minutes. Jabari Parker followed up with 23 points, 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal, while Zach LaVine added 24 points, nine assists, four rebounds and one block. The Bulls (5 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Timberwolves in Minnesota on Saturday. The Heat (7 - 11) head to Toronto to take on the Raptors on Sunday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Chicago Bulls, 108 - 107, at United Center on Monday night. The struggling Bulls (5 - 16) came out ready to defend home court Monday, as they matched the Spurs (10 - 10) basket for basket in the first quarter and trailed by only two at halftime. Chicago actually took a three - point lead int the final quarter, but they'd fallen behind 108 - 101 by the 2:13 mark of the period. However, Ryan Arcidiacono would drain a pair of three - pointers over a period of 1:2, bringing the home squad within one. After missed three - pointers by either side, the second - year guard's 18 - foot jumper with under a second remaining couldn't find the basket, leading to a Spurs win. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 21 points, a total he supplemented with eight rebounds and five assists. Bryn Forbes poured in 13 points and added six assists and two rebounds. Jakob Poeltl posted 10 points, four rebounds and four assists in 18 minutes. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 28 points and added eight rebounds and seven assists. Arcidiacono totaled 22 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals. Jabari Parker mustered an 18 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that included two assists and two steals. Justin Holiday filled out the stat sheet with 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. The Spurs remain on the road and tangle with the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday night, while the Bulls travel to take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday evening as well.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 114 - 112, at United Center on Friday evening. The Bulls (6 - 20) kept the Thunder (16 - 7) on their heels throughout the first half on their way to compiling an impressive 70 points. They'd see their eight - point halftime advantage evaporate in the third quarter, however, as Oklahoma City outscored them by a 29 - 17 margin. That set up an exciting final 12 minutes, one that saw Chicago claw their way back to outscore the visitors by six and notch the hard - fought win when Lauri Markkanen hit a game - winning layup with 5 seconds remaining. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 25 points and added seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Markkanen collected 22 points, six rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block. Justin Holiday contributed 17 points, six boards and three steals. Jabari Parker delivered 16 points, seven rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Thunder heads back home to take on the Utah Jazz on Monday night, while the Bulls remain home to take on the Boston Celtics on Saturday evening.

The Boston Celtics defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 133 - 77, at United Center on Saturday. Boston came into this game as a big favorite but no one could ever anticipate a 56 - point win. The Celtics actually started the game with 17 unanswered points, as that obviously killed the Bulls demeanor. It's not like they rebounded in the second half though, as Boston outscored Chicago, 69 - 34. Every statistic was lopsided in the Celtics favor, as they really dominated through defense. In fact, they held the Bulls to 38 percent from the field and 25 percent from three - point range while winning the turnover differential, 15 - 7. In addition, Boston outrebounded Chicago, 54 - 37, while connecting on 54 percent from the field and 51 percent from long range. Terry Rozier also played well off the bench, providing 15 points, eight rebounds, two assists and three steals. The Bulls (6 - 21) had just one starter reach double figures, as Zach LaVine totaled 11 points, three rebounds and two assists. Lauri Markkanen and Justin Holiday combined for 13 points on 5 - of - 20 shooting. Shaquille Harrison led the team in scoring, providing 20 points off the bench. Cameron Payne accrued 10 points, three rebounds and three assists off the bench as well. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Chicago welcoming the Sacramento Kings to United Center and Boston playing host to the New Orleans Pelicans.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 108 - 89, at United Center on Monday evening. The Kings jumped out to an early, 10 - 4, lead, but the Bulls battled back to take a, 33 - 26, lead by the end of the first. De'Aaron Fox led the Kings with 25 points, six assists, four rebounds, four steals and one block, in 33 minutes. Bogdan Bogdanovic and Marvin Bagley III tallied 16 points each, while Willie Cauley-Stein added 11 points, 16 rebounds, three assists and three steals. The Kings shot 46 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 37 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 19 points, three steals, two rebounds and two assists, in 32 minutes. Lauri Markkanen tallied 13 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Kris Dunn, Bobby Portis and Justin Holiday chipped in nine points each. The Bulls shot 45 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 28 from long range. The Bulls (6 - 22) will look to bounce back as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Thursday. The Kings (14 - 12) host the Timberwolves on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 96 - 93, at United Center on Wednesday. Spencer Dinwiddie was their best player, as he provided 27 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals off the bench. The Chicago Bulls defeated the Orlando Magic, 90 - 80, at United Center on Friday evening. Nikola Vucevic delivered a 19 - point, 19 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Aaron Gordon produced 14 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. D.J. Augustin mustered eight points, three rebounds and two assists. The Bulls were led by Lauri Markkanen, who racked up 32 points, six rebounds, three asists and one block. Robin Lopez followed with a bench - leading 14 points and also had four rebounds, two assists and one block. Justin Holiday posted an 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, one steal and one block. The Magic heads back home to face the Miami Heat on Sunday evening, while the Bulls pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Sunday evening as well.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 119 - 94, at United Center on Wednesday. Minnesota won this game in wire - to - wire fashion, as a 29 - 18 first quarter really set the tone. They followed that up with a 31 - 19 second quarter, as the T'Wolves led by 31 points at times in the second half. Their defense was the difference, as they held the Bulls to 41 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range. Minnesota connected on 50 percent from the field and 34 percent from long range. Rebounding was also a big factor, with Minnesota outrebounding Chicago, 52 - 45. The Timberwolves (16 - 18) got another vintage performance from Derrick Rose, as he tallied 24 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Karl-Anthony Towns collected 20 points, 20 rebounds and four assists. Taj Gibson totaled 16 points, three rebounds and two assists. Tyus Jones led their bench with 13 points and five assists. The Bulls (9 - 26) got Zach Lavine back from an ankle injury, as he provided 28 points and two assists off the bench. Lauri Markkanen led the starters with 16 points and seven boards. Wendell Carter Jr. amassed 12 points, nine rebounds and two blocks. Kris Dunn flirted with a triple - double, as he accumulated nine points, eight rebounds and seven assists before fouling out. Justin Holiday had a game to forget, as he scored two points on 1 - of - 11 shooting. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Chicago traveling to face the stumbling Washington Wizards and Minnesota playing host to the struggling Atlanta Hawks.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Chicago Bulls,112 - 84, at United Center on Wednesday. It didn't take long for this game to get out of hand, as the Magic (17 - 20) opened up a 16 - point lead in the first quarter and didn't look back. They continued to pile it on from there behind the stellar play of their starting frontcourt. Nikola Vucevic played just 26 minutes in the outing, but he still managed to post 22 points and and 12 rebounds on 10 - of - 15 shooting from the field. Close behind was Aaron Gordon, who had a terrific all - around performance, scoring 18 points to go along with seven rebounds and nine assists in 37 minutes. As a team, the Magic managed to take advantage of a poor defense effort from the home team, shooting 42 percent from three and a scorching 58 percent from the field overall. As for the Bulls (10 - 28), this was their second straight loss and the second straight game they failed to score at least 90 points. It was another miserable shooting night for Chicago, as while they managed to shoot a decent mark from three (35 percent), they hit just seven shots from deep and still shot just 42 percent from the field overall. Zach LaVine was the lead scorer with only 16 points, while Lauri Markkanen and Kris Dunn scored just 14 points each. What hurt the Bulls immensely was getting absolutely nothing out of starting center Wendell Carter Jr., as the rookie shot 0 - of - 5 from the field and posted zero points and one rebound in just 13 minutes.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 119 - 116, in overtime at United Center on Friday evening. The Bulls got out to a great start at home with a 30 - 18 lead after one quarter. However, the Pacers rallied in the second to cut the deficit to just four points by halftime. The third quarter was a bit quieter, as the Pacers outscored the Bulls 21 - 20 in the quarter. The Pacers continued to chip away through the fourth and took the lead mid way through the quarter, but the home squad did not give up and thanks to a clutch three - pointer from Zach LaVine, forced overtime. Victor Oladipo came up as the savior for Indiana, as the he drilled a last - second three in OT, to seal the win for the visitors. Oladipo led the Pacers with 36 points, seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and one block, in 37 minutes. Domantas Sabonis came up huge off the bench, with 23 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal, while Thaddeus Young finished with 16 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 31 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals, in 34 minutes. Lauri Markkanen finished with 27 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Wendell Carter Jr. added 15 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. The Bulls (10 - 29) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Sunday. The Pacers (26 - 12) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Sunday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Chicago Bulls, 117 - 100, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The Nets (20 - 21) came out ready to roll in enemy territory, building a 28 - 21 first - quarter lead. The two teams then alternated the advantage throughout the middle periods, but it was Brooklyn who carried the 88 - 82 lead into the final 12 minutes. They built on their edge from there, finishing the game on a 29 - 18 run to take home the double - digit victory. D'Angelo Russell led the way for the Nets with 28 points, supplementing them with five assists, four rebounds and one steal. DeMarre Carroll followed with 20 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. Jarrett Allen contributed 19 points, six rebounds and two blocks. Shabazz Napier registered 18 points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Jared Dudley supplied 10 points, four assists and one steal. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 27 points and added two rebounds, two assists and one block. Bobby Portis delivered 17 points and five rebounds. Kris Dunn managed 16 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen totaled 14 points, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Chandler Hutchison collected eight points, four rebounds and one assist. Wendell Carter, Jr. offered six points, eight rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. The Nets remain on the road and visit the Boston Celtics on Monday evening, while the Bulls take on the Portland Trail Blazers out west on Wednesday night.

The Miami Heat defeated the Chicago Bulls, 117 - 103, at United Center on Saturday evening. The Heat (22 - 22) walked into a hornet's nest despite the Bulls' unsightly 10 - 36 record, as Chicago came out ready to defend home court. Miami faced a slim 57 - 55 halftime deficit, but they came out of intermission ready to take control. The visitors outscored their hosts by a 62 - 46 in the second half to eventually secure the double - digit victory, The Heat shot an outstanding 57 percent, and the Miami second unit scored 64 of the team's points. Josh Richardson returned from a one - game absence due to an illness to lead the way with 26 points. He added three rebounds and two assists. Dion Waiters tallied 21 points, six boards and two assists. Tyler Johnson and Dwyane Wade managed matching 14 - point efforts. Wade added 10 rebounds and seven assists. Justise Winslow supplied 11 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. James Johnson generated 10 points, three boards, two assists and one steal. Hassan Whiteside offered six points but hauled in 10 rebounds, dished out three assists and recorded three blocks. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 22 points, adding six assists, three rebounds and one steal. Bobby Portis followed with 21 points and also posted six boards, two assists and one steal. Lauri Markkanen followed with 20 points, nine rebounds, two steals and one block. Jabari Parker delivered 11 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Heat remain on the road and face the Boston Celtics on Monday evening, while the Bulls pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday afternoon.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 121 - 101, at United Center on Wednesday. Atlanta hasn't had many dominant wins this season but this was a much needed wire - to - wire victory for them. In fact, a 42 - 25 first quarter really set the tone, as they held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Rebounding was key for the Hawks, as they outrebounded the Bulls, 51 - 37. Ball movement was huge as well, with Atlanta out - assisting Chicago, 31 - 20. The Hawks ended up shooting 50 percent from the field while holding the Bulls to 44 percent shooting. The Hawks (15 - 32) got a career - best 35 points from John Collins, adding eight rebounds, two assists and two steals to his tally on 14 - of - 16 from the field. Taurean Prince totaled 15 points, six rebounds and two assists. Dewayne Dedmon amassed 14 points, seven rebounds and five assists while Trae Young led the team with 12 assists despite going 1 - of - 12 from the field. Alex Len recorded a double - double off the bench. The Bulls (11 - 37) were led by Zach LaVine, as he collected 23 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Lauri Markkanen amassed 22 points and six rebounds. Kris Dunn accumulated 16 points, four rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks while Wayne Selden led the bench with 11 points. Chicago returns to action on Friday, as they play host to the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Atlanta, they travel to face the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday for their next fixture.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 106 - 101, at United Center on Friday. There were six ties and eight lead changes in this competitive game, as it came down to the wire. Los Angeles did most of their damage in the first and fourth quarters, outscoring Chicago, 53 - 39. The Clippers defense was key, as they held the Bulls to 39 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range. Ball movement was huge as well, with Los Angeles out - assisting Chicago, 27 - 20. The Clippers were much more effective with the whistle too, as they hit 22 - of - 29 of their free throws while the Bulls connected on 11 - of - 12. The Clippers bench was also a huge factor, outscoring the Bulls bench, 54 - 20; The Clippers (27 - 22) got a triple - double from Lou Williams off the bench, as he provided 31 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Tobias Harris led the starters with 29 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Avery Bradley totaled 11 points, five rebounds and two assists while Montrezl Harrell amassed 11 points and four rebounds off the bench. The Bulls (11 - 38) were led by Zach LaVine, as he tallied 29 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Bobby Portis started and finished with 18 points and 14 rebounds. Chandler Hutchinson accrued 12 points, 12 rebounds and two assists while Kris Dunn finished with nine points, four rebounds, 10 assists and four steals. Jabari Parker led the bench with 15 points, four rebounds and three assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Los Angeles playing host to the Sacramento Kings and Chicago welcoming the Cleveland Cavaliers to United Center.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 104 - 101, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The Cavaliers (10 - 41) finally reached the double - digit win mark in a tough contest on the road against the Bulls (11 - 39), as both struggling sides locked horns but ended delivering a tightly - contested affair that was only decided in the final minutes. Chicago won the first quarter by a two - point margin (29 - 27) and they held that lead at half time (53 - 51), but Cleveland turned things around. They won the remaining two quarters by slim margins as well (28 - 26 and 25 - 22, respectively) to walk away with a huge win away from home. Five Cleveland players reached the 10 - point mark in this game and their best scorer was Jordan Clarkson, who came off the bench to finish with 18 points, seven rebounds and six assists in only 22 minutes of action. Matthew Dellavedova also chipped in with 16 points and five assists in 22 minutes off the bench. As for the starters, Alec Burks had 18 points, Rodney Hood chipped in with 17, and Cedi Osman added 17 points with eight boards. Only four Chicago players scored in double digits and all of them were part of the starting lineup. The top scorer was Lauri Markkanen, as he contributed 21 points and 15 rebounds to the losing cause. Zach LaVine posted an oddly - similar stat line since he finished with 17 points and 12 boards. Wayne Selden had 15 points, and Robin Lopez added 16 points.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 125 - 120, at United Center on Wednesday. This was a tale of two halves, as Chicago dominated the first half but New Orleans prevailed in the second half. In fact, the Bulls led for the entirety of the first half while the Pelicans led for the final 16 minutes of action. A 27 - 17 third quarter really made the difference, as Chicago couldn't recover from that. Rebounding was key for New Orleans, as they outrebounded Chicago, 46 - 36. The shooting disparity was also key, with the Pelicans shooting 53 percent from the field and the Bulls hitting 49 percent of their shots. They also outscored Chicago in the paint, 60 - 50, while outscoring their bench, 63 - 27. The Pelicans (24 - 31) were led by Julius Randle, as he provided 31 points, seven rebounds and three assists off the bench. Jrue Holiday led the starters with 18 points, six rebounds and 11 assists. Jahlil Okafor amassed 14 points and five boards while Cheick Diallo totaled 18 points and nine boards off the bench. The Bulls (12 - 42) were led by Lauri Markkanen, as he finished with 30 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Zach LaVine accumulated 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and two blocks. Kris Dunn collected 18 points, four rebounds, eight assists and two steals while Robin Lopez generated 11 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Friday, with New Orleans playing host to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Chicago traveling to face the surging Brooklyn Nets.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 134 - 125, at Capital One Arena on Saturday. These teams made a huge move at the trade deadline on Thursday, as many of those pieces were huge factors here. Washington got the better of Chicago thanks to a 42 - 29 second quarter, as the Wizards led by at least six points for the entirety of the second half. The Wizards offense was unstoppable, as they shot 58 percent from the field and 44 percent from three - point range while holding Chicago to 50 percent from the field and 25 percent from long range. Much of that can be attributed to ball movement, with the Wizards out - assisting the Bulls, 38 - 28. Bench production was also critical, with Washington outscoring Chicago's bench, 64 - 38. The Wizards (24 - 32) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 31 points, two rebounds, four assists and four steals. Trevor Ariza accumulated 19 points, four rebounds and four assists. Tomas Satoransky finished with seven points, seven rebounds and 11 assists. Jabari Parker led the bench with 20 points, five rebounds and six assists. Bobby Portis also played well off the bench, amassing 10 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. The Bulls (13 - 43) were led by Zach LaVine, as he accrued 26 points, four rebounds and six assists. Lauri Markkanen finished with 20 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Otto Porter generated 17 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals while Robin Lopez totaled 18 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Wayne Selden Jr. led the bench with 17 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Chicago playing host to the surging Milwaukee Bucks and Washington traveling to face the Detroit Pistons.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 112 - 99, at United Center on Monday. Milwaukee came into this game as a sizable favorite and they won in workman - like fashion. In fact, they won or tied all four individual quarters, as a 62 - 50 second half really put separation between the two teams. That allowed Milwaukee to hold the lead for the final three quarters, as the Bucks finished the game on a 12 - 2 run to cap off the victory. The shooting disparity was key, with the Bucks shooting 48 percent from the field while holding the Bulls to 39 percent shooting. Rim protection was also critical, with Milwaukee out - blocking Chicago, 7 - 2. In addition, the Bucks outrebounded the Bulls on the defensive end, 44 - 36. The Bucks (42 - 14) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he tallied 29 points, 17 rebounds, eight assists and three blocks. Eric Bledsoe accrued 19 points, two assists and two steals. Malcolm Brogdon accrued 17 points, six rebounds and three assists while Khris Middleton collected 16 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals. The Bulls (13 - 44) were led by Zach LaVine, as he accumulated 27 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Lauri Markkanen amassed 20 points, 17 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Otto Porter totaled 18 points, seven rebounds and four assists while Robin Lopez finished with 17 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Chicago playing host to the Memphis Grizzlies and Milwaukee traveling to face the resurgent Indiana Pacers.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 122 - 110, at United Center on Wednesday evening. The hometown Bulls (14 - 44) got off to a surprisingly fast start against the typically defensive - minded Grizzlies (23 - 36), racking up 67 first - half points. However, given Chicago's defensive vulnerability, Memphis essentially kept pace, and the hosts' lead was only five at intermission. The Bulls kept coming in the third by adding another four points to their advantage, and a 13 - 7 run over the first 3:4 of the final period gave them the cushion they'd need for the double - digit home win. Chicago shot especially well and dominated on the boards, draining 56 percent of its attempts while outrebounding the visitors by a 47 - 31 margin. Avery Bradley put together a second straight productive outing by pacing the Grizzlies with 15 points. He added five assists, one rebound and one steal. Jaren Jackson, Jr., Mike Conley, Jonas Valanciunas and Delon Wright generated a quartet of 12 - point tallies. Bruno Caboclo and Joakim Noah had eight points apiece, with the former also supplying five rebounds and two assists, and the latter totaling three boards, three dimes and two blocks. Otto Porter, Jr. paced the Bulls with a career - high 37 points and supplemented them with 10 rebounds, two assists and one block. Robin Lopez furnished 25 points, five rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Lauri Markkanen generated a 21 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and one steal. Zach LaVine delivered 15 points, seven assists and six rebounds. Cristiano Felicio led the bench with eight points. Ryan Arcidiacono drew the start for Kris Dunn (back) and mustered just two points but also dished out 11 assists, hauled in six rebounds and recorded a steal. The Grizzlies are now off until Feb. 22, when they'll host the Los Angeles Clippers. The Bulls return to action that same night with a road matchup against the Orlando Magic.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Boston Celtics, 126 - 116, at United Center on Saturday night. The Bulls (16 - 44) were riding high after a hard - fought one - point road victory Friday against the Magic, but they had an exponentially difficult challenge just 24 hours later in the form of the Celtics (37 - 23). Matters looked a bit worrisome for Chicago early, as Boston forged a five - point lead after 12 minutes. However, the visitors never saw what hit them in the second, as the Bulls doubled them up by a 36 - 18 margin in the second to carry a 13 - point advantage into halftime. After both teams matched each other bucket for bucket in the third, the hosts put the final nail in the proverbial coffin with a 32 - point fourth quarter, ultimately allowing the Celtics to cut three points into their lead. Both teams shot well, but it was Chicago that dominated the boards with a 49 - 32 rebounding advantage. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 37 points, adding 10 assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Al Horford contributed 19 points, three assists, two rebounds and one block. Jaylen Brown registered 14 points, three rebounds and two steals. Jayson Tatum and Marcus Morris contributed 12 points apiece, with the latter notably hauling in six boards as well. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 42 points and supplemented them with six rebounds and four assists. Lauri Markkanen turned in 35 points, 15 rebounds, two assists and one steal. Robin Lopez collected 17 points, six boards and four assists. Wayne Selden saw extra playing time after Otto Porter, Jr. exited early with a leg injury, totaling nine points, six rebounds, two assists and one block. The Celtics remain on the road and next face off with their biggest Eastern Conference rival in the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday night. The Bulls remain home and tangle with the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 117 - 106, at United Center on Monday. Milwaukee came into this game as a sizable favorite and a double - digit victory vindicates that notion. Despite the fact that Chicago led by 13 points after the first quarter, Milwaukee responded with a 38 - 16 second quarter to take control. That allowed the Bucks to lead for the entirety of the second half, as Chicago never got it within a six - point margin in the third or fourth quarter. Rim protection was key for the Bucks, as they doubled up the Bulls in blocks, 6 - 3. Fastbreak scoring was also huge, with Milwaukee winning that battle, 15 - 5. The Bucks bench was also decisive, as they outscored the Bulls, 42 - 24 The Bucks (46 - 14) had to play without Giannis Antetounmpo (knee soreness) but this game was no problem. Khris Middleton led the way in his absence, as he tallied 22 points, four rebounds and three assists. Malcolm Brogdon accrued 22 points, two rebounds and five assists. Brook Lopez finished with 13 points, four rebounds and five blocks. The Bulls (16 - 45) were led by Robin Lopez, as he accumulated 26 points, three rebounds and two assists. Lauri Markkanen totaled 26 points, 12 rebounds and three assists. Timothe Luwawu-Cabbarrot started and accrued 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Zach LaVine collected 11 points, eight rebounds and nine assists. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Chicago traveling to face the Memphis Grizzlies and Milwaukee playing the Sacramento Kings on the road as well.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 123 - 118, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The contest picked up where it left off in the Bulls' and Hawks' last meeting, which was four - overtime shootout. The first quarter was a high - scoring one, with the Hawks taking a 35 - 32 lead into the second. They managed to hold the edge through the second and pushed their lead to seven by halftime. The Hawks kept up the momentum in the third, as they pushed their lead to 15, just minutes into the quarter. However, the Bulls kept fighting and managed to cut the deficit to five by the start of the fourth. They played hard through the fourth as well, but the Hawks stayed in control and held on for the road win. Alex Len led the Hawks with 28 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two blocks, in 26 minutes. Trae Young followed up with 18 points, five assists and three rebounds, while Dewayne Dedmon added 13 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and one steal. The Hawks shot 47 percent from the field, including 21 - of - 43 from long range. Meanwhile, Lauri Markkanen led the Bulls with 19 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two steals, in 28 minutes. Robin Lopez followed up with 16 points, six rebounds, four assists and a block, while Kris Dunn chipped in 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. The Bulls shot 51 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 27 from long range. The Bulls (18 - 46) will look to bounce back as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Tuesday. The Hawks (22 - 42) take on the Heat in Miami on Monday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 108 - 107, at United Center on Wednesday evening. The 76ers got out to a good start on the road, with a 12 - 4 lead early on. However, the Bulls battled back to tie the score at 30 by the end of the first quarter. The contest stayed tight through the second, with neither team leading by more than a couple of possessions, until they sat tied at 57, entering halftime. The contest stayed close in the third. The Bulls led by one with a minute left in the quarter, but the Sixers closed strong, to take a four - point lead into the final frame. The Sixers pushed their lead to eight, four minutes into the fourth, but the Pelicans hung around, and managed to tie it up at 98, with 3:41 to go. The lead changed hands a few times in the final minute, before the Bulls came out on top, thanks to a game - winning bucket from Zach LaVine. LaVine led the Bulls with 39 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 36 minutes. Robin Lopez followed up with 19 points, nine rebounds and three assists, while Otto Porter Jr. added 15 points, nine rebounds, three assists and three steals. The Bulls shot 44 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 23 from deep. Meanwhile, Jimmy Butler led the 76ers with 22 points, four assists, three rebounds and three steals, in 35 minutes. Ben Simmons added 18 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists and four steals, while J.J. Redick added 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. The 76ers (41 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Rockets in Houston on Friday. The Bulls (19 - 47) play host to the Pistons on Friday.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Chicago Bulls, 112 - 104, at United Center on Friday evening. The Pistons (33 - 31) got themselves into a first - half hole, falling behind by a 66 - 49 halftime margin. The light went on at intermission, however, as Detroit held the Bulls (19 - 48) to just 14 third - quarter points and then racked up 43 over the final 12 minutes to secure the hard - fought road win. The visitors won the rebounding battle by a 41 - 35 margin, with Andre Drummond contributing 24 of those boards. Blake Griffin paced the Pistons with 27 points, adding three rebounds, three assists and one block. Reggie Jackson poured in 21 points and added two assists, one rebound and one steal. Drummond supplemented his outstanding work on the boards with 20 points, two assists, three steals and two blocks. Langston Galloway led the bench with 15 points, while Luke Kennard contributed 14. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 24 points and complemented them with six rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Otto Porter, Jr. supplied 23 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen turned in 18 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Robin Lopez furnished 13 points, four boards and one block. Kris Dunn totaled seven points, seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 28 minutes. The Pistons and Bulls next face off in a rematch in Detroit on Sunday afternoon.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 123 - 107, at United Center on Tuesday evening. The final score seemed especially improbable after one quarter, considering the Bulls (19 - 50) jumped out to a 34 - 16 lead through the first 12 minutes. However, the Lakers (31 - 36) began chipping away at their deficit in the second, shaving 13 points off Chicago's lead by halftime. The third quarter is when the game truly turned, as the visitors racked up a whopping 43 points during the period to erase the remaining deficit and build a 14 - point edge going into the fourth. Los Angeles ultimately cruised to a comfortable win, riding a red - hot 55 percent success rate from the floor to success. LeBron James led the Lakers with 36 points, complementing them with 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope supplied 24 points, six rebounds, one assist and two steals. Kyle Kuzma checked in with 21 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. Rajon Rondo generated a 14 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds and two steals. JaVale McGee delivered 10 points, 11 rebounds, three blocks and one steal. Reggie Bullock furnished nine points, two rebounds and two steals. Robin Lopez paced the Bulls with 20 points, adding seven rebounds and three assists. Otto Porter, Jr. delivered 19 points, nine rebounds and two assists. Kris Dunn contributed 18 points, nine assists and seven rebounds. Ryan Arcidiacono started for Zach LaVine (knee) and compiled 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen shot just 4 - for - 17 on his way to 11 points and five boards. The Lakers remain on the road and head north of the border to take on the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night, while the Bulls pay a visit to the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday evening.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Washington Wizards, 126 - 120, in overtime at United Center on Wednesday night. The Bulls (21 - 52) got off to a quick start by forging a 35 - 28 first - quarter lead, but the game was knotted at 60 by intermission. Fittingly, the game continued as a see - saw affair throughout the second half, and Bradley Beal sent the contest into overtime with a jumper at the 2 - second mark of the fourth period. However, Chicago opened the extra period on a 50 run and eventually outscored Washington by a 13 - 7 margin for the victory. Jabari Parker led the way for the Wizards with 28 points, adding six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Beal delivered 27 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks. Tomas Satoransky managed 16 points, seven assists, five rebounds and three steals. Bobby Portis posted 15 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Jeff Green provided 10 points, five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Trevor Ariza managed six points, two rebounds and two assists across 14 minutes before exiting with a groin injury. Lauri Markkanen paced the Bulls with 32 points, complementing them with 13 rebounds, five assists and one block. Kris Dunn turned in a 26 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included six rebounds and two steals. Shaquille Harrison registered 18 points, six rebounds and four steals. Cristiano Felicio totaled 15 points, six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot contributed 13 points, four boards, three assists and two steals. The Wizards head back home to face the Denver Nuggets on Thursday evening, while the Bulls remain home and take on the Utah Jazz at Saturday night.

The Utah Jazz defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 114 - 83, at United Center on Saturday. Utah came into this game as a sizable favorite and this final scoreline shows just why. A 33 - 18 first quarter really set the tone and then a 37 - 18 second quarter was the dagger. In fact, that allowed the Jazz to lead by at least 28 points for the entirety of the second half. Utah ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 34 percent from three - point range while holding Chicago to 36 percent from the field and 13 percent from long range. The Jazz also out - rebounded the Bulls, 57 - 44, and out - assisted them, 27 - 16. The Jazz (43 - 30) were led by Rudy Gobert, as he tallied 21 points, 14 rebounds, two assists and four blocks on 9 - of - 11 from the field. Donovan Mitchell finished with 16 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Joe Ingles accrued 13 points, six rebounds and three assists while Jae Crowder led the bench with 11 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Bulls (21 - 53) got a double - double from Lauri Markkanen to lead the team, as he amassed 18 points and 10 rebounds. Robin Lopez totaled 10 points and four boards. Shaquille Harrison collected six points, nine rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Cristiano Felicio led the bench with 10 points, six rebounds and two assists. On deck for Utah is a home matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Monday. As for Chicago, they're off until Tuesday when they travel to face the Toronto Raptors.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 118 - 98, at United Center on Wednesday. The Blazers (47 - 27) were widely expected to dominate the game against the Bulls (21 - 55) and that's exactly what happened at United Center, as they controlled the action right from tip - off. Portland quickly jumped to a 27 - 14 lead in the first half, and they would never relinquish that advantage. The second quarter finished 32 - 27 and the third one finished 28 - 24, so by the time of the final 12 minutes, Portland had the game already wrapped up. Chicago won the final quarter by a 33 - 31 score, but that didn't affect the score since Portland cruised their way to a 20 - point win. Six Portland players finished with a double - digit scoring total but surprisingly, Seth Curry led the way off the bench with 20 points. Rodney Hood had 15 points and Zach Collins added 13 points, meaning most of the heavy scoring was done thanks to the bench players. Damian Lillard finished with 11 points, seven assists and six rebounds. Enes Kanter delivered 13 points and six boards. Al-Farouq Aminu had 12 points and 11 boards. Six Chicago players scored over 10 points. Shaquille Harrison led the way with a double - double of 21 points and 10 rebounds, while Wayne Selden had 11 points, 12 boards and four assists. Robin Lopez delivered 15 points with nine rebounds, and Cristiano Feliciano filled the stat sheet with 15 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Ryan Arcidiacono chipped in with 12 points.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 124 - 101, at United Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with a few lead changes early on, before the Bulls emerged with a 28 - 26 lead after one quarter. However, the Raptors took over from there, outscoring the Bulls by 13, in the second quarter to take an 11 - point lead into halftime. The Raptors carried the momentum through the third and pushed their lead to 93 - 75, entering the fourth. They cruised through the fourth to earn their third straight win. This marks the fourth straight loss for the Bulls. Serge Ibaka led the Raptors with 23 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and a block, in 28 minutes. Fred VanVleet finished with 23 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, while Marc Gasol tallied 17 points, nine rebounds, five assists and one block. The Raptors shot 52 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 38 from long range. Walt Lemon Jr. led the Bulls with 19 points, six assists, four rebounds, four steals and a block, in 31 minutes off the bench. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 116 - 96, at United Center on Saturday night. The New York Knicks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 96 - 86, at United Center on Tuesday. In a battle between two of the worst teams in the league, New York won in dominating fashion. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 133 - 111, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday evening. This marked the first home game of the season for the Cavaliers, who started off with two tough road losses. Jordan Clarkson was the high - point man for Cleveland, with 19 points, on 7 - of - 12 shooting, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Cavs shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 27 from long range. The Cavs (0 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Wednesday. The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 119 - 107, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday. The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 110 - 91, at Quicken Loans Arena on Thursday. Despite the fact that the Cavaliers led by 12 points after the first quarter, the Nuggets dominated from there. The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 95 - 86, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday night. The Thunder (6 - 4) had to deal with the absence of Russell Westbrook after he got injured on Monday against the New Orleans Pelicans, and they managed to dominate most of the contest against a Cavaliers (1 - 10) team that already reached double - digit losses through their first 11 games of the campaign. Smith had 13 points, and Rodney Hood chipped in with 11 points, five boards and four assists. Jordan Clarkson had 11 points, nine rebounds and eight assists off the bench.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 113 - 89, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 109 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 117 - 108, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday. The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 102 - 95, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday evening. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 106 - 95, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Raptors head back home for a Monday night showdown with the Denver Nuggets, while the Cavaliers hit the road and face the Brooklyn Nets on Monday evening as well.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 110, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday evening. Jordan Clarkson was the high - point man, with 26 points on 11 - of - 19 shooting, in 29 minutes off the bench. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Washington Wizards, 116 - 101, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the New York Knicks, 113 - 106, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday evening. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 128 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday evening. The Miami Heat defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 117 - 92, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. The Utah Jazz defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 117 - 91, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday night. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 133 - 98, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Pelicans (18 - 22) haven't exactly had much success on the road this season, so it wasn't completely surprising to see the Cavaliers (8 - 31) mostly hang with them in the first half. However, New Orleans then separated in the third quarter, extending a 61 - 52 halftime lead by 17 points to essentially seal the win. As the final score implied, the visitors enjoyed big advantages in multiple categories. Two of the most prominent were shooting and rebounding - - the Pelicans drained 58 percent while limiting Cleveland to a 41 percent success rate, and they won the battle of the boards, 44 - 34. Julius Randle and Jrue Holiday led the Pelicans with matching 22 - point tallies. Randle notably added 12 rebounds, eight assists and one steal. Anthony Davis provided 20 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, four steals and two blocks. Darius Miller led the bench with 14 points, while Elfrid Payton tallied 13. Jahlil Okafor and E'Twaun Moore generated 10 points apiece. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 23 points and added four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Collin Sexton and Jalen Jones pitched in 15 points apiece. Cedi Osman supplied 13 points, five assists, one rebound and three steals. Tristan Thompson managed a 10 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two steals and one block. The Pelicans head back home to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night, while the Cavaliers remain home to tangle with the Indiana Pacers on Tuesday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 123 - 115, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Pacers (27 - 13) were an absolutely dominant team during the first half of this game against the Cavaliers (8 - 33), as they quickly took control of the game and didn't look back. Indiana won the first quarter by a 38 - 16 differential, and that 22 - point lead practically ended the game after the first 12 minutes. The Pacers would end up losing the remaining three quarters (25 - 27, 29 - 36 and 31 - 36, respectively) but it wasn't enough since Cleveland were never able to come back from such a huge deficit following the first 12 minutes of action. Thaddeus Young led the offense for the Pacers with 26 points, but he filled the stat sheet since he also added five rebounds, three assists and two steals. Bojan Bogdanovic contributed 23 points, and Domantas Sabonis chipped in with 15 points, nine boards, four assists and two steals in a rare start. Victor Oladipo had 17 points, and Cory Joseph delivered 11 points and six assists off the bench. Alec Burks led the way for the Cavaliers with 19 points while going 7 - 9 shooting from the field, but he also added seven rebounds to the mix. Cedi Osman and Tristan Thompson both had 15 points, but the Canadian big man did an excellent job on both ends of the court since he also added 13 rebounds, five assists and two blocks. Collin Sexton added 14 points.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 104 - 88, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday afternoon. Ante Zizic looked productive, as the big man chipped in with 13 points and nine rebounds in 28 minutes. Jordan Clarkson had 12 points, five rebounds and four assists off the bench. Cameron Payne had 11 points as well.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Washington Wizards, 116 - 113, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 107 - 104, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday. In a battle between the two worst teams in the NBA, it came down to the final shot. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers in triple overtime, 148 - 139, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday evening. The Nets (30 - 29) and Cavaliers (12 - 46) had both been involved in their fair share of shootouts this season, but what unfolded Wednesday ended up being on another level altogether. Most of regulation hinted at what was to come in the latter stages, as the game was a back - and - forth affair for the majority of the first four quarters. Cleveland had pulled ahead by as much as five points with under four minutes to go in the final period before Brooklyn fought back and ultimately sent the game into the first overtime on a D'Angelo Russell driving layup with 1:1 remaining. Collin Sexton returned the favor for the hosts at the end of the first extra period with 3 seconds left to force a sixth quarter. At the end of the second overtime, it was DeMarre Carroll making up for missing a floater at the end of regulation by hitting a 26 - foot step back jumper at the buzzer to knot the score back up at 128. The visitors finally got the best of the exhausted Cavs in the third overtime, outscoring them by a 20 - 11 margin and finishing on a 7 - 2 run over the final 1:5 to secure the win. Russell overcame a forgettable start to lead the way for the Nets with 36 points. He added eight assists and seven rebounds. Joe Harris netted 25 points and also contributed four rebounds and two assists. Carroll offered 18 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one block. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson delivered 17 points, five rebounds and one steal. Allen Crabbe supplied 14 points and seven boards, while Caris LeVert turned in 12 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and one block. Jarrett Allen and Shabazz Napier had matching 10 - point tallies while also compiling 12 rebounds and seven assists, respectively. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 42 points and complemented them with eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Sexton managed 24 points, six boards and five assists. Marquese Chriss registered 23 points, seven boards, one assist and two steals. Cedi Osman returned from injury to offer 13 points, five rebounds and three assists. Larry Nance, Jr. mustered eight points and 14 rebounds. The Nets are now off until Feb. 21, when they'll host the Portland Trail Blazers. The Cavaliers return to action that same evening and host the Phoenix Suns.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 112 - 107, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 123 - 110, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday evening. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 93, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday afternoon. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 112 - 90, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday afternoon.
