The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 124 - 97, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Hornets (39 - 42) had their backs against the wall in this game against the Cavaliers (19 - 63), who were simply looking to end the year as soon as possible, and Charlotte got the job done as they needed a win - - as well as other results - - to keep their playoff chances alive on Wednesday. The Hornets didn't waste any time and jumped to a 33 - 31 lead in the first half and they would blow the game open the rest of the way. Charlotte won every single quarter in this contest (with the others being 31 - 25, 26 - 19 and 34 - 22) to secure a huge 27 - point win. They never stepped the foot out of the gas, but that was expected given their situation on the standings. Kemba Walker led the way for the Hornets since he finished with 23 points and seven assists in only 27 minutes of action. Miles Bridges filled the stat sheet with 18 points, seven rebounds and four assists, while Dwayne Bacon chipped in with 18 points, Jeremy Lamb had an impressive effort off the bench with 23 points and five assists, while Frank Kaminsky (14 points) and Devonte Graham (10 points) also scored in double digits. Colllin Sexton led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points and 10 assists, while Cedi Osman contributed 17 points and four rebounds. Larry Nance Jr. filled the stat sheet admirably since he ended with 10 points, 12 boards, six assists and two blocks. Jordan Clarkson chipped in with 16 points in 23 minutes off the bench, while Channing Frye ended with 10 points.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 105 - 87, at TD Garden on Tuesday. The fact that Boston held the lead for over 40 minutes of this game shows just how dominant they were, as they maintained the lead for the final three quarters. In fact, the Celtics led by at least nine points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Defense was critical for Boston, as they held Philly to just 39 percent from the field and 19 percent from three - point range while forcing 16 turnovers. Free-throw shooting was also a killer for the Sixers, as they connected on just 14 - of - 24 from the charity stripe. Three-point shooting was also a decisive stat, with Boston hitting 11 - of - 37 and Philadelphia connecting on just 5 - of - 26. Bench production was huge as well, with the Celtics winning that battle, 44 - 26. The Sixers (0 - 1) got a near triple - double out of Ben Simmons, as he collected 19 points, 15 rebounds, eight assists, four steals and two blocks. Joel Embiid was the only other starter in double figures, as he accrued 23 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two blocks. J.J. Redick led the bench with 16 points and two boards. The Celtics (10) were led by Jayson Tatum, as he tallied 23 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Jaylen Brown amassed 12 points, five rebounds and two assists. Kyrie Irving struggled mightily, as he went just 2 - of - 14 from the field to accrue seven points, four rebounds and seven assists. Marcus Morris was huge off the bench, providing 16 points, 10 boards and two steals. On deck for Philly is a home matchup versus the Chicago Bulls on Thursday. As for the Celtics, they travel north of the border to play the Toronto Raptors on Friday for their next fixture.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Boston Celtics, 93 - 90, at TD Garden on Monday. After losing 14 of their previous 15 games in Boston, Orlando picked up their biggest win of the season on Monday. In fact, this was a wire - to - wire win for the Magic, as a 28 - 19 first quarter was too much for the Celtics to overcome. Defense was critical for Orlando, as they held Boston to just 40 percent from the field and 23 percent from three - point range while winning the turnover differential, 12 - 9. Ball movement was also huge for the Magic, out - assisting Boston, 28 - 21. The Magic (2 - 2) got another spectacular performance out of Nikola Vucevic, as he tallied 24 points, 12 rebounds and three steals on 11 - of - 18 from the field. Jonathan Issac finished with 18 points and 12 boards. Evan Fournier provided 14 points, six rebounds and 10 assists while D.J. Augustin amassed 10 points, three rebounds and 10 assists. The Celtics (2 - 2) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he accrued 22 points, eight rebounds, five assists and two steals. Al Horford collected 15 points, six rebounds and four assists. Gordon Hayward generated 11 points, four rebounds and three assists. Jayson Tatum totaled seven points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Both teams return to action on Thursday, with Orlando playing host to the Portland Trail Blazers and Boston traveling to face the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 108 - 105, at TD Garden on Tuesday. There were seven ties and nine lead changes in this competitive game, as it wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, Jayson Tatum executed an intentionally missed free - throw with 0 seconds left to seal the win after Detroit hit a three - pointer on their previous possession. The third quarter really made the difference for Boston, as they outscored Detroit, 25 - 13. The Celtics defense was on point once again, as they held the Pistons to 42 percent from the field and 27 percent from three - point range while forcing 17 turnovers. Ball movement was also critical, with Boston out - assisting Detroit, 25 - 17. The Pistons (4 - 2) got a monster double - double out of Blake Griffin, as he led the way with 24 points, 15 rebounds and three assists. Andre Drummond amassed 17 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Reggie Bullock totaled 16 points and three boards. Ish Smith led the bench with 13 points, four rebounds and two assists. The Celtics (5 - 2) got a season - high 31 points out of Kyrie Irving, as he did that damage on 10 - of - 16 from the field. He also added five rebounds and five assists to his impressive line. Jayson Tatum finished with 16 points, six rebounds and three assists. Jaylen Brown accumulated 14 points, five rebounds and three assists. Marcus Morris led the bench with 15 points and nine boards. On deck for Detroit is a road matchup versus the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. As for Boston, they return to action on Thursday in a home matchup versus the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Chicago Bulls, 111 - 82, at TD Garden on Wednesday night. The Celtics (8 - 6) got off to a slow start against the Bulls (4 - 11) and they lost the first quarter 24 - 19, perhaps showing that their loss to the Portland Trail Blazers wasn't entirely on the rear view. However, they looked dominant in the second quarter and won 32 - 11, establishing a huge advantage that they would never relinquish. Boston then won the remaining two quarters (26 - 24 and 34 - 23, respectively), and sealed the deal comfortably. Despite the slow start, it was a huge win for the Celtics as it will certainly allow them to gain momentum going forward. The Celtics showcased their balanced offense once again, as all of their starters scored in double digits but no player reached the 20 - point mark. Jaylen Brown was the team's top scorer with 18 points and six rebounds, while Kyrie Irving filled the stat sheet thanks to 17 points, seven assists, six rebounds and two steals. Jayson Tatum had 14 points and six boards, Gordon Hayward chipped in with 11 points, four assists and four rebounds, and Al Horford delivered 10 points with eight boards. Shaquille Harrison led the way for the Bulls with 16 points coming off the bench. Jabari Parker had 14 points with five rebounds, and talented rookie Wendell Carter Jr. contributed 11 points and seven rebounds. Zach LaVine filled the stat sheet, as he finished with 10 points, nine rebounds and four assists.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 123 - 116, at TD Garden on Friday. There were 11 ties and nine lead changes in this competitive matchup, as it took an overtime session to determine a winner. Boston dominated that extra session, outscoring Toronto, 16 - 9. In fact, the Celtics never trailed in overtime, despite the fact that the Raptors held the lead for the majority of the second half. Boston ended up shooting 53 percent from the field and 35 percent from three - point range while holding Toronto to 43 percent from the field and 28 percent from long range. The Raptors (12 - 4) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 31 points, 15 rebounds, four assists and three steals. Serge Ibaka amassed 21 points and four rebounds. Pascal Siakam collected 16 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. Kyle Lowry finished with 14 points, two rebounds, seven assists and two steals. The Celtics (9 - 6) got a spectacular performance out of Kyrie Irving, as he accumulated 43 points, two rebounds, 11 assists and three steals. Jayson Tatum totaled 21 points, seven rebounds and two steals. Gordon Hayward had one of his best games of the season, finishing with 15 points, five rebounds, five assists and four steals. Both teams will have to play the second half of a back - to - back set on Saturday, with Toronto traveling to face the Chicago Bulls and Boston playing host to the Utah Jazz.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Boston Celtics, 98 - 86, at TD Garden on Saturday night. The Jazz (8 - 8) had battled inconsistency since the start of the season, but they managed one of their more complete performance in a difficult road environment. Utah got a combined 48 points from their starting backcourt duo of Ricky Rubio and Donovan Mitchell and held the Celtics (9 - 7) to 38 percent shooting, including an unsightly 15 percent from three - point range. The third quarter was the launching pad to the win, as Utah held Boston to just 17 points. Mitchell spearheaded the Jazz with a game - high 28 points, a total he supplemented with six assists, three rebounds, three steals and one block. Rubio tallied 20 points, four rebounds, two assists and three steals. Rudy Gobert totaled 12 points, nine boards, three assists, two steals and one block. Derrick Favors generated matching 10 - point efforts from the starting five and bench. They pulled down eight and seven rebounds, respectively. Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 20 points and added eight rebounds, one assist and two steals. Jayson Tatum was the only other double - digit scorer for Boston with 10 points, and he added seven rebounds. Al Horford filled out the stat sheet with nine points, six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. Guerschon Yabusele led the bench with nine points of his own. The Jazz next visit the Indiana Pacers on Monday evening, while the Celtics hit the road as well and face the Charlotte Hornets on Monday night.

The New York Knicks defeated the host Boston Celtics, 117 - 109, at TD Garden on Wednesday evening. The Celtics got out to a slow start at home, as they only tallied 18 points in the first quarter, while they allowed the Knicks 26 points. The Knicks kept up the momentum in the second, and pushed their lead to 26 late in the quarter, before settling on a 65 - 49 lead at halftime. The Celtics came out battling in the third, but the Knicks would not budge, as they carried a 15 - point lead into the final frame. The Celtics kept fighting and almost completed the comeback, as they made it a four - point game with one minute remaining. However, the Knicks executed down the stretch in order to secure the impressive road win and end a six - game losing streak. Trey Burke led the Knicks with 29 points, 11 assists, six rebounds and two steals, in 31 minutes. Tim Hardaway Jr. followed up with 21 points, four rebounds, four assists, while Noah Vonleh tallied 16 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. The Knicks shot 49 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 30 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 22 points, 13 assists, six rebounds, three steals and one block, in 36 minutes. Al Horford followed up with 19 points, seven rebounds, five assists, three blocks and one steal, while Marcus Morris finished with 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Celtics shot 39 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 33 from deep. The Celtics (9 - 9) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hawks in Atlanta on Friday. The Knicks (5 - 14) play host to the Pelicans on Friday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 128 - 95, at TD Garden on Friday evening. The Celtics (12 - 10) came into the contest the recipients of plenty of heat due to what was considered a disappointing record based on the lofty expectations they came into the season with. The first half was more tightly contested than was likely expected, as Boston only held a relatively modest 10 - point halftime lead over the Cavaliers (4 - 17). However, they exerted their superiority in the third quarter, racking up 39 points while limiting Cleveland to 20. That essentially sealed the win, as the Celtics were essentially able to take their foot off the proverbial gas over the final 12 minutes. The home team's play stood out on both ends of the floor, as they kept the Cavs to 42 percent shooting while draining 55 percent of their attempts, including 52 percent of their 29 tries from three - point range. Jordan Clarkson led the Cavaliers off the bench with 16 points, adding one rebound. Rookie Collin Sexton followed with 15 points and also provided four boards and four assists. Alec Burks was solid in his Cleveland debut with 14 points. Tristan Thompson posted a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double, while Rodney Hood poured in 10 points. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 29 points and also supplied four rebounds and four assists. Marcus Morris registered 15 points, four rebounds and one assist. Gordon Hayward delivered a bench - leading 14 points, along with four rebounds and four assists. Jayson Tatum turned in 13 points and four rebounds, while Marcus Smart drew another start for Jaylen Brown (back) and filled out the stat sheet with 12 points, seven assists, three rebounds, three steals and one block. The Cavaliers head back home to face the Raptors on Saturday night, while the Celtics pay a visit to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday night as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the New York Knicks, 128 - 100, at TD Garden on Thursday. The hot play of the Celtics (14 - 10) continued Thursday night, as the dominating win in New York gave the team their fourth straight victory. It was a wire - to - wire victory for Boston after they opened up an eight - point lead in the first quarter and never looking back before piling it on in the final stretch. It was a complete team effort too, with seven different players scoring in double figures. Kyrie Irving led the way with a team - high 22 points to go along with four rebounds and eight assists across 30 minutes, while Al Horford posted a double - double of 19 points and 12 rebounds. Jaylen Brown provided crucial minutes off the bench as he works his way back from injury, scoring 21 points on 7 - of - 10 shooting in just 25 minutes as a reserve. In the end, it was a very efficient offensive showcase from the Celtics, as they shot 53 percent from the field and dished out 32 assists to just nine turnovers. As for the Knicks (8 - 18), they dropped their second straight game and have lost four of their last five. It was a miserable night on both ends for the home team, but their performance on offense was especially porous. New York shot just 40 percent from the field, making it impossible to keep up with the Celtics, who seemed to be getting whatever shots they wanted Thursday. Tim Hardaway Jr. led the way once again for the Knicks with 22 points while shooting 6 - of - 13 from behind the arc. Emanuel Mudiay shot just 5 - of - 15 from the field, but still managed to finish with 17 points, while Enes Kanter posted yet another double - double of 14 points and 11 rebounds.

The Boston Celtics defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 113 - 100, at TD Garden on Monday night. The Celtics (16 - 10) came into the game fielding something akin to a preseason roster, considering Kyrie Irving (shoulder), Al Horford (knee) and Gordon Hayward (illness) were all out of action. They let their deep roster do what it's intended to do, however, jumping out a 28 - 21 first - quarter lead and remaining consistent throughout all four quarters. Boston held off any designs of a Pelicans (14 - 15) comeback in the final 12 minutes by outscoring their visitors, 30 - 28. New Orleans suffered a key injury during the game, as Nikola Mirotic exited the contest with an ankle injury after logging just seven minutes. Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 41 points, a total he supplemented with seven rebounds, two assists and four steals. Julius Randle provided 20 points as the only other double - digit scorer on New Orleans. Tim Frazier mustered eight points and dished out 10 assists. Jrue Holiday could only compile seven points on 3 - for - 10 shooting. He added six assists, one rebound and three steals. Marcus Morris paced the Celtics with 31 points, adding four rebounds and four assists. Jayson Tatum registered 21 points, six boards, one assist and one block. Jaylen Brown poured in 19 points and also supplied seven rebounds, three assists and one block. Semi Ojeyele totaled 11 points and six rebounds. Terry Rozier filled in for Irving and collected 10 points, seven rebounds, six assists and two steals. The Pelicans head back home to take on the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday night, while the Celtics hit the road and take on the Washington Wizards on Wednesday evening as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 129 - 108, at TD Garden on Friday. This marks Boston's eighth - straight win, as they won this game in dominating fashion. A 42 - 19 first quarter really set the tone, as the Celtics never trailed from there. In addition, Boston led by at least 10 points for the entirety of the second half and by at least 20 for the whole of the fourth quarter. The Celtics ended up shooting 48 percent from the field, 49 percent from three - point range and 90 percent from the free - throw line while holding the Hawks to 42 percent from the field, 42 percent from long range and 63 percent from the charity stripe. Boston did a ton of damage down low too, outscoring Atlanta in the paint, 48 - 32. The Hawks (6 - 22) were led by Kevin Huerter, as he tallied 19 points, two rebounds, three assists and three steals. Kent Bazemore amassed 13 points, three rebounds, seven assists and two steals. John Collins totaled 11 points and 14 boards. Alex Len and Vince Carter both reached double figures in scoring off the bench. The Celtics (18 - 10) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he collected 24 points, five rebounds, five assists and four steals. Jayson Tatum accrued 22 points, three rebounds and two steals. Marcus Morris generated 20 points and six boards. Gordon Hayward led the bench with 19 points and five assists. On deck for Boston is a road matchup versus the Detroit Pistons on Saturday. As for Atlanta, they're off until Sunday when they travel to face the Brooklyn Nets.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the Boston Celtics, 111 - 103, at TD Garden on Wednesday evening. The Suns (8 - 24) came into the contest with an unsightly road record that had seen them notch just two wins in 15 tries. That futility, combined with the 37 - 26 first - quarter lead forged by the Celtics (18 - 12), didn't seem to bode well for Phoenix's chances. However, they began to claw back in the second period, which left their halftime deficit a very manageable 62 - 59. The third quarter was the turning point, with Phoenix outscoring its hosts by a 27 - 18 margin and taking an 86 - 80 advantage that they wouldn't relinquish into the final 12 minutes. The visitors surprisingly won the rebounding battle by a 56 - 37 margin, with the fact Aron Baynes exited the game with what turned out to be a broken hand certainly playing a part. Celtics tormentor Devin Booker paced the Suns with 25 points and added eight assists, five rebounds, two blocks and one steal. Deandre Ayton was a big reason for Phoenix's success down low, posting a 23 - point, 18 - rebound double - double. T.J. Warren offered 21 points, five rebounds, one assist and two steals. Kelly Oubre, Jr. enjoyed a successful team debut with 13 points, six rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal. Josh Jackson went for 11 points, five boards, two assists, one steal and one block. Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 29 points and also tallied 10 assists, five rebounds, four steals and one block. Jayson Tatum followed with 18 points, eight boards, four blocks and one steal. Marcus Smart and Terry Rozier turned in matching 12 - point tallies, with Smart notably adding five assists, four rebounds and four steals. Gordon Hayward delivered 10 points, five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal. The Suns remain on the road and visit the Washington Wizards on Saturday night, while the Celtics remain home and take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Boston Celtics, 120 - 107, at TD Garden on Friday. It's rare to see a team go into TD Garden and dominate the Celtics but that was the case here for the Bucks. In fact, a 35 - 22 first quarter really set the tone, as they held a double - digit lead for the final 30 minutes of action. What makes that even more bizarre is the fact that Boston started the game with a 10 - 1 lead, as the Bucks scored the next 16 points after that and never relinquished the lead. Milwaukee ended up shooting 51 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range while holding Boston to 39 percent from the field and 29 percent from long range. Defensive rebounding was also critical, with the Bucks winning that battle, 44 - 27. The Bucks (22 - 9) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he tallied 30 points, eight rebounds, five assists and three blocks. Khris Middleton accrued 21 points, nine rebounds and five assists. Eric Bledsoe accumulated 16 points, four rebounds and two assists. Malcolm Brogdon finished with 10 points, nine rebounds and four assists. The Celtics (18 - 13) were led by Jaylen Brown, as he provided 21 points, seven rebounds, two assists and four steals off the bench. Jayson Tatum led the starters with 20 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals. Kyrie Irving collected 15 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. No other player had more than five rebounds or four assists. On deck for Boston is a home matchup versus the Charlotte Hornets on Sunday. As for Milwaukee, they play again on Saturday, as they travel to South Beach to play the Miami Heat.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers in overtime, 121 - 114, at TD Garden on Tuesday. In a Christmas Day showdown between the Eastern Conference elite, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. In fact, there were nine ties and nine lead changes in total, as neither club led by more than 11 points. Boston ended the overtime strong, scoring the final nine points of the game across the last two minutes. Turnovers really decided this game, as Boston forced Philly to commit 19 turnovers while the Celtics committed just nine on their end. That allowed them to win the points off turnover differential, 22 - 5. The Celtics also did a ton of damage down low, outscoring the Sixers in the paint, 50 - 30. The Sixers (22 - 13) were led by Joel Embiid, as he tallied 34 points, 16 rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Jimmy Butler finished with 24 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals. Ben Simmons fell just shy of a triple - double, collecting 11 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. J.J. Redick totaled 17 points and three boards while Wilson Chandler amassed 15 points, five rebounds and three assists. The Celtics (20 - 13) got a gem from Kyrie Irving, as he accumulated 40 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Marcus Morris generated 23 points, six rebounds and three assists. Jayson Tatum accrued 23 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Al Horford scored just four points but provided nine rebounds and five assists. Both teams return to action on Thursday, with Boston traveling to play the Houston Rockets and Philly facing the Utah Jazz on the road as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 115 - 102, at TD Garden on Wednesday. The final scoreline makes this game look closer than it actually was, as Boston won in wire - to - wire fashion. In fact, a 35 - 21 second quarter really set the tone, with the Celtics leading by at least five points for the final 30 minutes. Their offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 59 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range while recording 34 assists. Rim protection was also critical, with the Celtics out - blocking the T'Wolves, 8 - 2. Transition offense was also big for Boston, as they outscored Minnesota in fastbreak points, 23 - 10. Bench production can't be overlooked either, with the Celtics outscoring the Timberwolves bench, 62 - 18. The Timberwolves (17 - 21) got another spectacular performance from Karl-Anthony Towns, as he collected 28 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists. Andrew Wiggins was just as good, as he scored a season - high 31 points to go along with two rebounds and three assists. Tyus Jones got another start and tallied 14 points, nine assists and four steals. No other player reached 10 points, five rebounds or three assists. The Celtics (22 - 15) played without Kyrie Irving (eye), as Gordon Hayward had his best game of the season. In fact, Hayward went 14 - of - 18 from the field to lead the bench with 35 points and five assists. Terry Rozier got a rare start and totaled 16 points, three rebounds, five assists and five steals. Al Horford accrued 15 points, five rebounds, four assists and two blocks. On deck for Minnesota is a home matchup versus the Orlando Magic on Friday. Boston also returns to action on Friday, as they welcome the Dallas Mavericks to Beantown.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 114 - 93, at TD Garden on Friday. While Boston came into this matchup extremely shorthanded, they won this game in dominating fashion. In fact, a 34 - 23 first quarter really set the tone, as the Celtics won in wire - to - wire fashion. Their defense was critical, as they held the Mavericks to 39 percent from the field and 25 percent from three - point range. Ball movement definitely played a factor in that, with Boston out - assisting Dallas, 35 - 16. The Celtics three - point shooting was also big, as they connected on 21 - of - 45 from long range. Boston's bench was also decisive, as they outscored Dallas' bench, 40 - 22. The Mavericks (18 - 20) were led by Harrison Barnes, as he totaled 20 points and three boards. Luke Doncic collected 19 points, nine rebounds and four assists. DeAndre Jordan finished with 12 points, 15 rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Wesley Matthews accrued 11 points, three rebounds and two assists. The Celtics (23 - 15) were led by Jaylen Brown, as he tallied 21 points, two rebounds, two assists and three steals. Jayson Tatum amassed 18 points and six rebounds. Al Horford flirted with a triple - double, accumulating 10 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. Gordon Hayward was huge off the bench, as he provided 16 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists. On deck for Dallas is a road matchup versus the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday. As for Boston, they return to action on Monday, when they play host to the Brooklyn Nets.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 116 - 95, at TD Garden on Monday night. The Celtics (24 - 15) came into the contest the much more well - rested team, considering they'd last played Friday. In contrast, the Nets (20 - 22) were playing their third game in four nights, and the disparity seemed evident right from the opening tip. Boston established a 34 - 22 first - quarter lead and continued piling on from that point forward. The home squad outscored Brooklyn by a 60 - 50 margin in the second half and shot an impressive 50 percent overall while eliciting 23 turnovers. Rodions Kurucs led the way for the Nets with 24 points, adding a rebound and an assist. Spencer Dinwiddie followed with 15 points and also posted two rebounds and one assist. Kenneth Faried generated a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, one steal and one block. Eric Davis delivered 11 points, nine rebounds and two steals. Shabazz Napier supplied 10 points, six assists, five rebounds, two blocks and one steal. Treveon Graham tallied nine points. The Celtics had eight double - digit scorers overall, led by Kyrie Irving, who turned in 17 points, six assists, two rebounds and three steals. Jayson Tatum finished with 16 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Marcus Morris, Al Horford, Marcus Smart and Gordon Hayward all pitched in 12 points each. Horford notably also brought down nine rebounds, while Smart dished out seven assists. Daniel Theis totaled 11 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Terry Rozier poured in 10 points and also had four rebounds and four assists. The Nets head back home to take on the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday night, while the Celtics remain home and take on the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday evening as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Indiana Pacers, 135 - 108, at TD Garden on Wednesday night. The Celtics (25 - 15) played one of their best games of the season at home against the Pacers (27 - 14), as they were the better side from tip - off until the final whistle. This was absolutely reflected on the score since the Celtics won every single quarter and managed to look dominant even on garbage time. Boston quickly jumped to a 29 - 23 lead after the first 12 minutes of action, and they never looked back after that. The remaining three quarters ended 39 - 30, 37 - 27 and 30 - 28 for Boston, showing they were absolutely no match for Indiana. At least for these 48 minutes. The Celtics had seven players scoring in double digits in this game and there's no doubt Jaylen Brown caught the eye of everyone with his impressive 22 - point performance coming off the bench. Marcus Morris also delivered 22 points, while Jayson Tatum chipped in with 20 points and Kyrie Irving had 12 points. Gordon Hayward had 14 points and both Terry Rozier and Daniel Theis had 12 - all three coming off the bench. Domantas Sabonis once again got the start and looked surprisingly productive since he finished with 20 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Victor Oladipo chipped in with 17 points, while Thaddeus Young had 10 points and eight rebounds. Kyle O'Quinn looked productive coming off the bench since he finished with 11 points, five rebounds and three assists. Tyreke Evans added 15 points.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Toronto Raptors, 117 - 108, at TD Bank Arena on Wednesday evening. The Celtics (26 - 18) came into the contest looking to put an end to the perpetual underachieving they've been guilty of this season. A victory over a quality division rival like the Raptors (33 - 13) certainly would be a step in the right direction, yet things didn't exactly start off on the right foot in the first quarter. Toronto outscored Boston by a 36 - 30 margin over the first 12 minutes, but the home squad roared back to forge a 64 - 53 lead by halftime. True to form, however, the Raptors clawed back in the third, and they led by a 104 - 100 margin as late as the 4:22 mark of the final period. The Celtics then finished on a 17 - 4 run over the final 3:54 to eradicate that deficit and nearly notch a double - digit win. Kawhi Leonard paced the Raptors with 33 points, adding four rebounds, two assists and four steals. Serge Ibaka turned in 22 points and 10 rebounds. Danny Green managed 15 points, six rebounds and one assist. Greg Monroe and Norman Powell generated matching 11 - point tallies, with Monroe also notably bringing in nine rebounds. Kyle Lowry mustered 10 points, seven assists, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 27 points, supplementing them with a career - high 18 assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Al Horford managed 24 points, seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Gordon Hayward delivered 18 points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Jayson Tatum generated a 16 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one block. The Raptors head back home to take the Phoenix Suns on Thursday night, while the Celtics remain home and tangle with the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday evening.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 122 - 116, at TD Garden on Friday evening. The Celtics (27 - 18) haven't been exactly been the most consistent team in the NBA this season, but at least they've been mostly reliable on their home court. Boston owned a 16 - 5 record at TD Garden coming into Friday, and accordingly, they got off to a fast start against the Grizzlies (19 - 26) by forging a 35 - 24 first - quarter lead. However, Memphis flipped the script in the second to the extent they entered halftime with a 62 - 58 advantage. The home squad then responded by eliminating their deficit in the third and carrying a five - point edge into the final period. The visitors would get as close as 106 - 104 with 4:53 remaining, but the Celtics never relinquished the lead and hung on. Mike Conley led the way for the Grizzlies with 26 points, adding four assists. Jaren Jackson, Jr. totaled 23 points, four rebounds, one assist and one block. Shelvin Mack tallied 15 points, seven assists, three rebounds and one steal. Justin Holiday supplied 14 points, six rebounds, two assists and four steals. JaMychal Green and Omri Casspi managed matching 12 - point tallies while providing two and four rebounds, respectively. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 38 points, adding 11 assists, seven rebounds and one block. Marcus Smart went for 20 points, six boards, three assists, three steals and one block. The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 107 - 99, at TD Garden on Monday evening. The Celtics got out to a great start at home, with a 33 - 23 lead after one quarter. The Heat did not give up and put together a strong fourth quarter, where they outscored the Celtics by 11 points. However, it was not enough, as the Celtics held on for their fourth straight win. The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Boston Celtics, 115 - 111, at TD Garden on Saturday. In what many expect to be a Finals preview, this game was full of swings. Jayson Tatum totaled 20 points, five rebounds and three assists. Marcus Smart generated 12 points, three rebounds and two assists. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Golden State traveling to face the Indiana Pacers and Boston playing host to the surging Brooklyn Nets.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Brooklyn Nets, 112 - 104, at TD Garden on Monday evening. Despite missing Kyrie Irving (hip), the Celtics got out to a good start at home, with a 32 - 26 lead after one quarter. The Nets managed to tie it up mid way through the second, but the Celtics kept the edge and rallied back ahead, to take a 10 - point lead into halftime. Marcus Smart led the Celtics with 21 points, seven assists, five steals, two rebounds and two blocks, in 32 minutes. Meanwhile, D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 25 points on 10 - of - 20 shooting, four assists, three steals and two rebounds, in 23 minutes. Shabazz Napier followed up with 20 points, five assists, two steals and two rebounds, in 26 minutes off the bench, while Rondae Hollis-Jefferson added 14 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks. The Nets shot 38 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. The Nets (27 - 24) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Bulls on Tuesday. The Celtics (31 - 19) play host to the Hornets on Wednesday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 126 - 94, at TD Garden on Wednesday. Boston came into this game as a big favorite and this 36 - point victory shows just why. A 35 - 28 first quarter really set the tone, as a 63 - 35 second half put the game to bed. Every statistic was extremely lopsided, with the Celtics winning the rebounding battle, 53 - 31. Boston also shot 56 percent from the field and 87 percent from the free - throw line while holding Charlotte to 44 percent from the field and 43 percent from the charity stripe. Jayson Tatum led the starters with 20 points and five boards. Al Horford collected 14 points, seven rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks. Terry Rozier collected 17 points, five rebounds and 10 assists in his start for Kyrie Irving (hip). Both teams return to action on Friday, with Charlotte playing host to the Memphis Grizzlies and Boston traveling to face the struggling New York Knicks.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 134 - 129, at TD Garden on Sunday afternoon. The Celtics (34 - 19) came into the contest with a stellar record, but that didn't spare them from having something to prove on their home floor against one of the opposite conference's elite. Boston got off to a good start in that regard, turning a 31 - 29 first - quarter lead into a 66 - 58 halftime advantage over the Thunder (33 - 19). OKC naturally hung tough, however, and the game ultimately came down to a possession in the closing seconds. The visitors were down by just one point when Russell Westbrook attempted a drive to the basket and lost the ball to Al Horford with 8 seconds remaining. Jayson Tatum's two subsequent free throws essentially sealed the victory for the Celtics, although the win wasn't iron clad until Westbrook failed to hit the rim while trying to purposely miss a second free - throw attempt with 5 seconds left. Paul George led the Thunder with 37 points, adding four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Westbrook finished with yet another triple - double, furnishing 22 points, 16 assists, 12 rebounds and two steals. Steven Adams and Dennis Schroder had matching 16 - point tallies, while hauling in nine and six rebounds, respectively. Jerami Grant totaled 15 points, three boards, one steal and one block. Terrance Ferguson tallied 11 points. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 30 points while also dishing out 11 assists, posting four rebounds and recording one block. Marcus Morris supplied 19 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Marcus Smart contributed 18 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Horford collected 17 points, nine assists, two rebounds, two steals and a block. Daniel Theis compiled 14 points, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Jaylen Brown pitched in 12 points, while Tatum had a well - balanced line of 11 points, seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. The Thunder heads back home to face the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night, while the Celtics visit the Cleveland Cavaliers on Tuesday evening.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Boston Celtics, 129 - 128, at TD Garden on Thursday. While Boston led by 18 points in the second quarter, Los Angeles made this game competitive thanks to a 42 - 27 third quarter. The Celtics then led for the majority of the fourth quarter but the Lakers took a one - point lead with 19 seconds remaining. Kyrie Irving then responded by hitting a floater with 11 seconds left to re - take the lead but Rajon Rondo hit a game - winning jumper at the buzzer to capture the win. Free-throw shooting nearly killed the Lakers, as they hit 7 - of - 18 while the Celtics went a perfect 20 - of - 20. Los Angeles' other shooting was on point though, as they shot 52 percent from the field and 54 percent from three - point range. The Lakers (28 - 27) got a triple - double from LeBron James, as he collected 28 points, 12 rebounds, 12 assists and three steals. Kyle Kuzma amassed 25 points, five rebounds and two assists. Rondo finished with 17 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists. JaVale McGee totaled 17 points and eight boards. The Celtics (35 - 20) were led by Irving, as he tallied 24 points, seven rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Jayson Tatum accrued 22 points, 10 rebounds and five assists. Daniel Theis led the bench with 20 points, six rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Terry Rozier provided 19 points, four rebounds and six assists off the bench as well. On deck for Boston is a home matchup versus the Los Angeles Clippers on Saturday. As for Los Angeles, they travel to face the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday for their next fixture.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Boston Celtics, 123 - 112, at TD Garden on Saturday. When Boston led 43 - 20 after the first quarter, this game looked nearly over but Los Angeles had other ideas. The key point was the Kyrie Irving (knee) injury at the end of the second quarter, as the Clippers ended up outscoring the Celtics in the second half, 70 - 38. In addition, Los Angeles ended the game on a 17 - 7 run to gain separation. Ball movement was key for the Clippers, as they out - assisted the Celtics, 28 - 22. Patrick Beverley collected 12 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. Montrezl Harrell led the bench with 21 points, six rebounds and two assists. Landry Shamet dropped 17 points off the bench in his debut. The Celtics (35 - 21) were led by Gordon Hayward, as he provided 19 points, five rebounds and three assists off the bench. Irving finished with 14 points and two assists before departing due to a non - contact knee injury. Jayson Tatum led the starters with 16 points and eight boards. Terry Rozier also played well off the bench, accumulating 16 points, five rebounds and three assists. On deck for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the struggling Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday. As for Boston, they travel to face the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Detroit Pistons, 118 - 110, at TD Garden on Wednesday. The Celtics (37 - 21) didn't get off to a good start against the Pistons (26 - 30), as Detroit still carried the momentum of their four - game winning streak to jump ahead 29 - 28 after the first quarter. However, Boston picked themselves up from the ground in the second quarter and they finished the first half up by five points (57 - 52) following a 29 - 23 second quarter. The Celtics pulled away for good in the third quarter since they dominated the third quarter (34 - 20) and they entered the final 12 minutes of action up 91 - 72. Detroit tried to turn things around in the final quarter and they actually won the final 12 minutes rather comfortably, 38 - 27, but it wasn't enough and the Celtics closed things out for good. Even if they ended suffering a bit more than expected. Boston featured a very balanced attack since they had six players scoring in double figures, led by second - year phenom Jayson Tatum who finished with 19 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Gordon Hayward added 18 points but he also contributed eight assists and five rebounds. Marcus Smart had 16 points with five assists, and Al Horford came close to a triple - double thanks to a 17 - points, 14 - rebound, eight - assist stat line. Blake Griffin led the way for the Pistons since he finished with 32 points, eight rebounds and five assists, but it wasn't enough for the Motor City franchise. Andre Drummond had 21 points with 17 rebounds, but also added four steals. Reggie Jackson finished with 18 points, and Luke Kennard added 11. Wayne Ellington chipped in with 13 points in 33 minutes coming off the bench.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Boston Celtics, 97 - 92, at TD Garden on Wednesday evening. The Trail Blazers (38 - 23) have impressively been making short work of Eastern Conference opposition during their current road trip, but Wednesday seemingly promised a formidable challenge. Despite recent struggles, the Celtics (37 - 25) still figured to be a force to be reckoned with, yet it was Portland forging a 43 - 42 halftime lead. They then separated in the third by adding nine points to their advantage, giving them enough cushion to withstand a couple of late Boston surges in the fourth. While the home squad actually enjoyed a better shooting night by draining 46 percent of their attempts, the visitors won both the rebounding (48 - 41) and turnover (11 - 16) battles. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 33 points, adding seven rebounds, four assists and two steals. Maurice Harkless turned in 17 points, 10 boards and three steals. Jusuf Nurkic tallied 16 points, six boards, three assists, two blocks and one steal. C.J. McCollum delivered 14 points, five boards and three assists. Al-Farouq Aminu mustered just four points but brought down nine boards. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 31 points and also provided five boards, three assists and one block. Jayson Tatum posted 14 points, four rebounds and one steal. Marcus Smart and Al Horford contributed matching 13 - point, five - assist tallies and hauled in six and five rebounds, respectively. Marcus Morris had eight points on just 3 - for - 10 shooting. The Trail Blazers next pay a visit to the Toronto Raptors on Friday night, while the Celtics remain home to face the Washington Wizards on Friday evening.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 107 - 96, at TD Garden on Friday. Boston desperately needed a win here and a double - digit victory shows just how important it was. They did all their damage in the first and fourth quarters, outscoring Washington, 55 - 35. That allowed the Celtics to lead for 45 minutes of this 48 - minute game. The Celtics defense was critical, as they held the Wizards to 40 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range while recording 12 steals. The assist - to - turnover ratio was huge as well, with Boston recording six more assists than Washington while committing six fewer turnovers. The Wizards (25 - 37) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 29 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals. Jeff Green totaled 15 points and four boards. Tomas Satoransky accrued 15 points, five rebounds and five assists while Bobby Portis amassed seven points and 11 boards. Jabari Parker led the bench with 12 points, five rebounds and four assists. The Celtics (38 - 25) were led by Al Horford, as he finished with 18 points, six rebounds and three assists. Kyrie Irving tallied 13 points, six rebounds and 12 assists. Marcus Morris generated 17 points and nine boards while Jayson Tatum accumulated 10 points, eight rebounds, three assists and five steals. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Washington playing host to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Boston welcoming the Houston Rockets to TD Garden.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 115 - 104, at TD Garden on Sunday afternoon. The Rockets got out to a strong start on the road, with a 33 - 23 lead after one quarter. They kept up the momentum in the second, and outscored the Celtics by 12, to take a 22 - point lead into halftime. The Celtics picked up the pace in the third, but could not cut into the difference, as they only matched Houston for 35 points each in the quarter, so as to still trail by 22, entering the fourth. The Celtics rallied to start the fourth, and cut the deficit to 11, with seven minutes left in the contest. However, the Rockets would not let them within striking distance, as they held strong for their fifth straight win. James Harden led the Rockets with 42 points, seven rebounds, four assists, two steals, and one block, in 38 minutes. Eric Gordon followed up with 32 points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal, while, Chris Paul tallied 15 points, 12 assists, six rebounds, three steals and one block. The Rockets shot 48 percent from the field, including 21 - of - 51 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 24 points, nine rebounds and six assists, in 35 minutes. Al Horford followed up with 19 points, six rebounds and two assists, while Marcus Smart chipped in 18 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal. The Celtics shot 48 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 28 from deep. The Celtics (38 - 26) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors in Golden State on Tuesday. The Rockets (38 - 25) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Tuesday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 126 - 120, at TD Garden on Thursday evening. The Kings got out to a great start on the road, with a 38 - 25 lead after one quarter. The Celtics picked it up in the second, as they chipped away through the quarter, to make it a six - point game bay halftime. The Celtics picked up where they left off to start the third, as they overtook the lead just minutes into the quarter. The Kings rallied back ahead and led by double digits for much of the quarter, however, the Celtics closed the quarter on a 14 - 2 run, to take a two - point lead into the fourth. The Celtics managed to stay in control through the four, and held on for their fourth win in their last five games. Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 31 points, 12 assists, 10 rebounds, one steal and one block, in 37 minutes. Marcus Morris followed up with 21 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Jaylen Brown added 22 points on 9 - of - 16 shooting, off the bench. The Celtics shot 50 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Buddy Hield led the KIngs with 34 points, seven assists and four rebounds, in 35 minutes. De'Aaron Fox followed up with 19 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and three steals, while Willie Cauley-Stein added 10 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Kings shot 50 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 34 from deep. The Kings (33 - 34) will look to bounce back as they take on the 76ers in Philadelphia on Friday. The Celtics (42 - 27) play host to the Hawks on Saturday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 129 - 120, at TD Garden on Saturday afternoon. The Celtics (43 - 27) looked ready to roll for the rare Saturday afternoon tip, racking up 43 first - quarter points versus the defensively challenged Hawks (24 - 46). However, Atlanta kept pace by scoring 36 of their own, and they refused to go away despite Boston totaling 105 points through only three quarters. Atlanta remained competitive despite entering the final period with a 13 - point deficit, coming all the way back to knot the game at 112 at the 5:53 mark of the fourth quarter. However, the home squad made a final push, finishing the game on a 17 - 8 run to seal the win. Trae Young paced the Hawks with 26 points, adding four rebounds, four assists and two steals. John Collins followed with a 20 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included six assists, one steal and one block. Taurean Prince furnished 17 points, four boards, two assists and two blocks. Vince Carter poured in 16 points off the bench. Kent Bazemore totaled 12 points, four assists and one rebound. Kyle Huerter delivered 10 points, five rebounds, three assists and one steal. Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 30 points and supplemented them with 11 rebounds, nine assists, two blocks and one steal. Jaylen Brown led the second unit with 23 points, adding three boards and two assists. Marcus Morris generated a 19 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks and one steal. Jayson Tatum finished with 18 points, eight rebounds, four assists and one steal. Marcus Smart managed 16 points, nine assists, one rebound, five steals and one block. The Hawks remain on the road and take on the Orlando Magic on Sunday evening, while the Celtics remain home and face the Denver Nuggets on Monday night.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Boston Celtics, 114 - 105, at TD Garden on Monday. There were 11 lead changes in this game, as Denver rode a big fourth quarter to victory. In fact, the Nuggets outscored the Celtics, 34 - 25, in the fourth quarter, as they achieved a game - high 12 - point lead in the final minutes. Rebounding was the difference for the Nuggets, as they outrebounded the Celtics, 51 - 37. Denver also shot 49 percent from the field and 36 percent from three - point range while holding Boston to 42 percent from the field and 31 percent from long range. Denver also won the fastbreak points battle, 18 - 7 and the points in the paint differential, 46 - 38. The Nuggets (47 - 22) were led by Nikola Jokic, as he tallied 21 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and three blocks. Will Barton accrued 20 points, four rebounds and two assists. Gary Harris amassed 16 points, four rebounds and two assists. Paul Millsap finished with 12 points, 11 rebounds and five assists. The Celtics (43 - 28) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he accumulated 30 points, five rebounds, four assists and four steals. Al Horford generated 20 points, six rebounds and six assists. Marcus Morris amassed 12 points and five rebounds while Jayson Tatum accumulated eight points, seven rebounds and six assists. On deck for the Celtics is a road matchup versus the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday. As for the Nuggets, they return to action on Thursday in a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Boston Celtics, 115 - 96, at TD Garden on Sunday night. The Spurs (43 - 31) came into the contest looking to get back on the winning track and keep a hold of their currently slotting as the eighth seed in the Western Conference, but they knew they figured on an uphill battle against the home - court Celtics (43 - 31). However, San Antonio helped itself with an early 31 - 24 lead after one quarter, and they'd managed to build a 10 - point cushion heading into the final period. Boston was unable to ever mount a series comeback at that point, with the visitors outscoring them by the same 31 - 24 margin they had in the first. The Celtics' biggest issue was having no answer for LaMarcus Aldridge, who trampled them for 48 points, 13 rebounds and six assists over 37 minutes. DeMar DeRozan was a distant second to Aldridge, generating 16 points, 11 assists and two blocks. Patty Mills was the only other double - digit Spurs scorer, pouring in 12 points off the bench while also dishing out four assists and recording one rebound. Jakob Poeltl mustered six points, 10 rebounds and two blocks. The starting backcourt of Derrick White and Bryn Forbes posted matching four - point tallies. Marcus Smart led the Celtics with 14 points, adding four rebounds and one assist. Marcus Morris and Gordon Hayward provided 13 points each while hauling in six and 10 rebounds, respectively. Kyrie Irving contributed a 11 - point, 12 - assist double - double that also included two rebounds, two steals and one block. Daniel Theis led the second unit with 11 points, seven boards, one assist and one block. The Spurs remain on the road and next visit the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday evening, while the Celtics travel to Cleveland and tangle with the Cavaliers on Tuesday night as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 114 - 112, at TD Garden on Friday. In this potential playoff preview, this game wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Kyrie Irving hit a game - winning lay - up with 0 seconds left to break a tied game. That was the only shot made in the final 80 seconds, as there were nine ties and four lead changes alone in the second half. The Celtics dominated through defensive rebounding, winning that battle, 36 - 27. Boston also shot 51 percent from the field while holding Indiana to 47 percent shooting. The Celtics also won the fastbreak scoring battle, 26 - 8, and the points in the paint differential, 54 - 40.
