The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Miami Heat, 113 - 112, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday night. It would have been difficult to envision the final score at the half, when the Hornets (2 - 1) held a commanding 72 - 52 lead. However, the Heat (1 - 2) refused to be embarrassed in their home opener, shaving 10 points off their deficit with a 30 - point third quarter and matching that total in the fourth while holding the visitors to 21. That left them just a point short at the final buzzer, but Miami's bench generated 43 points to help spearhead the rally. Ultimately, the Heat won both the rebounding battle by a 49 - 40 margin and slightly out - shot Charlotte, 46 percent to 44 percent. Kemba Walker led the way with a game - high 39 points, a total he supplemented with seven assists and five rebounds. Malik Monk was a distant second with 15 points, one rebound, one assist and one steal. Marvin Williams generated 13 points, six boards, one assist and three blocks. Jeremy Lamb supplied 12 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. Cody Zeller managed 11 points and eight rebounds. Dwyane Wade paced the Heat with 21 points off the bench, adding three rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Goran Dragic provided 20 points, seven assists and four rebounds. Rodney McGruder continued his productive start to the season with a 19 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two steals and one block. Derrick Jones, Jr. and Bam Adebayo - - the latter another key bench performer - - mustered matching 12 - point tallies. Hassan Whiteside contributed an 11 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. The Hornets remain on the road and head north of the border to tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Monday night, while the Heat remain home and next take the court against the New York Knicks on Wednesday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 120 - 111, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday. A 33 - 22 first quarter in advantage of Miami really set the tone in this game, as they held the lead for nearly 40 minutes of action. A late run did decide the game for the Heat though, as they finished their victory on a 19 - 7 run. Rebounding was the difference for the Heat, as they outrebounded the Trail Blazers, 56 - 42. In addition, Miami won the points in the paint battle, 48 - 32, while outscoring Portland in fastbreak points, 15 - 4. The Trail Blazers (3 - 2) got a spectacular performance out of Damian Lillard, as he tallied 42 points, seven rebounds and six assists. C.J. McCollum finished with 19 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Zach Collins was the only other Blazer in double figures, as he provided 13 points, four rebounds and two blocks off the bench. The Heat (3 - 2) were led by Goran Dragic, as he collected 28 points, three rebounds and five assists. Kelly Olynyk finished with 19 points, five rebounds and five assists. Rodney McGruder amassed 14 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Hassan Whiteside scored just five points but still provided 16 rebounds and six blocks. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Portland playing the Indiana Pacers on the road while Miami plays host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Miami Heat, 123 - 113, at American Airlines Arena on Monday. While Miami came into this game as a sizable favorite, Sacramento rode some elite offense to a road win. In fact, the Kings connected on 50 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range while recording 28 assists. Despite the fact the Heat led by 11 points after the first quarter, the Kings ended up outscoring them, 77 - 55, in the second and third quarters. Sacramento absolutely dominated down low, outscoring the Heat in the paint, 68 - 38. Turnovers were also key for the Kings, as they forced 19 turnovers from the Heat while committing just 12 on their end. The Kings (4 - 3) were led by Willie Cauley-Stein, as he tallied 26 points and 13 rebounds. Buddy Hield finished with 23 points, eight rebounds, five assists and two steals. De'Aaron Fox accrued 20 points, four rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Nemanja Bjelica generated 19 points, five rebounds and five assists. The Heat (3 - 3) were led by Josh Richardson, as he collected 31 points, three rebounds, two steals and three blocks. Goran Dragic accumulated 20 points, five assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside finished with 16 points, 24 rebounds, two steals and five blocks. Tyler Johnson led the bench with 11 points, four rebounds and four assists. Both teams play road games on Tuesday for their next outing, with Sacramento playing the Orlando Magic and Miami facing the Charlotte Hornets.

The Miami Heat defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 95 - 88, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat (5 - 5) came into the contest undermanned, as Goran Dragic was announced as unavailable shortly before tip - off due to an ankle injury. However, the Spurs (6 - 4) were missing a key starting piece in their own right, as veteran wing Rudy Gay was sidelined yet again with a heel injury. The home squad looked more engaged in the first half, jumping out to a 50 - 42 lead at intermission. They would create even more of a cushion in the third, expanding their advantage by another three points entering the final 12 minutes. San Antonio trailed by as much as 89 - 71 with 5:56 remaining before finishing the game on a 17 - 6 run. However, all it did was serve to make the final score appear more respectable in a contest in which they shot just 33 percent from the field. Patty Mills paced the Spurs with 20 points and four rebounds. Davis Bertans came off the bench to supply 19 points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. DeMar DeRozan led the starting five with an 18 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists, two steals and one block. Bryn Forbes provided 12 points. LaMarcus Aldridge mustered just six points on 2 - for - 14 shooting but did haul in 16 rebounds and record two blocks. Hassan Whiteside, who'd been a game - time decision due to a knee issue, with led the Heat with a 29 - point, 20 - rebound double - double that also included nine blocks. Wayne Ellington drew the start and delivered 20 points, four rebounds, one assist and two steals. Justise Winslow managed 16 points, five boards and three assists. Josh Richardson turned in 14 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals. The Spurs head back home to take on the Houston Rockets on Saturday evening, while the Heat remain home and await a Friday night visit from the Indiana Pacers.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Miami Heat, 110 - 102, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The game was a tale of two halves, with the short - handed Heat (5 - 6) forging a 59 - 51 first - half lead despite playing without Goran Dragic (knee). However, the Pacers (8 - 5) turned it on coming out of intermission despite seeing Thaddeus Young get ejected for elbowing Kelly Olynyk after playing just 17 minutes. Indiana outscored Miami by a 59 - 43 margin over the final 24 minutes and excelled on both ends of the floor. The Pacers shot a stellar 54 percent from the floor while also eliciting 23 turnovers from their hosts. Both benches thrived in the contest, with the Indiana second unit generating 44 points and the Miami reserves posting 48. Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 22 points, a total he supplemented with 10 assists, five rebounds and four steals. Darren Collison and Domantas Sabonis turned in 17 points each, with the latter also supplying 11 rebounds. Bojan Bogdanovic poured in 16 points, while Cory Joseph turned in 14 points, five rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes. Olynyk paced the Heat with 20 points and added four boards and two assists. Josh Richardson shifted to point guard with Dragic out and produced 18 points, six assists and two steals. Tyler Johnson supplied 15 points, five assists, two rebounds and one block. Hassan Whiteside posted an 11 - point, 20 - rebound double - double. Justise Winslow and Rodney McGruder managed 11 points and five assists apiece. The Pacers remain on the road and head to the Lone Star State, where they'll tangle with the Houston Rockets on Sunday night. The Heat remains home and faces the Washington Wizards on Saturday evening.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Miami Heat, 116 - 110, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday evening. The first quarter started out close, but the Heat closed the quarter on a 12 - 3 run, to take a 35 - 25 lead into the second. The Heat held their lead through most of the second, leading by nine, with just over four minutes left, but the Wizards closed the quarter well, to cut the deficit to just three, as they trailed, 61 - 58, at halftime. Neither team could break away in the third, while the Heat maintained a small advantage, the Wizards stayed close behind, trailing by two entering the final frame. Finally, the Wizards broke out in the fourth quarter, as they started off with a quick 9 - 1 run, to take a six - point lead just two minutes into the quarter. The Wiz did not look back from there, as they pushed their lead to 10, halfway through the quarter, and held on to earn the much - needed win. John Wall led the way for Washington with 28 points, nine assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block, in 40 minutes. Jeff Green followed up with 19 points, 10 rebounds and one steal, while Bradley Beal and Austin Rivers tallied 18 points each. Dwight Howard contributed 11 points, 16 rebounds and one steal. The Wizards shot 48 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 22 from deep. Meanwhile, Josh Richardson led the Heat with 24 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 36 minutes. Rodney McGruder followed up with 22 points, two rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Hassan Whiteside tallied 15 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, four blocks and one steal. The Heat (5 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the 76ers on Monday. The Wizards (3 - 9) play host to the Magic on Monday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Miami Heat, 124 - 114, at American Airlines Arena on Monday. This final scoreline is a bit unfair to Miami, as neither club attained a double - digit lead until the final five minutes. With that said, Philly held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as they finished the game on a 13 - 7 run. The assist - to - turnover ratio was the difference in the game, with Philly recording 24 assists to nine turnovers while Miami committed 15 turnovers to just 19 assists. These benches did a whole lot of damage, as they combined for 92 points between the two teams. The Sixers (9 - 6) got a gem out of Joel Embiid, as he tallied 25 points, 18 rebounds and three assists. Ben Simmons collected 13 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. J.J. Redick amassed 25 points and three assists. Furknan Korkmaz, Mike Muscala and Landry Shamet all reached double figures in scoring off of the bench. The Heat (5 - 8) were led by Goran Dragic, as he accumulated 22 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. Josh Richardson dropped 17 points in an otherwise empty stat line. Hassan Whiteside played 21 minutes as he battled foul trouble, finishing with 13 points and 11 boards. Tyler Johnson, Wayne Ellington and Kelly Olynyk all scored between 12 and 14 points to lead the bench. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Miami traveling to face the Brooklyn Nets and Philly playing the Orlando Magic on the road as well. Jimmy Butler is expected to make his Sixers debut in that game on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Miami Heat, 113 - 97, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Lakers got out to a great start on the road, as they jumped out to a 34 - 21 lead after one quarter. They kept their cushion for most of the second quarter, until the Heat cut the deficit to seven with 3:30 to go. However, the Lakers closed the half on an 11 - 3 run, to take a 15 - point lead into halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, but the Heat could not cut into the lead, as the Lakers held a double - digit advantage for almost the entire quarter. The fourth featured no surprises, as the Lakers were able to hold their ground and cruise to a much - needed win. LeBron James went off against his former squad, as he finished with 51 points on 19 - of - 31 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope followed up with 19 points, four rebounds, one steal and one block, in 28 minutes off the bench, while Kyle Kuzma chipped in 15 points on 7 - of - 12 shooting. The Lakers shot 45 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, the Heat were without Goran Dragic (toe). Wayne Ellington led Miami with 19 points on 7 - of - 14 shooting, in 37 minutes. Josh Richardson and Tyler Johnson added 17 points each, while Rodney McGruder tallied 14 points, seven rebounds and four assists. The Heat shot 40 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 32 from deep. The Heat (6 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Tuesday. The Lakers (9 - 7) head to Cleveland to take on the Cavaliers on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets took down the Miami Heat, 104 - 92, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday evening. Last week, Brooklyn (8 - 10) took a loss to Miami (6 - 11) on its home court. On Tuesday, the Nets evened the score, stealing one from the Heat in Miami. While the Heat entered the fourth quarter with the lead, Brooklyn was able to quickly jump ahead, going on a 90 run to take the lead in the first three minutes of the fourth quarter. After returning from a timeout, point guard D'Angelo Russell returned to the floor, delivering an electric performance to close out the game. Eight of Russell's 20 points came in the fourth quarter, including two jumpers in under 20 seconds, which helped push the Brooklyn lead to six. The win snapped Brooklyn out of a bit of a cold streak, as the team had dropped four of its previous five contests. Russell led the Nets with 20 points; he also added nine rebounds, six assists, and four steals. Big man Jarrett Allen, meanwhile, scored 13 points to go with 14 rebounds and two blocks. Both Russell and Allen have stepped up in recent games, as the team continues to cope with the absence of breakout star Caris LeVert (ankle). Miami's offense simply could not get things going, as the team shot just 36 percent from the field. Star center Hassan Whiteside did everything he could to make up for his team's poor shooting, grabbing 11 offensive rebounds to finish with a whopping 23 total boards. Even a 20 - 20 night from Whiteside could not win it for the Heat, though, as the team went just 7 - of - 32 from three - point range in a night they will hope to soon forget. Veteran star Dwyane Wade made his return to action after missing nearly two weeks due to the birth of his child. He scored five points in 13 minutes off the bench. The Nets face the second half of a back - to - back on Wednesday, as they will visit the Mavericks in Dallas. Miami, meanwhile, will regroup on Friday to face off against the Bulls.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Miami Heat, 115 - 113, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday night. The Hawks (5 - 16) entered this game as the team with fewer wins in the entire Association, while the Heat (7 - 13) ranked dead last in home wins, with only three over the course of the season thus far. But in this matchup of struggling teams, Atlanta came through and managed to survive Miami's furious comeback attempt in the fourth quarter. Miami jumped to a 38 - 35 lead after the first quarter, but Atlanta responded with a 33 - 14 second quarter that proved to be decisive. Miami won the third quarter by a two - point margin (34 - 32) and the final one by a 12 - point differential (27 - 15), but it wasn't enough and a late free throw sealed the deal for Atlanta. Josh Richardson had the chance to win it for the Heat, but missed his three - point attempt with 1 seconds left on the clock. Taurean Prince converted the decisive free throw late in the fourth quarter, but also led Atlanta offensively with an 18 - point, five - rebound performance. Rookie sensation Trae Young continues to lit it up for the Hawks and finished with 17 points, 10 assists and five rebounds. John Collins contributed 16 points, and Omari Spellman added 14 points in 20 minutes off the bench. Kent Bazemore chipped in with 12 points. As it has been the trend for the Heat this season, Richardson once again led the team in scoring with 22 points, but also added eight rebounds, four assists and five steals. Hassan Whiteside had 11 points with 10 rebounds, and Wayne Ellington added 15 points, five rebounds, and five steals. Dwyane Wade (18 points), Bam Adebayo (12 points) and Justise Winslow (11 points) thrived off the bench.

The Miami Heat defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 106 - 101, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The Heat (8 - 13) arguably played their best quarter of basketball of the season over the first 12 minutes of the contest, exiting the period with a 37 - 17 lead. They still held a 20 - point lead at halftime, but the Pelicans (11 - 12) refused to go quietly. New Orleans cut their deficit down to six entering the final quarter, and they'd continue to threaten throughout. The Pels were as close as 103 - 100 with 1:12 remaining, but Miami managed to hold on for only their fourth home win of the campaign. Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 41 points and added nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks. Jrue Holiday supplied 21 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one block. Nikola Mirotic registered 15 points and four boards. Julius Randle managed eight points, 10 rebounds, two assists and one block. E'Twaun Moore posted six points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes before exiting late in the game with a foot injury. Josh Richardson paced the Heat with 20 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block. Dwyane Wade totaled 18 points, six assists and five rebounds. Kelly Olynyk contributed 13 points, seven boards, two assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside delivered 12 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Rodney McGruder collected 11 points, five boards, one assist and two steals. The Pelicans next head to Charlotte to tangle with the Hornets on Sunday afternoon, while the Heat remain home and take on the Utah Jazz on Sunday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the Utah Jazz, 102 - 100, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Heat (9 - 13) came into the contest looking to build a little momentum, as they'd struggled to string wins together in the early portion of the season. Things looked to be headed in the wrong direction early against the Jazz (11 - 13), as Utah jumped out to a 35 - 27 first - quarter lead. Miami was able to claw back and reduce their deficit to 55 - 53 by intermission. The game ultimately came down to the final seconds, with Donovan Mitchell's misfire on a 24 - foot three - point jumper with 1 seconds remaining sealing the win for the home squad. The Heat was able to escape with a victory despite shooting just 40 percent overall. Ricky Rubio paced the Jazz with 23 points, a total he supplemented with six assists, five rebounds and one steal. Jae Crowder drew the start and produced 19 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Donovan Mitchell managed 18 points despite shooting just 8 - for - 24, and he added five rebounds, three assists and one steal. Rudy Gobert generated a 12 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists, three blocks and one steal. Joe Ingles supplied 11 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside led the Heat with a 23 - point, 20 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, three blocks and one steal. Kelly Olynyk contributed 16 points and eight rebounds, while Josh Richardson matched his scoring total and added four assists and three rebounds. Dwyane Wade poured in 15 points and also registered eight assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Wayne Ellington turned in 12 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Jazz head back home to take on the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday evening, while the Heat remains home and tangles with the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night as well.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Miami Heat, 105 - 90, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday. While Miami led for the majority of the first half, Orlando dominated in the second half. The third quarter was the difference, as the Magic outscored the Heat, 30 - 12. That allowed Orlando to lead by at least five points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The Magic's defense was key, as they held the Heat to 42 percent from the field and 34 percent from three - point range. Orlando was lights out from long distance, hitting 14 - of - 28 of their three's. Getting to the free - throw line was also critical, with the Magic hitting 15 - of - 20 and Miami connecting on just 2 - of - 5. The Magic (12 - 12) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he collected 20 points, 13 rebounds and five assists. Nikola Vucevic finished with 19 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Terrence Ross was a huge spark off the bench, as he provided 19 points, three rebounds and three assists. Evan Fournier, Jonathan Isaac and D.J. Augustin all scored between 11 and 13 points as well. The Heat (9 - 14) had no player score more than 14 points, as Justise Winslow led the team with 14 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks off the bench. Hassan Whiteside led the starters with 12 points, nine rebounds and three blocks on 6 - of - 7 shooting. Kelly Olynyk also played well off the bench, totaling 13 points, six rebounds and two assists. Josh Richardson had a nightmare game, as he accrued six points, four rebounds and five assists on 2 - of - 14 from the field. On deck for Orlando is a home matchup versus the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday. As for Miami, they'll travel to play the Phoenix Suns on Saturday for their next outing.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 101 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Thursday. While there were only two ties and five lead changes in this game, it was full of swings. In fact, Houston led for the entirety of the first half thanks to a 33 - 21 first quarter but Miami led for the majority of the second half. That can be attributed to the Heat outscoring the Rockets, 61 - 43, in the second and third quarters. Houston then went on a 12 - 2 run at the beginning of the fourth to make it close, as it stayed within a five - point margin for the final eight minutes. Miami was able to prevail though, as Eric Gordon missed a three - pointer at the buzzer that would have won the game. The Heat's defense was the difference, as they held the Rockets to 35 percent from the field and 33 percent from three - point range. They also controlled the boards, outrebounding Houston, 62 - 41. Much of that came on the offensive end, with Miami winning that battle, 20 - 9. That allowed the Heat to win the points in the paint differential, 52 - 20. The Rockets (16 - 15) were led by James Harden, as he collected 35 points, six rebounds, 12 assists and two steals. Eric Gordon totaled 20 points, three rebounds and three assists. P.J. Tucker totaled 14 points and seven boards while Clint Capela led the team with 14 rebounds. Chris Paul played just 12 minutes, as he departed in the second quarter due to a hamstring injury. The Heat (14 - 16) were led by Josh Richardson, as he accumulated 22 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Tyler Johnson tallied 19 points, four rebounds and two blocks. James Johnson accrued 11 points, five rebounds and three assists while Hassan Whiteside generated nine points, 17 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Derrick Jones Jr. led the bench with 15 points, eight rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Houston welcoming the San Antonio Spurs to Toyota Center and Miami remaining home to face the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Miami Heat defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 94 - 87, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday night. The Heat (15 - 16) came into the contest on a bit of a surge, having won seven of their prior 10 games after a rough start to the season. They seemed to set a dominant tone early against the Bucks (22 - 10), jumping out to a 21 - 8 lead during the first 12 minutes. However, Milwaukee turned the tables on their hosts in the second with a 30 - 16 advantage, allowing them a slim 38 - 37 halftime edge. Miami came out of intermission a focused bunch, and their 35 - point third quarter proved to be pivotal to their win. The Heat did allow a 16 - point fourth - quarter lead to be whittled down to just one point with 2:42 remaining, but they finished the game on a 12 - 6 run to secure victory. Khris Middleton led the way for the Bucks with 18 points and added seven rebounds, four assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe produced 17 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal. George Hill turned in 10 points, three rebounds and three assists. Giannis Antetokounmpo mustered nine points, 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Brook Lopez and Tony Snell posted nine points apiece as well. Josh Richardson paced the Heat with 16 points and supplemented them with five rebounds, three assists and two steals. Dwyane Wade managed 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal. Hassan Whiteside generated an 11 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included one assist. James Johnson and Kelly Olynyk had matching 11 - point tallies and hauled in six and five rebounds, respectively. The Bucks next take the court against the New York Knicks in the Big Apple on Christmas Day, while the Heat make the short trip to Central Florida to tangle with the Orlando Magic on Sunday evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Miami Heat, 106 - 104, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat got out to a good start at home as they outscored the East's top team 31 - 23 through the first quarter. The Heat kept their foot on the gas in the second, where they outscored the visitors by six, to push their lead to 58 - 44 by halftime. The Heat led by as many as 17 points early in the third, but the Raptors kept fighting and put together a great quarter, where they outscored the Heat by 16, to take a two - point lead into the final frame. The score stayed tight through the fourth, with Miami holding a two - possession lead with 2:27 to go, but the Raptors came up clutch with a couple of threes and some solid defense to earn an impressive road win, and end the Heat's five - game winning streak. Kawhi Leonard led Toronto with 30 points, eight rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 35 minutes. Danny Green followed up with 18 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Fred VanVleet added 16 points, two assists and one rebound. The Raptors shot 47 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 30 from long range. Meanwhile, Justise Winslow led the Heat with 21 points, four assists, two rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. Hassan Whiteside finished with 16 points, 12 rebounds, three blocks and one assist, while Josh Richardson tallied 17 points, seven assists, two rebounds, one steal and a block. The Heat shot 52 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 29 from distance. The Heat (16 - 17) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Cavs on Friday. The Raptors (26 - 10) head to Orlando to take on the Magic on Friday.

The Miami Heat defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 118 - 94, at American Airlines Arena on Friday night. The Heat (17 - 17) came into the contest a much improved team of late, winning five of their prior six games. However, the Cavaliers (8 - 28) arrived in South Florida ready to play, as they jumped out to a surprising 30 - 29 first - quarter lead. That seemed to wake up the home squad, as they owned a 56 - 52 lead by halftime and an 82 - 69 advantage at the end of three. They then finished off the game with their best offensive quarter, compiling 36 points overall in the final 12 minutes. Miami was impressive on both ends of the floor, shooting 53 percent while limiting Cleveland to a 38 percent success rate from the floor. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 18 points off the bench, adding five boards and four assists. Alec Burks mustered 17 points, six rebounds and five assists. Cedi Osman supplied 12 points, five boards, one assist and one steal. Larry Nance, Jr. pitched in 11 points, seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block, Matthew Dellavedova poured in nine points, while Channing Frye and Jaron Blossomgame had matching eight - point tallies. The Heat had seven players hit double digits in the scoring column led by Justise Winslow, who totaled 24 points. He added 11 rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Bam Adebayo followed with 18 points, nine rebounds and five assists. Rodney McGruder and Josh Richardson generated 16 points apiece. Hassan Whiteside turned in 12 points, four rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Tyler Johnson and Dwyane Wade posted 11 and 10 points while hauling in four and six rebounds, respectively. The Cavaliers remain on the road and jump right back into action against the Hawks on Saturday night, while the Heat remain home to take on the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday evening.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Miami Heat, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Timberwolves (17 - 19) came into the contest with an unsightly 4 - 13 road record, while the Heat (17 - 18) had been trending in the right direction with a 6 - 1 record over their last seven games. All of that went out the window after the opening tip, as Minnesota jumped out to a 30 - 19 first - quarter lead. While Miami put a 10 - point dent into that deficit with a 35 - point second period, the visitors would ensure victory with a 58 - point second half. The T-Wolves benefited from balanced contributions, as all five members of their starting five hit double digits in the scoring column. Karl-Anthony Towns paced the Timberwolves with 34 points, a total he supplemented with 18 rebounds, seven assists, six blocks and three steals. Robert Covington followed with 16 points, four rebounds and one steal. Taj Gibson supplied 14 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Andrew Wiggins pitched in 13 points. Tyus Jones filled in again for both Jeff Teague and Derrick Rose, who both sat due to ankle issues, and registered 12 points, five assists, four rebounds and five steals. Dario Saric mustered a bench - leading 13 points. Dwyane Wade paced the Heat with 21 points and added five assists, four rebounds and one block. Josh Richardson was next with 17 points and also mustered four rebounds and two assists. Derrick Jones, Jr. compiled 16 points, nine boards, one steal and one block. Kelly Olynyk tallied 13 points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. Justise Winslow shot just 4 - for - 15 but still produced 10 points, seven rebounds, three assists and four steals. Hassan Whiteside delivered eight points and 13 rebounds. The Timberwolves remain on the road and tangle with the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Heat pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 115 - 109, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The Heat got out to a strong start at home, as they took a 31 - 24 lead after one quarter. The Wizards gained some ground in the second, outscoring the Heat by four in the quarter, to cut the deficit to just three by halftime. However, the Heat stayed strong through a hotly contested third quarter and pushed their lead to nine by the start of the final frame. The Wizards made a valiant push in the fourth but ultimately came up short, as the Heat held on for their second straight win. Hassan Whiteside led Miami with 21 points, 18 rebounds, two blocks and one steal, in 29 minutes. Justise Winslow tallied 13 points, 10 assists and three rebounds, while Josh Richardson finished with 18 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. The Heat shot 49 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 33 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, in 40 minutes. Trevor Ariza followed up with 21 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal, while Otto Porter Jr. added 14 points, six rebounds, three steals and one assist. The Wizards shot 43 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 36 from deep. The Wizards (15 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Thunder in OKC on Sunday. The Heat (19 - 18) take on the Hawks in Atlanta on Sunday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Miami Heat, 103 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday. The Nuggets (27 - 12) and the Heat (20 - 19) have been two of the hottest teams in the league of late and as expected, this was a thrilling contest that was only decided during the final minutes of the contest. Denver went ahead in the first quarter (24 - 18), but Miami responded brilliantly during the second quarter and entered halftime leading by three points (52 - 49) following a 34 - 25 second - quarter score. But the Nuggets turned things around in the final two quarters and after winning both in the second half (27 - 24 and 27 - 23, respectively) they ended clinching a huge win against a tough opponent. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 113 - 102, at Spectrum Center on Tuesday evening. New York closed the quarter strong, to claim a two - point lead heading into halftime. The third quarter was more of the same, as neither team could create any real separation. However, the Pacers turned it up a notch in crunch time, where they outscored the Knicks, 12 - 4, in the final minutes to walk away with their third road win of the season. Domantas Sabonis led the Pacers with 30 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks, in 21 minutes off the bench. Victor Oladipo followed up with 24 points, six rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, in 32 minutes. Thaddeus Young tallied 13 points, 10 rebounds, five steals, three blocks and one assist. The Pacers shot 54 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 20 from long range. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. tallied 37 points on 10 - of - 19 shooting, to lead the Knicks. Noah Vonleh followed up with 14 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals, while Alonzo Trier chipped in 14 points, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Knicks shot 43 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 25 from deep. The Knicks (2 - 6) will look to bounce back as they take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Friday. The Pacers (5 - 3) take on the Bulls in Chicago on Friday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the New York Knicks, 116 - 115, after two overtime periods at Madison Square Garden on Monday night. Two of the weakest teams in the Eastern Conference ended playing one of the most entertaining, intense games of the 2018 - 19 NBA season thus far, as the Bulls (3 - 8) and the Knicks (3 - 8) both entered this game under .500 and playing some sloppy basketball by most standards. But this game ended being extremely intense, to the point that 58 minutes of basketball were needed to find a winner.. and the differential was only one point. In the end, Zach LaVine's clutch free - throw with less than two seconds on the clock gave the Bulls a huge win on the road. LaVine was the game's top scorer with 41 points, although he also committed eight turnovers, while Jabari Parker had 15 points with eight rebounds and Wendell Carter Jr. delivered 11 points, 13 boards and two assists. Antonio Blakeney contributed with 17 points in 20 minutes coming off the bench, as he filled the "absence "of Justin Holiday, who only scored six points while going 2 - for - 10 from the field in 47 minutes. Allonzo Trier carried the Knicks with a strong 21 - point performance, but Enes Kanter stole the show for the Knicks since he came off the bench and posted a huge double - double of 23 points and 24 rebounds, while also adding seven assists. Emmanuel Mudiay had 16 points and Mario Hezonja added 15, both off the bench. Two starters, Frank Ntilikina and Mitchell Robinson, failed to score.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host New York Knicks, 115 - 89, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. It's rare to see a home team dominated so thoroughly in the NBA but that's just what the Magic did here to the Knicks. In fact, Orlando took advantage of a 30 - 10 first quarter, as they held a double - digit lead for the final three quarters. In addition, the Knicks never got the game within a 20 - point margin in the second half. Orlando's defense was stifling, as they held New York to just 35 percent from the field and 18 percent from three - point range. The assist - to - turnover ratio was also huge, with the Magic recording 31 assists to nine turnovers while New York committed 19 turnovers to 13 assists. The 10 steals recorded by the Magic was a big part of that, as the Knicks recorded just two steals on their end. The Magic (6 - 7) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he totaled 21 points and 14 boards on 10 - of - 17 from the field. Evan Fournier collected 12 points, two rebounds and four assists. Terrence Ross led the bench with 22 points, three assists and two blocks. Mo Bamba also played well off the bench, amassing 15 points and eight boards. The Knicks (4 - 10) had no starters reach double figures in scoring, as Tim Hardaway Jr. led them with seven points and six boards on 2 - of - 12 shooting. Kevin Knox led the team in scoring off the bench, as he tallied 17 points and three boards. Enes Kanter was their best player, as he provided 16 points and 15 rebounds off the bench as well. On deck for Orlando is a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Monday. As for New York, they travel to play the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the New York Knicks 118 - 114 at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday. CJ McCollum and Damian Lillard were too much to handle for the Knicks at home as they fell for a sixth straight game. New York paced the game well and entered the half up two points, but their very small lineup that consisted of four guards late failed to secure a defensive rebound down two points. Evan Turner's timed a missed Lillard shot perfectly which gave him the easy two point put back shot, and Enes Kanter missed a skyhook in the waning seconds of the fourth quarter, which secured the win for the Blazers (11 - 5). McCollum finished with 31 points and four rebounds on 13 - of - 23 shooting, which included five made threes. Lillard added 29 points, eight assists and six rebounds, while Jusuf Nurkic pitched in 13 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes. The Knicks (4 - 13) were led by Tim Hardaway Jr, who has now scored 29 - plus points in his last three outings, and finished Tuesday with 32 points, to go with five rebounds and four assists on 10 - of - 21 shooting. Rookies Kevin Knox and Mitchell Robinson were quiet off the bench and combined for eight points. Robinson did add two blocks in his 18 minutes of action. Both teams play the second game of a back - to - back on Wednesday, as the Knicks visit the Boston Celtics and the Blazers visit the Milwaukee Bucks.

The New York Knicks defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 114 - 109, at Madison Square Garden on Friday evening. The Pelicans got out to a good start on the road, as they built a 34 - 28 advantage after one quarter. The Knicks kept up the fight and answered back in the second, by outscoring the Pelicans by five points in the quarter, so that they trailed by one, 60 - 59, at halftime. The Pelicans came out strong in the third and quickly pushed their lead to seven, but the Knicks stayed with it, so as to trail by just three points, heading into the final frame. The Pelicans held the advantage to start the fourth and even pushed their lead to 101 - 92, with six minutes left in the contest. However, the Knicks mounted a 16 - 2 run, to take a five - point advantage with 34 seconds left. The Knicks were able to hang on for their second straight win. Emmanuel Mudiay came up huge for New York with 27 points, seven rebounds, four steals and two assists, in 28 minutes of action. Alonzo Trier also had a big night, with 25 points, eight rebounds and four assists, in 34 minutes off the bench. Enes Kanter finished with 17 points, 12 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal, while Noah Vonleh added 14 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks. Meanwhile, Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 33 points, 12 rebounds and four assists, in 32 minutes. Jrue Holiday followed up with 22 points, eight assists, five rebounds and three steals, while Nikola Mirotic chipped in 19 points nine rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block. The Pelicans shot 40 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from deep. The Pelicans (10 - 9) will look to bounce back as they take on the Wizards in Washington on Saturday. The Knicks (6 - 14) head to Memphis to take on the Grizzlies on Sunday.

The New York Knicks defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks in overtime, 136 - 134, at Madison Square Garden on Saturday. While Milwaukee led for the majority of this game, it took an extra session to determine a winner. In fact, New York finished regulation on a 14 - 5 run to send the game into overtime. There were three ties and three lead changes in the overtime alone, as neither club led by more than three points. The Knicks defense was critical late, as they forced the Bucks to miss their final five shots, with all of those to either tie or take the lead. Three-point shooting was also huge, with New York hitting 20 - of - 34 and Milwaukee connecting on just 18 - of - 42. The Knicks also connected on 53 percent from the field while holding Milwaukee to 49 percent shooting. The Bucks (16 - 6) got another gem out of Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 33 points, 19 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks. Eric Bledsoe accrued 27 points. five rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Malcolm Brogdon finished with 22 points, six rebounds and four assists. Brook Lopez totaled 13 points and nine boards but missed two free throws in the final seconds that would have tied the game. The Knicks (7 - 17) got a career - best 26 points from Kevin Knox, as he did that damage off the bench. Emmanual Mudiay led the starters with 28 points, three rebounds and seven assists. Tin Hardaway Jr. amassed 21 points, four rebounds and eight assists. Damyean Dotson was also a huge spark off the bench, providing 21 points and five boards. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Monday. As for Milwaukee, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the Detroit Pistons.

The Washington Wizards defeated the New York Knicks, 110 - 107, at Madison Square Garden on Monday evening. The two teams came into the contest dealing with their respective share of struggles, and it was the hometown Knicks (8 - 17) that seemed more prepared to wage battle in the first half. New York had forged a 61 - 52 lead by intermission, but they saw that quickly wiped away in a disastrous third quarter. The Wizards (10 - 14) outscored their hosts by a 34 - 19 margin during that period, allowing them to go into the final 12 minutes with a six - point edge. New York would eventually go on a 120 run to close the gap to 107 - 104 with 35 seconds remaining, but a 26 - foot John Wall three - point jumper with 12 seconds left helped seal the win for the visitors. Bradley Beal led the way for the Wizards with 27 points, a total he supplemented with eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block. Kelly Oubre, Jr. provided 21 points, five rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal. Wall generated an 18 - point, 15 - assist double - double. Markieff Morris matched Wall's scoring total off the bench and added seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. Otto Porter, Jr. supplied 15 points, five rebounds, three steals and three blocks. Tim Hardaway, Jr. paced the Knicks with 20 points, a total he supplemented with two assists. Dewayne Dotson followed with a bench - leading 17 points and also contributed nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. Emmanuel Mudiay registered 16 points, five rebounds, four assists and one block. Enes Kanter posted a 13 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one steal. Noah Vonleh tallied 11 points, eight boards, one assist and one block. The Wizards remain on the road and head south to face the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday night, while the Knicks pay a visit to the Boston Celtics on Wednesday evening as well.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the New York Knicks, 112 - 104, at Madison Square Garden on Saturday evening. The Nets (10 - 18) got the early jump on their inter - city rivals in the first quarter by taking a 30 - 23 lead, an edge that they'd expanded to 11 by the half. They ultimately entered the final 12 minutes with a 94 - 77 advantage that was more than enough to withstand the Knicks' (8 - 19) best all - around quarter of the game. Brooklyn put on a shooting display, draining 49 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent from three - point range. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 25 points off the bench and added six assists, three rebounds and one steal. Rodions Kurucs supplied 20 points, six boards, two assists, two steals and one block. Allen Crabbe registered 17 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Jarrett Allen generated a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. Joe Harris poured in 11 points. Enes Kanter paced the Knicks with a 23 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Allonzo Trier managed 15 points and two rebounds. Emmanuel Mudiay contributed 13 points, four assists and one rebound. Mario Hezonja and Damyean Dotson pitched in 12 points apiece. Tim Hardaway, Jr. could only muster seven points on 2 - for - 12 shooting. The Nets remain on the road and pay a visit to the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday night, while the Knicks remain home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Sunday evening.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the New York Knicks, 119 - 117, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday evening. Charlotte (13 - 13) brought its record back to .500 with the relatively painless win on Sunday. The Hornets jumped out to a quick lead in the second quarter and brought it to double - digits with a run to start the third. While the Knicks (8 - 20) chipped away at the lead throughout the fourth quarter, Kemba Walker and the Hornets continued their strong 48 percent shooting night to earn the win. The Hornets overcame a career night for Knicks rookie Kevin Knox, who scored 26 points to go with 15 rebounds. Knox's standout performance was accompanied by similarly strong play from Frank Ntilikina. Ntilikina had seen multiple DNPs in the last two weeks after his slow start to the season, but on Sunday, he looked ready to go. The sophomore point guard shot 7 - of - 11 from the field en route to 18 points. Still, Charlotte was able to earn the win with ease, thanks, as usual, to a strong night from Kemba Walker. Walker scored 25 points to go with six assists and four steals in the win. It was also a big night for Tony Parker. The former San Antonio Spur delivered a gut - punch to the Knicks off the bench, scoring 16 points in just 16 minutes of action. On Wednesday, Charlotte will host the Detroit Pistons while the Knicks will travel to Cleveland to face the Cavaliers.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the host New York Knicks, 128 - 110, at Madison Square Garden on Monday, While this game was competitive in the first half, Phoenix rode a monster third quarter to victory. In fact, the Suns outscored the Knicks in the third, 41 - 17, as that allowed them to hold a double - digit lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Pheonix's defense came up big, as they held New York to 40 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range. The Suns connected on 52 percent from the field and 33 percent from long range while out - assisting the Knicks, 27 - 15. The Suns (7 - 24) were led by Devin Booker, as he collected 38 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two steals. T.J. Warren scored 19 of his 26 points in the third quarter, as he added five rebounds, three steals and two blocks to his tally. DeAndre Ayton totaled 21 points and 13 rebounds. Jamal Crawford was huge off the bench, providing six points and a season - high 14 assists. The Knicks (9 - 23) got another career - high from Emmanuel Mudiay, as he tallied 32 points, six rebounds and six assists. Kevin Knox amassed 17 points and five boards. Enes Kanter finished with 13 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Mario Hezonja led the bench with 14 points and five rebounds. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Phoenix traveling to face the Boston Celtics and New York playing the Philadelphia 76ers on the road as well.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 107, at Madison Square Garden on Friday evening. The Hawks (8 - 23) had come in having notched just two road wins in 16 tries, so it was difficult to have a positive outlook on their chances of prevailing after falling behind by a 39 - 28 score through one quarter. To its credit, Atlanta progressively battled back over the subsequent three quarters, and they sealed the victory by outscoring the Knicks (9 - 25) by a 27 - 18 margin in the final 12 minutes. The Hawks' dominance on the boards greatly helped their cause, as they outrebounded New York by a 54 - 35 margin. Kent Bazemore led the way with 22 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds, one assist and one steal. John Collins followed with a 17 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included four assists. Kyle Huerter poured in 16 points. Tre Young registered 15 points, 10 assists, three rebounds and one steal. DeAndre Bembry and Alex Len managed 12 points apiece, while Jeremy Lin contributed 11. Emmanuel Mudiay paced the Knicks with 32 points and also dished out four assists. Kevin Knox went for 24 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. Tim Hardaway, Jr. collected 15 points, five assists and four rebounds. Noah Vonleh generated a 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Enes Kanter had 10 points and five rebounds. The Hawks remain on the road and tangle with the Detroit Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the Knicks remain home and face off with the Milwaukee Bucks on Christmas Day.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the New York Knicks, 109 - 95, at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday afternoon. The Bucks (23 - 10) encountered a feisty Knicks (9 - 26) squad ready to defend their home court on Christmas Day, as New York forged a quick 24 - 22 lead after 12 minutes. However, Milwaukee began to assert itself with a strong 26 - point second quarter, leading to a slim 48 - 46 halftime lead. The third quarter was the pivotal period, however, as the visitors pulled away for good by adding 14 points to their advantage. New York acquitted itself well on the boards with a 58 - 50 rebounding advantage, but the Bucks' 45 percent success rate from the floor was markedly better than their hosts' 36 percent figure. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with a 30 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, four steals and two blocks. Brook Lopez followed with 20 points, four boards and two blocks. Malcolm Brogdon mustered 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and three steals. Thon Maker paced the bench with 12 points and added three rebounds and two blocks. Eric Bledsoe supplied 11 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal. Khris Middleton managed just six points on 2 - for - 12 shooting. Kevin Knox paced the Knicks with 21 points, adding six rebounds and three assists. Noah Vonleh followed with a 14 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. Tim Hardaway, Jr. matched Vonleh's scoring total and added 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Enes Kanter totaled 12 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. Emmanuel Mudiay registered 11 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Bucks and Knicks meet up again on Thursday night in Milwaukee for a rematch.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host New York Knicks, 121 - 106, at Madison Square Garden on Friday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Indiana, they led for all but a couple minutes. In fact, Indiana won all four individual quarters, as a 31 - 22 first quarter really set the tone. The Pacers ended up shooting 52 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range while holding the Knicks to 44 percent from the field and 36 percent from long range. Rebounding was also critical, with Indiana outrebounding New York, 47 - 37. The Pacers also went a perfect 11 - of - 11 from the free - throw line. The Pacers (28 - 14) were led by Domantas Sabonis, as he tallied 22 points, 15 rebounds and three assists. Victor Oladipo accrued 19 points, four rebounds six assists. Bojan Bogdanovic totaled 15 points and two boards while Darren Collison accumulated seven points, five rebounds and 10 assists. Thaddeus Young finished with 13 points, six rebounds, three assists and four steals. The Knicks (10 - 32) were led by Emmanuel Mudiay, as he generated 21 points, two rebounds and three assists. Kevin Knox amassed 14 points, two rebounds and two assists. Tim Hardaway Jr. collected 12 points, six rebounds and two assists while Damyean Dotson led the bench with 15 points, six rebounds and four assists. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday. As for Indiana, they return to action on Saturday when they play host to the Phoenix Suns.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the New York Knicks, 108 - 105, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. The 76ers (28 - 16) and the Knicks (10 - 33) played a surprisingly close contest at The Big Apple and the hosts came quite close to send the game into overtime, but Philadelphia survived when a last - second three - point jumper from Emmanuel Mudiay didn't go in. The 76ers got off to a better start, though, leading 36 - 24 after the first quarter and extending the gap to 16 points at the break following a 30 - 26 second quarter. But the Knicks flipped the script admirably in the third, edging their rivals 32 - 17 and making it a one - point game heading into the fourth. Their rally fell short, however, and Philly ended winning the game on Joel Embiid's return to the starting lineup. Joel Embiid finished with 26 points and eight rebounds during 32 minutes, but the star of the game for the Sixers was Ben Simmons. The Australian phenom might have fallen short of a triple - double, but he still posted a strong stat line of 20 points, 22 rebounds and nine assists. J.J. Redick also added 22 points, and Jimmy Butler chipped in with 16 points and eight boards. T.J. McConnell had six points and four assists off the bench. Emmanuel Mudiay might have missed the game - tying three - point shot at the end of regulation, but still had a decent game with 19 points, four assists and four rebounds. The best player for the Knicks was Kevin Knox, however, since he finished with 31 points, seven rebounds, and two steals across 44 minutes of action. Luke Kornet thrived off the bench and chipped in with 23 points, five assists and five rebounds.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the New York Knicks, 127 - 109, at Madison Square Garden on Monday afternoon. The Thunder (28 - 18) and the Knicks (10 - 35) opened the MLK-Day-slate on the NBA this Monday, but this was a one - sided game as soon as the ball started rolling. The Thunder destroyed the Knicks in the first quarter and quickly jumped to a 34 - 16 lead following the first 12 minutes of action. As expected, they never relinquished that lead but they never gave New York a chance to mount a comeback, either. OKC won both the second (33 - 31) and third quarters (36 - 35), so the final 12 minutes of action, where the Knicks won 27 - 24, were not going to change the outcome of the game. A silver lining for the Knicks is that the final three quarters were quite tight, but it's impossible to hide the fact that the Thunder always played with a huge lead on their favor. Russell Westbrook came close to register a triple - double thanks to 17 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists, while Paul George contributed with 31 points, four rebounds and four assists to the winning cause. Jerami Grant chipped in with 16 points and six boards, while Steven Adams added 10 points, seven boards and three dimes. Dennis Schroder had 17 points coming off the bench. Tim Hardaway Jr. led the way for the Knicks since he finished with 23 points in 27 minutes of action while shooting 7 - 14 from the field. Emmanuel Mudiay added 14 points, while Noah Vonleh contributed 10 points and five boards to the losing cause. Allonzo Trier had a strong effort off the bench thanks to 16 points, eight assists, and six rebounds. Enes Kanter had 11 points.

The Houston Rockets defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 110, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday. Wednesday night's outing in New York City ended up being a thriller highlighted by career performances for each team. The Rockets (27 - 20) held a six - point lead with a minute to go and appeared to be well on their way to ending things, but then a 70 run by the Knicks over the next 30 seconds put the home team up by one. Ultimately, an Eric Gordon three - pointer put the Rockets up three with just over nine seconds remaining, and that was followed by a James Harden steal and dunk that ended the game. That dunk gave Harden 61 points, which is tied for the most points scored by a visiting player in Madison Square Garden, and he also recorded 15 rebounds, four assists and five steals. Eric Gordon added 20 points on 8 - of - 15 shooting from the field, and the new Rocket, Kenneth Faried, scored 11 points to make him the third and final Houston player to reach double figures. As for the Knicks (10 - 36), they were lead by a career - best performance from rookie Allonzo Trier, who scored 31 points on 12 - of - 18 shooting in 33 minutes off the bench. He hit a go - ahead layup with just 20 seconds to go, but Gordon's three ended up ruining the point guard's chances at being the hero Wednesday night. Four other New York players scored in double figures, but none scored higher than Emmanuel Mudiay's 14 points in 28 minutes. Ultimately what killed the Knicks' chances was their inability to take care of the ball, as the team committed 18 turnovers to recording just 15 assists, so it was fitting that the game ended on a Houston steal.

The Miami Heat defeated the host New York Knicks, 106 - 97, at Madison Square Garden on Monday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the Knicks holding a one - point lead after one quarter. The Knicks kept up the solid play through the second, and outscored the visitors by five points in the quarter, to take a 58 - 52 lead into halftime. However, the Heat came out on fire in the third, as they outscored the Knicks 29 - 12 in the quarter, to claim an 11 - point lead by the start of the fourth quarter. The Knicks battled through the fourth, but it was not enough to make up for the deficit accumulated through the third. The Heat held on to earn their second straight win, while this marks the ninth straight loss for the Knicks. Wayne Ellington led the Heat with 19 points on 6 - of - 13 shooting and one rebound, in 30 minutes. Dwyane Wade tallied 15 points, 10 assists, five rebounds and one steal, while Hassan Whiteside finished with 13 points, 16 rebounds, three blocks and two assists. The Heat shot 46 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. led the Knicks with 22 points on 7 - of - 16 shooting, six rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 30 minutes. Trey Burke followed up with 16 points, two assists and one rebound, while Damyean Dotson added 14 points, four assists, two steals, one block and one rebound. The Knicks shot 43 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 26 from long range. The Knicks (10 - 38) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Monday. The Heat (24 - 24) play host to the Bulls on Wednesday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the host New York Knicks, 114 - 90, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday evening. The Mavs got out to a good start on the road, as they held a four - point advantage after one quarter of action. The Knicks pushed to take a small lead around the mid - way point in the second, but the visitors pulled back ahead to reclaim the advantage, and took a 55 - 47 lead into halftime. The Mavericks came out strong in the third and outscored the Knicks by 12 in the quarter, to bring their lead 20 by the start of the final frame. The Mavs were able to cruise from there and hang on for just their fifth road win of the season. This marks the 11th straight loss for the Knicks. Dennis Smith Jr. tallied a triple - double for Dallas, with 13 points, 10 rebounds and 15 assists, in 28 minutes of action. Harrison Barnes tallied 19 points on 7 - of - 14 shooting, four rebounds and two assists, while Luka Doncic added 16 points, eight rebound and five assists. The Mavs shot 54 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 38 from deep. Meanwhile, Kevin Knox led the Knicks with 17 points on 6 - of - 16 shooting, five rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 27 minutes. Trey Burke added 16 points, three assists, two steals, one rebound and one block, while Mario Hezonja tallied 13 points, two rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Knicks shot 41 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 26 from long range. The Knicks (10 - 40) play host to the Celtics on Friday. The Mavericks (23 - 27) head to Detroit to take on the Pistons on Thursday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the host New York Knicks, 113 - 99, at Madison Square Garden on Friday. Boston came into this game as a sizable favorite against this shorthanded New York squad and this 14 - point victory shows why. In fact, the Celtics held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as a 33 - 26 fourth quarter really put things to bed. The Celtics defense was critical, as they recorded 11 steals and seven blocks while the Knicks picked up just two steals and two blocks. That was evident in the turnover differential, with Boston winning that battle, 17 - 7. The Celtics (33 - 19) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he tallied 23 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and two steals. Marcus Morris amassed 18 points, five rebounds and two steals. Al Horford accrued 14 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Gordon Hayward led the bench with 14 points, three rebounds, two assists and two blocks. The Knicks (10 - 41) were led by Damyean Dotson, as he totaled 22 points and six rebounds. Kevin Knox collected 21 points, five rebounds and two assists. Noah Vonleh accumulated seven points, 11 rebounds and seven assists. Mario Hezonja led the bench with 10 points, three rebounds and two assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Boston playing host to the Oklahoma City Thunder and New York welcoming the Memphis Grizzlies to MSG.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the New York Knicks, 96 - 84, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday afternoon. The Grizzlies (21 - 33) were pretty shorthanded entering this game, but they managed to leave the injuries behind and didn't have many problems to defeat this new - look Knicks (10 - 42) that don't have Kristaps Porzingis anymore. New York grabbed the lead in the first quarter, however, and they jumped to a 22 - 19 lead following the first 12 minutes of action, but Memphis turned things around with a 23 - 19 second quarter that saw them up by one at the break (42 - 41). They pulled ahead for good in the third quarter (32 - 21) and entered the fourth up by 12 points, and since the fourth quarter ended 22 - 22, the Grizzlies won this game rather comfortably. The duo of Mike Conley and Marc Gasol lifted Memphis here; while the point - guard had 25 points, eight rebounds and seven assists, the Spanish center delivered a strong effort thanks to 24 points, nine rebounds, and five assists. Jaren Jackson Jr. had 16 points with seven boards, while Justin Holiday had 19 points. They did most of the heavy lifting in this one, as Memphis' entire bench combined for only 12 points between six players. Despite a poor shooting performance, Kevin Knox was the top scorer for the Knicks since he finished with 17 points, while DeAndre Jordan had a strong double - double of 12 points and 12 rebounds. Mario Hezonja had 14 points and eight rebounds coming off the bench, while Luke Kornet chipped in with 11 points. Dennis Smith Jr. only had eight points while shooting 3 - 9 from the field.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the New York Knicks, 105 - 92, at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night. The Pistons (24 - 29) were playing their third game in four nights Tuesday, but they were riding high following a strong double - digit win against the Nuggets on Monday. With Detroit's front - line players having the luxury of logging minutes in the 20s due to that lopsided win, the Pistons came out of the gates running hot, racking up 63 first - half points against the Knicks (10 - 43). The third quarter then turned into an unexpected defensive struggle, but Detroit found its shooting stroke again over the final 12 minutes to seal the win. Blake Griffin led the way for the Pistons, posting 29 points and supplementing them with eight assist and six rebounds. Reggie Jackson and Reggie Bullock provided matching 19 - point tallies while contributing seven assists and seven rebounds, respectively. Andre Drummond generated a 17 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included five blocks. Dennis Smith, Jr. paced the Knicks in only his second game with the club, collecting 25 points and dishing out six assists. He also hauled in five rebounds. Mitchell Robinson posted a 13 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. Kevin Knox managed 11 points and seven boards. Wesley Matthews drew his first start in a New York uniform and totaled nine points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 121 - 107, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. The Lakers shot 46 percent from the field, including, 6 - of - 24 from long range. The Lakers (4 - 6) will look to bounce back, as they play host to the Timberwolves on Wednesday. The Raptors (9 - 1) head to Utah to take on the Jazz on Monday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 107 - 106, in a last - second thriller at Staples Center on Sunday evening. LeBron James won his team the game after almost giving it up, scoring the go - ahead basket on a put - back dunk with 15 seconds remaining after going 0 - of - 2 at the free - throw line. Young drove to the basket and put up a lay - up as time expired, but was blocked by veteran center Tyson Chandler to end the game. LA, meanwhile, will host the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 126 - 117, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. McCollum followed up with 23 points, four assists, two steals and one rebound, in 35 minutes, while Jusuf Nurkic tallied 21 points, 14 rebounds, four blocks, three steals and one assist. The Trail Blazers shot 44 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 33 from long range. The Trail Blazers (10 - 4) will look to bounce back as they take on the Timberwolves in Minnesota on Friday. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Utah Jazz, 90 - 83, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Lakers remain home and tangle with the Orlando Magic on Sunday afternoon.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 108 - 104, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. The Lakers (11 - 8) and the Magic (10 - 10) played a very intense game and while Orlando seemed ready to cruise their way in the final minutes, Los Angeles mounted a furious comeback in the final 12 minutes that saw them tie the game into the final 60 seconds of the contest. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Indiana Pacers, 104 - 96, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. The Lakers (12 - 9) came out of the gates seemingly intent on eradicating a two - game skid in short order, as they exploded for 38 first - quarter points while limiting the Pacers (13 - 9) to 15. Doug McDermott and Cory Joseph had matching 10 - point tallies off the bench. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 114 - 103, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Mavericks got out to a great start on the road, with a 17 - 6 lead, just four minutes into the quarter. They kept up the momentum and build a, 32 - 22, lead by the end of the quarter. LeBron James led the Lakers with 28 points, five rebounds, four assists and one block, in 31 minutes. The Mavs (10 - 10) will look to get back on track as they play host to the Clippers on Sunday. The Lakers (13 - 9) play host to the Suns on Sunday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 120 - 96, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. The Lakers (14 - 9) have been on a roll of late, and clinched a third - straight win while winning eight of their last 11 contests with another dominant performance; this time, they bounced back from a poor performance in the first quarter to destroy the Suns (4 - 19). Phoenix started strong and finished the first quarter up by 10 points (31 - 21), but the Lakers bounced back and a 40 - 15 win during the second quarter saw them up by 15 points at half time. Los Angeles won the remaining two quarters as well, 34 - 28 and 25 - 22, respectively. They showed composure and didn't have much problems to defeat one of the worst teams in The Association in front of their own crowd. Six Lakers players scored in double digits in this one and Kyle Kuzma paced the offense with a 23 - point, eight - rebound performance. LeBron James delivered another strong outing, and finished with 22 points, eight assists, and six rebounds. Brandon Ingram contributed with 15 points, and JaVale McGee chipped in with 14 points and eight boards. Michael Beasley added 14 points coming off the bench. Richaun Holmes led the way with 15 points off the bench, while Josh Jackson and Trevor Ariza each added 13 points. Rookie DeAndre Ayton had a strong double - double of 10 points with 10 rebounds. Devin Booker, who was questionable, only scored six points in 17 minutes of action.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the San Antonio Spurs, 121 - 113, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. The Lakers (15 - 9) trailed by three heading into the fourth quarter, but scored 43 points in the final period to pull ahead. Fellow veteran Rudy Gay was not far behind, tallying a season - high 31 points in the narrow loss. LaMarcus Aldridge scored 21 points and added another nine rebounds. It was a poor shooting night for the Spurs, who hit just 26 percent of their three - point attempts. The two teams will rematch in San Antonio on Friday night.

The Los Angeles Lakers escaped with a win over the visiting Miami Heat, 108 - 105, at Staples Center on Monday evening. It was a hotly anticipated contest, as it likely marked the last time that LeBron James and Dwyane Wade, two friends and future Hall of Famers, would face each other. The Heat hit just 44 percent of its shots from the field in the loss and committed 17 turnovers. The Heat will visit Utah on Wednesday, while the Lakers travel to Houston to clash with the Rockets on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 112 - 104, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Pelicans shot 43 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 27 from deep. The Pelicans (15 - 18) will look to bounce back as they take on the Kings in Sacramento on Sunday. The Lakers (19 - 13) play host to the Grizzlies on Sunday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 118 - 107, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Clippers got out to a strong start as they led 28 - 23 after on quarter. The New York Knicks defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 119 - 112, at Staples Center on Friday night. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 131 - 120, at Staples Center on Friday night. The Bucks shot 52 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 40 from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 31 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and one steal, in 38 minutes. The Lakers shot 48 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 40 from deep. The Lakers (30 - 32) will look to bounce back as they take on the Suns on Saturday. The Denver Nuggets blew out the Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 99, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. The Boston Celtics defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 120 - 107, at Staples Center on Saturday. Boston came into this game as a sizable favorite, as they added to Los Angeles' struggles here. Rajon Rondo accrued four points, six rebounds and nine assists. Johnathan Williams led the bench with 18 points and 10 boards. Boston returns to action on Monday, when they travel to face the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the Chicago Bulls on Tuesday

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 111 - 106, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Sacramento Kings, 111 - 106, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 129 - 115, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The contest got out to a high - scoring start, as the Hornets led for most of the first quarter, and took a 35 - 33 lead into the second. The Lakers kept up the pace in the second, while the visitors slowed down, as the Lakers outscored the Hornets by 12 in the quarter, to take a 10 - point lead into halftime. Both squads came out firing again in the third, as they matched each other for 32 points each in the quarter, with the Lakers taking a 101 - 91 lead into the final frame. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope followed up with 25 points, four rebounds, four assists and a steal, while Kyle Kuzma added 20 points, three rebounds and an assist. The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 104 - 101, at Amway Center on Wednesday. In the opener for both of these Florida teams, it wasn't decided until the final seconds. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the host Orlando Magic, 120 - 88, at Amway Center on Friday. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Orlando Magic, 128 - 114, at Amway Center on Thursday. This was an impressive performance from Portland, as they pulled out a wire - to - wire win. They did most of their damage in the first and fourth quarters, outscoring Orlando, 70 - 52. The Sacramento Kings defeated the Orlando Magic, 107 - 99, at Amway Center on Tuesday evening. The Magic (2 - 5) appeared to catch the visitors a bit flat early, jumping out to a 31 - 26 first - quarter lead. Aaron Gordon paced the Magic with 18 points, and he added 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks. Terrence Ross came off the bench to pour in 17 points. Nikola Vucevic contributed 15 points and a game - high 15 rebounds. He also dished out five assists. Jonathon Simmons supplied 12 points, five assists and three rebounds. Jonathan Isaac and Evan Fournier pitched in nine points apiece. The Kings remain on the road and take on the Atlanta Hawks on Thursday night, while the Magic remain home and tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Orlando Magic, 120 - 95, at Amway Center on Friday. It's rare to see a home team dominated so thoroughly in the NBA but that was, unfortunately, the case for the Magic here. The Clippers really made their mark in the second quarter, outscoring Orlando, 35 - 22. The Magic never got the game within an eight - point margin from there, as the Clippers led by at least 13 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The Magic (2 - 6) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he tallied 22 points, 11 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Evan Fournier finished with 19 points, three rebounds, four assists and three steals. D.J. Augustin was the only other Orlando player in double figures, as he collected 13 points, five rebounds and three assists. On deck for Orlando is a road matchup versus the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday. As for Los Angeles, they're off until Monday when they play host to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 102 - 100, at Amway Center on Monday. It's rare to see a game with just seven ties and five lead changes come down to the last shot but that was the case here. Evan Fournier played the hero, as he hit a game - winning jumper at the buzzer to break a tied game. Orlando rode a big fourth quarter to victory, outscoring Cleveland, 32 - 21, in the final quarter. The Detroit Pistons defeated the host Orlando Magic, 103 - 96, at Amway Center on Wednesday. This was truly a battle of four quarters, as each individual quarter was decided by at least five points. Detroit did their damage in the second and fourth quarters, outscoring Orlando, 57 - 36. The swings are evident by the fact that there were eight ties and nine lead changes in total. Blake Griffin finished with 20 points, five rebounds and three assists. Reggie Jackson totaled 15 points and four assists. Stanley Johnson led the bench with 13 points, six rebounds and three assists. The Magic (4 - 7) were led by Evan Fournier, as he collected 27 points, four rebounds, three assists and three steals on 12 - of - 19 shooting. D.J. Augustin accumulated 16 points, four rebounds and seven assists. Aaron Gordon amassed 15 points, 10 rebounds and six assists. Terrence Ross led the bench with 15 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Orlando playing host to the struggling Washington Wizards and Detroit traveling to face the Atlanta Hawks.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 117 - 108, at Amway Center on Friday. While Washington led for the majority of the first quarter, Orlando never relinquished the lead from there. In fact, the Magic led by 15 points at the half, as they held a double - digit lead for the majority of this game.
