On deck for Washington is a road matchup versus the Miami Heat on Saturday. As for Orlando, they travel to The Big Apple to play the New York Knicks on Sunday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 111 - 106, at Amway Center on Wednesday night. The 76ers (9 - 7) featured Jimmy Butler for the first time since acquiring him from the Minnesota Timberwolves, but that wasn't enough to secure the win on the road as the Magic (7 - 8) used a huge comeback to secure the win following their Monday loss against the Washington Wizards. But in reality, this game shifted leads time and time against. Philadelphia jumped to a 30 - 27 lead in the first quarter, but Orlando came back and finished the first half up by one (53 - 52). Philly recovered control of the game with a 35 - 23 third quarter, but the Magic flipped the script in the fourth quarter and with a 35 - 19 lead in the final 12 minutes (including a 210 scoring run) and secured a huge win against one of the top contenders in the Eastern Conference. Nikola Vucevic led the way for the Magic with an impressive performance of 30 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Aaron Gordon had 17 points, six rebounds and six assists, while Wesley Iwundu contributed 11 points and two steals. Two bench players made a big impact, as Jonathon Simmons had 12 points and Terrence Ross added 15, including a decisive three - pointer with less than 10 seconds on the clock. J.J. Redick was the top scorer for the 76ers with 22 points, but he also added six assists and four rebounds. Joel Embiid had a triple - double since he contributed with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists. Wilson Chandler had 14 points, and debutant Jimmy Butler chipped in with 14 points in 33 minutes. Ben Simmons only had nine points, six assists and three rebounds.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 130 - 117, at Amway Center on Saturday. While Los Angeles held the lead for the first 15 minutes of this game, Orlando dominated from there. In fact, the Magic outscored the Lakers, 75 - 50 in the second and third quarters. In addition, Orlando held a double - digit lead for the final 20 minutes of this game. The Magic ended up shooting 54 percent from the field while holding the Lakers to 48 percent shooting. Augustin amassed 22 points and seven assists. Evan Fournier finished with 15 points, five rebounds and four assists. Jonathan Simmons was a huge spark off the bench, providing 12 points, five rebounds and six assists. The Orlando Magic defeated the New York Knicks, 131 - 117, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Magic (9 - 8) have shown a penchant for some prolific tallies on the scoreboard this season, and Sunday shaped up as a possible scenario for another big offensive night. That much was confirmed from the opening tip, as Orlando racked up 44 first - quarter points and held a 67 - 66 halftime lead on the Knicks (4 - 13). As their final point total implies, the home squad enjoyed a sharp shooting night, draining 57 percent of their attempts. The bench played a pivotal role for the Knicks, but it was Tim Hardaway, Jr. who led the way with 32 points. He added two rebounds, two assists and three steals. Jonathan Isaac delivered 16 points, four boards, three assists, two steals and one block. D.J. Augustin generated 12 points, seven assists and three rebounds. Terrance Ross poured in 10 points off the bench. The Knicks return home to take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday night, while the Magic remains home and tangles with the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday evening as well.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Orlando Magic, 93 - 91, at Amway Center on Tuesday. The Raptors (14 - 4) and the Magic (9 - 9) played a tight encounter on Tuesday, as this game was decided on a last - second bucket by Danny Green with only 0 seconds remaining after several back - and - forth buckets down the stretch. Toronto jumped ahead in the game with a 29 - 17 lead after the first quarter, but Orlando flipped the script in the subsequent two quarters: 20 - 18 in the second, and 38 - 26 in the third one. As such, the Magic entered the final 12 minutes of action with a two - point lead. But Toronto once again showed their ability to close games down, and ended winning after a 20 - 16 fourth quarter, and Green's jumper following an assist from Kyle Lowry. Serge Ibaka chipped in with 14 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Evan Fournier was the highest - scorer in the game since he finished with 27 points, four assists, and three rebounds. Aaron Gordon scored 16 points with nine rebounds and three blocks, and Nikola Vucevic posted a strong double - double of 14 points, 17 boards and four assists. No other player scored in double digits, but Jonathan Isaac (nine points, five boards) and Mo Bamba (seven points, five rebounds) contributed off the bench.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Orlando Magic, 124 - 118, at Amway Center on Wednesday evening. The Nuggets got out to a good start on the road, as they built a 22 - 10 lead early on, however the home team battled back to cut the deficit to just three points by the end of the quarter. The Magic continued their push early in the second, where they tied it up at 33. The second quarter was tight the whole way, as the Magic outscored the Nuggets, 26 - 25, in the quarter. The teams played to a standstill through the third, as they poured in 32 points each. The Magic trailed by two to start the fourth, but fought hard, swapping the lead back - and - forth with the Nuggets. The Magic trailed by three with just a few seconds left in regulation, when Terrence Ross hit a clutch three to send the game to overtime. Unfortunately for the home team, the Nuggets took control in overtime, where they outscored the Magic, 12 - 6, to earn their seventh straight win. Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 31 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 46 minutes. Paul Millsap came up big with 18 points, eight rebound and two assists, while Nikola Jokic tallied 12 points, 13 assists, eight point and one steal. The Nuggets shot 54 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 19 from long range. Meanwhile, Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 24 points, 15 rebounds and four assists, in 37 minutes. Evan Fournier tallied 26 points, eight rebounds, four assists and one block, while Aaron Gordon tallied 19 points, six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. The Magic shot 47 percent from the field, including 20 - of - 49 from long range. The Magic (12 - 13) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pacers on Friday. The Nuggets (17 - 7) take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Friday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Orlando Magic, 112 - 90, at Amway Center on Friday evening. Tyreke Evans poured in 11 points, while Myles Turner registered 10 points, six rebounds and one block. Nikola Vucevic paced the Magic with a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists. Aaron Gordon posted a 20 - point, 14 - rebound double - double and added four assists, one steal and one block. Terrence Ross mustered 11 points to lead the second unit. Evan Fournier finished with nine points. The Pacers head back home and face the Sacramento Kings on Saturday evening, while the Magic pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Monday night.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Chicago Bulls, 97 - 91, in Mexico City, at Mexico City Arena on Thursday evening. The Bulls took the lead early on, but the Magic were able to keep it close, as they trailed 26 - 24 at the end of the quarter. The Magic picked up the momentum in the second, and built a 10 - point lead by the halfway mark of the quarter. They held no to take a 51 - 46 lead at the half. The Magic grinded it out down the stretch, as they held a one - point lead for almost two minutes down the stretch, allowing them to come up clutch on the offensive end, thanks to a couple of timely buckets by Nikola Vucevic. Augustin followed up with 15 points, seven rebounds and two assists, while Evan Fournier and Jonathan Isaac added 10 points each. Justin Holiday followed up with 18 points, five rebounds, three steals and two assists, while Bobby Portis chipped in 15 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 21 minutes off the bench. The Bulls (6 - 23) will look to bounce back as they take on the Spurs in San Antonio on Saturday. The Magic (13 - 15) play host to the Jazz on Saturday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Utah Jazz, 96 - 89, in Mexico City on Saturday afternoon. The Magic (14 - 15) and Jazz (14 - 16) engaged in a tightly contested first half, with Utah holding a slim two - point halftime advantage. The San Ajntonio Spurs defeated the Orlando Magic, 129 - 90, at Amway Center on Wednesday evening. The Miami Heat defeated the host Orlando Magic, 115 - 91, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Heat got out to a great start on the road by outscoring the Magic by 11 in the first quarter. The Phoenix Suns defeated the Orlando Magic, 122 - 120, in overtime at Amway Center on Wednesday evening. Evan Fournier poured in 16 points and also netted five assists and four rebounds. Aaron Gordon compiled 11 points, nine rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. The Suns head back home to take on the OKC Thunder on Friday night, while the Magic remain home and tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Friday evening as well.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 116 - 87, at Amway Center on Friday. While Toronto came into this game as the favorite, Orlando looked like the far better team on this night. Fred VanVleet was the only other player in double figures, as he dropped 11 points. Pascal Siakam went just 1 - of - 8 from the field to provide four points and four rebounds. The Magic (15 - 19) got one of the best games of the season from Nikola Vucevic, as he collected 30 points, 20 rebounds and eight assists on 12 - of - 17 shooting. D.J. Augustin amassed 17 points and six assists. Aaron Gordon tallied nine points, nine rebounds and four assists while Terrence Ross led the bench with 14 points and four rebounds. The Orlando Magic defeated the Detroit Pistons, 109 - 107, at Amway Center on Sunday. The Magic (16 - 19) and the Pistons (16 - 18) engaged in quite a battle this Sunday, in the game that opened Sunday's slate in The Association, but Orlando's first - quarter lead in the initial first 12 minutes got the job done for them. Orlando jumped to a 10 - point lead in the first quarter and despite Detroit's efforts to crawl back into the game, the Magic never looked back. The remaining three quarter ended 38 - 31, 24 - 23 (both for Detroit) and 24 - 24. So Orlando won by a slim two - point margin, but it was more than enough. Nine out of 10 Orlando players scored in this game, but four starters scored over 10 points and three finished with 20 or more points. Derroit had a balanced offensive output with six players topping the 10 - point mark, although none had more than 16 points in total. Luke Kennard was the Pistons' top scorer with 16 points, while Reggie Bullock scored 15 points. Blake Griffin had 15 points too, but he added five assists and two boards. Andre Drummond had a strong double - double of 14 points and 15 boards. Reggie Jackson filled the stat sheet with 11 points, five rebounds and four assists

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 105 - 103, at Amway Center on Saturday. While Boston led by 10 points at the half, Orlando prevailed with a much - needed victory. In fact, they outscored the Celtics, 64 - 52, in the second half, as they held the lead for the final six minutes of action. Orlando's defense was key, as they held Boston to 42 percent from the field and 25 percent from three - point range. The Magic (18 - 24) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he collected 29 points, 12 rebounds and two assists. Nikola Vucevic finished with 16 points, 13 rebounds and five assists. Evan Fournier got out of his slump by generating 18 points, three rebounds and five assists. Terrence Ross was huge off the bench, providing 25 points, four rebounds and two assists. On deck for Orlando is a home matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Sunday. As for Boston, they return to action on Monday when they face the Brooklyn Nets on the road.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Houston Rockets, 116 - 109, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Magic (19 - 24) found themselves in an early hole against a surging Rockets (24 - 18) squad, falling behind by a 26 - 18 margin after 12 minutes. The light went on for Orlando at that point, however, as they chipped away over the middle periods by outscoring Houston, 68 - 62. Austin Rivers provided 25 points, two assists, one rebound and one steal. Clint Capela generated a 17 - point, 10 - rebound double - double and added three assists. Danuel House, Jr. tallied 14 points, two assists and one rebound. P.J. Tucker collected eight points, eight rebounds and two steals. Aaron Gordon and Nikola Vucevic co - led the Magic with 22 - point contributions. Gordon added eight rebounds, five assists and two steals, while Vucevic supplied nine boards, six assists and one steal. Evan Fournier poured in 19 points and also mustered five rebounds and two assists. Terrence Ross registered 17 points to lead the bench, supplementing them with four rebounds, two assists and one steal. D.J. Augustin checked in with a full line of nine points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. The Rockets head back home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night, while the Magic pay a visit to the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday evening.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Orlando Magic, 117 - 115, at Amway Center on Friday. Orlando looked well in control when they led by 21 points late in the second quarter but they collapsed in the second half. In fact, Brooklyn outscored Orlando, 63 - 48, in the second half. Three-point shooting was the difference, with the Nets hitting 19 - of - 46 and the Magic connecting on just 10 - of - 26. Brooklyn's bench was also huge, as they outscored Orlando's bench, 52 - 34. The Nets (24 - 23) got a spectacular performance from D'Angelo Russell, as he led all scorers with 40 points, two rebounds and seven assists on 16 - of - 25 from the field. Joe Harris totaled 11 points and four assists. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 20 points, two rebounds and two assists. Shabazz Napier also played well off the bench, providing 12 points, four rebounds and four assists, The Magic (19 - 26) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he tallied 23 points, four rebounds and five assists. D.J. Augustin amassed 17 points and four assists. Nikola Vucevic collected 16 points, 17 rebounds and six assists while Evan Fournier accumulated 16 points, eight rebounds, three assists and four steals. On deck for Orlando is a home matchup versus the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. As for Brooklyn, they play host to the Sacramento Kings on Monday for their next fixture.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Orlando Magic, 118 - 108, at Amway Center on Saturday evening. The Bucks got out to a great start on the road with a 33 - 24 lead after one quarter. They kept the upper hand through the second, where they outscored the Magic by four, to push their lead to 59 - 46 by halftime. The Magic came alive in the third quarter and managed to cut the deficit to five points, heading into the fourth. However, the Bucks managed to keep the upper hand and hung on for their fourth straight win. Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 30 points on 12 - of - 14 shooting, seven rebounds and two assists, in 30 minutes. Giannis Antetokounmpo followed up with 25 points, 13 rebounds, five assists and two steals, while Malcolm Brogdon tallied 18 points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Bucks shot 55 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 30 from long range. Meanwhile, Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 27 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks, in 29 minutes. Terrence Ross followed up with 16 points, two assists, two steals and one rebound, in 29 minutes off the bench, while D.J. Augustin tallied 14 points, seven assists and two rebounds. The Magic shot 47 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 32 from long range. The Magic (19 - 27) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hawks in Atlanta on Monday. The Bucks (33 - 12) play host to the Mavericks on Monday.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Orlando Magic, 95 - 91, at Amway Center on Friday night. The Wizards (21 - 27) looked to be firmly in control during a first half in which they forged a 50 - 38 advantage. However, the Magic (20 - 29) put up more of a fight in the second half, clawing all the way back to take a 91 - 89 lead with 1:37 remaining before allowing the visitors to finish the game on a 60 run. Bradley Beal paced the Wizards with 27 points, adding seven assists, six rebounds and two steals. Jeff Green supplied 24 points, six boards and three assists. Aaron Gordon generated a 22 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and one block. Terrance Ross poured in 16 points, adding six rebounds, four assists and one steal. Jonathan Isaac delivered eight points, eight rebounds and one assist. The Wizards remain on the road and tangle with the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday evening, while the Magic pay a visit to the Houston Rockets on Sunday night.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Orlando Magic, 126 - 117, at Amway Center on Tuesday evening. The Thunder (32 - 18) got an early message from the home - court Magic (20 - 31) that they'd be in a for a wire - to - wire battle, as Orlando jumped up to a 35 - 32 first - quarter lead. However, OKC bounced back in the second to forge a 69 - 63 edge by halftime. In a testament to the back - and - forth nature of the contest, the hosts would reclaim the advantage by a slim three - point margin heading into the fourth quarter before the visitors outscored them, 35 - 23, to claim the victory. The short - handed Thunder, which were down Steven Adams (ankle), were outrebounded, 53 - 43, but they drained 54 percent of their attempts while limiting the Magic to a 43 percent success rate. Paul George paced the Thunder with 37 points, adding six rebounds, four assists and three steals. Russell Westbrook followed with a 23 - point, 14 - rebound, 14 - assist triple - double that also included one block. Dennis Schroder generated 21 points, four assists, three rebounds and one block. Jerami Grant finished with 18 points, seven rebounds, one assist and three steals. Nerlens Noel drew the start for Adams and produced 12 points, seven boards, one assist, five blocks and one steal. Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 27 points and also hauled in 11 rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal. Evan Fournier posted 17 points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal. Aaron Gordon and Terrance Ross turned in matching 16 point tallies while hauling in nine and six rebounds, respectively. Jonathan Isaac and D.J. Augustin poured in 11 points apiece. Isaac notably brought down eight rebounds, while Augustin dished out five assists. The Thunder next visit the Miami Heat on Friday night, while the Magic remain home and tangle with the Indiana Pacers on Thursday evening.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 107 - 100, at Amway Center on Thursday. While Orlando led for the majority of this game, it took 10 ties to determine a winner. The fourth quarter really made the difference for the Magic, as they outscored the Pacers, 38 - 27. Three-point shooting was key, with the Magic connecting on 11 - of - 25 and the Pacers hitting just 4 - of - 19. Bench production was also huge, with Orlando winning that battle, 40 - 16. Rebounding was also decisive for the Magic, as they out - rebounded the Pacers, 48 - 42. The Pacers (33 - 18) were led by Myles Turner, as he amassed 27 points and seven rebounds. Bojan Bogdanovic tallied 21 points, four rebounds and two assists. Thaddeus Young finished with 16 points, 10 rebounds and four assists while Darren Collison accrued 16 points, four rebounds and 10 assists. No other Indiana player had more than five points. The Magic (21 - 31) starters were led by D.J. Augustin, as he totaled 20 points, three rebounds and two assists. Nikola Vucevic accumulated 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists. Jonathan Isaac collected 13 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and two blocks while Terrence Ross led the bench with 30 points, four rebounds and three steals. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Orlando playing host to the surging Brooklyn Nets and Indiana traveling to South Beach to face the Miami Heat.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Brooklyn Nets, 102 - 89, at Amway Center on Saturday. The recent form of these teams would indicate a Brooklyn victory but Orlando won this game in dominating fashion. A 34 - 22 third quarter really made the difference, as the Magic led by at least five points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Defense was key for Orlando, as they recorded 11 steals and seven blocks while Brooklyn picked up just six steals and two blocks. The Magic (22 - 31) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he collected 24 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Evan Fournier totaled 16 points, three rebounds and four assists. Jonathan Isaac accumulated 10 points, 12 rebounds, three steals and three blocks while D.J. Augustin finished with 12 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two steals. On deck for Brooklyn is a home matchup versus the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday. As for Orlando, they travel to face the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 112, at Amway Center on Thursday evening. The Magic (23 - 32) haven't had much reason to smile lately, and they'd also been particularly inept offensively at home this season. Both of those trends were eradicated for at least one night against the defensively challenged Timberwolves (25 - 29), which saw Orlando outscore them by a 70 - 54 margin over the second and third quarters to take a commanding lead into the final period. While Minnesota was able to play more competitively in the fourth quarter, they never got close enough to threaten. As the final score implies, the Magic were particularly successful shooting - wise, draining an impressive 54 percent of their attempts. Karl-Anthony Towns paced the Timberwolves with 27 points, adding 11 rebounds and five assists. Andrew Wiggins supplied 23 points, nine rebounds, three assists, three steals and two blocks. Dario Saric managed 17 points and eight boards. Josh Okogie and Isaiah Canaan generated matching 13 - point tallies while also posting four rebounds and six assists, respectively. Taj Gibson turned in 10 points, four rebounds and one steal. Terrence Ross led the Magic with 32 points in 31 minutes off the bench and also provided five rebounds and one assist. Nikola Vucevic registered 21 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Aaron Gordon compiled 19 points, six rebounds, five assists and one block. Jonathan Isaac contributed nine points, six rebounds, two assists, three blocks and two steals. The Timberwolves remain on the road and are right back in action versus the Pelicans on Friday night, while the Magic also travel and face the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday evening.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets,127 - 89, at Amway Center on Thursday. With Charlotte hosting the all - star game this weekend, it was clear they checked out before this finale. In fact, the Magic led 71 - 36 at the half, as the Hornets could never get the game within a 25 - point margin in the second half. The shooting disparity was embarrassing for Charlotte, as they shot 35 percent from the field and 13 percent from three - point range while Orlando connected on 52 percent from the field and 44 percent from long range. Ball movement played a huge factor in that, with the Magic out - assisting the Hornets, 32 - 18. Orlando also on the defensive rebounding battle, 42 - 32. The Hornets (27 - 30) were led by Malik Monk, as he provided 15 points, four rebounds and two assists off the bench. Jeremy Lamb led the starters with 14 points, four rebounds and two assists. Cody Zeller finished with 13 points, seven rebounds, three assists and two steals. Kemba Walker went just 4 - of - 20 from the field to total 10 points and three assists. The Magic (27 - 32) were led by Terrence Ross, as he provided 21 points and two assists off the bench. Nikola Vucevic led the starters with 17 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Jonathan Isaac amassed 16 points and six boards while Aaron Gordon accrued 10 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Evan Fournier tallied 12 points, three rebounds, six assists and two steals. Both teams return to action next Friday, with Charlotte playing host to the Washington Wizards and Orlando welcoming the Chicago Bulls to Amway Center.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Orlando Magic, 110 - 109, at Amway Center on Friday evening. The Bulls (15 - 44) came into the contest looking to build on the rare double - digit win that they'd notched in the last game prior to the All-Star break, but they were slightly overmatched in the first half by the even hotter Magic (27 - 33). Orlando had rattled off a 7 - 1 record in their last eight games prior to the week - long pause in the season, and they forged a slim 53 - 51 halftime advantage. However, Chicago erased that deficit and built up a seven - point lead entering the final period, giving them a strong opportunity for a rare road win. The hosts battled back in defense of home court and even held a one - point edge with just 2 seconds remaining, but an Aaron Gordon shooting foul against Lauri Markkanen allowed the latter to the opportunity to drain a pair of game - winning free throws. Markkanen led the way for the Bulls with 25 points, adding 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal. Zach LaVine followed with 22 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Robin Lopez supplied 18 points, six boards, one assist and three steals. Otto Porter, Jr. furnished 17 points, five boards, four assists, one steal and one block. Kris Dunn registered eight points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Evan Fournier paced the Magic with 22 points and complemented them with five assists and three rebounds. Nikola Vucevic generated a 19 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included seven assists, two steals and two blocks. Gordon produced 17 points, five rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Terrence Ross poured in 15 points and also hauled in seven rebounds and dished out one assist. D.J. Augustin contributed 14 points, five boards and five dimes. Isaiah Briscoe delivered 10 points, three assists and two rebounds. The Bulls head back home to take on the Boston Celtics on Saturday night, while the Magic hit the road and tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Sunday afternoon.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Golden State Warriors, 103 - 96, at Amway Center on Thursday evening. The Magic (29 - 34) caught a break of sorts when Kevin Durant was ruled out for rest earlier in the day, but they were still naturally facing an intimidating challenge in the defending champion Warriors (43 - 19). Orlando forged a 59 - 51 halftime lead, yet it would be tale of two quarters in the second half. Golden State came roaring out of intermission to wipe out their deficit and build a 10 - point lead going into the fourth quarter. However, Orlando was up to the task, turning the tables during the final period by outscoring the visitors, 33 - 15, to secure victory. While the Magic prevailed in the battle of the boards by a 53 - 47 margin, the fact they held the Warriors to 40 percent shooting may have been their most impressive accomplishment. Stephen Curry led the way for the Warriors in Durant's absence, posting 33 points and adding eight rebounds and six assists. DeMarcus Cousins and Klay Thompson generated matching 21 - point tallies, with Cousins notably hauling in 11 rebounds. Draymond Green contributed five points, six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Alfonzo McKinnie drew the start for Durant but mustered just four points, three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Aaron Gordon paced the Magic with 22 points, adding 15 rebounds, three assists and one block. Terrence Ross poured in 16 points and also supplied five assists, four rebounds and one steal. D.J. Augustin turned in 14 points, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Nikola Vucevic and Jonathan Isaac generated matching 12 - point tallies, with the former also hauling in 13 rebounds, dishing out six assists and recording three blocks. The Warriors next pay a visit to the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday night, while the Magic travel to meeting the Indiana Pacers on Saturday evening as well.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 111 - 106, at Amway Center on Friday. While the five - point final margin makes this game look close, Orlando led throughout. In fact, the Magic led by 10 points after the first quarter, by 15 at the half and by 19 heading into the fourth quarter. Dallas responded with a 33 - 19 fourth quarter but they were simply too far behind at that point to come back. Three-point shooting was the difference in the game, with the Magic connecting on 14 - of - 29 and the Mavericks hitting just 10 - of - 34. Rim protection was also key, with Orlando doubling up Dallas in blocks, 6 - 3. The Mavericks (27 - 38) were led by Luka Doncic, as he provided 24 points, eight rebounds and five assists. Jalen Brunson finished with 19 points, two rebounds and nine assists. Dwight Powell amassed 13 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals while Dirk Nowitzki led the bench with 15 points and five boards. The Magic (31 - 36) were led by Terrence Ross, as he provided 22 points, three rebounds and two assists off the bench. Nikola Vucevic accrued 20 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks. Aaron Gordon finished with 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and three blocks while Jonathan Isaac totaled 14 points and nine boards. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Orlando traveling to face the Memphis Grizzlies and Dallas playing host to James Harden and the Houston Rockets.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 120 - 91, at Amway Center on Thursday evening. The Magic (32 - 38) left little doubt about the eventual outcome with a dominant first half. After forging a 36 - 20 lead through the first 12 minutes. Orlando added another four points to their advantage in the second to give them a formidable 20 - point lead. Any hopes of a Cavaliers (17 - 52) comeback were dashed when the hosts extended their edge to 25 points entering the final period. The Magic leveraged strong rebounding and defense, winning the battle of the boards by a 50 - 43 margin while forcing 15 turnovers and holding Cleveland to 41 percent shooting. Collin Sexton led the way for the Cavaliers with 23 points, adding four rebounds, three assists and one block. Jordan Clarkson led the way with 15 points and supplemented them with four boards, two assists and one steal. Brandon Knight poured in 12 points, while Ante Zizic contributed 11 and also pulled down eight rebounds. Kevin Love generated 10 points, eight rebounds, one steal and one block across 24 minutes. Aaron Gordon paced the Magic with 21 points and complemented them with six rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. D.J. Augustin followed with 20 points, seven assists, three rebounds and two steals. Nikola Vucevic turned in a 19 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and two steals. Terrence Ross poured in 14 points and also totaled four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block. Khem Birch contributed a 13 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included one assist and two steals. The Cavaliers next pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday night, while the Magic remains home to face the Atlanta Hawks on Sunday evening.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 101 - 91, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Magic got out to a good start at home, as they got out to an early 11 - 4 lead, before taking a 28 - 25 advantage into the second. The Magic pushed their lead back to double digits early in the second and held on until they took a 56 - 46 lead into halftime. The Magic stayed strong in the third, as they held the lead for the whole quarter, however, the Hawks trimmed the deficit to seven by the start of the fourth. The Hawks kept fighting but could not make any progress, as the Magic held on for their second straight win. Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 27 points, 20 rebounds, three assists and three steals, in 34 minutes. Aaron Gordon followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal, while Wes Iwundu chipped in 14 points, seven rebounds, two blocks and one steal. The Magic shot 39 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 37 from long range. Meanwhile, Trae Young led the Hawks with 20 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 32 minutes. Dewayne Dedmon added 10 points, 14 rebounds, two assists and two steals, while John Collins chipped in 10 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one block. The Hawks shot 41 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 35 from deep. The Hawks (24 - 47) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Rockets on Tuesday. The Magic (33 - 38) play host to the Pelicans on Wednesday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 119 - 96, at Amway Center on Wednesday. It's rare to see a game essentially over at the half but that was the case here. In fact, Orlando led by 14 points after the first quarter, by 22 at the half and by 31 points heading into the fourth quarter. That's domination at its finest, as Orlando won this game in wire - to - wire fashion. The Magic's defense was the difference in the game, as they held the Pelicans to 37 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range while outrebounding them, 65 - 49. Orlando also out - blocked the Pelicans, 10 - 2. The Pelicans (31 - 43) were led by Stanley Johnson, as he provided 18 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals off the bench. Ian Clark tallied 17 points, five rebounds and four assists off the bench as well. Frank Jackson was the only starter in double figures, as he amassed 14 points, four rebounds and four assists. The Magic (34 - 38) were led by Evan Fournier, as he tallied 22 points, five rebounds and three assists. Aaron Gordon finished with 20 points, seven rebounds, six assists and two steals. Nikola Vucevic collected 15 points, 17 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Terrence Ross led the bench with 19 points and three boards. On deck for Orlando is a home matchup versus the Memphis Grizzles on Friday. As for New Orleans, they're off until Friday when they play host to the Houston Rockets.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies in overtime, 123 - 119, at Amway Center on Friday. While Memphis either tied or held the lead for the entirety of regulation, Orlando prevailed in overtime. In fact, the Magic rode a 29 - 15 fourth quarter to tie the game and then outscored the Grizzlies in overtime, 13 - 9. The overtime was extremely competitive, as there were seven lead changes before the Magic finished the game on a 6 - 1 run. Free-throw shooting was the difference in the game, with Orlando connecting on 21 - of - 27 and Memphis hitting just 10 - of - 21. The Grizzlies (29 - 43) were led by Tyler Dorsey, as he provided a career - high 29 point to go along with three rebounds and nine assists. Jonas Valanciunas also had a career game, as he tallied 23 points, 24 rebounds, three assists and four blocks. Justin Holiday amassed 22 points and four boards. Delon Wright accrued 12 points, seven rebounds and eight assists while Chandler Parsons led the bench with 17 points, five rebounds and three assists. The Magic (35 - 38) were led by Evan Fournier, as he accumulated 27 points, eight rebounds and six assists. Nikola Vucevic finished with 25 points, four rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks. D.J. Augustin generated 20 points, six rebounds and eight assists while Terrence Ross led the bench with 31 points on 8 - of - 12 from long range. Memphis will have to play again on Saturday, as they play host to the Minnesota Timberwolves. As for Orlando, they're off until Monday when they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 119 - 98, at Amway Center on Monday. While there were 10 ties and 23 lead changes in the first 30 minutes of this game. , Orlando dominated the second half. In fact, the Magic outscored the Sixers, 63 - 38, in the second half, holding a double - digit lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Turnovers were the difference in the game, with Orland winning that battle, 15 - 7. That allowed them to win the points off turnover differential, 23 - 12. The Magic also out - assisted the Sixers, 28 - 20 and won the fastbreak scoring differential, 17 - 4. The Sixers (47 - 27) were led by Joel Embiid, as he tallied 20 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Tobias Harris accrued 15 points, four rebounds and three assists. The Magic (36 - 38) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he tallied 28 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Evan Fournier accumulated 24 points, seven assists and two steals. Aaron Gordon totaled 12 points, eight rebounds, three assists and two steals. Michael Carter-Williams led the bench with 15 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Orlando has to play again on Tuesday, as they travel to face the Miami Heat. As for Philadelphia, they return to action on Thursday when they play host to the Brooklyn Nets.

The Orlando Magic defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 100, at Amway Center on Wednesday. The Magic (39 - 40) are on the verge of the playoff bubble and they had their backs against the wall entering this game against a Knicks (15 - 63) team that keeps both eyes on the Draft Lottery and just want the season to end. The first quarter ended with a 26 - 26 score, but the Magic would pull away in the second quarter and they'd never look back thanks to a 32 - 19 score. Even though the Knicks kept things close the rest of the way (29 - 27 win in the third and 26 - 29 loss in the fourth), they just couldn't bounce back and ended losing deservedly. Meanwhile, Orlando kept themselves alive for one more day on the playoff race. And that's all they could ask for at this stage. As it has been the trend during the entire season, Nikola Vucevic once again was Orlando's best player since he finished with 29 points, 13 rebounds and three assists. Evan Fournier chipped in with 19 points, while Aaron Gordon filled the stat sheet with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Terrence Ross delivered a strong performance off the bench since he scored 23 points while adding four rebounds and five assists in only 24 minutes. Only four Knicks scored in double digits although all of them were part of the starting lineup. Mario Hezonja led the way with 29 points, nine rebounds and five assists, while Kevin Knox chipped in with 21 points and four boards. Mitchell Robinson contributed 12 points, nine rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Emmanuel Mudiay had 13 points with 10 assists.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 149 - 113, at Amway Center on Friday evening. The Magic got out to a great start at home, with a 42 - 18 lead after one quarter. They kept their foot on the gas in the second, while the Hawks managed to scored 30 points in the quarter, the Magic outscored them by nine, to take a 33 - point into the halftime. The Hawks picked it up in the third but only managed to match the 32 points that the Magic scored in the quarter. The Magic stayed on top through the fourth and were able to cruise to their second straight win. Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 25 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 29 minutes. Evan Fournier tallied 25 points, four rebounds and one assist, while Terrence Ross added 25 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 27 minutes off the bench. The Magic shot 61 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 36 from deep. Meanwhile, Trae Young led the Hawks with 22 points, seven rebounds, six assists and three steals, in 27 minutes. John Collins added 20 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal, while DeAndre' Bembry tallied 14 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and three rebounds. The Hawks shot 44 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 39 from long range. The Hawks (29 - 51) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bucks in Milwaukee on Sunday. The Magic (40 - 40) take on the Celtics on Sunday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 140 - 136, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The tone for what would turn out to be a scoreboard - busting affair was set in the first quarter, with the two clubs combining for 83 points during the period. The Mavericks (1 - 1) tightened up enough on defense during the second period to erase an eight - point deficit and send the contest into intermission deadlocked at 69 - 69. Both teams essentially matched each other basket for basket in the third, and the Timberwolves (1 - 2) entered the final quarter with a slim two - point lead. However, Dallas saved their best for last, putting up a game - high 43 points in the fourth quarter. Dennis Smith, Jr. scored the final three points on free throws after Minnesota had gotten to within a point after a pair of Karl-Anthony Towns buckets from the charity stripe with 4 seconds left. Towns led the way for Minnesota with 31 points and added five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Derrick Rose followed with a bench - leading 28 points, a total he supplemented with five rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block. Jeff Teague just missed out on a double - double with 22 points, nine assists, two rebounds and one steal. Andrew Wiggins poured in 19 points and also supplied three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Taj Gibson's contributions included nine points and six boards, while first - round pick Josh Okogie pitched in six points, five boards, two assists and one steal while filling in for Jimmy Butler (rest). Dallas' first - rounder Luka Doncic made significantly more noise, leading the Mavericks with 26 points. He also posted six rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. DeAndre Jordan posted a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, five blocks and two steals. Dennis Smith, Jr., Wesley Matthews and Dwight Powell turned in a trio of 19 - point tallies, the latter doing so off the bench. J.J. Barea was productive off the second unit as well, pitching in a 12 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included a rebound and two steals. The Timberwolves head back home for a Monday night showdown with the Indiana Pacers, while the Mavericks remain home and face the Chicago Bulls on that same evening.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Chicago Bulls, 115 - 109, at American Airlines Center on Monday evening. The visiting Bulls (0 - 3) impressively jumped out to a 61 - 59 halftime lead, with some red - hot shooting from Zach LaVine helping lead the way. However, it was the Mavericks (2 - 1) which made a statement in the second half, keeping their new - look offense humming while buckling down on the other end of the floor to outscore the visitors by a 56 - 48 margin. Chicago was still markedly better shooting - wise, draining 51 percent of their attempts, including 56 percent from three - point range. However, Dallas countered with a 41 - 34 edge on the boards and by committing four fewer turnovers. LaVine tallied a game - high 34 points, which he supplemented with three rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Jabari Parker followed with a bench - leading 20 points and added three rebounds, an assist and a steal. Justin Holiday poured in 16 points, while Bobby Portis contributed 12 points, eight rebounds and two blocks in another start at power forward. Kris Dunn went for nine points, seven assists and four rebounds in his season debut. Wesley Matthews' 20 points paced the Mavericks. He added four assists, two rebounds and two steals. Luka Doncic provided 19 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal. DeAndre Jordan posted an 18 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included one block. The forward trio of Dorian Finney-Smith, Dwight Powell and Maxi Kleber all generated 12 - point contributions. Finney-Smith and Kleber also brought down four rebounds each, while Powell had four boards and four assists. The Bulls head back home to face the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday evening, while the Mavericks hit the road and take on the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday night as well.

The visiting Utah Jazz defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Sunday. Utah withstood a tough comeback effort from the Mavericks, re - establishing a strong lead in the third quarter after having given away an 11 - point advantage in the second. The Jazz went on an 18 - 6 run in the late third and early fourth quarters, rebuilding a lead after the Mavericks tied it at 73 - 73. Dallas cut the lead to as little as six in the fourth, but Utah was able to hold firm until the final buzzer. Rudy Gobert led the Jazz (4 - 3) with 23 points and 16 rebounds in the win. Six of Gobert's rebounds came on the offensive end, and he shot 9 - of - 13 from the field. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year also tallied two steals and three blocks on the defensive end. Sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell also made a big contribution, scoring 20 points on 10 - of - 19 shooting. Dallas (2 - 4) saw a similarly impressive night from its own All-Star center, DeAndre Jordan. Jordan flirted with a triple - double, as he scored 12 points, grabbed 19 rebounds, and dished out nine assists in the loss. Dennis Smith, Jr. led the team with 27 points and hit 3 - of - 4 three - point attempts on the night. As a whole, though, the Mavericks could not find their rhythm offensively. The team shot just 42 percent on the night. The Mavericks will travel to San Antonio to take on the Spurs on Monday, while the Jazz have three days of rest before taking on the Timberwolves in Minnesota on Wednesday.

The New York Knicks defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 118 - 106, at American Airlines Center on Friday evening. The Knicks (3 - 6) impressively came out of the gates strong, taking a 33 - 27 first - quarter lead. However, the Mavericks (2 - 7) were able to climb all the way back and carry a slim three - point lead into halftime. The light went on for New York at intermission, however, as they compiled 33 points while limiting their hosts to 18 in the third period. That proved enough to help carry them to victory, as did their 55 percent success rate from the field and 18 - 12 turnover advantage. Allonzo Trier paced the Knicks with 23 points in 24 minutes off the bench. Tim Hardaway, Jr. supplied 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal. Mitchell Robinson and Enes Kanter posted matching 13 - point tallies. Robinson added 10 rebounds, while Kanter hauled down five. Dewayne Dotson and Mario Hezonja each provided 11 points, with the former also supplying eight rebounds. Dennis Smith, Jr. led the Mavericks with 23 points and also posted two rebounds. Dorian Finney-Smith followed with a bench - leading 19 points and seven rebounds. He added two assists and two steals. Luka Doncic managed 18 points, nine rebounds, six assists and one steal. Harrison Barnes turned in 14 points, two assists and one rebound. The Knicks remain on the road and pay a visit to the Washington Wizards on Sunday evening, while the Mavericks remain home and also tangle with the Wizards in their next game, which unfolds Tuesday night.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 119 - 100, at American Airlines Center on Tuesday, In a battle between two struggling teams, Dallas prevailed with a dominating win. In fact, they led for all but one minute, as they held a double - digit lead for over half of this fixture. The Mavericks ended the game strong, finishing on a 20 - 7 run. Aside from a 29 - 17 third quarter in advantage of the Wizards, the Mavericks ended up outscoring them by 31 points in the other three quarters. Rebounding was the difference for Dallas, as they outrebounded Washington, 49 - 33. Three-point shooting was also key, with the Mavericks hitting 15 - of - 34 from long range and the Wizards connecting on just 11 - of - 35. Free-throw shooting was also critical, as Dallas connected on 26 - of - 27 while Washington hit just 15 - of - 20. The Wizards (2 - 8) were led by John Wall, as he tallied 24 points, four rebounds, 10 assists and three steals. Bradley Beal finished with 19 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Otto Porter Jr. accrued 19 points, six rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Dwight Howard amassed eight points and 11 boards. The Mavericks (3 - 7) were led by Luka Doncic, as he accumulated 23 points, six rebounds and three assists. Wesley Matthews totaled 22 points and two boards. Harrison Barnes had his best game of the year, generating 19 points, 14 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Dennis Smith Jr. finished with 19 points, four rebounds and seven assists. On deck for Dallas is road matchup versus the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. As for Washington, they're off until Friday when they travel to face the Orlando Magic.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 111 - 96, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks (4 - 8) haven't exactly enjoyed a smooth start to their season, but the little success they have had, they've found on their home floor. Dallas had secured all three of their wins at American Airlines Center, and Saturday, they were facing a short - handed Thunder (7 - 5) squad once again playing without Russell Westbrook (ankle). To their credit, OKC matched Dallas basket for basket in the first quarter, but the Mavs created space in the second period with some sharp shooting, leading to a 34 - point haul. That proved to be enough, as the home squad was able to keep pace with whatever the visitors threw at them in the second half. Dallas shined on both ends of the floor, shooting 56 percent from the floor (including 48 percent from three - point range) while limiting the Thunder to a 39 percent success rate. Paul George and Steven Adams co - led the Thunder with matching 20 - point, 13 - rebound double doubles. Dennis Schroder drew another start for Westbrook and posted 19 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Jerami Grant provided 13 points, two rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Luka Doncic paced the Mavericks with 22 points and added eight assists, six rebounds and one steal. J.J. Barea followed with 21 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal in 22 minutes off the bench. Harrison Barnes and Dorian Finney-Smith posted matching 11 - point tallies, while Dennis Smith, Jr. turned in 10 points, five assists, three rebounds, two steals and one block. The Thunder heads back home and takes on the Phoenix Suns on Monday night, while the Mavericks hit the road and tangle with the Chicago Bulls on Monday evening as well.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Utah Jazz, 118 - 68, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. The Jazz got out to a good start on the road, with a 15 - 10 lead halfway into the first quarter. However, the Mavericks rallied back to take a 30 - 24 lead into the second. The Jazz came back to start the second and tied the game at 34, just a couple minutes into the quarter, but the Mavericks turned it up a notch, once again, to build a 58 - 46 by halftime. The Mavs did not look back from there as they held the Jazz to just 22 points for the entire third and fourth quarter, while they poured in 60 points, to pull off the wild, 50 - point victory. This marks the third straight win for the Mavs, and the end of a three - game win streak for Jazz. Harrison Barnes led the Mavericks with 19 points on 6 - of - 11 shooting, four rebounds and two assists, in 26 minutes. Luka Doncic had a solid night, with 13 points, six rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block, in 25 minutes. DeAndre Jordan finished with four points, 10 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 22 minutes. The Mavericks shot 58 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Ricky Rubio was the high - point man for the Jazz, with 11 points, along with four steals, three rebounds and three assists, in 24 minutes. Donovan Mitchell tallied 10 points, three rebounds and three assists, while Rudy Gobert added 10 points, 10 rebounds, three steals and two assists, in 25 minutes. They shot 31 percent from the field, including a poor 6 - of - 35 from long range. The Jazz (7 - 7) will look to bounce back as they take on the 76ers in Philadelphia on Friday. The Mavericks (6 - 8) play host to the Warriors on Saturday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 112 - 109, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks got out to a solid start at home, with an early 12 - 6 lead, which they were able to evolve into a 26 - 22 lead after one quarter. The Warriors made a push to start the second and took the lead within the first four minutes. However, the Mavericks hung around and trailed by just two, 59 - 57, at halftime. The Warriors pulled ahead by six early in the third, but the Mavericks quickly closed the gap to just two again. Nonetheless, the Warriors kept pressing and took an 86 - 82 lead into the final frame. The Mavericks simply would not back down, as they stayed within reach through the fourth quarter, before they overtook the Warriors thanks to solid defense and some clutch play in the final minutes. This marks the fourth straight win for the Mavericks, and the fourth loss in the last six games for Golden State. Luka Doncic led the way for Dallas, with 24 points, nine rebounds and four assists, including a couple super clutch plays down the stretch. Harrison Barns had a solid outing, with 23 points, eight rebounds and one assist, in 36 minutes, while DeAndre Jordan tallied 13 points, 10 rebounds, one steal and one block. The Mavericks shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, the Warriors were without Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe). Kevin Durant led the way with 32 points, four rebounds, three assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Klay Thompson followed up with 22 points, four assists, three rebounds and two steals. The Warriors shot 45 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 33 from deep. The Warriors (12 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Spurs in San Antonio on Sunday. The Mavericks (7 - 8) take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Monday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 119 - 113, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. After a tightly contested first quarter, the Mavericks (8 - 9) built some cushion by outscoring the Nets (8 - 11) by a 27 - 18 margin during the second period. However, Brooklyn battled back in the third, and they entered the final 12 minutes with a 85 - 81 deficit. After multiple ties, Brooklyn was down just two points as late as the 4:3 mark of the fourth quarter before Dallas finished the game with a 16 - 12 run that was enough to hold off the visitors. Allen Crabbe returned to the starting lineup for the Nets and led the way with 27 points, a total he supplemented with three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Spencer Dinwiddie came off the bench to supply 19 points, seven assists, two rebounds and one steal. D'Angelo Russell and Ed Davis each pitched in 17 points. Joe Harris and Jarrett Allen had quiet games with eight and six points, respectively. Harrison Barnes paced the Mavericks with 28 points and added five rebounds and a steal. Luka Doncic produced 21 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. Devin Harris and J.J. Barea each delivered 18 points off the bench. DeAndre Jordan generated a 12 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two steals. Maxi Kleber totaled 11 points. The Nets head back home and face the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday afternoon, while the Mavericks take on the visiting Boston Celtics on Saturday evening.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Boston Celtics, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks (9 - 9) came into the contest having notched seven of their eight victories on the season on their home floor, and with two full days of rest since their most recent contest. In contrast, the Celtics (10 - 10) had lost in six of their 11 road tilts prior to Saturday, and were playing their fourth game in six nights. All of those trends surfaced as the game wore on, with Dallas holding an 87 - 82 lead by the end of three quarters. They then remained similarly ahead during the final 12 minutes, adding another four points to their advantage for the nine - point victory. Both teams were fairly even across the stat sheet, but the home squad benefited from a 40 - point effort from their bench. Jayson Tatum paced the Celtics with 21 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. Kyrie Irving delivered 19 points, six assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block. Marcus Smart matched Irving's scoring total off the bench and also contributed two rebounds, two assists and one steal. Jaylen Brown turned in 16 points and five boards, while Marcus Morris supplied 13 points. Harrison Barnes and J.J. Barea co - led the Mavericks with matching 20 - point efforts. Barnes added three rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, while Barea provided eight assists, three rebounds and two steals. Luka Doncic registered 15 points, eight assists, three steals and one block. Wesley Matthews matched Doncic's scoring total in his return from a hamstring injury. DeAndre Jordan managed a 14 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. The Celtics remain on the road and tangle with the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Mavericks make the short trip to take on the in - state rival Houston Rockets on Wednesday evening.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 111 - 102, at American Airlines Center on Tuesday evening. The Mavericks (12 - 10) came into the contest with an impressive track record on their home floor, having notched nine wins in 11 tries. They looked to make it 10 of 12 on Wednesday, and they made an immediate statement by taking a 34 - 20 first - quarter lead. The Trail Blazers (13 - 11) managed to claw back and get as close as 105 - 99 with 1:20 remaining following a Damian Lillard tip shot, but Dallas would finish the game on a 6 - 3 run to seal the victory. Lillard paced the Blazers with 33 points, a total he supplemented with eight rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block. C.J. McCollum poured in 18 points and also provided four assists, three rebounds and two steals. Evan Turner led the Portland bench with 13 points and also managed five rebounds, four assists and one block. Al-Farouq Aminu generated a 12 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one steal. Luka Doncic shook off the questionable designation he started the day with due to a hip injury and supplied 21 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Wesley Matthews netted 17 points, two assists, one rebound and one steal. DeAndre Jordan managed a 12 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Dennis Smith, Jr. matched Jordan's scoring total and also dished out nine assists. Harrison Barnes registered 11 points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. J.J. Barea and Devin Harris pitched in matching nine - point tallies. The Trail Blazers head back home to tangle with the Phoenix Suns on Thursday night, while the Mavericks pay a visit to the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 107 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Saturday. When Houston led 100 - 92 with four minutes remaining, it looked like the game was in hand but Dallas had other ideas. In fact, the Mavericks finished the game on a 15 - 4 run, as Luka Doncic scored 11 - straight points in that span to capture the win. It was a competitive game throughout, as there were 16 ties and 26 lead changes in total, with neither team attaining a double - digit lead. Rebounding was key for Dallas, as they out - rebounded Houston, 44 - 36. The Mavericks ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range while holding the Rockets to 45 percent from the field and 32 percent from long range. The Rockets (11 - 14) were led by James Harden, as he tallied 35 points, four rebounds and eight assists. Chris Paul finished with 23 points, two rebounds and eight assists. Clint Capela amassed 12 points and 13 boards. Eric Gordon led the bench with 12 points but no other player on the roster scored more than 10 points. The Mavericks (13 - 11) were led by Luka Doncic, as he collected 21 points, seven rebounds and three steals. Wesley Matthews matched those 21 points, adding three rebounds and three assists to his tally. DeAndre Jordan had a monster double - double, as he totaled 12 points, 20 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Dorian Finney-Smith, Harrison Barnes and Jalen Brunson scored 14 points apiece. On deck for Dallas is a home matchup versus the Orlando Magic on Monday. As for Houston, they play host to the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 101 - 76, at American Airlines Center on Monday. Dallas won this game in wire - to - wire fashion, as it wasn't close in the second half. In fact, the Mavericks won all four individual quarters, as they led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Dallas' defense was the difference, as they held Orlando to 36 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range. Getting to the free - throw line was huge as well, with the Mavericks connecting on 21 - of - 25 while the Magic hit just 4 - of - 5. Ball movement was also critical, with Dallas out - assisting Orlando, 28 - 18. The Mavericks did a ton of damage down low too, outscoring the Magic in the paint, 44 - 30. The Magic (12 - 15) had just two players reach double figures in scoring, as Jonathon Simmons led the team with 18 points and three rebounds. Aaron Gordon totaled 10 points, three rebounds and two assists. Nikola Vucevic finished with eight points, 16 rebounds, four assists and two steals. The Mavericks (14 - 11) were led by Harrison Barnes, as he accrued 19 points and five boards. Jalen Brunson started once again and provided 17 points, three rebounds and four assists. Wesley Matthews totaled 10 points, three rebounds and two assists. Luka Doncic fell just shy of a triple - double, as he accumulated seven points, 11 rebounds and nine assists. On deck for Dallas is a home matchup versus the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday. As for Orlando, they play host to the Chicago Bulls on Thursday for their next fixture.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 114 - 107, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. The Mavs got out to a good start, with an early 12 - 5 lead, and held the advantage through the first quarter. The Hawks cut the deficit to just one, but the Mavs answered to take a 28 - 26 lead into the second. The Hawks took the lead early in the second with a quick 6 - 2 run. The teams stayed within one possession of each other through the rest of the quarter, with the Hawks taking a 52 - 51 lead into halftime. The Hawks stayed strong to start the third, and led 63 - 57 with seven minutes to go. However, the Mavs closed the quarter strong and took a 81 - 78 lead into the final frame. The Mavs carried the momentum into the fourth, and pushed their lead to 10 in the first minutes. They did not let up, as they pushed to a 15 - point advantage with 3:23 left in the contest. However, the Hawks gave the home steam a scare, with an 11 - 1 run, to cut the deficit to just five points, with 40 seconds left. The Mavs were able to seal their third straight win with clutch free throw shooting down the stretch. Luka Doncic had a huge night for Dallas, with 24 points, 10 rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Harrison Barnes tallied 25 points, three rebounds and one steal, while DeAndre Jordan finished with 11 points, 11 rebounds and two assists. The Mavs shot 47 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Trae Young led the Hawks with 24 points, 10 assists and two steals, in 35 minutes. John Collins added 20 points, 17 rebounds, one assists and one block, while Kent Bazemore finished with 22 points, five rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Hawks (6 - 21) head to Boston to take on the Celtics on Friday. The Mavericks (15 - 11) take on the Suns in Phoenix on Thursday.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Dallas Mavericks, 120 - 113, at American Airlines Center on Sunday evening. The Kings got out to a good start on the road as they outscored the Mavs 34 - 31 through the first quarter. The Mavs kept it close through the second, where they matched the visitors with 27 points each in the quarter. The Kings held a 61 - 58 lead at halftime and carried the momentum into the second half, as they outscored the Mavs by seven in the third quarter to expand their lead to 10 by the start of the fourth. The home team did not give up and fought until the end, as they outscored the Kings by three in the quarter, but could not make up the difference in the end. De' Aaron Fox led the Kings with 28 points, three rebounds, four assists, three steals and one block, in 33 minutes. Buddy Hield tallied 28 points, four rebounds and two assists, while Nemanja Bjelica finished with 15 points and 10 rebounds, while Bogdan Bogdanovic added 15 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic led the Mavs with 28 points, nine assists, six rebounds and two steals, in 35 minutes. DeAndre Jordan finished with eight points, 23 rebounds and four blocks, while Harrison Barnes chipped in 15 points. The Mavericks shot 42 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 35 from long range. The Mavs (15 - 13) will look to avoid a third straight loss as they take on the Nuggets in Denver on Tuesday. The Kings (16 - 13) head to Minnesota to take on the Timberwolves on Monday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 122 - 119, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. The Mavs got out to a good start at home as they battled through a competitive first quarter to emerge with a 33 - 30 lead heading into the second. The contest stayed close through the second, as the Pelicans and Mavericks tallied 34 points each in the quarter, resulting in a three - point lead for the home team at halftime. The Pelicans came out strong in the third and managed to turn the tables by outscoring the Mavericks by seven in the quarter to take a 94 - 90 lead heading into the final frame. However, the Mavericks chipped away through the fourth and managed to tie the game at 105 with six minutes left in the game. The two teams treaded buckets down the stretch and the score was tied at 119 with 30 seconds left. The Mavericks were able to capitalize as Luka Doncic hit three out of four free throws in the final seconds to secure their 14th home win of the season. Doncic led the Mavs with 21 points, 10 assists, nine rebounds and one steal, in 31 minutes. DeAndre Jordan followed up with 20 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and one block, while J.J. Barea added 18 points, seven assists, five rebounds and one steal. The Mavs shot 48 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 35 from long range. Meanwhile, Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 32 points, 18 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Jrue Holiday followed up with 25 points, six assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block, while Julius Randle chipped in 23 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. The Pelicans (15 - 20) will look to avoid a sixth straight loss as they play host to the Mavs on Friday. The Mavericks (16 - 17) next contest will be Friday in New Orleans.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 105 - 103, at American Airlines Center on Sunday. In a battle between Western Conference rivals, this game wasn't decided until the final seconds. Dallas made the run that mattered most though, as they finished the game on a 10 - 2 spurt to turn a six - point deficit into a two - point victory. There were 11 ties and 18 lead changes though, as neither club led by more than 11 points. Three-point shooting was the difference, with Dallas connecting on 14 - of - 39 and Oklahoma City hitting just 9 - of - 38. Rebounding was also critical, with the Mavericks outrebounding the Thunder, 49 - 39. The 13 steals recorded by Oklahoma City was the only thing keeping it close, as they won the turnover differential, 23 - 11. The Thunder (22 - 13) were led by Paul George, as he accrued 36 points, five rebounds and two steals. Russell Westbrook went just 4 - of - 22 from the field but still finished with nine points, nine rebounds, eight assists and six steals. Steven Adams accumulated eight points, nine rebounds, two assists and two steals while Dennis Schroder led the bench with 19 points, four rebounds and three assists. The Mavericks (17 - 18) were led by Luke Doncic, as he tallied 25 points, three rebounds and seven assists. Harrison Barnes totaled 16 points, six rebounds and two steals. Dennis Smith Jr. finished with 14 points and four rebounds while DeAndre Jordan collected 12 points, 17 rebounds, two steals and two blocks. J.J. Barea provided 10 assists off the bench to lead the team. These teams next game will actually be a rematch on Monday, although that game will be played in Oklahoma City.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Dallas Mavericks, 107 - 97, at American Airlines Center on Monday evening. The home team got out to a strong start, with a 33 - 25 lead after one quarter. The Mavs kept the momentum through the second and pushed their lead to 67 - 54 by halftime. However, the Lakers turned up the defense in the second half and outscored the Mavericks 32 - 13 in the third quarter, to take an 86 - 80 lead by the start of the fourth. The Lakers kept the upper hand in the fourth, as they pushed to a 14 - point lead minutes into the quarter and held on for the much - needed win. Brandon Ingram led the Lakers with 29 points on 12 - of - 21 shooting, six assists, three rebounds and two steals, in 37 minutes. Lonzo Ball followed up with 21 points, seven rebounds, five assists and two steals, while Josh Hart tallied 14 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and five steals. The Lakers shot 44 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic led the Mavs with 27 points, eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Harrison Barnes, Dennis Smith Jr. and J.J. Barea added 11 points each, while DeAndre Jordan tallied 10 points, 19 rebounds, three blocks and two steals. The Mavs shot 42 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 30 from long range. The Mavericks (18 - 22) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Suns on Wednesday. The Lakers (22 - 19) play host to the Pistons on Wednesday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 104 - 94, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday. Dallas came into this game as a sizable favorite and this final scoreline shows just why. The Mavericks did most of their damage in the third quarter, outscoring the Suns, 32 - 19. That allowed Dallas to lead by at least five points for the entirety of the fourth quarter, despite the fact that Phoenix led for the majority of the first half. Free-throw shooting was the difference in the game, with the Mavericks connecting on 32 - of - 45 while the Suns hit just 15 - of - 21. Three-point shooting was also big, with Dallas hitting 12 - of - 34 and the Suns connecting on just 7 - of - 25. Dallas' starters really put it to Phoenix's starters, outscoring them, 85 - 53. The Suns (10 - 33) were led by T.J. Warren, as he amassed 20 points and seven boards. Josh Jackson was their best player, as he collected 17 points, six rebounds, three assists and three steals. Richaun Holmes led the bench with 16 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Kelly Oubre Jr. and Elie Okobo both reached double figures in scoring off the bench as well. The Mavericks (19 - 22) got another spectacular performance from Luka Doncic, as he tallied 30 points, six rebounds, five assists and three steals. Harrison Barnes accumulated 17 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Wesley Matthews provided 14 points, two rebounds and five assists. On deck for Dallas is a road matchup versus the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday. As for Phoenix, they play host to the Denver Nuggets on Saturday for their next fixture.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 119 - 114, at American Airlines Center on Sunday night. The Warriors (29 - 14) knew they were in for an uphill battle against a home - dominant squad in the Mavericks (20 - 23), which had notched 16 of their 20 wins coming in at American Airlines Center. Accordingly, the defending champs found themselves down by four coming out of the first quarter, but they'd forged a 62 - 54 lead by halftime. However, this was a game that wouldn't be decided until the final minute, with Golden State coming back from a five - point deficit with 3:51 remaining to finish the contest on an 11 - 1 run. Stephen Curry was key to both the comeback and the victory overall, as he tallied a game - high 48 points, including the last seven. Curry added six rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal to his aforementioned scoring haul. Kevin Durant provided 28 points, seven boards, five assists, two blocks and one steal. Klay Thompson mustered 16 points, four rebounds and one assist. Alfonzo McKinnie offered 10 points and five rebounds. Draymond Green mustered just four points but added seven assists, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Luka Doncic led the Mavericks with 26 points and supplemented them with six boards, five assists and one steal. Harrison Barnes supplied 22 points and four rebounds. Deandre Jordan generated a 13 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists. Jalen Brunson managed 12 points, four rebounds, one assist and one block. Wesley Matthews couldn't help make up for the absence of Dennis Smith, Jr. (back), managing just eight points on 3 - for - 11 shooting. The Warriors remain on the road and next visit the Denver Nuggets on Tuesday evening, while the Mavericks remain home to take on the San Antonio Spurs on Wednesday night.

Reggie Jackson finished with 21 points, four rebounds and two assists. Stanley Johnson accrued six points, 12 rebounds and two assists. Ed Davis also played well off the bench, amassing 10 points and 10 boards. Joe Harris led the starters with 23 points and five boards. Caris LeVert accumulated 19 points, six rebounds and six assists. On deck for Brooklyn is a home matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Friday. As for Detroit, they travel to play the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday for their next outing.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 119 - 111, at Barclay's Center on Friday. Despite the fact that Brooklyn led by 14 points at times in the second quarter, Houston was able to prevail thanks to a big second half. In fact, tje Rockets rode a 35 - 25 third quarter to victory, as they held the lead for the final 20 minutes of action. Getting to the free - throw line was the difference for Houston, as they hit 22 - of - 32 from the charity stripe while Brooklyn connected on just 12 - od - 20. Rim protection was also critical, with the Rockets recording 10 blocks and the Nets picking up just four. The Rockets (2 - 5) got a vintage performance out of Chris Paul, as he tallied 32 points, seven rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and two blocks.
