Joe Harris went 7 - of - 9 from the field to total 18 points, two rebounds and four assists. D'Angelo Russell collected 12 points, three rebounds and three assists. Houston will play the second half of a back - to - back set on Saturday, as they travel to face the Chicago Bulls. As for Brooklyn, they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday for their next fixture.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 122 - 97, at Barclay's Center on Sunday. Philly came into this game winless on the road this season and Brooklyn continued that ugly trend here. Despite the fact that the Sixers led after the opening quarter, the Nets outscored them by 28 points across the final three quarters. Prior to that, there were 11 ties and 17 lead changes in the first half, as Brooklyn led by at least 14 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The assist - to - turnover differential was a glaring difference, with Brooklyn recording 27 assists to nine turnovers while Philly committed 27 turnovers to just 16 assists. The Sixers (6 - 5) were led by Ben Simmons, as he tallied 20 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. Joel Embiid took just eight shots but finished with 16 points, 15 rebounds and four assists. Dario Saric amassed 14 points and three boards. J.J. Redick led the bench with 15 points and two assists. The Nets (4 - 6) highest scorers both had 21 points, as D'Angelo Russell led the starters with 21 points, two rebounds and six assists. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson led the bench with 21 points, six rebounds and three assists. Caris LeVert collected 20 points, five rebounds, two assists and four steals. Jarrett Allen accrued 15 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks. Spencer Dinwiddie also played well off the bench, providing 12 points and eight assists. On deck for Brooklyn is a road matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Tuesday. As for Philadelphia, they travel to play the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Miami Heat defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 120 - 107, at Barclays Center on Wednesday evening. The Heat (6 - 8) came into the contest reeling and looking to address some uncharacteristic defensive deficiencies that had seen them give up 110 points or more in four of the prior five games. Miami got off to an excellent start in that regard, limiting the Nets (6 - 9) to 21 points while collecting 37 of their own. The lead remained 61 - 49 at the half, and the visitors were able to expand it to a full 18 points entering the final 12 minutes. That allowed them to withstand Brooklyn's best quarter, as they tallied 35 points in the fourth. Miami leveraged six double - digit scoring efforts and 54 percent shooting to secure victory. Tyler Johnson paced the Heat off the bench with 24 points and supplemented them with five rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Goran Dragic supplied 21 points, four assists and three rebounds. Hassan Whiteside posted a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two steals and two blocks. Bam Adebayo had 12 points in just 10 minutes, while Rodney McGruder matched his scoring total while posting four rebounds and three assists. Justise Winslow mustered six points but also hauled in 11 rebounds and dished out three assists. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 18 points and also managed five assists, three rebounds and one steal. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson contributed 14 points and nine rebounds, while Shabazz Napier tallied 13 points, meaning bench players served as Brooklyn's top trio of scorers. D'Angelo Russell shot just 6 - for - 18 on his way to 12 points. Joe Harris pitched in 11 points, five rebounds and three assists, while Jared Dudley generated 10 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. The Heat remain on the road and next visit the Indiana Pacers on Friday night, while the Nets visit the Washington Wizards that same evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 127 - 119, at Barclays Center on Saturday evening. The Nets got out to a good start at home, as they kicked things off with an 11 - 4 lead. The Clippers pushed back, but the Nets held on to take a, 37 - 32, lead into the second quarter. The Nets stepped it up with a 14 - 4 run to start the quarter, and once again held off the Clippers, who continued to chip away. The Nets led 67 - 60 at halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third and matched each other bucket for bucket, until the score was settled at 97 - 90, with the Nets' advantage heading into the final frame. The tides turned in the fourth quarter, as the Clippers hit a quick 70 run to tie it up. The game was tied at 110, with 4:36 to go, when the Clippers mounted a 9 - 2 run, to take a seven - point advantage with 2:13 remaining. The Clippers held on to earn their fourth straight win. Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 28 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting, in 32 minutes. Tobias Harris followed up with 27 points, eight rebounds and three assists, while Montrezl Harrell added 16 points, 10 rebounds, one assist and a block, in 27 minutes off the bench. The Clippers shot 51 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 23 from long range. Meanwhile, Jarrett Allen led the Nets with 24 points, 11 rebounds, two assists and a block, in 28 minutes. D'Angelo Russell followed up with 23 points, 10 assists, three rebounds, two steals and a block, while Joe Harris tallied 19 points, four rebounds, an assist and a steal. The Nets shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 28 from long range. The Nets (7 - 10) will look to bounce back as they take on the Heat in Miami on Tuesday. The Clippers (10 - 5) head to Atlanta to take on the Hawks on Monday.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 112 - 102, at Barclay's Center on Friday. While there were four ties and five lead changes in the first half, Minnesota dominated from there. In fact, they led by at least four points for the final 20 minutes of action. They did most of their damage in the second and third quarters, outscoring Brooklyn, 67 - 46. The Timberwolves defense was critical, as they held the Nets to 42 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. The Timberwolves (8 - 11) best player came off the bench, as Derrick Rose provided 25 points, two rebounds and three assists on 11 - of - 17 from the field. Karl-Anthony Towns led the starters with 21 points and nine boards. Taj Gibson amassed 16 points, 11 rebounds and three assists while Jeff Teague tallied 15 points, two rebounds and nine assists. The Nets (8 - 12) were led by Joe Harris, as he collected 18 points, six rebounds and four assists. , Jarrett Allen totaled 12 points and four boards. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 18 points, three rebounds and eight assists. DeMarre Carroll also played well off the bench, generating 13 points, seven rebounds and two assists. On deck for Minnesota is a home matchup versus the Chicago Bulls on Saturday. As for Brooklyn, they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 127 - 125, at Barclay's Center on Sunday. While Brooklyn held the lead for over 45 minutes of this game, Philly recaptured the lead when it mattered most. In fact, the Sixers finished the game on a 22 - 7 run, as they capped off their win with Jimmy Butler dagger. Butler hit a step - back three - pointer with 0 seconds left to turn a one - point deficit into a two - point victory. Brooklyn dominated offensively though, as they connected on 57 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range. The nine steals recorded by Philly was huge, as Brooklyn recorded just two on their end. The Sixers (14 - 8) not only got a game - winner from Jimmy Butler, but he also provided 34 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and four steals. Joel Embiid finished with 32 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and two blocks. J.J. Redick amassed 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. Ben Simmons accrued 13 points, five rebounds, nine assists, three steals and two blocks. Landry Shamet led the bench with 16 points. The Nets (8 - 13) got a spectacular performance from D'Angelo Russell, as he tallied 38 points, eight rebounds and eight assists on 16 - of - 28 shooting. Jarrett Allen totaled 17 points and 10 boards. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson finished with 13 points and six boards. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 31 points, three rebounds and five assists on 11 - of - 15 from the field. Both these teams return to action on Wednesday, with Brooklyn playing host to the Utah Jazz and Philly welcoming the New York Knicks to Wells Fargo Center.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 101 - 91, at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. The Jazz (10 - 12) came into the contest looking for any type of reprieve from a forgettable stretch where they'd dropped six of eight games. Despite their unsightly record, the Nets (8 - 14) had played several quality teams tough already this season, so it promised to be an uphill battle for Utah. Sure enough, the two clubs essentially matched each other basket for basket in the first half, and the visitors entered the halftime locker room with a slim 43 - 42 advantage. They saw that get erased and then some during the third period, which put the Jazz at a 78 - 70 deficit entering the final 12 minutes. However, they locked up the much - needed road victory with a dominant 31 - 13 advantage during the fourth quarter, capping off a strong defensive effort in which they limited Brooklyn to 35 percent shooting. Donovan Mitchell led the way for the Jazz with 29 points and supplemented the total with five rebounds, one assist and four steals. Rudy Gobert took advantage of one of the most appealing matchups for centers in the NBA by generating a 23 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, four blocks and one steal. Royce O'Neal moved back to the bench with Mitchell back in action and led the reserves with 13 points and four rebounds. Raul Neto poured in 11 points, while Derrick Favors mustered nine points and 10 rebounds. Ricky Rubio notably went 0 - for - 9 from the field on his way to a six - point tally. Spencer Dinwiddie paced the Nets with 18 points in 22 minutes off the bench, adding three rebounds and two blocks. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, Jarrett Allen and D'Angelo Russell all contributed 14 - point efforts. Hollis-Jefferson and Allen made theirs double - doubles with 11 and 10 rebounds, respectively. Shabazz Napier pitched in 10 points in 16 minutes off the bench. The Jazz next pay a visit to the Charlotte Hornets on Friday night, while the Nets remain home to tangle with the Memphis Grizzlies on that same evening.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Brooklyn Nets in double overtime, 131 - 125, at Barclays Center on Friday night. The Grizzlies (13 - 8) and Nets (8 - 15) engaged in an epic battle, one that didn't seem headed toward the eventual final score through three quarters. Memphis held a modest 85 - 80 lead heading into the final 12 minutes, but they needed a Jaren Jackson three - pointer with 16 seconds left in regulation to knot the game at 111 - 111 and send it into overtime. The first extra period ended in a 117 - 117 deadlock thanks to Mike Conley's 10 - foot driving floating jump shot with 10 seconds remaining. Memphis finally pulled away in the second overtime by scoring the last seven points over the final 2:32, six which came from Conley. Conley led the way for the Grizzlies with a career - high 37 points, a total he supplemented with 10 assists, five rebounds and one block. Jackson registered 36 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Marc Gasol contributed a 15 - point, 15 - rebound double - double. Garrett Temple tallied 13 points. JaMychal Green pitched in 11 points and four rebounds off the bench. D'Angelo Russell paced the Nets with 26 points and added eight assists, one rebound, three steals and one block. DeMarre Carroll led the bench with 21 points and also posted 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal in 39 minutes off the bench. Jarrett Allen generated a 15 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, one steal and one block.Spencer Dinwiddie and Rondae Hollis-Jefferson had matching 15 - point tallies as well. The Grizzlies remain on the road and pay a visit to the 76ers on Sunday evening, while the Nets travel to the Nation's Capital and face the Wizards on Saturday night.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 99 - 97, at Barclays Center on Monday evening. The contest got out to a very competitive start with multiple lead changes. The Nets used a 9 - 1 run to create some separation mid way though the quarter, however, the Cavaliers battled back to take a one - point, 30 - 29, lead to start the second. The Cavs carried the momentum, as they stayed one step ahead through the entire quarter, and pushed their lead to 56 - 50 by halftime. The Cavs came out strong in the second half and pushed their lead to 10, within the first couple of minutes. Nonetheless, the Nets kept fighting and cut the deficit to four, 80 - 76, entering the fourth. The Cavs pulled ahead to start the quarter, and held a decent cushion until about the three - minute mark, when the Nets began creeping back. The Nets managed to tie it up at 97, with 18 seconds on the clock. However, the Cavs' newest addition, Alec Burks stepped up in the clutch and threw - down a game - winning dunk. Jordan Clarkson led the Cavaliers with 20 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 28 minutes off the bench. Tristan Thompson followed up with 19 points, 14 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, while Collin Sexton tallied 15 points on 7 - of - 16 shooting. Alec Burks added 13 points seven rebounds and one assists, in 28 minutes off the bench. Meanwhile, D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 30 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, in 32 minutes. Spencer Dinwiddie followed up with 18 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal, while Shabazz Napier chipped in 10 points, four rebounds and two assists off the bench. The Nets (8 - 17) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Thunder on Wednesday. The Cavs (5 - 18) play host to the Warriors on Wednesday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 114 - 112, at Barclays Center on Wednesday. Things were looking bleak for the visiting Thunder (16 - 7), as they fell behind in the first half and faced an 18 - point deficit heading into the final quarter. Then, Paul George decided it was time to take over. The All-Star forward scored 24 points in the fourth quarter, including the Thunder's final seven points and a game - winning three - pointer with 3 seconds left on the clock. In the end, George finished with a game - high 47 points (15 - 27 FG, 6 - 13 3Pt), 15 rebounds and four assists across 37 minutes. As a team, it was a poor shooting night in all facets of the game, as Oklahoma City shot 34 percent from three, 43 percent from the field overall and just 58 percent from the free throw line. Fortunately, George came through to save the day over the final eight minutes. The Thunder's next highest scorer was Russell Westbrook, who didn't score a single point in the fourth quarter but finished with 21 points, 15 rebounds and 17 assists in 40 minutes. As for the Nets (8 - 18), they were on cruise control for 36 minutes Wednesday and looked to be well on their way to putting an end to their seven - game losing streak. However, just 19 points in the fourth quarter and failing to score in the final two and half minutes was not enough to get the job done. As a team, Brooklyn shot a fairly impressive 15 - of - 36 (42 percent) from behind the arc, but shot just 43 percent from the field overall. Allen Crabbe led the way with a team - high 22 points on 7 - of - 13 shooting from behind the arc, while Joe Harris added 19 points of his own. Point guards D'Angelo Russell and Spencer Dinwiddie each dropped 17 points but combined for just six assists.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors in overtime, 106 - 105, at Barclay's Center on Friday. While Brooklyn led for the majority of the first half, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. The second half was extremely competitive, as there were 10 ties and 12 lead changes, with neither club leading by more than five points. Brooklyn played some stifling defense at the end of overtime, as they held Toronto scoreless for the final 100 seconds, forcing them to miss their final four shots. Rebounding was the difference for the Nets, as they outrebounded the Raptors, 60 - 41. Brooklyn also played well defensively throughout, holding Toronto to 39 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. The Raptors (21 - 6) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he collected 32 points, three rebounds, four assists and four steals. Jonas Valanciunas finished with 24 points and eight boards. Pascal Siakam finished with 16 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Kyle Lowry went just 1 - of - 8 from the field but still led the team with 11 assists. The Nets (9 - 18) got a gem from D'Angelo Russell, as he tallied 29 points, five rebounds and five assists. Spencer Dinwiddie was huge off the bench, providing 17 points, two rebounds and eight assists. Jarrett Allen amassed 12 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks while Rondae Hollis-Jefferson totaled 11 points, four rebounds and two assists. Ed Davis scored just one point but provided 15 rebounds off the bench to lead the team. On deck for Brooklyn is a road matchup versus the New York Knicks on Saturday. As for Toronto, they return to action on Sunday, when they host the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 125 - 118, at Barclay's Center on Friday. In a battle between two struggling teams, Brooklyn prevailed with a victory. The second quarter really set the tone, with Brooklyn outscoring Washington, 43 - 28. That allowed the Wizards to lead for the entirety of the second half. Free-throw shooting was the difference in the game, with the Nets connecting on 26 - of - 31 and the Wizards hitting just 9 - of - 16. Rebounding was also critical, with Washington outrebounding Brooklyn, 46 - 25. Both offenses were on point, with both clubs hitting over 50 percent of their shots. The Wizards (11 - 18) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 31 points and nine assists. John Wall totaled 17 points and 13 assists. Markieff Morris led the bench with 15 points, three rebounds and two assists. Austin Rivers played his final game as a Wizard and provided 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. The Nets (12 - 18) just signed Spencer Dinwiddie to an extension yesterday and he rewarded his organization by leading the team with 27 points, four rebounds and six assists off the bench. Joe Harris led the starters with 19 points, two rebounds and six assists. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson accrued 15 points, nine rebounds and six assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Brooklyn welcoming the Atlanta Hawks to The Big Apple and Washington playing host to the Los Angeles Lakers.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 144 - 127, at Barclays Center on Sunday afternoon. The Nets (13 - 18) entered this game on the heels of a four - game winning streak, and managed to extend that positive run against a Hawks (6 - 23) squad that looked overmatched from start to finish. Brooklyn jumped to a 19 - point lead after the first quarter (42 - 23) and they never looked back in this one. Atlanta tried to turn things around and reduced the deficit to six points after a 43 - 30 second quarter. It seemed as if Atlanta were set to continue their push in the second half, but the Nets won the next two quarters (39 - 30 and 33 - 31, respectively) and secured a comfortable win by a 17 - point margin. Now Brooklyn have won their last five in a row, while Atlanta have now lost seven of their past eight. D'Angelo Russell was the star of the game for the Nets since he finished with 32 points, seven assists, six rebounds and two steals in only 29 minutes of action. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson filled the stat sheet as well thanks to 18 points, four boards, three assists and two steals, while Jeff Harris added 16 points with six assists. Jarrett Allen and Rodions Kurucs had 11 points, while Jared Dudley (16 points), DeMarre Carroll (15 points) and Spencer Dinwiddie (15 points, five assists) all reached double - digit scoring off the bench. Jared Collins was the best player for the Hawks since he finished with 29 points and eight rebounds. Trae Young had a double - double with 13 points and 10 assists, while Dewayne Dedmon also had one thanks to his 24 points and 12 rebounds, as well as three assists and one block. Kent Bazemore delivered 20 points and seven assists.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 110, at Barclays Center on Tuesday evening. The Nets (14 - 18) started the game off with in the same impressive form that had netted them a five - game winning streak coming in. Brooklyn jumped out to a 62 - 57 halftime lead over the Lakers (18 - 13), and they didn't let up after intermission. The home squad matched Los Angeles basket for basket in the second half, holding off the visitors after they got as close as 113 - 110 with 17 seconds remaining. The shooting was impressive for both clubs, but the Nets were just a bit better with a 48 percent success rate overall, including 41 percent from three - point range. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 36 points, supplementing them with 13 rebounds, eight assists, one block and one steal. Lonzo Ball turned in 23 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Kyle Kuzma posted a 22 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Josh Hart and Tyson Chandler both started but provided just six and five points, respectively. D'Angelo Russell paced the Nets against his former squad, totaling 22 points, 13 assists, four rebounds and one block. Joe Harris supplied 19 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Spencer Dinwiddie registered 18 points, six assists and one rebound. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson turned in 17 points and added eight rebounds, three assists and one steal. Jared Dudley and DeMarre Carroll generated matching 13 - point tallies and hauled in five and three rebounds, respectively. The Lakers remain on the road and tangle with the Pelicans on Friday night, while the Nets are right back in action Wednesday night on the road against the Chicago Bulls.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 114 - 106, at Barclay's Center on Friday. There were some major swings in this game, as it took seven ties and seven lead changes to determine a winner. In fact, Brooklyn overcame a 15 - point second quarter deficit to lead late in the fourth quarter but Indiana finished the game on a 14 - 3 run to prevail with a victory. The Pacers offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 54 percent from the field and 42 percent from three - point range while holding the Nets to 46 percent shooting. Indiana's defense was also huge, as they recorded 10 steals and eight blocks while winning the turnover differential, 20 - 11. In addition, the Pacers outscored the Nets, 48 - 32, in paint points. The Pacers (21 - 12) were led by Victor Oladipo, as he tallied 26 points, nine rebounds, six assists and two steals. Thaddeus Young totaled 21 points, two steals and two blocks. Bojan Bogdanovic accrued 17 points, two rebounds and four assists while Myles Turner finished with 15 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and five blocks. The Nets (15 - 19) were led by Rodions Kurucs, as he totaled 24 points and three rebounds. Joe Harris finished with 13 points, four rebounds and two assists. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson generated 13 points, five rebounds and two assists. Spencer Dinwiddie provided 15 points and nine assists off the bench. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Indiana playing host to the Washington Wizards and Brooklyn welcoming the Phoenix Suns to Barclay's Center.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 111 - 103, at Barclays Center on Sunday evening. The Nets (16 - 19) came into Sunday's contest with a couple of built - in advantages, one of which was the fact they were on their home floor. The other was that they were catching the feisty Suns (8 - 26) less than 24 hours removed from a triple - overtime defeat against the Wizards. However, to its credit, Phoenix came out and stayed close in the first quarter, trailing just 38 - 31 after 12 minutes. By the third quarter, fatigue apparently was settling in, as they scored just 18 points while Brooklyn added 10 more points to what had been a 63 - 56 halftime edge. Deandre Ayton showed he still had plenty of life left in his legs by leading the Suns with a 26 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, three blocks and two steals. Devin Booker followed with 25 points, nine assists and two rebounds. Josh Jackson led the bench with 11 points, three rebounds and one assist. Malik Bridges mustered nine points, four assists, three rebounds, five steals and one block. T.J. Warren had just four points on 2 - for - 11 shooting. Spencer Dinwiddie paced the Nets with 24 points and added seven assists and two rebounds. D'Angelo Russell supplied 18 points, eight assists, six rebounds and two steals. Rodions Kurucs followed with a 16 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one block. Eric Davis posted 15 points, nine boards, three steals and one block. Joe Harris offered 13 points, three boards and two assists. Jarrett Allen just missed a double - double with 11 points, nine boards, two assists and one steal. The Suns remain on the road and visit the Orlando Magic on Wednesday evening, while the Nets remain home to face the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday night as well.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 134 - 132, in double overtime at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. The Nets (17 - 19) didn't let a 29 - 22 first - quarter deficit deter them, as they turned the tables on the Hornets (16 - 17) in the second quarter to take a 56 - 51 lead into intermission. Ultimately, the game went into overtime after a wild sequence in the closing seconds of regulation when Spencer Dinwiddie made three free throws after being fouled by Jeremy Lamb with 6 seconds remaining to knot the game at 113 - 113, and both Kemba Walker and DeMarre Carroll subsequently drained a free throw apiece, although the latter missed a second one that would have likely handed Brooklyn the win. In the second overtime, Malik Monk lost the ball with 7 seconds remaining, leading to a game - winning layup by Joe Harris with 3 seconds left. Walker paced the Hornets with 35 points and added six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Lamb posted 31 points, six boards, three assists and two steals. Marvin Williams generated a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks and one steal. Nicolas Batum turned in 13 points, three assists, two rebounds and one steal. Tony Parker led the bench with 10 points. Dinwiddie paced the Nets with 37 points, a total he supplemented with 11 assists and two rebounds. Harris scored a season - high 27 points and also provided six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson contributed a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and three blocks. D'Angelo Russell matched Hollis-Jefferson's scoring and also tallied four assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Rodions Kurucs pitched in a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, three steals and one block. Carroll delivered 12 points overall. The Hornets and Nets face off and do it all over again in the second game of the home - and - home series in Charlotte on Friday night.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 116 - 100, at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. The Hawks (12 - 29) managed to jump ahead in this game and led by an astonishing 15 - point margin (38 - 23) following the first quarter, but that would be everything they do as the Nets (21 - 22) bounced back and quickly gained control of the contest. Brooklyn trimmed the deficit to just six points by halftime thanks to a 28 - 19 second quarter, and they would never look back in the second half. They won the remaining two quarters comfortably (35 - 23 and 30 - 20, respectively) and ended cruising their way towards a 16 - point victory that extended their current run to four wins in their last five games. Meanwhile, Atlanta have now dropped five of their last six games. Seven Brooklyn players scored in double digits in this game, led by D'Angelo Russell who finished with 23 points, four assists and three rebounds. Joe Harris delivered 16 points, while Jarrett Allen and Rodions Kurucs each chipped in with 11. DeMarre Carroll contributed 17 points off the bench, while Spencer Dinwiddie (16 points, five assists, four rebounds) and Shabazz Napier (11 points) also had good games while coming off the second unit. The best player for the Hawks was John Collins, who ended with 30 points and 14 rebounds. Trae Young had 17 points with seven assists, but he went 6 - 15 from the field and only 2 - 9 from three - point range. Kevin Huerter added 14 points and 10 boards, and Jeremy Lin played very well off the bench: 16 points, five rebounds, three assists and three steals.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Boston Celtics, 109 - 102, at Barclays Center on Monday. The Nets (22 - 23) have been quite inconsistent over the current 2018 - 19 NBA season, but they managed to deliver an impressive performance while facing one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference such as the Celtics (25 - 18). Brooklyn quickly jumped ahead to a 27 - 25 lead in the first quarter, but Boston kept things close and the first half ended with a 46 - 45 edge for the hosts. Brooklyn would jump through a huge 44 - 21 after the third quarter, which gave them a 24 - point edge heading into the final 12 minutes and even though Boston would cut the deficit in the final quarter (36 - 19), the Nets ended winning the game by a rather comfortable seven - point advantage. Undoubtedly, D'Angelo Russell was the biggest scoring threat for the Nets since he finished with 34 points, seven assists and five rebounds. Jarrett Allen had an impressive performance on both ends of the floor, as he chipped in with 19 points, 12 rebounds and four blocks. Rodions Kurucs had 19 points, while Joe Harris added 13 points, eight boards and three assists. DeMarre Carroll added 10 points off the bench. Only three Boston players ended scoring with more than 10 points, and second - year player Jayson Tatum led the way with an impressive 34 - point performance, but he also contributed five rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Jaylen Brown had 22 points, but he also chipped in with six rebounds and two steals. Brad Wanamaker had a solid outing off the bench, with 13 points, four assists and three boards.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 123 - 94, at Barclay's Center on Monday. While Sacramento held a small lead at the half, Brooklyn absolutely dominated the second half. Frank Mason III turned in a full line of 14 points, seven assists, five rebounds and one steal. Iman Shumpert drew a second straight start and contributed 12 points, three assists, two rebounds and two steals. Willie Cauley-Stein and Yogi Ferrell generated matching 11 - point tallies. Jamal Murray overcame his left tibial contusion to pace the Nuggets with 19 points, four assists, one rebound and one steal. Gary Harris poured in 18 points and added five assists, three rebounds and one steal. Paul Millsap registered 15 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Nikola Jokic pitched in a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and one steal. Trey Lyles contributed 12 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. The Kings head back home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday evening, while the Nuggets head to Los Angeles for a showdown with the Lakers on Thursday night.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 116 - 111, at Pepsi Center on Monday. Anthony Davis was sidelined on Monday due to an elbow injury, but that did not stop New Orleans (4 - 2) from putting up a strong fight in the loss. After Denver (5 - 1) led by as much as 18 in the third quarter, the Pelicans clawed back through the third and fourth, eventually cutting the lead to as little as three. Ultimately, though, Denver's strong offense got the best of the Pelicans. The Nuggets hit 11 three - pointers and dished out 28 assists in the win. 10 of those dimes were dished out by Nikola Jokic, who narrowly missed out on a triple - double on Monday. The star big man finished with 12 points, 10 assists, and nine rebounds, continuing his strong third - year campaign. The Nuggets' backcourt of Gary Harris and Jamal Murray scored 23 points each and combined to shoot 17 - of - 35 on the night. New Orleans, meanwhile, saw offseason acquisition Julius Randle step up in Davis's absence. Randle scored 24 points to lead all scorers, and also finished with eight rebounds and six assists. Starting power forward Nikola Mirotic added another 17 points, 10 rebounds, and three steals. The team will look to continue its strong offensive production when Davis returns from his injury. On Wednesday, the Nuggets will visit Chicago while the Pelicans will travel to Golden State.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Utah Jazz, 103 - 88, at Pepsi Center on Saturday evening. The two division rivals came into the contest pretty evenly matched despite the two - win difference in their records. The first half bore that out, as the Nuggets (7 - 1) only held a slim 47 - 46 edge at intermission. However, the Jazz (4 - 5) managed to separate some in the third, erasing their deficit and building a five - point lead going into the final 12 minutes. Then everything went downhill for the visitors, as they saw star two - guard Donovan Mitchell have to be helped off the court due to an ankle injury and were outscored by a 35 - 15 margin to close out the game. Mitchell did manage to return after getting his ankle taped, but it was a case of too little too late. Jae Crowder led the Jazz off the bench with 21 points in 32 minutes. Mitchell paced the first unit with 16 points despite missing some time, and he added five rebounds, two assists and five steals. Derrick Favors and Rudy Gobert had matching 12 - point tallies, with the Stifle Tower also hauling in 12 boards. Ricky Rubio contributed 11 points, six assists, four rebounds and four steals. Gary Harris paced the Nuggets with 20 points while adding four rebounds and an assist. Jamal Murray supplied 19 points, five rebounds and four assists. Paul Millsap turned in 13 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals. Nikola Jokic provided just seven points but dished out 16 assists, hauled in 10 rebounds and recorded one steal. Malik Beasley paced the second unit with 12 points. The Jazz next head north of the border to tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Monday evening, while the Nuggets remain home for a showdown with the Boston Celtics on Monday night as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 115 - 107, at Pepsi Center on Monday evening. The Celtics got out to a great start on the road, with a quick 10 - 2 run, before going on to build a 34 - 19 lead by the end of the quarter. The Nuggets answered in the second, as they kicked things off with a 90 run, just minutes into the quarter, to cut the deficit to six. The Celtics managed to push their lead back to 10, but the Nuggets did not back down, as they outscored the Celtics, 19 - 11, through the rest of the quarter, to trail by just two at halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, as they went back - and - forth to keep the score within one or two possessions, however, the Nuggets took over in the final minutes, where they outscored the Celtics 11 - 4, to take a seven - point lead into the fourth. The Nuggets did not look back from there, as they managed to stay one step ahead throughout the fourth, to earn their fifth straight win, and move to 60 at home. Jamal Murray went off for a career - high 48 points on 19 - of - 30 shooting, in 38 minutes, to lead the Nuggets. Gary Harris and Trey Lyles chipped in 13 points each, while Nikola Jokic tallied eight points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. The Nuggets shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 31 points on 13 - of - 17 shooting, five rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block, in 33 minutes. Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown tallied 15 points each, while Al Horford finished with 12 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. The Celtics shot 51 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 31 from deep. The Celtics (6 - 4) will look to avoid a third straight loss, as they take on the Suns in Phoenix on Thursday. The Nuggets (9 - 1) take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Denver Nuggets, 112 - 110, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Nets got out to a strong start on the road, as they outscored the Nuggets by 10 in the first, to take a 34 - 24 lead into the second quarter. The game tightened up in the second, but the Nuggets could not make much of a dent in the lead, as they trailed 55 - 47 at the half. The Nuggets came out strong in the third and managed to tie it up at 65, halfway though the quarter, however, the Nets picked it up again, and pulled ahead by six, heading into the fourth. The Nuggets tightened things up early in the quarter, and the two teams fought it out down the stretch, tied at 102, with three minutes left. The game went down to the wire, with a tie game and the Nets' ball with 22 seconds left. Caris LeVert came up as the hero, as he drained a jumper to seal the win with 0 seconds left. This marks the third straight win for the Nets and the second straight loss for the Nuggets. LeVert finished with 17 points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block, in 31 minutes, while D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 23 points, five assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 26 minutes. Jarrett Allen added 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists, five blocks and one steal, in 30 minutes. The Nets shot 41 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Nikola Jokic led the Nuggets with 37 points, 21 rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal, in 33 minutes. Jamal Murray tallied 16 points, five assists, two rebounds and one steal, while Paul Millsap chipped in 11 points and 11 rebounds. The Nuggets shot 46 percent from the field, including 5 - of - 18 from long range. The Nuggets (9 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Bucks on Sunday. The Nets (6 - 6) take on the Warriors in Golden State on Saturday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Denver Nuggets, 121 - 114, at Pepsi Center on Sunday evening. The game had the feel of a heavyweight fight, as it featured two of the elite squads from each conference. The Bucks (10 - 3) established that they'd be able to hang in the challenging environment of Pepsi Center from the opening tip, as they essentially matched the Nuggets (9 - 4) basket for basket during the first quarter. Milwaukee then forged ahead in the middle periods, outscoring Denver by a 66 - 53 margin that allowed them to create enough cushion to head into the fourth quarter with an 11 - point advantage. The visitors got it done with some sharp shooting, as they drained 57 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent of their tries from distance. Brook Lopez led the way for the Bucks with 28 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal. Giannis Antetokounmpo filled out the stat sheet with 22 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block. Khris Middleton supplied 21 points, five rebounds and two assists. Malcolm Brogdon totaled 20 points, six boards, five assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe contributed 12 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Paul Millsap paced the Nuggets with 25 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two blocks. Nikola Jokic delivered 20 points, six rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block. Trey Lyles managed 16 points and five rebounds. Gary Harris registered 15 points, four boards and three steals. Jamal Murray provided 14 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals. Malik Beasley poured in 10 points off the bench. The Bucks head back home to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday evening, while the Nuggets remain home for a conference showdown with the Houston Rockets on Tuesday night.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Denver Nuggets, 109 - 99, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday evening. The Rockets (6 - 7) have progressively been resembling the team everyone envisioned after a forgettable start. The veteran - laden team had begun to hit their stride in recent games, but Tuesday presented a formidable test in a difficult road environment. Houston proved to be up to the task, coming out of the gates hot and trailing by just one point at halftime. The third quarter was pivotal, as the visitors gained 10 points worth of separation on the Nuggets (9 - 5). Then, the Rockets managed to match Denver basket for basket during the final 12 minutes, leading to a surprising double - digit victory. Both teams shot particularly well, but Houston's 55 percent success rate slightly edged the home squad's 50 percent figure. Clint Capela led the way for the Rockets with 24 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. James Harden followed with a 22 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds, three steals and one block. Chris Paul supplied 21 points, five rebounds, four assists and two steals. James Ennis III had one of his better offensive performances, registering 16 points. P.J. Tucker contributed a full line of 12 points, six boards, two assists, one steal and one block. Monte Morris paced the Nuggets with 19 points over 31 minutes off the bench. He added six assists and two rebounds. Jamal Murray and Gary Harris generated 15 points apiece. Nikola Jokic posted a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included seven assists and two steals. Paul Millsap tallied 13 points, one assist and two steals. The Rockets head back home for a Friday night showdown against the Golden State Warriors, while the Nuggets remain home to tangle with the Atlanta Hawks on Friday evening as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 138 - 93, at Pepsi Center on Thursday evening. The Nuggets went straight to work, as they kicked the game off with a 130 run, through the four minutes of the quarter. They went on to outscore the Hawks, 35 - 23, in the first quarter. The Hawks picked it up to start the second, and cut the deficit to nine, however the Nuggets kept up the pace and managed to increase their lead to 73 - 57 by halftime. Denver remained relentless, as the Nuggets outscored the Hawks by 20 in the third quarter, to put the game entirely out of reach, with a 36 - point deficit heading into the fourth. The win marks the end of a four - game skid for the Nuggets, and also the sixth straight loss for Atlanta. Seven players scored in double digits for the Nuggets, led by Juancho Hernangomez, who tallied 25 points, nine rebounds, one assists and one steal, in 31 minutes. Garry Harris followed up with 18 points, four assists, three rebounds and two blocks, while Paul Millsap finished with 18 points, nine rebounds, five assists, four steals and two blocks. The Nuggets shot 56 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 31 from deep. Meanwhile, Jeremy Lin led the Hawks with 16 points, five rebounds and five assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. Kent Bazemore added 14 points and two rebounds, while Omari Spellman finished with 10 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, three steals and a block. The Hawks shot just 35 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 42 from long range. The Hawks (3 - 12) will look to end the slide as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Saturday. The Nuggets (10 - 5) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Saturday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Orlando Magic, 112 - 87, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. Following a tightly contested first quarter, the Nuggets (12 - 7) pulled ahead in the second to forge a 54 - 41 halftime lead. They kept their foot on the gas over the final two periods as well, outscoring the Magic (9 - 10) by a 58 - 46 margin. In addition to the scoreboard, Denver enjoyed a sizable advantage on the boards, outrebounding Orlando by a 51 - 37 margin. The Magic had only three double - digit scorers, with Terrance Ross leading the way. The sharpshooting wing posted 18 points and added an assist over 23 minutes off the bench. Nikola Vukevic turned in 16 points, hauled in eight rebounds and recorded a steal. Aaron Gordon delivered 14 points, nine rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Jonathan Isaac supplied nine points off the bench. Evan Fournier (five points), D.J. Augustin (four points) and Wesley Iwundu (three points) all underwhelmed offensively. Trey Lyles paced the Nuggets with 22 points off the bench. Jamal Murray registered 16 points, six assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block. Paul Millsap tallied 14 points, seven rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. Juancho Hernangomez finished with 10 points, while Nikola Jokic mustered a modest six points but also dished out 11 assists and hauled in 10 rebounds. The Magic remain on the road and visit the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday afternoon, while the Nuggets visit the Oklahoma City Thunder on Saturday night.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 105 - 99, at Pepsi Center on Monday. Injuries have continued to plague the Nuggets (18 - 9) this season, but they fought through the absence of two starters Monday to earn a key victory over the Grizzlies after dropping back - to - back games to the Hornets and Hawks. They were led by a stellar outing from Nikola Jokic, who contnues to show how he's one of the best all - around players in the NBA. Jokic posted a game - high 27 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting to go along with 12 rebounds and six assists in 38 minutes. The most important performance from a Nuggets players Monday night, however, was from reserve point guard Monte Morris. Morris came off the bench to score 20 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting on top of five rebounds and six assists in 28 minutes. As for the Grizzlies (15 - 11), they have now dropped two games in a row, and Monday's loss can be chalked up to a lack of production from the starting unit. Mike Conley shot just 5 - of - 14 from the field, but he was the only Memphis starter to reach double figures, scoring a team - high 19 points in 32 minutes. Marc Gasol was just 2 - of - 6 from the field and scored just seven points, while rookie sensation Justin Jackson Jr. played just 20 minutes and managed to post only seven points in the process. The Grizzlies' bench, however, did everything it could to keep the team in the game. Led by Shelvin Mack's 14 points, the five Memphis reserves scored 51 of the team's 99 points, outscoring the five starters.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 109 - 98, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Nuggets got out to a solid start at home as they outscored the visitors, 39 - 32, through the first quarter. The game tightened up in the second, but the Nuggets were able to keep the edge, as they took a 60 - 52 lead into halftime. The Thunder came out strong in the third and made it a one - point game halfway through the quarter, but the Nuggets bounced back to reclaim a six - point lead by the end of the quarter. The Nuggets pushed their lead to 11 in the fourth, but the Thunder cut it back down to three with 3:20 remaining. However, the Nuggets closed the contest on a 10 - 2 run, to secure their second straight win, and hand the Thunder their second straight loss. Nikola Jokic had a monster night for the Nuggets, with 24 points, 15 rebounds, nine assists and three steals, in 35 minutes. Jamal Murray followed up with 19 points, nine assists and one rebound, while Juancho Hernangomez added 16 points, four rebounds, three assists and a steal, in 33 minutes. The Nuggets shot 50 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Paul George was the high - point man for the Thunder, with 32 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal, in 39 minutes. Russell Westbrook tallied 13 points, 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal, while Steven Adams finished with 26 points, 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. The Thunder (17 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Clippers on Saturday. The Nuggets (19 - 9) play host to the Raptors on Sunday.

The Denver Nuggets took down the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 123 - 116, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday evening. Denver (21 - 9) brought its win streak to four games by taking down Dallas (15 - 14) on Tuesday. While the game was a back - and - forth affair for much of regulation, the Nuggets began to swing momentum in their favor with a big 140 run late in the third quarter. Despite missing multiple starters, including Gary Harris (hip) and Paul Millsap (toe), Denver was electric offensively, shooting 56 percent from the field in the win. When the team's shots weren't falling, Denver did an excellent job cleaning the glass, finishing with a 12 - 6 advantage on the offensive boards. Seven Nuggets players scored in double digits to contribute to the win. Superstar big man Nikola Jokic continued his impressive 2018 - 19 campaign, scoring 32 points to go with 16 rebounds. Jokic's six offensive boards matched Dallas's team total, and the seven - footer also made an impact defensively, tallying three steals and a block. Third-year guard Jamal Murray, meanwhile, also helped set the tone offensively. Murray notched a career - high 15 assists, 13 of which came in the first half. He added 22 points to give him his second double - double of the season. For Dallas, on the other hand, rookie sensation Luka Doncic recorded a double - double of his own. The 19 - year - old wing dished out 12 assists and scored 23 points, aided by a solid 10 - of - 12 night at the free - throw line. Harrison Barnes, meanwhile, led the Mavs with 30 points, though he did not record an assist on the night. Despite the two wings' best efforts, the Mavericks shot just 46 percent from the field, as Dallas proved unable to match the Nuggets blistering shooting splits. The Mavericks will hope to remain above .500 as they visit the Clippers at Staples Center on Thursday. Denver, meanwhile, will have three days off before making its own visit to LA to take on the Clippers on Saturday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting San Antonio Spurs, 102 - 99, at Pepsi Center on Friday. While Denver led for 47 minutes of this 48 - minute game, it came down to the final shot. In fact, San Antonio missed a free - throw in the final 30 seconds that would have tied the game, as they made a mess of the final possession by not even getting off a three - point shot in the final 10 seconds. Free-throw shooting was the difference for the Nuggets, with Denver connecting on 14 - of - 17 and San Antonio hitting just 11 - of - 20. Rebounding was also critical, with the Nuggets outrebounding the Spurs, 53 - 38. The Nuggets won despite being dominated in the turnover differential, with the Spurs winning that, 21 - 10. The Spurs (19 - 17) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he tallied 24 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three steals. DeMar DeRozan accrued 15 points, five rebounds and five assists. Derrick White returned home and collected 10 points, six rebounds, three assists and six steals. Byrn Forbes was the only other Spur in double figures, scoring 13 points. The Nuggets (22 - 11) were led by Jamal Murray, as he tallied 31 points, six rebounds and three assists. Nikola Jokic totaled 21 points, nine rebounds and nine assists. Mason Plumlee scored just three points but led the team with 13 rebounds. Malik Beasley was huge off the bench, providing 21 points and three rebounds. On deck for Denver is a road matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Saturday. As for San Antonio, they also return to action on Saturday, traveling to face the Los Angeles Clippers.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 115 - 108, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday. There were nine ties and 10 lead changes in the first three quarters of this game, as Denver took control in the fourth quarter. In fact, the Nuggets outscored the Knicks, 33 - 24, in the fourth, despite the fact that neither club led by more than 10 points. Rebounding was huge for the Nuggets, as they won that battle, 53 - 43. Ball movement was also critical, with Denver out - assisting New York, 36 - 28. The Nuggets bench was also key, as they outscored the Knicks bench, 59 - 35. The Knicks (9 - 29) were led by Luke Kornet, as he totaled 19 points and six boards. The Nuggets (24 - 11) got another triple - double from Nikola Jokic, as he collected 19 points, 14 rebounds, 15 assists and three blocks. Malik Beasley led the team in scoring, providing 23 points, six rebounds and five assists off the bench. Paul Millsap also played well off the bench, accumulating 16 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two steals. On deck for Denver is a road matchup versus the Sacramento Kings on Thursday. As for New York, they stay on the road to face the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday for their next outing.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 123 - 110, at Pepsi Center on Sunday. The first three quarters of this game were extremely competitive, as there were nine ties and 12 lead changes in total. Denver took control in the fourth though, outscoring Charlotte, 34 - 26. Points off turnovers were the difference, with the Nuggets winning that battle, 27 - 3. That's evident when you see that Denver won the turnover differential, 17 - 7 while out - assisting the Hornets, 30 - 22. The Nuggets bench was also huge, as they outscored the Hornets bench, 56 - 37. The Hornets (18 - 20) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 20 points, four rebounds and three assists. Marvin Williams finished with 16 points, six rebounds and three steals. Bismack Biyombo got a rare start and set a season - high with 16 points, 12 rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Malik Monk led the bench with 16 points, three rebounds and two assists. The Nuggets (26 - 11) got another gem from Nikola Jokic, as he collected 39 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and three steals. Jamal Murray totaled eight points, six rebounds and seven assists. Paul Millsap was huge off the bench, providing 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and four steals. Gary Harris was also imperative off the bench, amassing 17 points, six rebounds and five assists. On deck for Charlotte is a road matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. As for Denver, they're off until Monday when they travel to face the Houston Rockets.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 121 - 100, at Pepsi Center on Thursday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Denver, it was as dominating as it gets. In fact, the Nuggets rode a 37 - 25 first quarter to their victory, as they led by at least five points for the final three quarters. Rebounding was the difference in the game, with Denver outrebounding Los Angeles, 53 - 38. The shooting disparity was also critical, with the Nuggets shooting 51 percent from the field and 39 percent from three - point range while the Clippers hit just 44 percent from the field and 25 percent from long range. Much of that can be attributed to the fact that Denver out - assisted Los Angeles, 29 - 21. The Clippers (24 - 17) were led by Lou Williams, as he provided 19 points and five assists off the bench. Tobias Harris led the starters with 18 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Danilo Gallinari matched those 18 points, adding three rebounds and four assists to his tally. Montrezl Harrell amassed 16 points and six boards off the bench as well. The Nuggets (28 - 12) got another triple - double from Nikola Jokic, as he collected 18 points, 14 rebounds, 10 assists and two blocks. Jamal Murray led the team in scoring, totaling 23 points, six rebounds and two assists. Malik Beasley started and accrued 15 points, five assists and two steals. Mason Plumlee was a huge spark off the bench, providing 17 points, 12 rebounds and five assists. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Los Angeles playing host to the Detroit Pistons and Denver traveling to Arizona to face the Phoenix Suns.

The Denver Nuggets took down the Portland Trail Blazers, 116 - 113, at Pepsi Center on Sunday evening. A 40 - point night from Nikola Jokic propelled Denver (29 - 13) to another win on Sunday, allowing the Nuggets to hold first place in the Western Conference. Portland (26 - 18), however, answered back with a jump shot from C.J. McCollum. Still, the Nuggets managed to hold on to the lead until the final buzzer. Denver was aided by a wildly efficient offensive performance, as the team shot 56 percent from the field. In addition to his team - high scoring performance, Jokic recorded 10 rebounds and eight assists. The big man shot 15 - of - 23 from the floor en route to his big night. Jamal Murray added an additional 24 points and four rebounds. As a team, Denver totaled nine three - pointers and shot 17 - of - 20 from the free - throw line. Portland, meanwhile, saw a strong night from its own superstar. Damian Lillard dropped 26 points and dished out seven assists. The team as a whole, though, struggled to match Denver's offensive output. The Blazers shot only 45 percent from the field and 35 percent from three - point range. The Trail Blazers will visit Sacramento on Monday evening, while Denver will host the Golden State Warriors on Tuesday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Chicago Bulls, 135 - 105, on Thursday at Pepsi Center. It appears as though the Nuggets (30 - 14) had some pent up anger and energy after they laid an egg at home Tuesday against the Warriors. While the Bulls (10 - 35) jumped out to a two - point after the first 12 minutes, it was all Denver after that. The Nuggets went on to outscore the Bulls in the second and third quarters by a total of 32 points, and it ended up being smooth sailing for the home team. Seven players scored in double figures for them and 11 of the 12 players who saw the floor scored at least three points. Jamal Murray led the way, shooting 7 - of - 11 from behind the arc en route to scoring a team - high 25 points in 29 minutes, while likely All-Star Nikola Jokic posted a double - double of 18 points and 11 rebounds to go along with eight assists in 25 minutes. Gary Harris made his return after a five - game absence due to a hamstring injury, and while he played just 19 minutes as a reserve, he still managed to score 14 points. As for the Bulls, it was their eighth loss in a row as their record continues to tank. It wasn't a horrible offensive night for Chicago, as they shot 36 percent from behind the arc and 47 percent from the field overall, but they had no answer for the Nuggets on defense. The 135 points they gave up was the second highest opponent total this season for Chicago, with the 146 points they gave up to Golden State last week serving as the highest. Lauri Markkanen did score a game - high 27 points on 10 - of - 18 shooting to go along with 10 rebounds in just 25 minutes, but the other four Bulls starters would combine to score just 36 minutes. Robin Lopez and Jabari Parker were both solid off the bench, however, scoring 17 and 15 points, respectively.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 124 - 102, at Pepsi Center on Saturday night. The Nuggets (31 - 14) came out of the gates like the dominant home squad they've often proven to be, building a 37 - 25 first - quarter lead that they'd expanded to an insurmountable 70 - 46 by halftime.
