Ante Zizic led the way for the Cavaliers with 23 points, adding six rebounds. Rodney Hood poured in 18 points and also provided three assists and two steals. Cedi Osman supplied 17 points, three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Jordan Clarkson generated 13 points, four rebounds and an assist. Collin Sexton managed 10 points, seven assists, four rebounds and one steal. Jamal Murray paced the Nuggets with 26 points and supplemented them with five assists and two rebounds. Trey Lyles followed with a bench - leading 16 points and also turned in six boards, four assists and one steal. Monte Morris contributed 15 points. Paul Millsap delivered 14 points, five rebounds, one assist and two steals. Malik Beasley totaled 13 points, four rebounds and one assist. The Cavaliers remain home and take on the Chicago Bulls on Monday afternoon, while the Nuggets hit the road and take on the Utah Jazz on Wednesday evening.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 126 - 110, at Pepsi Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a high - paced start, as the Nuggets led 41 - 37 after one quarter. The Sixers battled through the second, but the Nuggets closed the quarter strong, to extend their lead to nine by halftime. The Nuggets stayed in control through the third and managed to push their lead to double digits by the start of the fourth. They pushed their lead to 16 mid way though the fourth and cruised to their second straight win. Nikola Jokic led the Nuggets with 32 points on 12 - of - 22 shooting, 18 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Mason Plumlee followed up with 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and one block, while Torrey Craig added 15 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Nuggets shot 52 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 24 from long range. Meanwhile, J.J. Redick led the 76ers with 22 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting, three assists and two rebounds, in 27 minutes. Corey Brewer followed up with 20 points, six rebounds, four steals and two assist, while Ben Simmons finished with 19 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. The Sixers shot 42 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 36 from long range. The 76ers (32 - 18) will look to bounce back as they take on the Lakers in L.A. on Tuesday. The Nuggets (33 - 15) take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Monday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 136 - 122, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Rockets got out to a strong start on the road, as they outscored the Nuggets 43 - 35 in the first quarter. However, the Nuggets responded by outscoring the Rockets by 20 in the second quarter, to take an 83 - 71 lead into halftime. The Nuggets maintained a double - digit lead through most of the third quarter, and built their lead to 18 by the start of the fourth. The Rockets kept battling through the fourth, but it was not enough, as the Nuggets cruised to their fifth straight win. Nikola Jokic came up huge for the Nuggets, with 31 points on 12 - of - 15 shooting, 13 rebounds, nine assists and one steal, in 31 minutes. Malik Beasley finished with 35 points on 12 - of - 17 shooting, three assists, two rebounds and one steal, while Torrey Craig added 22 points, four rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block. The Nuggets shot 62 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 31 from long range. Meanwhile, James Harden led the Rockets with 30 points on 9 - of - 21 shooting, nine assists, six rebounds, two steals and one block, in 37 minutes. Chris Paul tallied 20 points, six assists and three rebounds, in 29 minutes, while Kenneth Faried added 23 points, six rebounds and one assist. The Rockets shot 53 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 44 from long range. The Rockets (29 - 22) will look to bounce back as they take on the Jazz in Utah, on Saturday. The Nuggets (36 - 15) take on the Timberwolves in Minnesota on Saturday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 123 - 96, at Pepsi Center on Sunday. Denver came into this game as a sizable favorite and a 27 - point victory shows just why. Not only did the Nuggets win this game in wire - to - wire fashion, but they won all four individual quarters as well. That allowed Denver to lead by at least 15 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Denver ended up shooting 52 percent from the field while holding Los Angels to 35 percent from the field and 14 percent from three - point range. Rebounding was key for the Nuggets, as they outrebounded the Clippers, 56 - 38. Ball movement was also critical, with Denver out - assisting Los Angeles, 30 - 20. The Clippers (33 - 28) were led by Lou Williams, as he provided 24 points, two rebounds and two assists off the bench. Danilo Gallinari was the only starter in double figures, as he amassed 19 points and four rebounds. JaMychal Green came off the bench to total 13 points and nine boards. No other player on the roster had more than eight points, eight rebounds or four assists. The Nuggets (41 - 18) were led by Nikola Jokic, as he tallied 22 points, 16 rebounds, three assists and three steals. Paul Millsap collected 21 points, 16 rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocks. Jamal Murray amassed 16 points, four rebounds and six assists while Gary Harris led the bench with 14 points, two rebounds and two assists. On deck for Los Angeles is a home matchup versus the Dallas Mavericks on Monday. As for Denver, they return to action on Tuesday when they play host to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Denver Nuggets bested the Oklahoma City Thunder, 121 - 112, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday. Denver (42 - 18) got the best of OKC (38 - 22) despite a close first half. The Nuggets pulled away, though, with a quick run at the close of the second quarter to take a double - digit lead. Denver was spearheaded by superstar Nikola Jokic, who recorded 19 points and seven assists in the first half. Jokic went on to lead all scorers in the game with 36 points. He also finished with 10 assists. Strong three - point shooting proved crucial to Denver's success. While OKC shot just 27 percent from deep, the Nuggets went an impressive 13 - of - 28 from beyond the arc. Jamal Murray and Will Barton also delivered gems for the Nuggets. Murray finished the game with 20 points while dishing out five assists, while Barton scored an additional 23 points. Veteran big man Paul Millsap also came up big for Denver, recording 10 rebounds for a double - double. Thunder All-Stars Russell Westbrook and Paul George could not get the job done despite strong efforts on Tuesday. Westbrook flirted with a triple - double, finishing one assist shy despite 22 points and 14 rebounds. George, meanwhile, scored 25 to go with seven assists and six steals. The loss came at a bad time for OKC, as the team has now dropped three of its last four games. The Thunder will have a chance to turn things around with a matchup against Philadelphia on Thursday. Denver, meanwhile, has a tilt with the Jazz on Thursday up next.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the host Denver Nuggets, 120 - 112, at Pepsi Center on Saturday. While Denver came into this game as a sizable favorite, New Orleans prevailed. The Nuggets looked well on their way when they led by 12 after the first quarter and 19 points in the second quarter but the Pelicans responded by dominating the final three quarters. In fact, New Orleans won each of the final three quarters by at least five points apiece, as they held the lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The Pelicans defense was key, as they held the Nuggets to 42 percent from the field and 28 percent from three - point range. New Orleans shot 49 percent from the field and 40 percent from long range while outscoring them in the paint, 62 - 52. The Pelicans (28 - 36) were led by Jrue Holiday, as he tallied 29 points, three rebounds, five assists and three steals. Julius Randle finished with 28 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Elfrid Payton accrued eight points, seven rebounds and 10 assists. Cheick Diallo provided 12 points and 10 rebounds off the bench. The Nuggets (42 - 19) were led by Nikola Jokic, as he accumulated 20 points, nine rebounds, seven assists, two steals and two blocks. Jamal Murray amassed 20 points, three rebounds and four assists. Paul Millsap collected 16 points, seven rebounds, two assists, five steals and two blocks. Mason Plumlee led the bench with 14 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Denver traveling to face the struggling San Antonio Spurs and New Orleans facing the Utah Jazz on the road as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 133 - 107, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday. A 31 - 20 first quarter really set the foundation in this game, as Denver dominated throughout. In fact, they held the lead for the final three quarters, as the Timberwolves never got the game within 13 points in the fourth quarter. The 40 assists were the difference for Denver, as Minnesota handed out just 24. That allowed the Nuggets to shoot an unheard of 60 percent from the field and 60 percent from three - point range, which are both two of the highest totals of the season for any team. The Timberwolves (32 - 36) had to play without Jeff Teague, Derrick Rose and Andrew Wiggins, as they simply didn't have enough to compete here. Karl-Anthony Towns did all he could, as he led the way with 34 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Tyus Jones started and totaled 16 points, two rebounds, three assists and two steals. The Nuggets (44 - 22) were led by Jamal Murray, as he amassed 30 points, three rebounds and three steals. Nikola Jokic collected 18 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. Paul Millsap tallied 23 points, five rebounds and two assists while Monte Morris led the bench with 16 points, five rebounds and six assists. Both teams return to action on Thursday, with Denver playing host to the Dallas Mavericks and Minnesota traveling to Salt Lake City to face the Utah Jazz.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 100 - 99, in a last - minute thriller at Pepsi Center on Thursday. Everything seemed poised to go the Mavericks' (27 - 40) way after a strong third quarter left Dallas with a double - digit lead. Denver (44 - 22), however, managed to put together a defensive masterpiece in the fourth to eke out the win. The Mavericks were limited to just 10 points in the fourth quarter, which culminated in a wild back - and - forth finish. Rookie sensation Luka Doncic put the Mavericks up by one point on a dunk with just 6 seconds remaining. He was fouled on the play, but missed the free - throw, allowing Denver a final possession to take the lead. The Nuggets did that, winning the game on a buzzer - beating floater from star center Nikola Jokic. Jokic flirted with a triple - double, finishing with 11 points, 14 rebounds, and eight assists. He was not particularly aggressive offensively, shooting just 3 - of - 8 on the night. Veteran Paul Millsap took the lead instead, shooting 14 - of - 19 from the field en route to a season - high 33 points. Doncic nearly had a triple - double of his own, finishing with 24 points, 11 rebounds, and nine assists. The rookie star continued to struggle at the free - throw line, though, going just 3 - of - 7 at the stripe. Fellow rookie guard Jalen Brunson also had a memorable game, finishing with 20 points. Both teams will take the floor again on Saturday, with Denver hosting the Indiana Pacers and Dallas seeing a visit from the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 102 - 100, at Pepsi Center on Saturday. While Indiana led 36 - 25 after the first quarter, this game wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Paul Millsap broke a tied game with a runner in the final seconds which ultimately won the Nuggets the game. Bojan Bogdanovic then missed a shot in the final second that would have won the game for the Pacers. Denver prevailed because of the middle quarters though, as they outscored Indiana, 54 - 39, in the second and third quarters. Ball movement was the difference for the Nuggets, as they out - assisted the Pacers, 27 - 20. Denver also connected on 11 - of - 38 from long range while Indiana hit just 6 - of - 24. The Pacers (44 - 26) were led by Thaddeus Young, as he totaled 18 points and 10 rebounds. Darren Collison accrued 17 points, two rebounds, four assists and two steals. Bojan Bogdanovic tallied 16 points, six rebounds and two assists. Myles Turner totaled 15 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals while Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 16 points, seven rebounds and two assists. The Nuggets (46 - 22) were led by Nikola Jokic, as he collected 26 points, seven rebounds and five assists before being ejected in the fourth quarter. Paul Millsap finished with 15 points, 13 rebounds and three assists. Will Barton accumulated 17 points, six rebounds and five assists while Jamal Murray generated 17 points, three rebounds and three assists. On deck for the Pacers is a road matchup versus the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday. As for the Nuggets is a road matchup versus the Boston Celtics on Monday as well.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Denver Nuggets, 95 - 90, at Pepsi Center on Sunday. Denver came into this game as a sizable favorite but they weren't able to prevail. The Nuggets really fell apart in the second half, with the Wizards outscoring them, 42 - 28. The 28 second - half points for Denver marked a season - low at home. Washington's defense was critical, as they held Denver to 37 percent from the field and 19 percent from three - point range. The Wizards ended up winning the points in the paint battle, 58 - 46, and the fastbreak scoring differential, 26 - 12. The Wizards (32 - 46) were led by Troy Brown, as he totaled 24 points and seven rebounds. Thomas Bryant finished with 20 points, 14 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Bradley Beal accrued 17 points, three rebounds, six assists and three steals. Jabari Parker led the bench with 20 points, six rebounds and three steals. The Nuggets (51 - 25) were led by Nikola Jokic, as he collected 23 points, 14 rebounds and four assists. He did get kicked out with three minutes left in a tied game because of two technical fouls. Paul Millsap accrued 13 points, 16 rebounds and three assists. Jamal Murray amassed 12 points, two rebounds and two assists before departing with an ankle injury. Denver has its biggest game of the season on Tuesday, as they travel to face the Golden State Warriors. As for Washington, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the Chicago Bulls.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 113 - 85, at Pepsi Center on Wednesday. It did not take long for Wednesday's outing to get out of hand, as just over a minute into the game with the Nuggets (52 - 26) up 60, Gregg Popovich got hit with double technical fouls and was ejected. From there, the Spurs (45 - 34) didn't exactly play inspired basketball, and after keeping it close for one quarter, Denver opened things up in the second period and never looked back. The Nuggets were dominant on both ends of the floor, but their defensive effort is what really stood out, as they didn't allow San Antonio to score more than 24 points in a quarter. Offensively, Nikola Jokic led the way with a game - high 20 points, and he almost notched yet another triple - double with 11 rebounds and nine assists across 29 minutes. Malik Beasley and Monte Morris were close behind, with each scoring 19 points in expanded roles off the bench thanks to the blowout nature of the contest. Overall, it was a very efficient offensive performance for the Nuggets, who shot a scorching 54 percent from the field with 41 of their 47 field goals coming off assists. As for San Antonio, it was a night to forget with Popovich setting the tone early. LaMarcus Aldridge and Lonnie Walker IV were the team's leading scorers with just 16 points a piece, and DeMar DeRozan and Davis Bertan were the only other players to score in double figures with each scoring 11. 85 points is tied for the team's lowest point total of the season, and it came as a result of horrendous shooting. The Spurs shot a miserable 18 percent on 27 three - point attempts and made just 38 percent of their total field goals. The loss also dropped the Spurs back into the No. 8 seed in the Western Conference.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 119 - 110, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Trail Blazers got out to a good start on the road, as they owned a 29 - 22 lead after one quarter. However, the Nuggets awoke in the second, where they outscored the visitors by 13, to take six - point lead into halftime. The Trail Blazers kept pushing and chipped away through the third quarter, to reclaim three - point lead heading into the final frame. Fittingly, the fourth quarter featured another swing, as the Nuggets immediately took the lead back and stayed in front the rest of the way for their second straight win. Paul Millsap led the Nuggets with 25 points, seven rebounds, two assists and a steal, in 30 minutes. Nikola Jokic tallied 22 points, 13 rebounds, nine assists, two steals and a block, while Jamal Murray added 23 points, six assists, four rebounds and a steal. The Nuggets shot 51 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 27 from deep. Enes Kanter led the Trail Blazers with 24 points, seven rebounds and four assists, in 38 minutes. Al-Farouq Aminu finished with 12 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block, while Rodney Hood chipped in 17 points, three steals, two rebounds and an assist. The Blazers shot 49 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 29 from long range. The Nuggets (53 - 26) and Trail Blazers (50 - 29) will got at it again on Sunday in Portland.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 99 - 95, on Wednesday at Pepsi Center. Despite still having something to play for Wednesday night, the Nuggets played 45 minutes of lifeless basketball in their regular season finale. With just over three minutes remaining in the game, Denver found itself down by 11 points and on the verge of wasting a prime opportunity to avoid the Houston Rockets, the team's kryptonite all season, in a potential second - round matchup. Then, something clicked. From that point on, the visiting Timberwolves, who were without All-Star center Karl-Anthony Towns due to injury, failed to score a single point as the Nuggets rattled off a 120 run that was capped off by a Jamal Murray three to take the lead. In the end, Denver would close the game on a 150 run and lock up the No. 2 seed in the Western Conference. Murray finished with a quality all - around game, posting 17 points, eight rebounds and seven assists across 35 minutes, but it was Nikola Jokic who once again led the way for this Denver team, scoring a game - high 29 points to go along with 14 rebounds. As for the Timberwolves, they finish the season with three straight loses and end up a dreadful 11 - 30 on the road. With Towns out of the lineup, Andrew Wiggins led the way scoring for Minnesota with 25 points on 11 - of - 20 shooting. Cam Reynolds came off the bench to scoring career - high 19 points in 26 minutes as reserve, while Gorgui Dieng recorded 18 points and 11 rebounds in his spot start.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 111 - 83, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Wednesday on the regular - season opener for both teams. The Grizzlies (0 - 1) entered the game as clear underdogs after mustering a 22 - 60 record in the 2017 - 18 campaign, but with one key component back in their lineup. Star point guard Mike Conley was back to full health after missing the last 70 games of the prior season with a heel injury, providing Memphis with much - needed scoring punch. However, the end result Wednesday was highly reminiscent of last season's failures, as the Pacers (10) rode a 27 - 16 first - quarter advantage to a comfortable win. Indiana extended its lead to 56 - 39 by halftime, and they ultimately tacked on another 55 points in the second half. The home squad saw seven players hit double digits in the scoring column - - including four from the second unit - - while enjoying a 57 percent - 30 percent edge in shooting. Marc Gasol led the way for the Grizzlies with 13 points, adding six rebounds, three assists and three steals. Garrett Temple finished with 12 points, two assists and one block. Conley shot 3 - for - 11 on his way to 11 points, which he supplemented with three assists, two rebounds and one steal. Rookie Jaren Jackson, Jr. paced the second unit with 10 points and also hauled in five boards, dished out one assist, recorded three steals and posted one block. JaMychal Green and MarShon Brooks generated matching nine - point tallies; the former added seven rebounds, two assists and two steals, while the latter compiled two rebounds and one assist. Bojan Bogdanovic paced Indiana with 19 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds. Victor Oladipo totaled 16 points, five rebounds and five assists. Tyreke Evans co - led the bench with 14 points and also supplied six assists and four rebounds. Domantas Sabonis matched his scoring total and also contributed a game - high 15 rebounds and two assists. Doug McDermott poured in 12 points in 24 minutes off the bench, while Cory Joseph pitched in 11 off the second unit as well. Thaddeus Young tallied 10 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block. The Grizzlies next face the Atlanta Hawks in Memphis' home opener on Friday, while the Pacers head to Milwaukee to tangle with the Pacers on Friday evening as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 132 - 112, at Bankers Lief Fieldhouse on Saturday evening. The Pacers (2 - 1) started and finished fast, which was key to what eventually turned out to be a comfortable victory. Indiana racked up an impressive 67 first - half points, but the Nets (1 - 2) kept the pressure on by tallying 58 of their own. The visitors continued to hang tough in the third, but the home squad finally pulled away by posting their best point total (37) of any quarter in the final period. As the combined point total implied, both teams shot very well. The Nets drained 48 percent of their attempts, while the Pacers generated a 55 percent success rate from the field. Joe Harris and Caris LeVert led the Nets with matching 19 - point efforts. Harris added three assists, two rebounds and one block, while LeVert hauled in four boards, dished out three assists, recorded two steals and managed one block. Spencer Dinwiddie supplied 13 points, four assists, one rebound and one steal. Rodions Kurucs and D'Angelo Russell registered matching 12 - point tallies, while Allen Crabbe totaled 10 points and three rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench. Victor Oladipo paced the Pacers with 25 points and also contributed seven rebounds, three assists and four steals. Kyle O'Quinn managed 16 points, eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal. Bojan Bogdanovic poured in 15 points and brought in two rebounds, while Tyreke Evans matched Bogdanovic's scoring total and also pitched in three rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block. Myles Turner (14 points, eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block), Darren Collison (13 points, three assists, two rebounds, one steal) and Thaddeus Young (10 points, two boards, two assists, two steals) rounded out the starting five's productive night. The Nets remain on the road and next take the floor versus the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night, while the Pacers head to Minnesota and take on the Timberwolves in a Monday evening matchup.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 103 - 93, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Monday. It's rare to see a bench dominate a game so thoroughly but that was the case here for Portland. In fact, they had four bench players reach double - figures in scoring, as they outscored Indiana's bench, 54 - 15. Rebounding was also a huge factor, with the Trail Blazers winning that battle, 50 - 35. Portland ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 94 percent from the free - throw line while holding Indiana to just 41 percent from the field and 65 percent from the charity stripe. The Trail Blazers (4 - 2) were led by C.J. McCollum, as he tallied 17 points and six rebounds. Damian Lillard finished with 16 points and two assists. Al-Farouq Aminu totaled 11 points and 10 boards. Zach Collins led the bench with 17 points, three rebounds and three assists. Caleb Swanigan provided 11 points and 10 boards off the bench as well. The Pacers (4 - 3) got a near triple - double out of Victor Oladipo, as he collected 21 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. Darren Collison accrued 17 points, two rebounds, six assists and two steals. Myles Turner totaled 10 points, nine rebounds and three blocks while Thaddeus Young generated 16 points, four rebounds and two steals. On deck for Portland is a road matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Tuesday. As for Indiana, they travel to play the New York Knicks on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 102 - 101, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Saturday evening. The Pacers jumped out to a quick 70 lead, but the Celtics came roaring back with a 28 - 11 run, to take control with a 28 - 18 lead heading into the second quarter. The Pacers got back on track in the second, as they chipped away at the deficit, eventually outscoring the Celtics by 10 in the quarter, to tie the game at 45 by halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, trading buckets, with no one gaining more than a two - possession lead, until they matched each other with 27 points each in the quarter. The contest stayed close right down to the wire, and after multiple lead changes and ties, the Pacers emerged with the one - point win thanks to a clutch three - pointer from Victor Oladipo, with just four second left. This marks the third straight win for the Pacers and the end of a four - game win streak for the Celtics. Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 24 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals, in 36 minutes. Tyreke Evans followed up with 17 points on 6 - of - 12 shooting, in 21 minutes off the bench, while Bojan Bogdanovic added 16 points, three rebounds, three steals and one assist, in 23 minutes. The Pacers shot 41 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Marcus Morris led the way for the Celtics with 23 points, six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block, in 32 minutes off the bench. Kyrie Irving tallied 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and one block, while Al Horford and Jayson Tatum chipped in 14 points each. The Celtics shot 43 percent from the field, including 19 - of - 46 from long range. The Celtics (6 - 3) will look to bounce back as they take on the Nuggets in Denver on Monday. The Pacers (7 - 3) play host to the Rockets on Monday.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Indiana Pacers, 98 - 94, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday night. The Rockets (4 - 5) and the Pacers (7 - 4) played a very interesting game on Monday, as neither club gave an inch to the other and the game had to be decided in the final minutes thanks to an impressive comeback from the visiting team. Houston was up 29 - 22 following the first quarter, but Indiana flipped the script and won the second quarter 33 - 24, as well as the third one 20 - 16, to put themselves ahead by six points entering the final 12 minutes of action. But the Rockets didn't give up, and won the final quarter 29 - 19 to pull away for good. Both teams struggled with their shooting percentages, as Houston shot 44 percent from the field and 32 from three - point range, as opposed to Indiana's 44 and 29, respectively. James Harden led the Rockets offensively with 28 points, but he also added six assists, four rebounds and three steals, while Clint Capela back him up with a double - double of 18 points and 10 rebounds. Chris Paul only had nine points, but contributed with 13 assists and five boards. James Ennis III had 13 points, while Carmelo Anthony chipped in with eight points and five rebounds off the bench. Victor Oladipo paced the Pacers offensively with 28 points, six rebounds and two assists, while Bojan Bogdanovic contributed with 11 points. Thaddeus Young and Myles Turner disappointed, however, since they combined for only 15 points while going 6 - of - 17 from the field between them. Domantas Sabonis (17 points, eight rebounds, five assists) and Tyreke Evans (11 points in only 16 minutes) looked solid coming off the bench, though.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Indiana Pacers, 100 - 94, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Wednesday evening. The 76ers (7 - 5) came into Wednesday looking to redeem themselves from a rather unexpected 122 - 97 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday night. They got off to a strong start against a hot Pacers (7 - 5) squad, jumping out to an early 13 - 12 lead over the first 4:29. However, Indiana had knotted the game at 50 - 50 by halftime, only to see Philadelphia open up their lead back up by seven points in the third period. The visitors were then essentially able to match the home squad basket for basket in the final 12 minutes, sealing the victory. The Sixers played particularly impressive defense, limiting the Pacers to 39 percent shooting, including 26 percent from three - point range. Joel Embiid led the Sixers with a 20 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, three blocks and one steal. Dario Saric managed 18 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Ben Simmons provided a 16 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists and two blocks. Robert Covington turned in 13 points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks. Landry Shamet (12 points) and J.J. Redick (10 points) were both productive off the bench. Victor Oladipo paced the Pacers with a game - high 36 points and added seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks and two steals. Domantas Sabonis followed with a bench - leading 16 points and also hauled in 11 rebounds, three assists and one block. Bojan Bogdanovic registered 13 points, five rebounds, one assist and one steal. Cory Joseph went for nine points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals in 31 minutes off the second unit. The Sixers head back home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Friday evening, while the Pacers pay a visit to the Miami Heat that same night.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 99 - 91, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Friday. While Miami got out to an eight - point lead after the first quarter, Indiana dominated from there. The second quarter was key, with the Pacers outscoring the Heat, 32 - 16. Indiana held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as there were only three ties and two lead changes in total. The shooting disparity was also critical, with Indiana connecting on 44 percent from the field and 52 percent from three - point range while holding Miami to just 38 percent from the field and 39 percent from long range. The Heat (6 - 9) were led by Josh Richardson, as he tallied 28 points, four rebounds and two assists on 10 - of - 16 from the field. Hassan Whiteside finished with 12 points, 17 rebounds and two blocks. Rodney McGruder totaled 11 points and five rebounds while Tyler Johnson led the bench with 10 points, five rebounds and four assists. The Pacers (9 - 6) were led by Tyreke Evans, as he scored a season - high 23 points to lead the bench. He also provided 10 rebounds and went 5 - of - 7 from three - point range. Bojan Bogdanovic led the starters with 16 points and six boards. Myles Turner accrued 12 points, seven rebounds, four assists and three blocks. On deck for Indiana is a home matchup versus the Atlanta Hawks on Saturday. As for Miami, they're off until Sunday when they play host to the Los Angeles Lakers.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 97 - 89, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Saturday. There were six ties and 14 lead changes in this game, as it took a big second half for Indiana to pull away. In fact, the Pacers outscored the Hawks, 50 - 33, in the second half. Defense was key for Indiana, as they held Atlanta to just 36 percent from the field and 28 percent from three - point range. Rebounding was also a huge factor, with the Pacers outrebounding the Hawks, 54 - 41. These teams combined for 39 combined steals and blocks, which is one of the highest totals of the season. The Hawks (3 - 13) had just one starter reach double figures in scoring, as Kent Bazemore collected 13 points, five rebounds, four assists and four steals. Jeremy Lin led the team in scoring off of the bench, providing 16 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals. John Collins made his season debut, as he amassed 12 points and two rebounds in 12 minutes of action. The Pacers (10 - 6) lost their leading scorer in this game, as Victor Oladipo left after eight minutes due to a sore knee. Bojan Bogdanovic stepped up in his absence, leading the way with 22 points and four rebounds. Darren Collison accumulated 12 points, two rebounds, five assists and two steals. Myles Turner generated 10 points, 11 rebounds, two assists and three blocks. Domantas Sabonis was huge off the bench, providing nine points, 16 rebounds and six assists. Both teams play home games on Monday for their next fixture, with Indiana welcoming the Utah Jazz and Atlanta facing off with the Los Angeles Clippers.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Indiana Pacers, 111 - 100, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Friday. The Spurs (9 - 9) jumped out to a 54 - 45 halftime lead and kept up their steady offensive performance in the second half to notch a much - needed road victory. San Antonio had the hot hand throughout the night, posting 51 percent shooting, including 48 percent from three - point range. The Pacers (11 - 8) played short - handed, as Myles Turner missed the game with an ankle injury. Indiana did get a strong performance from their bench, as their reserves combined for 42 points. LaMarcus Aldridge led the way for the Spurs with a 33 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two blocks. DeMar DeRozan followed with 16 points, six assists, three rebounds and one block. Patty Mills turned in 15 points, two assists, one rebound and two steals. Bryn Forbes tallied 13 points, three boards and two assists. Rudy Gay generated an 11 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included seven assists. Bojan Bogdanovic paced the Pacers with 21 points and added two assists, one rebound and one steal. Domantas Sabonis filled in for Turner and posted a 19 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included four assists. Cory Joseph delivered 18 points to lead the bench. He also dished out seven assists and brought down four rebounds. Thad Young finished with 12 points, five rebounds, one assist and two steals. T.J. Leaf and Aaron Holiday managed matching 11 - point contributions. The Spurs remain on the road and head to Milwaukee to take on the Bucks on Saturday night, while the Pacers pay a visit to the Utah Jazz on Monday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 96 - 90, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday. The Pacers (14 - 10) and the Bulls (5 - 20) engaged on a tight ball on Indiana's home, but the hosts ended securing the win thanks to a solid performance in the second half. Indiana jumped to a 23 - 21 lead in the first quarter, but Chicago stormed back to secure a two - point lead at half time (45 - 43). Indiana would storm back in the third quarter, and a 27 - 22 lead saw them jump to a three - point advantage. The Bulls tried to fight back, but Indiana won the final 12 minutes of action by a 26 - 23 score. It was closer than expected, but the Pacers ended getting the job done. Even though the nine Pacers that saw action scored points, only four players scored in double digits. Darren Collison led the way with 23 points, eight rebounds and three assists, while Myles Turner contributed with 18 points, 11 rebounds, five blocks and three rebounds. Bojan Bogdanovic delivered 14 points and six rebounds, while Tyreke Evans filled the stat sheet thanks to 10 points, three rebounds, and two assists. Six Bulls players scored in double digits and Lauri Markkannen led the way thanks to 21 points, 10 rebounds, and two steals. Justin Holiday contributed 15 points, six rebounds and three assists, while Zach LaVine came close to a double - double thanks to 13 points and nine assists. Wendell Carter Jr. had 12 points and 13 rebounds. Jabari Parker had 12 points and eight rebounds coming off the bench.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 107 - 97, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Saturday. This was a tale of four quarters, as Indiana rode the second and fourth quarters to victory. In fact, the Pacers outscored the Kings, 64 - 48, in those 24 minutes. Indiana really finished strong, ending the game on a 23 - 14 run across the final eight minutes. Rebounding was key for the Pacers, as they out - rebounded the Kings, 52 - 43. They also dominated scoring down low, as they outscored the Kings in the paint, 56 - 46. Bench production was also huge, as Indiana had three bench players reach double figures in scoring while Sacramento had just one player reach that threshold. The Kings (13 - 12) were led by Buddy Hield, as he tallied 20 points and four rebounds. De'Aaron Fox accrued 18 points, six assists and two blocks. Willie Cauley-Stein totaled 14 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Bogdan Bogdanovic started and finished with 11 points, three rebounds, six assists and three steals while Nemanja Bjelica amassed six points and 12 boards. The Pacers (16 - 10) were led by Thaddeus Young, as he generated 20 points and nine rebounds. Bojan Bogdanovic accumulated 18 points, four rebounds and two assists. Darren Collison finished with 14 points, three rebounds and six assists while Myles Turner provided nine points, 13 rebounds and four blocks. Domantas Sabonis, Cory Joseph and Doug McDermott all reached double figures in scoring off the bench. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Indiana playing host to the Washington Wizards and Sacramento traveling to face the Chicago Bulls.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Washington Wizards, 109 - 101, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday evening. The Pacers (17 - 10) received an early wake - up call from the short - handed Wizards (11 - 16) in the first quarter, as they fell behind by a 33 - 29 margin. The light seemed to go on at that point, as Indiana exploded for 30 points over the ensuing 12 minutes while limiting Washington to 17. That gave them enough cushion to overcome some second - half surges by the visitors and emerge with the hard - fought victory. Indiana won despite turning the ball over on 23 occasions, with their big advantages in shooting (54 percent - 42 percent) and rebounding (50 - 34) integral to their success. Bradley Beal stepped up in the absence of John Wall (heel) and led the Wizards with 30 points, a total he supplemented with three rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Kelly Oubre, Jr. followed with 23 points, adding five rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block. Austin Rivers totaled 13 points, four assists. three rebounds and one steal. Thomas Bryant contributed 10 points, three rebounds and two rebounds. Myles Turner led the Pacers with a 26 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, five blocks and one steal. Bojan Bogdanovic poured in 22 points and also posted seven rebounds, two assists and one steal. Tyreke Evans supplied 18 points, six rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Thaddeus Young managed a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double, while Darren Collison mustered 10 points and dished out 17 assists. The Wizards head back home to tangle with the Boston Celtics on Wednesday evening, while the Pacers remain home for a divisional showdown with the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks, 113 - 97, at Bankers Life Field House on Wednesday evening. It was a good night for the Pacers as they finally got Victor Oladipo back in the lineup, and also grabbed their fifth straight win. The Pacers jumped out to a quick 8 - 2 lead, and pushed their advantage to 22 - 9, mid way though the first quarter. They held on to take a 29 - 23 lead into the second. The Pacers kept the pressure on the visitors, as they pushed their lead to 16 halfway through the second. They outscored the Bucks 29 - 20 in the quarter, to take a 58 - 43 lead by halftime. The Bucks came out stronger in the third quarter, but could not cut into the deficit, as they still trailed by 15 entering the final frame. The Pacers held their lead through the fourth, hardly letting the Bucks within reach, as they cruised to their 10th home win of the season. Thaddeus Young led the Pacers with 25 points, 11 rebounds, five steals, four assists and one block, in 33 minutes. Myles Turner followed up with 23 points, seven rebounds, four assists and three blocks, while Oladipo finished with 12 points, 10 rebounds, and six assists, in 29 minutes. The Pacers shot 48 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 26 points, six assists, two steals, one block and one rebound, in 33 minutes. Brook Lopez tallied 15 points, five rebounds, four blocks, one assists and one steal, while Giannis Antetokounmpo added 12 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists, in 31 minutes. The Bucks (18 - 9) will look to bounce back as they take on the Cavs in Cleveland on Friday. The Pacers (18 - 10) take on the 76ers in Philadelphia on Friday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 110 - 99, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Sunday. It's rare to see a game with 10 ties and 11 lead changes finish in a double - digit spread but that was the case here. All those swings happened in the first three quarters, as Indiana held the lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. In addition, the Pacers won all four individual quarters. Indiana's defense was critical, as they held New York to 41 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. The Pacers connected on 46 percent from the field and 35 percent from long range while out - assisting the Knicks, 28 - 21. Indiana's bench came up big too, outscoring New York's bench, 35 - 20. The Knicks (9 - 22) were led by Enes Kanter, as he totaled 20 points and 15 rebounds on 7 - of - 11 shooting. Tim Hardaway Jr. finished with 19 points, two rebounds, three assists and two steals. Emmanuel Mudiay amassed 18 points and six assists. Kevin Knox generated 15 points, four rebounds and two steals. The Pacers (20 - 10) got a vintage performance from Victor Oladipo, as he collected 26 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and five steals. Myles Turner tallied 24 points, six rebounds and two blocks. Bojan Bogdanovic accumulated 12 points, four rebounds and three assists while Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 13 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Monday. As for Indiana, they return to action on Tuesday when they play host to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers, 92 - 91, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday. The Cavaliers (8 - 23) were one of the worst teams in the Eastern Conference entering Tuesday's action, so there's no question that this win against the Pacers (20 - 11), who were riding a seven - game winning streak, should qualify as quite an upset. The game was tight and sloppy during most of the game, as both teams struggled from the field during the entire contest, but they saved the best for last. With Indiana up by only one point, Victor Oladipo missed two pivotal free throws, and that gave Cleveland a chance they wouldn't waste away. Rodney Hood missed a mid - range jumper, but Larry Nance Jr. tipped it home on the rebound to give the Cavs a huge win on the road, and their first one this season when they are trailing after three quarters. The final score in each quarter was: 21 - 19, 24 - 25, 22 - 24, 25 - 23. Larry Nance Jr. might have been the hero for Cleveland, but he also filled the stat sheet admirably in this game since he finished with 15 points, 16 rebounds, six assists, and three steals. Rodney Hood was the leading scorer with 17 points, and rookie Collin Sexton had 12 points. Cedi Osman chipped in with 13 points and seven rebounds, while Matthew Dellavedova (10 points, four assists) and Alec Burks (14 points) looked solid off the bench as well. Six Indiana players scored in double digits and Domantas Sabonis was the leading scorer thanks to a 17 - point, eight - rebound performance off the bench. Victor Oladipo had 12 points, but struggled from the field (4 - 15) and missed two clutch free throws. Bojan Bogdanovic added 14 points, and Myles Turner had a double - double of 12 points and 10 rebounds.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Washington Wizards, 105 - 89, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Sunday evening. The Pacers (22 - 12) came into the contest with a well - earned reputation for suffocating defense, and they'd use it frequently in their dominating win. The third quarter made all the difference, as Indiana outscored the Wizards (13 - 21) by a 31 - 18 margin during the period. Washington was clearly dealing with some fatigue in the second half, which was reflected in their 37 percent success rate from the field and 22 turnovers. They were also significantly out - hustled on the boards, losing the rebounding battle by a 57 - 37 margin. Markieff Morris paced the Wizards with 16 points and added six rebounds, one assist and one steal. Thomas Bryant produced 11 points and seven rebounds. Jeff Green tallied 10 points, three rebounds and two assists. Chasson Randle contributed 10 points off the bench. Bradley Beal (seven points, five assists, four rebounds, one steal) and John Wall (seven points, five rebounds, five assists, one steal) had underwhelming performances. Myles Turner led the Pacers with an 18 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two blocks and one steal. Domantas Sabonis followed with 15 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Bojan Bogdanovic finished with 14 points, three rebounds, two assists and three steals. Darren Collison and Victor Oladipo generated matching 12 - point tallies, with Oladipo also dishing out nine assists. Aaron Holiday poured in 12 points off the bench as well. The Wizards are back in action at home on Wednesday night against the Pistons, while the Pacers visit the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday evening as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 125 - 88, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Friday evening. The Pacers (24 - 12) set the tone for what would be a dominant win early, forging a 32 - 21 first - quarter lead. The Pistons (16 - 17) couldn't make any serious inroads into their deficit after that point, and Indiana's pinpoint shooting had a lot to do with it. The home squad shot an eye - popping 60 percent overall, with seven players hitting double digits in the scoring column. They were nearly as impressive on the defensive end, as they limited Detroit to 37 percent shooting - - including 25 percent from three - point range - - and forced them into 22 turnovers. Blake Griffin led the way for the Pistons with 18 points, a total he supplemented with seven rebounds and five assists. Luke Kennard followed with a bench - leading 14 points and added two rebounds and one steal. Reggie Bullock poured in 13 points and added three boards, one steal and one block. Andre Drummond generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks and one steal. Reggie Jackson mustered eight points, six assists and four rebounds. Darren Collison co - led the Pacers with 19 points and also provided seven assists, three rebounds and two steals. Domantas Sabonis matched Collison's scoring total and also pulled down 12 rebounds, dished out three assists and recorded one block. Myles Turner and Thaddeus Young had matching 17 - point tallies. Bojan Bogdanovic supplied 12 points, five rebounds and two assists. Doug McDermott had 12 of his own and also posted three boards. The Pistons remain on the road and tangle with the Orlando Magic on Sunday afternoon, while the Pacers remain home and face the Atlanta Hawks on Sunday afternoon as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 116 - 108, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday afternoon. The Pacers (25 - 12) were heavy favorites entering this game against the Hawks (11 - 25), and they made sure they would make that happen right from tip - off. Indiana quickly jumped to a 33 - 25 lead following the first quarter, but the Hawks showed some signs of life in the second quarter and made it a three - point game (63 - 60) at the half. The Pacers decided they didn't want to suffer any sort of scare, though, and pulled away for good in the third quarter (34 - 21) that made it 97 - 81. Such differential was impossible for Atlanta to turn around and despite the fact they they won the final quarter 27 - 19, it wasn't enough and Indiana won comfortably. Victor Oladipo led the way for the Pacers since he finished with 22 points, seven assists, four rebounds and four steals. Myles Turner contributed with 20 points, eight rebounds and four assists, while Domantas Sabonis chipped in with 20 points coming off the bench. Bojan Bogdanovic added 16 points, four rebounds and three assists, while Darren Collison had 12 points, six assists, four boards and two steals. Tyreke Evans also contributed with 10 points. John Collins and Kevin Huerter both led the way for the Hawks with 22 points, although they were only two of four players that managed to score in double digits for the Hawks. Alex Len contributed with 19 points and seven rebounds, while rookie point guard Trae Young chipped in with 16 points, seven assists, four rebounds and three steals.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 131 - 97, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday. Indiana came into this game as a huge favorite and a 131 - 97 scoreline vindicates that thought. A 38 - 19 first quarter really set the tone, as the Pacers won in wire - to - wire fashion. In addition, they won the first, third and fourth quarters by at least 11 points apiece. Defensive rebounding was big for Indiana, as they won that battle, 43 - 33. The assist - to - turnover differential was also decisive, with the Pacers recording five more assists than the Suns while committing five fewer turnovers. Indiana shot 52 percent from the field, 48 percent from three - point range and 75 percent from the free - throw line while Phoenix hit just 42 percent from the field, 30 percent from long range and 50 percent from the charity stripe. The Suns (11 - 34) were led by T.J. Warren, as he amassed 19 points and three boards. Devin Booker returned to provide eight points, five rebounds and five assists. DeAndre Ayton totaled 14 points and eight rebounds while Kelly Oubre Jr. led the bench with 16 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Pacers (29 - 14) were led by Bojan Bogdanovic, as he tallied 20 points, five rebounds and three assists. Myles Turner accrued 18 points, six rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Darren Collison finished with 15 points, four rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Thaddeus Young totaled 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists while Victor Oladipo generated eight points, six rebounds and five assists. Tyreke Evans led the bench with 20 points and four rebounds. Both teams return to action on Thursday, with Pheonix traveling to face the Toronto Raptors and Indiana playing host to the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Philadephia 76ers defeated the Indiana Pacers, 120 - 96, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Thursday evening. The Pacers (29 - 15) came in with a stellar 15 - 5 home record, while the 76ers (30 - 16) had limped to a 10 - 12 mark over their first 22 road contests. However, it was Philadelphia had a different look about them from the opening tip, and they went on to forge a 54 - 48 halftime lead. It was the third quarter when the visitors truly made their case, as they added nine more points to their advantage. The Sixers would go on to a comfortable victory, leveraging 53 percent shooting and a 51 - 40 rebounding advantage. Jimmy Butler led the way for the 76ers, posting 27 points, eight assists, five rebounds and three steals. Joel Embiid shook off a questionable designation due to back tightness to generate a 22 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists, three blocks and one steal. J.J. Redick poured in 20 points and added five assists and three rebounds. Ben Simmons and Mike Muscala contributed matching 11 - point tallies and hauled in eight and seven rebounds, respectively. Thaddeus Young led the Pacers with 27 points and also supplied six boards, one assist and one steal. Victor Oladipo had an especially rough shooting night, draining just six of 20 attempts on his way to 15 points. He added seven assists and two rebounds. Tyreke Evans followed with a bench - leading 13 points. Bojan Bogdanovic turned in nine points, one rebound and one assist. Myles Turner mustered just eight points but brought down 12 rebounds, recorded three steals and posted three blocks. The 76ers head back home and take on the Oklahoma City Thunder on Saturday afternoon. The Pacers remain home and tangle with the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 111 - 99, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the Mavs led for most of the first quarter, before the Pacers pulled ahead by one, to take a 24 - 23 lead into the second quarter. The Pacers carried the momentum and outscored the visitors by 15 in the second, to take a 58 - 42 lead into halftime. Things tightened up again in the third, but the Mavs could not do much, as they only cut into the deficit by one point, entering the final frame down by 15. The Mavericks kept chipping away through the fourth and cut the lead to single digits, however the Pacers were able to hold their position and walk away with the home win. Tyreke Evans led the Pacers with 19 points on 7 - of - 11 shooting, and two assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. Domantas Sabonis followed up with 16 points, 11 rebounds and two assists, in 27 minutes off the bench, while Darren Collison tallied 16 points, three rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. Meanwhile, Harrison Barnes led the Mavericks with 20 points on 6 - of - 15 shooting, three rebounds and two assists, in 32 minutes. DeAndre Jordan followed up with 15 points and 16 rebounds, while Wesley Matthews tallied 17 points, three rebounds and two assists. Luka Doncic finished with eight points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals. The Mavs (20 - 25) will look to avoid a fourth straight loss as they take on the Bucks in Milwaukee on Monday. The Pacers (30 - 15) play host to the Hornets on Sunday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 120 - 95, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Sunday evening. The Pacers got out to a great start at home, with a 34 - 26 lead after one quarter. They kept up the pressure in the second, where they outscored the visitors by seven, to take a 56 - 41 lead by halftime. The Hornets picked it up in the third quarter, as they outscored the Pacers 30 - 27 in the quarter, but still trailed by 12, heading into the final frame. However, the Pacers put the finishing touches on the contest in the final frame, as they outscored the Hornets by 13 in the quarter, to cruise to their second straight win. Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 21 points, seven assists, three steals and two rebounds, in 31 minutes. Darren Collison followed up with 19 points, nine assists, three rebounds and two steals, while Domantas Sabonis added 16 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Pacers shot 47 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 23 points, seven assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block, in 36 minutes. Bismack Biyombo finished with 10 points, 12 rebounds and one block, while Malik Monk added 11 points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 15 minutes off the bench. The Hornets shot 40 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 35 from long range. The Hornets (22 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Wednesday. The Pacers (31 - 15) play host to the Raptors on Wednesday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 110 - 106, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Wednesday. While Indiana led for 47 minutes of this 48 - minute game. it came down the wire. In fact, the Raptors overcame a 12 - point halftime deficit to make it a two - point game with a few minutes remaining. They simply couldn't recapture the lead or tie though, as Indiana hit some free throws late to seal the win. The Pacers defense was key, as they held the Raptors to 41 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. They also recorded six steals and seven blocks while Toronto picked up just two steals and five blocks. The Raptors (36 - 14) were led by Serge Ibaka, as he tallied 23 points, 11 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Kyle Lowry finished with 20 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Pascal Siakam accrued 16 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Fred VanVleet started again and provided 14 points, two rebounds and three assists. The Pacers (32 - 15) were led by Thaddeus Young, as he collected 23 points, 15 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks. The big story is Victor Oladipo though, as he was carted off with what appeared to be a serious knee injury. Darren Collison totaled 17 points, four rebounds and eight assists while Myles Turner amassed 13 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks. Toronto returns to action on Friday, as they travel to face the Houston Rockets. Indiana's next game will be on Saturday, as they play the Memphis Grizzlies on the road.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 136 - 94, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday evening. The Pacers (35 - 19) were looking to continue steadying the ship after losing Victor Oladipo (knee) for the season recently, and the Lakers (27 - 27) ended up being the unfortunate team that was in their way. Indiana essentially sealed the win with a 69 - point first half, but they were almost as prolific in the second while putting up another 67. Unsurprisingly, shooting was a strong point for the host squad, as they drained 57 percent of their attempts, including 56 from three - point range. Moreover, the Pacers saw seven players hit double digits in the scoring column. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 18 points, adding nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal. JaVale McGee furnished 16 points, four boards and one steal. Lance Stephenson poured in 13 points. Brandon Ingram and Kyle Kuzma generated matching 12 - point tallies, with Ingram notably hauling in six boards as well. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 24 points, supplementing them with five assists, one rebound and one steal. Myles Turner supplied 22 points and four blocks. Aaron Holiday, Domantas Sabonis and Edmond Sumner provided matching 17 - point contributions. Cory Joseph registered 13 points, four rebounds and four assists. Thaddeus Young stuffed the stat sheet with 12 points, 11 rebounds, eight assists and two steals. The Lakers next visit the Boston Celtics on Thursday evening, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday night as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 116 - 92, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Thursday. The Pacers (36 - 19) and the Clippers (30 - 26) were expected to be involved in a tight contest, but Indiana didn't have problems to dominate the game entirely and cruise to a huge win over Los Angeles. The Pacers quickly jumped to a five - point lead in the first quarter (36 - 31), but they ran away with the game in the second quarter where they opened up the gap to 18 points following a 35 - 22 run. Adding insult to the injury, the Clippers won the third quarter 27 - 20 and the game was essentially over from there. The Clippers won the final quarter 19 - 18, but they couldn't mount any sort of a comeback and Indiana cruised their way to a solid win. Bojan Bogdanovic was the top scorer for the Pacers since he finished with 29 points and seven rebounds. Myles Turner added 17 points with four blocks, and Darren Collison contributed 14 points and five assists. Thaddeus Young filled the stat sheet nicely since he ended the contest with 14 points, five rebounds, five steals and four assists. Cory Joseph chipped in with 13 points, nine boards and six assists off the bench. Montrezl Harrell was the top scorer for the Clippers since he contributed 19 points and four assists, but he also committed six turnovers. Danilo Gallinari had 12 points and also added five rebounds. No other Clipper in the starting lineup topped the 10 - point mark, but two bench players did it since both Lou Williams and Johnathan Motley had 10 points each.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 105 - 90, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Saturday night. The Pacers (37 - 19) came into Saturday's game showing signs of progress following some early struggles after Victor Oladipo's season - ending knee injury, as they'd won four consecutive contests. They showed every intention of keeping up their strong play early by jumping out to a 30 - 17 first - quarter lead. While the Cavaliers (11 - 44) were much more competitive in the second quarter, they only shaved one point off their deficit and couldn't make any further inroads. Jordan Clarkson led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points, adding six assists and two rebounds. Larry Nance, Jr. and Collin Sexton each posted 16 points, with Nance notably hauling in 10 rebounds. No other Cleveland player managed double - digit scoring, although Brandon Knight came closest with nine points off the bench in his team debut. Marquese Chriss drew the start at power forward but pitched in just seven points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 23 points and supplemented them with two assists and one rebound. Darren Collison delivered 18 points, nine assists, one rebound and one steal. Myles Turner compiled 14 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. Domantas Sabonis generated a 13 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Cory Joseph provided 10 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds and one steal. The Cavaliers head back home to take on the New York Knicks on Monday night, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Monday evening as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 99 - 90, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday evening. The Pacers (38 - 19) were already trending up coming into Monday's contest, and they opened the game seemingly intent on continuing their excellent stretch of play. Wesley Matthews offered eight points, five rebounds and three assists in his Indiana debut. The Hornets next pay a visit to the Orlando Magic on Thursday night, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 106 - 97, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Wednesday. In a battle between two of the best teams in the Eastern Conference, this game came down to the wire. In fact, there were nine lead changes in this game, as neither team led by more than 10 points in the second half. Milwaukee ended the game strong, as they went on an 110 run with 4:45 remaining to make it a nine - point margin with one minute remaining. Rebounding was key for Milwaukee, as they outrebounded Indiana, 52 - 43. They also dominated through scoring down low, outscoring the Pacers in the paint, 58 - 32. The Bucks (43 - 14) got another monster game from Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 33 points, 19 rebounds, 11 assists and two steals en route to a triple - double. Myles Turner accumulated 11 points, six rebounds, two assists and two blocks while Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 14 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two steals. On deck for Milwaukee is a home matchup after the break against the Boston Celtics on February 21. As for Indiana, they'll play host to the New Orleans Pelicans on the 22nd for their next fixture.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 126 - 111, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Friday. While New Orleans led by 20 points in the second quarter, they allowed Indiana to win in comeback fashion. In fact, the Pacers outscored the Pelicans, 68 - 40, in the second half. Indiana's defense was critical, as they won the turnover differential, 18 - 11 while doubling them up in steals, 10 - 5. Anthony Davis led the starters, as he amassed 15 points, eight rebounds and four assists in just 19 minutes. Julius Randle accumulated 15 points, four rebounds and two assists while Jrue Holiday finished with 14 points, seven rebounds and four assists. The Pacers (39 - 20) were led by Wesley Matthews, as he amassed 24 points and two boards. Bojan Bogdanovic accrued 20 points, five rebounds and two assists. Thaddeus Young totaled 16 points, seven rebounds and four steals while Darren Collison generated 10 points and 12 assists. Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 18 points, 13 rebounds and four assists. Both teams have to play again on Saturday, with New Orleans playing host to the Los Angeles Lakers and Indiana traveling to face the Washington Wizards.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 115, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Thursday. The Timberwolves (29 - 33) entered this game against the Pacers (41 - 22) in a good run of form with four wins in their last six games, and it showed since they quickly got themselves on top by nine points after the first quarter (35 - 26). However, the Pacers would flip the script in the second quarter and they got in the driver seat by halftime thanks to a huge 38 - 25 period that gave them a 64 - 60 lead. Minnesota made things tighter since they won the third quarter 30 - 28, and as a result, this was a two - point game heading into the final 12 minutes of action. Indiana didn't let the game slip away, however, and a 30 - 25 score in the fourth quarter sealed the deal in their favor. The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 124 - 88, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Sunday afternoon. The Indiana Pacers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 111 - 102, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Monday. The Boston Celtics defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 117 - 97, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Friday. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 108 - 96, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Sunday. This game meant much more to Brooklyn than Indiana and that was evident in the result. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 107 - 98, at Smoothie King Center on Wednesday evening. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 125 - 115, at Smoothie King Center on Saturday. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 140 - 126, at Smoothie King Center on Monday. The Boston Celtics defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 124 - 107, at Smoothie King Center on Monday It's been a tough stretch for the Celtics (11 - 10) here in late November, but they managed to pick up a marquee win against one of the NBA's more talented teams after dropping four of their last five games. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 132 - 106, at Smoothie King Center on Wednesday. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 103 - 100, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Detroit Pistons, 113 - 103, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 115 - 108, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Tuesday. The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 106 - 95, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Wednesday. While there were eight ties and 13 lead changes in the first half, Detroit led for the final 20 minutes of this game. In fact, a 31 - 17 third quarter really made the difference, as that gave them a game - high 22 - point lead. Rebounding was the difference for the Pistons, as they outrebounded the Wizards, 46 - 31. They also dominated through ball movement, out - assisting Washington, 25 - 17. Free-throw shooting was also a big factor, with Detroit hitting 18 - of - 19 and Washington connecting on just 10 - of - 13. The Wizards (13 - 22) were led by John Wall, as he tallied 21 points, seven rebounds and eight assists. Bradley Beal accrued 21 points, four rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Trevor Ariza finished with 16 points, five rebounds and three steals. Markieff Morris led the bench with 12 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals. The Pistons (16 - 16) were led by Blake Griffin, as he accumulated 23 points, nine rebounds, six assists and two steals. Reggie Jackson amassed 19 points, four rebounds and six assists. Andre Drummond collected 16 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. Langston Galloway was huge off the bench, providing 22 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Detroit traveling to face the Indiana Pacers and Washington playing host to the Chicago Bulls.

The Utah Jazz defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 110 - 105, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Saturday. It's hard to believe that Detroit led 31 - 13 after the first quarter and lost this game, as this marked Utah's biggest comeback of the season. A 35 - 22 second quarter got them right back into it, as they ended up outscoring the Pistons by 23 points across the final three quarters. Defense is what got the Jazz back into the game, as they recorded 11 steals and six blocks while holding the Pistons to under 40 percent from the field in those final three quarters. The assist - to - turnover ratio was decisive as well, with Utah recording 24 assists to 12 turnovers while Detroit matched their 18 turnovers with 18 assists. The Jazz (20 - 20) were led by Donovan Mitchell, as he tallied 26 points, five rebounds, five assists and three steals. Ricky Rubio finished with 18 points, two rebounds and four assists. Joe Ingles totaled 16 points, four rebounds and two steals. Derrick Favors amassed 13 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks. The Pistons (17 - 20) were led by Blake Griffin, as he collected 34 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and two steals. Reggie Bullock scored 18 points to go along with three rebounds and two assists. Andre Drummond accumulated 15 points, 18 rebounds and three steals while Bruce Brown tallied 12 points, three rebounds and seven assists. On deck for Detroit is a home matchup versus the San Antonio Spurs on Monday. As for Utah, they travel to face the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday for their next outing.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Detroit Pistons, 119 - 107, at Little Caesars Arena on Monday evening. The Spurs (24 - 17) and the Pistons (17 - 21) were expected to play a back - and - forth game, and that's what happened... at least during the first half of action. Detroit jumped to a rather surprising 31 - 25 following the first quarter, but San Antonio turned things around and a 34 - 20 advantage in the second quarter saw them go up by eight points (59 - 51) entering the break. The Spurs would dominate the second half completely, and they won the remaining two quarters, 25 - 22 and 35 - 34 respectively, as they ended cruising their way towards a comfortable win on the road. With the win, San Antonio extended their positive run: they have won 13 of their last 16 games. As it has been the case during the entire season, DeMar DeRozan (26 points, nine assists, seven rebounds) and LaMarcus Aldridge (25 points, six rebounds). They got help, though, since Derrick White contributed 17 points and Bryn Forbes registered 15 points. The bench provided a nice boost as well - Patty Mills chipped in with 13 points, while sharp - shooter Marco Belinelli had nine points in 21 minutes. Blake Griffin led the way for the Pistons despite the loss since he finished with 31 points and eight assists, flourishing in his primary ball - handler role. Andre Drummond filled the stat sheet nicely since he contributed 19 points, 14 rebounds, three steals and two assists. Reggie Jackson had 14 points and Reggie Bullock chipped in with 13 points and four boards.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Orlando Magic, 120 - 115 in OT, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday night. The Pistons (19 - 24) and the Magic (19 - 25) were expected to play an intense, down - to - the - wire contest, and they didn't disappoint since they needed an overtime period to find a winner. Orlando jumped to a 34 - 26 lead in the first, but Detroit rallied back and won the two subsequent quarters, 32 - 29 and 32 - 21, to gain a six - point lead entering the fourth quarter. But a 25 - 19 lead for the Magic in the fourth extended the game towards an OT period; the final five minutes of action, however, saw Detroit win 11 - 6, so they secured a huge win in front of their crowd. Six Detroit players scored in double digits as Blake Griffin led the way with an impressive 30 - point effort, while Andre Drummond delivered a strong double - double of 14 points and 22 rebounds. Both Reggie Bullock and Reggie Jackson chipped in with 13 points, while two bench players reached the 10 - point mark: Luke Kennard had 14 points and Langston Galloway added 13. As it has been the case all season long, Nikola Vucevic led the way for the Magic with 24 points, 13 rebounds, and three assists. Evan Fournier had 18 points, while Aaron Gordon came close to a double - double after finishing with 12 points and eight boards before getting fouled out. Terrence Ross had an impressive effort coming off the bench since he ended with 24 points in 33 minutes of action.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Miami Heat, 98 - 93, at Little Caesars Arena on Friday evening. The Pistons (20 - 24) got out to a start befitting a team with a much better record, as they owned a 30 - 17 lead after one quarter. While they were within one as late as the 20 second - mark of the fourth quarter, a pair of free throws apiece by Reggie Jackson and Blake Griffin sealed the hard - fought victory. Dwyane Wade led the way for the Heat with 20 points, adding eight assists and four rebounds. Tyler Johnson supplied 16 points, five rebounds, three dimes and one block. Justise Winslow supplied 15 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one steal. Rodney McGruder managed 11 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. Bam Adebayo pitched in nine points, six rebounds, one assist and one block. Hassan Whiteside mustered just eight points but hauled in 10 rebounds. Griffin paced the Pistons with 32 points and supplemented them with 11 rebounds, nine assists and one steal. Luke Kennard furnished 22 points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Reggie Bullock poured in 19 points. Stanley Johnson delivered 12 points, six rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Jackson contributed nine points, five boards and two assists. The Heat remains on the road and takes on the Chicago Bulls on Saturday evening, while the Pistons remain home and take on the Sacramento Kings on Saturday night.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 103 - 101, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Saturday. While Detroit led for the majority of this game, Sacramento was able to prevail with victory. In fact, Sacramento rode a 29 - 19 fourth quarter to victory, as Buddy Hield hit a game - winning three at the buzzer. The Kings actually ended the game on an 8 - 2 run. Zaza Pachulia started for Andre Drummond, as he totaled seven points, 12 rebounds and three assists. Luke Kennard led the bench with 19 points, three rebounds and two assists. Bruce Brown Jr. accumulated six points, 10 rebounds and four assists. On deck for Detroit is a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Monday. As for Sacramento, they return to action on Monday when they face the Brooklyn Nets on the road.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Detroit Pistons, 115 - 105, at Little Caesars Arena on Tuesday evening. The Bucks (36 - 13) came out of the gates hot, compiling 62 points in the first half on their way to a 13 - point halftime lead. The Bucks next pay a visit to the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night, while the Pistons remain home to tangle with the Dallas Mavericks on Thursday evening as well.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 93 - 89, at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday night. The Mavericks (23 - 28) had to have a bit of collective whiplash coming into Thursday's contest, considering the amount of players the exited and entered the franchise, at least on paper, earlier in the day. In the wake of a blockbuster trade between Dallas and the Knicks that saw marquee names like Kristaps Porzingis, Tim Hardaway, Jr., Dennis Smith, Jr. and DeAndre Jordan change uniforms, the Mavs took the court extremely short - handed. Their rotation was made even thinner by the notable absence of Luka Doncic (ankle), so it was certainly a testament to their grit when they jumped out to a 49 - 45 halftime lead. The visitors looked like they might pull off a rather improbable upset over the Pistons (22 - 28) well into the fourth quarter before Detroit finished on an 18 - 11 run over the final 6:17 to secure the win. Harrison Barnes paced the Mavericks with 27 points, adding seven rebounds and four assists. Devin Harris supplied 15 points, four rebounds and three assists. Dwight Powell was the only other double - digit scorer for Dallas, turning in 10 points, five rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal. Jalen Brunson registered nine points, six assists and two rebounds. Dirk Nowitzki and Ryan Broekhoff generated matching seven - point tallies. Andre Drummond and Blake Griffin co - led the Pistons with 24 points, and they notably hauled in 20 and 10 rebounds, respectively. Reggie Jackson managed 17 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and two steals. Langston Galloway managed 11 points, three boards and one block. Reggie Bullock had just four points on 1 - for - 8 shooting. The Mavericks next pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday night, while the Pistons remain home and tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Saturday afternoon as well.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 111 - 101, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Saturday. When Detroit led 40 - 22 after the first quarter, this game looked over but Los Angeles had other ideas. In fact, they got back into the game thanks to a 29 - 22 third quarter and completed their epic comeback with an incredible 34 - 15 fourth quarter. The Clippers ended up shooting close to 60 percent in the second half while holding the Pistons to 38 percent from the field.
