The Clippers (29 - 24) were led by Lou Williams, as he scored 16 of their final 18 points, finishing with 39 points, three rebounds and nine assists off the bench. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was the only starter in double figures, as he accrued 14 points, seven rebounds, five assists and three steals. Montrezl Harrell amassed 16 points and seven rebounds off the bench while Boban Marjanovic recorded a minimal 10 - point, 10 - rebound double - double in 16 minutes. The Pistons (22 - 29) were led by Reggie Jackson, as he collected 29 points, two rebounds and seven assists. Blake Griffin tallied 24 points, 11 rebounds and six assists. Reggie Bullock totaled 19 points and four boards while Andre Drummond accumulated 12 points, 11 rebounds, two steals and three blocks. On deck for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the Toronto Raptors on Sunday. As for Detroit, they return to action on Monday when they play host to the Detroit Pistons.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Denver Nuggets, 129 - 103, at Little Caesars Arena on Monday. The Pistons (23 - 29) were coming off five losses in their previous seven matches, while the Nuggets (37 - 16) entered this game riding a six - game winning run, so it seemed Denver were the favorites on paper but things looked different after tip - off. Denver finished the first quarter leading by two points (36 - 34), but they disappeared off the court during the remainder of the game. Detroit took full control of the contest thanks to a huge performance during the second quarter (34 - 19), so they entered half - time up by 13 points (68 - 55). Detroit would also win the subsequent two quarters (29 - 28 and 32 - 20, respectively), and they secured a huge win in front of their crowd. One that could mean quite a morale boost going forward. Seven Detroit players scored in double digits in this one. Andre Drummond led the way with an impressive 27 - point, 12 - rebound performance, while Blake Griffin registered 17 points, seven rebounds, and four assists. Reggie Jackson had 14 points and Reggie Bullock added 11, but the bench played a big role as well. Stanley Johnson had 21 points and seven rebounds, Langston Galloway chipped in with 18 points, and Luke Kennard added 14 points, four rebounds and four assists. The five starters for Denver scored in double digits, but the top scorer came off the bench since Trey Lyles had 20 points. Monte Morris had 18 points, while Nikola Jokic added 16 points, and Mason Plumlee contributed 15 points and 11 rebounds. Malik Beasley finished with 16 points, and Will Barton impressed with 10 points and seven assists.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 120 - 103, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Friday. While New York grabbed the first lead in this game, that was the only time they were competitive. In fact, Detroit rode a 41 - 22 first quarter to an easy victory, as they led by 23 points at times in a 31 - 19 fourth quarter. The Pistons ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 43 percent from three - point range while holding the Knicks to 45 percent from the field and 32 percent from long range. Detroit also outrebounded New York, 46 - 39. The Knicks (10 - 44) got a career - best 31 points from Dennis Smith Jr. as he added two rebounds, eight assists and two steals to his tally. DeAndre Jordan totaled 14 points, 11 rebounds and two blocks. Damyean Dotson accrued 10 points, two rebounds and two assists while Mitchell Robinson led the bench with 11 points, six rebounds and three blocks. The Pistons (25 - 29) got a monster double - double from Andre Drummond, as he collected 29 points, 20 rebounds, two assists and three blocks. Blake Griffin finished with 26 points, six rebounds and four assists. Reggie Jackson accumulated 20 points, two rebounds and six assists. Luke Kennard led the bench with 12 points, three rebounds and three assists. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Toronto Raptors on Saturday. As for Detroit, they're off until Monday when they play host to the Washington Wizards.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 121 - 112, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Monday. A 36 - 27 first quarter really set the tone in this game, as Detroit led throughout. A 29 - 20 third quarter was the nail in the coffin, as the Pistons led by at least five points for the final 16 minutes. Rebounding was the difference for Detroit, as they outrebounded Washington, 48 - 37. They did damage scoring down low too, as the Pistons outscored the Wizards in the paint, 56 - 40. Both offenses were on point, as they each shot above 50 percent from the field. The Wizards (24 - 33) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 32 points, six rebounds, 10 assists and two steals. Trevor Ariza accumulated 23 points, seven rebounds, five assists and two steals. Bobby Portis led the bench with 24 points, five rebounds and two steals. No other player scored more than 10 points. The Pistons (26 - 29) got a near triple - double from Blake Griffin, as he led the way with 31 points, nine rebounds and nine assists. Andre Drummond collected 32 points 17 rebounds and four steals. Reggie Jackson totaled 16 points and six assists. Luke Kennard led the bench with 15 points, three rebounds and two assists. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Detroit traveling to face the Boston Celtics and Washington facing the Toronto Raptors on the road as well.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Indiana Pacers, 113 - 109, at Little Caesars Arena on Monday evening. The Pistons (29 - 30) and the Pacers (40 - 21) met this Monday but the game didn't happen as many would have expected. Despite the gap between both franchises' records this season, Detroit started better and dominated the first quarter with no problems, quickly jumping to a 16 - point lead after the first 12 minutes (36 - 20). Indiana answered with a 31 - 19 second quarter, so the Pistons were up by four at the break although they re - extended their lead with a 29 - 26 third period. Detroit entered the fourth quarter up by seven points so it was up grabs and even though Indiana won the final quarter 32 - 29, the Pistons held on and secured a huge win. It was a very intense game, as evidenced by the fact that both Blake Griffin and Thaddeus Young were caught shoving opponents throughout the game. Andre Drummond led the Pistons offensively with 26 points and 16 rebounds, but Blake Griffin also had an impressive performance and finished with a triple - double thanks to 20 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Reggie Jackson and Wayne Ellington each had 14 points, although the injury - prone point guard also added five assists. Luke Kennard (19 points) and Langston Galloway (13 points) looked solid off the bench. Bojan Bogdanovic was the best player for the Pacers had 25 points but also added four rebounds, and Darren Collison chipped in with 21 points, five assists, three rebounds and two steals. Wesley Matthews had 14 points, and Thaddeus Young chipped in with 10 points and 12 rebounds. Domantas Sabonis delivered an impressive effort off the bench since he finished with 23 points and seven boards.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors in overtime, 112 - 107, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Sunday. On deck for Toronto is a home matchup versus the high - flying Houston Rockets on Tuesday. As for Detroit, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 131 - 114, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday night. The Timberwolves (30 - 35) came out of the gates hot, as they forged a 35 - 22 lead over the Pistons (32 - 31) in the first 12 minutes. However, that would prove to be the highlight of the night for Minnesota, considering the hosts outscored them by a 109 - 79 margin over the final three periods. Detroit scored no fewer than 30 points in any of those quarters, and they were exemplary on both the shooting and turnover front. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Chicago Bulls, 131 - 108, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday. The Bulls (19 - 41) got off to a solid start in this game and they actually jumped ahead following the first quarter (32 - 31), but that would be as far as they would get when it comes to leading the contest. Wayne Ellington had 13 points, and Langston Galloway offered instant offense off the bench with 21 points in 29 minutes. Lauri Markkanen had 17 points with six rebounds, and Otto Porter Jr. also had 17 points with six boards. Shaquille Harrison contributed 11 points and seven assists coming off the bench, while Ryan Arcidiacono added 10 points with three rebounds and two assists.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 111 - 97, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Friday. The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 110 - 107, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Sunday. In this potential playoff preview, it came down to the final shot. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Orlando Magic, 115 - 98, at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday evening. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 99 - 90, at Little Caesars Arena on Saturday night. After a first quarter that was a defensive slugfest, the two teams matched each other bucket for bucket in the second but still headed into halftime with only 65 combined points. The Indiana Pacers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 108 - 89, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday. The Pacers (47 - 32) wanted to earn a second - consecutive win over the Pistons (39 - 39) and that's exactly what they accomplished, although they far more dominant in this one. Bojan Bogdanovic had 17 points, four rebounds and three assists, while Myles Turner chipped in with 17 points and five boards. Cory Joseph thrived with 12 assists as well as six points. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Detroit Pistons, 104 - 91, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Hornets (38 - 42) and Pistons (39 - 41) both came into the contest with a chance at the postseason, but Detroit's chances were considerably higher. Considering they were also on their home floor, the boys from Motown figured to come out of the gates especially focused for the afternoon showdown. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 116 - 104, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday evening. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 127 - 106, at Scotiabank Arena on Monday night. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 116 - 107, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 129 - 112, at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday evening. Redick (13 points) and Mike Muscala (12 points, five boards) both looked solid off the bench.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Toronto Raptors, 126 - 110, at Scotiabank Arena on Monday evening. Anunoby added 17 points off the bench. Kyle Lowry struggled and only managed to score four points (1 - 9 from the field) but added 11 assists.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Washington Wizards, 123 - 101, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 122 - 105, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday night. The Houston Rockets defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 107 - 91, at Toyota Center on Friday evening. The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 118 - 106, at Toyota Center on Monday evening. The Golden State Warriors defeated the Houston Rockets, 106 - 104, at Toyota Center on Wednesday evening. The Houston Rockets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 108 - 102, at Toyota Center on Friday night. The Houston Rockets defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 117 - 102, at Toyota Center on Sunday evening. A scorching - hot third quarter helped Houston (44 - 26) open up a double - digit lead. The Magic (3 - 6) came into the contest in the midst of a tailspin, as they'd lost six of their previous seven games. However, they seemed like a different team from the start, as they took a 36 - 26 first - quarter lead. Even though the Spurs (6 - 3) regrouped to an extent in the second period, Orlando still took a 17 - point lead into the final 12 minutes, which gave them more than enough cushion to withstand a run by the home squad in the fourth quarter and escape with the win. The Magic drained 50 percent of their shots and turned the ball over just eight times, both keys to victory. Aaron Gordon led the way with 26 points, which he supplemented with eight rebounds and one steal. D.J. Augustin supplied 18 points, seven assists and five rebounds. Terrance Ross managed 17 points, four assists and three rebounds. Evan Fournier turned in 16 points and dished out seven dimes. Nikola Vucevic provided 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 25 points and added seven rebounds, five assists and two steals. Patty Mills paced the bench with 16 points. Marco Belinelli followed with 15 points in 21 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge collected 14 points, six rebounds and three assists. Bryn Forbes tallied 13 points, two assists and a rebound. The Magic head back home to take on the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday night, while the Spurs pay a visit to the Miami Heat on Wednesday evening.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 96 - 89, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The game got out to an interesting start, as the Spurs led, 17 - 8, six and a half minutes in, but then did not score for the next five minutes, as the Rockets caught up and managed to close the quarter with a 21 - 20 advantage. The game stayed close through the second, but the Spurs managed to pull back ahead, taking a 52 - 50 lead into halftime. The Spurs kept the momentum in the third, as they pulled ahead by seven halfway through the quarter, but the Rockets rallied back again, to make it a one - point game, as they trailed, 72 - 71, heading into the final frame. The fourth quarter featured more back - and - forth action, as the Spurs led, 86 - 85, with just over three minutes left. The Spurs held on and closed the game, as they outscored the Rockets 10 - 4 in the final minutes, to earn the impressive home win. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 27 points, 10 rebounds, one assist and one block, in 35 minutes. DeMar DeRozan tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds and three assists, while Derrick White tallied 14 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 29 minutes. The Spurs shot 45 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 20 from long range. Meanwhile, James Harden led the way for the Rockets with 25 points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 38 minutes. Clint Capela tallied 12 points, 17 rebounds, two blocks and an assist, while Eric Gordon added 23 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 30 minutes off the bench. Carmelo Anthony (illness) did not suit up. The Rockets (4 - 7) will look to avoid a third straight loss as they play host to the Pacers on Sunday. The Spurs (7 - 4) take on the Kings in Sacramento on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Golden State Warriors 104 - 92 at AT & T Center on Sunday. The Spurs returned home and picked up a needed win to end the three game losing streak they carried into the contest, although the win will be overshadowed by the beat up Warriors lineup that was run in light of Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe) being sidelined. The Warriors announced that Curry will be reevaluated in a week and have struggled to find an offensive rhythm without the two - time MVP in the lineup. On Sunday, the firepower from behind the arc was lacking, which in turn kept the Warriors just out of the lead every quarter. The Warriors (12 - 6) shot 5 - of - 26 from three, and needed 51 points on 51 shots combined from Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson. One half of the splash brothers did hit a big time three with 3:38 remaining in the fourth quarter to pull the game within one point, but the Spurs (8 - 7) came back with seven unanswered points on the backs of DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge to put the game away. DeRozan had 20 points, six rebounds and nine assists on 8 - of - 19 shooting, while Aldridge posted 24 points, 18 rebounds and two blocks. The Warriors mixed in Damian Jones and Quinn Cook for 23 minutes and 29 minutes, respectively, to try and answer the subtraction of Curry and Green. Cook contributed 16 points on 7 - of - 12 shooting, to go with eight rebounds and two assists. Next up, the Spurs go back on the road to take on the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, while the Warriors host the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 104 - 103, at AT & T Center on Wednesday. The Grizzlies (12 - 5) continue to be one of the biggest surprises of the NBA, as Wednesday's victory in San Antonio was their fifth straight, and they now boast the best record in the Western Conference. The win didn't come easy, however, as a DeMar DeRozan jumper that put the Spurs (8 - 9) up one with 1 seconds ago appeared to have sealed the deal for the home team. Memphis managed to catch a break shortly after, though, as Marc Gasol drew a foul with under a second left and knocked down two game - winning free throws. Gasol finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds in 35 minutes, but it was point guard Mike Conley who led the way for the Grizzlies, as he scored a game - high 30 points to go along with nine assists in 35 minutes of his own. Gasol and Conley were the only Memphis starters to reach double figures, while JaMychal Green and Omri Casspi put up 12 and 11 points respectively off the bench. As for the Spurs, they were once again led by DeMar DeRozan, who briefly thought he was the hero with hardly any time remaining on the game clock. DeRozan finished with a team - high 24 points on 10 - of - 20 shooting in addition to five assists and five rebounds in 37 minutes. Rudy Gay added 21 points of his own on 7 - of - 10 shooting. LaMarcus Aldridge struggled shooting from the field, going a brutal 6 - of - 20, but he still managed to finish with a double - double of 19 points and 11 rebounds in 41 minutes.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 136 - 105, at AT & T Center on Friday evening. The Rockets jumped out to a great start on the road, as they matched the Spurs with a 9 - 9 score after the first few minutes, before they outscored the home team, 30 - 12, through the remainder of the quarter. The Rockets carried the momentum in to the second, where they pushed their lead to 25, halfway through the quarter. The Spurs had no answer, as they trailed 70 - 47, at halftime. The third quarter did not bring any better luck for San Antonio, as the Rockets pushed their lead to 30, and went on to outscore the Spurs, 40 - 27, in the quarter, to take a, 110 - 74, lead into the final frame. None of the Spurs' starters played in the fourth, as they dropped their second game in a row. Clint Capela led the Rockets with 27 points, 12 rebounds, four blocks, one assist and a steal, in 29 minutes. Eric Gordon followed up with 26 points, three rebounds and two assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. James Harden finished with 23 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and one block, in 27 minutes. The Rockets shot 50 percent from the field, including 22 - of - 54 from long range. Meanwhile, LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 20 points, six rebounds and two blocks, in 30 minutes. DeMar DeRozan followed up with 18 points, five assists, two rebounds and two steals, in 26 minutes, while Derrick White chipped in 11 points, nine assists and five rebounds, in 33 minutes off the bench. The Spurs shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 28 from deep. The Spurs (10 - 12) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Sunday. The Rockets (10 - 11) play host to the Bulls on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Portland Trail Blazers 131 - 118 on Sunday at AT & T Center. The final score did not depict the back and forth nature of this battle as the Spurs were able to pull away early in the fourth quarter with big time scores from Rudy Gay, DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge. The game itself had over 10 ties and nearly 20 lead changes, with the all - star back court of Damian Lillard and CJ McCollum firing on all cylinders trying to match the Spurs all - stars in the process. Portland (13 - 10) entered the fourth quarter down 97 - 90, but McCollum drained a three pointer right out the gate to pull within four. Rudy Gay answered with his vintage mid - range jumper and that was the nature of the final period. Anytime the Blazers pulled within the reach, the Spurs (11 - 12) answered immediately and did damage in the paint, which led to easy free throws. DeRozan finished with 36 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals. Aldridge contributed 29 points and eight boards. Derrick White found a clutch rhythm off the bench and knocked down 4 - of - 7 from the field on his way to 10 points, while Patty Mills added 15 points in 25 minutes. Lillard led all scorers with 37 points, to go with 10 assists and a pair of steals. McCollum added 24 points and Al-Farouq Aminu pitched in 20 points and nine boards. Both teams play on Tuesday, as the Blazers visit the Dallas Mavericks, while the Spurs visit the Utah Jazz.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 133 - 120, at AT & T Center on Friday evening. The Lakers got out to a good start on the road, with an early. 9 - 2, lead. The Spurs picked it up and brought the game to a tie at 22, before the Lakers pulled ahead to lead, 36 - 32, after one. The Lakers kept the edge while the Spurs matched them bucket - for - bucket, with 36 points each in the quarter, to bring the lead to, 72 - 68, for the Lakers at halftime. The Spurs came out strong in the third quarter, and cut the deficit to just two, with 5:23 left in the quarter. However, the Lakers closed the quarter with a 17 - 9 run, to take a, 99 - 89, lead into the fourth. Nonetheless, the Spurs were not about to back down, as they started the fourth on a 10 - 2 run, to cut the deficit to just two points. They kept pushing an tied it up at 112, halfway through the quarter. The Spurs then used a quick 70 run, and did not look back from there, as clutch play, after clutch play sealed the much - needed win. For the Lakers, it marked the end of a four - game winning streak. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 36 points, nine assists, eight rebounds and two blocks, in 36 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge, Patty Mills and Jakob Poeltl finished with 14 points each, while Davis Bertans, who came up huge in the clutch, finished with 13 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 35 points, 11 assists, eight rebounds and two steals, in 37 minutes. Kyle Kuzma followed up with 27 points, eight rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Lonzo Ball tallied 13 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one steal. The Lakers (15 - 10) will look to bounce back as they take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Saturday. The Spurs (12 - 14) play host to the Jazz on Sunday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Utah Jazz, 110 - 97, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. The Jazz got out to an early, 9 - 4, lead, but the Spurs battled back to take a, 23 - 18, lead by the end of the first quarter. The Spurs carried the momentum into the second, where they opening things up by pushing their lead to 12, within the first four minutes of the quarter. They went on to outscore the visitors, 31 - 18, in the quarter, to take a, 54 - 36, lead by halftime. However, the Jazz responded in the third, as they chipped away at the deficit, cutting it to 10, to trail, 82 - 72, entering the final frame. The Jazz kept fighting and cut the gap to just five points, early in the fourth. However, the Spurs fired back, and quickly pushed the lead back to 10. They kept their foot on the gas down the stretch and held on for their second straight win. This marked the end of a two - game winning streak for Utah. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 26 points on 10 - of - 23 shooting, eight assists, six rebounds, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Rudy Gay also had a huge night, with 23 points, 15 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge added 20 points, six rebounds, three blocks and one assist. The Spur shot 53 percent from the field, including 5 - of - 14 from deep. Meanwhile, Donovan Mitchell led the Jazz with 27 points, five rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, in 35 minutes. Ricky Rubio tallied 26 points, three rebounds and two assists, while Rudy Gobert added 12 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block. The Jazz shot 44 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 29 from long range. The Jazz (13 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Thunder in OKC on Monday. The Spurs (13 - 14) play host to the Suns on Tuesday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Phoenix Suns, 111 - 86, at AT & T Center on Tuesday night. The Spurs (14 - 14) came into the contest looking to build on the impressive and much - needed defensive effort they'd managed against the Utah Jazz in their most recent contest, a game in which they'd surrendered just 97 points. They appeared to have a solid matchup against the Suns (4 - 24), which were coming in after having played an overtime game versus the Clippers just one night prior. Accordingly, San Antonio was able to jump out to a 29 - 20 lead after one quarter and held a solid 13 - point edge at intermission. They then put the game away for good in a third period during which they outscored their visitors by a 29 - 18 margin. The Spurs limited the Suns to 40 percent shooting, forced 17 turnovers and held them under 25 points in three of four quarters. T.J. Warren led the Suns with 23 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds and two assists. De'Anthony Melton started for Devin Booker (hamstring) once again and provided 17 points, seven rebounds, six assists and two steals. Deandre Ayton generated a 12 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and two blocks. Malik Bridges and Josh Jackson mustered just eight and seven points, respectively, in their starting assignments. Bryn Forbes paced the Spurs with 24 points, adding 11 rebounds, three assists and one steal. LaMarcus Aldridge totaled 18 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Dante Cunningham produced a bench - leading 14 points, to which he added three rebounds. Rudy Gay poured in 13 points and also registered four boards, two assists, two steals and one block. Marco Belinelli managed 11 points and three rebounds on the second unit. The Suns head back home to tangle with the Dallas Mavericks on Thursday night, while the Spurs remain home to take on the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday evening as well.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 125 - 87, at AT & T Center on Thursday. While this was supposed to be a close game, San Antonio dominated throughout. In fact, a 38 - 27 first quarter really set the tone, as they never trailed from there. The Spurs really put the game away in the second half, outscoring the Clippers, 59 - 30. That allowed San Antonio to hold a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half, in addition to leading by at least 20 points for the whole of the fourth quarter. The shooting disparity was critical, with San Antonio connecting on 58 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range while holding Los Angeles to 36 percent from the field and 32 percent from long range. The Spurs also won the defensive rebounding differential, 40 - 29. Rim protection was also huge, with San Antonio out - blocking Los Angeles, 7 - 1. The Clippers (17 - 11) were led by Tobias Harris, as he tallied 17 points, five rebounds and two assists. Danilo Gallinari totaled 15 points, three rebounds and four assists. Avery Bradley accrued 15 points, three rebounds and three assists. Shai Gilegous-Alexander was the only other Clipper in double figures, as he collected 13 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Spurs (15 - 14) got a gem from LaMarcus Aldridge, as he went 12 - of - 14 from the field to finish with 27 points, four rebounds and two steals. Rudy Gay accumulated 21 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals on 8 - of - 10 shooting. DeMar DeRozan tallied 14 points, four rebounds and seven assists. Marco Belinelli and Patty Mills provided double figures in scoring off the bench. Both these teams return to action on Saturday, with Los Angeles traveling to face the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio playing host to the struggling Chicago Bulls.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 98 - 93, at AT & T Center on Saturday. While there was only one tie and five lead changes in this game, it wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, Chicago overcame a 19 - point halftime deficit to win this game, as they outscored San Antonio in the second half, 55 - 31. The Bulls defense was key, as they held the Spurs to 44 percent from the field and 35 percent from three - point range while winning the turnover differential, 15 - 7. Much of that was attributed to the steals, as the Bulls recorded 12 of them while the Spurs picked up just three steals. Chicago also outscored San Antonio in the paint, 42 - 32. The Bulls (7 - 23) got a season - best performance from Kris Dunn, as he collected 24 points, seven rebounds, three assists and two steals. Lauri Markkanen amassed 23 points, seven rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Ryan Arcidiacono accrued 12 points, four rebounds, six assists and three steals. The Spurs (15 - 15) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he totaled 29 points and 12 boards. DeMar DeRozan accumulated 21 points, five rebounds and three assists. Rudy Gay finished with 12 points, six rebounds and four assists. Marco Belinelli was the only other player to score more than six points, as he led the bench with 17 points, four rebounds and two assists. On deck for San Antonio is a home matchup versus the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday. As for Chicago, they travel to play the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday as well.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 123 - 96, at AT & T Center on Monday evening. The 76ers got out to a good start on the road, as they took the lead early in the first and stayed ahead until they ended the first quarter with a 32 - 29 advantage. The Spurs flipped the switch in the second, as they took the lead three and a half minutes into the quarter and did not look back, as they outscored the visitors 31 - 17 in the quarter, to take a 60 - 49 lead at the half. The Spurs kept the pressure on the the third quarter, where they outscored the Sixers by 11, to put the game mostly out of reach, with a 22 - point deficit heading into the fourth. They were able to keep strong to start the final frame cruised to the finish, to close their home stand with a 4 - 1 record. The Spurs had three player top 20 points, as Rudy Gay led the way with 21 points, six rebounds, three assists, one block and a steal, in 29 minutes. DeMar DeRozan tallied 20 points, seven assists and six rebounds, while LaMarcus Aldridge tallied 20 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and two assists. The Spurs shot 56 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 23 from long range. Meanwhile, Ben Simmons led the 76ers with 16 points, six rebounds and six assists, in 29 minutes. J.J. Redick tallied 16 points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Joel Embiid finished with 13 points, 11 rebounds and five assists. The Sixers shot 41 percent from including 11 - of - 37 from long range. The 76ers (20 - 12) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Knicks on Wednesday. The Spurs (16 - 15) take on the Magic in Orlando on Wednesday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 124 - 98, at AT & T Center on Friday. San Antonio thoroughly dominated Minnesota in this game, as they held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. In fact, the Spurs won the first, third and fourth quarters by a total of 26 points, with all three being decided by eight points or more. Ball movement was the difference in the game, with San Antonio recording 36 assists on 46 made baskets. The T'Wolves recorded just 19 assists while being outrebounded, 50 - 39. That ball movement allowed the Spurs to shoot 53 percent from the field and 58 percent from three - point range while holding the Timberwolves to 40 percent from the field and 29 percent from long range. The Timberwolves (14 - 18) had just four players reach double figures in scoring, as Andrew Wiggins led the team with 15 points and six boards. Robert Covington accrued 13 points, seven rebounds and six steals. Karl-Anthony Towns totaled 13 points, six rebounds and four assists. Derrick Rose played just 15 minutes, as he left in the second quarter due to an ankle injury. The Spurs (18 - 15) were led by Bryn Forbes, as he tallied 22 points, four rebounds and seven assists. DeMar DeRozan accrued 12 points, five rebounds and eight assists. LaMarcus Aldridge finished with 10 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Marco Belinelli, Jakob Poeltl and Davis Bertans all reached double figures in scoring off the bench. On deck for San Antonio is a road matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Saturday. As for Minnesota, they travel to play the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday for their next outing.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Denver Nuggets, 111 - 103, at AT & T Center on Wednesday evening. The game marked the second straight loss for the Nuggets (21 - 11), who are still hanging onto first place in the Western Conference standings. Wednesday's game didn't help Denver's case, though, as the team shot just 39 percent from the field in the loss. The Spurs (19 - 16), meanwhile, continued to show improvement defensively after their early - season struggles. While San Antonio entered the month of December ranked 29th in the league defensively, the team has turned things around, ranking in the top ten since the start of the month. On Wednesday, the Spurs' revamped defense was on display, as the team held Denver to just 17 - of - 48 shooting from inside the arc. On offense, All-Stars DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge helped lead the charge for the Spurs. The duo scored 27 points each, shooting a combined 22 - of - 36 from the floor. San Antonio also got 15 points and four assists out of point guard Bryn Forbes, who knocked down a pair of three - pointers in the win. For Denver, meanwhile, big man Nikola Jokic delivered an uncharacteristically poor game. The superstar center led his team with 10 assists, but also finished with only four points and four rebounds. To make matters worse, Jokic committed five turnovers in the loss. His struggles were nearly offset by the play of Juancho Hernangomez, who scored 27 points to lead the Nuggets on Wednesday. Unfortunately for Denver, Hernangomez's contribution was not enough to secure the win. Denver will have a chance to even the score on Friday, as the two teams are set to rematch at Pepsi Center.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 120 - 111, at AT & T Center on Monday. While Boston led for 23 minutes of a 24 - minute first half, San Antonio took control in the third quarter. In fact, the Spurs matched their first - half point total by outscoring Boston, 46 - 30, in the third quarter. A 17 - 2 run in the middle of that quarter really made the difference, as they led by at least seven points for the final 16 minutes of play. Three-point shooting was critical, with the Spurs hitting 14 - of - 26 and the Celtics connecting on just 11 - of - 34. San Antonio's starters did most of the damage, outscoring Boston's starters, 84 - 62. The Celtics (21 - 15) best player came off the bench, as Jaylen Brown led the team with 30 points, four rebounds, two assists and two blocks on 10 - of - 15 from the field. Marcus Morris led the starters with 18 points and four boards. Kyrie Irving accrued 16 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two steals while Jayson Tatum amassed 12 points and 11 boards. The Spurs (21 - 17) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he tallied 32 points, nine rebounds, five assists and three blocks. Derrick White totaled 22 points, three rebounds, three assists and two blocks. DeMar DeRozan collected 13 points, seven rebounds and 11 assists while Davis Bertans led the bench with 17 points. On deck for Boston is a home matchup versus the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday. As for San Antonio, they're off until Thursday when they welcome Kawhi Leonard and the Toronto Raptors to AT & T Center.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Toronto Raptors, 125 - 107, at AT & T Center on Thursday evening. Normally, a meeting between two above - average squads from opposite conferences would be a storyline in itself, but the excitement leading up to Thursday's matchup was centered on the return of Kawhi Leonard to San Antonio for the first time. However, the Spurs (22 - 17) made sure the spotlight was put right back on them during the first 12 minutes, as they made a statement with a 38 - 19 first - quarter lead. While the Raptors (28 - 12) naturally found their stride to an extent after that trouncing, they still trailed 67 - 51 at halftime. San Antonio then sealed the victory by adding five more points to their advantage in the third quarter, leading to the comfortable double - digit victory. Leonard certainly wasn't bad in his return performance - - team - leading 21 points, along with five assists, one rebound and two steals over 33 minutes - - but as the final score indicates, his efforts were nowhere near enough. Delon Wright was second behind Leonard with 15 points off the bench, and he added four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Serge Ibaka and Norman Powell had matching 14 - point tallies, with the former adding six rebounds, one assist and one steal, and the latter supplying three rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Fred VanVleet furnished 12 points, five boards and two assists. Greg Monroe matched VanVleet's scoring total and also turned in six rebounds, one steal and one block. Pascal Siakam filled out the stat sheet with 10 points, seven assists, six rebounds, one steal and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge paced the Spurs with 23 points and also dished out five assists and pulled in two rebounds. DeMar DeRozan managed 21 points, 14 rebounds, 11 assists and two steals. Bryn Forbes poured in 20 points, hauled in three boards, dished out three assists and recorded one steal. Derrick White continued his productive run with 19 points, four assists and one steal. Rudy Gay registered 13 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one steal. Patty Mills led the bench with 12 points. The Raptors remain on the road and next pay a Saturday night visit to the Milwaukee Bucks, while the Spurs remain home to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday evening.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 108 - 88, at AT & T Center on Saturday night. The Grizzlies (16 - 21) came out ready to match the Spurs (23 - 17) basket for basket, and they trailed just 27 - 25 after one quarter. However, the game turned in the second, as San Antonio outscored Memphis by a 37 - 19 margin. Armed with a 20 - point advantage heading into the third quarter, the home squad essentially held serve in the second half to churn out the comfortable victory. Mike Conley paced the Grizzlies with 21 points, adding three assists and one rebound. Jaren Jackson, Jr. followed with 15 points, seven rebounds, one assist and four steals. Dillon Brooks matched Jackson's scoring total. No other Memphis player managed double - digit scoring, but JaMychal Green supplied eight points, 10 rebounds and one steal off the bench. Kyle Anderson and Garrett Temple had seven points each. Derrick White paced the Spurs with 19 points and supplemented them with four rebounds, two blocks and one steal. LaMarcus Aldridge posted 18 points, seven assists, two rebounds and two steals. Patty Mills generated 15 points, four assists, two rebounds and one steal. DeMar DeRozan totaled 12 points, nine rebounds, four assists and one steal. Jakob Poeltl turned in 11 points, six rebounds, two assists and one block. The Grizzlies remain on the road and visit the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Spurs also travel and face the Detroit Pistons on Monday evening.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 154 - 147, in double overtime at AT & T Center on Thursday evening. The Spurs got out to a great start at home, with a 33 - 23 lead after one quarter. The Thunder chipped away through the second and cut the deficit to seven by halftime. The Spurs maintained control through the third and pushed their lead to 105 - 93 entering the fourth, but the Thunder would not back down and outscored the Spurs by 12 in the quarter to force OT. The teams matched each other for 11 points each in the first overtime, which led to a second overtime period. The Spurs managed to pull ahead early and held on despite a relentless effort from the visitors. The Spurs held on for the impressive home win, mostly thanks to a career - high 56 points from LaMarcus Aldridge. This marks the third straight loss for the Thunder. Aldridge led the Spurs with 56 points on 20 - of - 33 shooting, in 48 minutes. Derrick White followed up with 23 points, eight assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block, while DeMar DeRozan finished with 16 points, 11 assists, eight rebounds, one steal and one block. The Spurs shot 56 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 19 from long range. Meanwhile, Russell Westbrook led the Thunder with 24 points, a career - high 24 assists, 13 rebounds and two steals, in 49 minutes. Paul George followed up with 30 points on 11 - of - 25 shooting, eight rebounds, three steals and one assist, in 46 minutes, while Jerami Grant tallied a career - high 25 points, along with 12 rebounds, three blocks and one assist. The Thunder (25 - 16) and Spurs (25 - 18) will have a rematch on Saturday.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 108 - 93, at AT & T Center on Monday. While San Antonio came into this game as a sizable favorite, Charlotte dominated this matchup. In fact, they led for 40 minutes of this 48 - minute game, as a 32 - 21 fourth quarter gave them enough separation to win. It was an 80 - 79 scoreline with eight minutes remaining but the Hornets finished the game on a 28 - 14 run. Rebounding was key for the Hornets, as they outrebounded the Spurs, 45 - 36. Three-point shooting was also critical, with Charlotte hitting 13 - of - 36 and San Antonio connecting on 7 - of - 20. The Hornets did a ton of their damage down low, outscoring the Spurs in the paint, 44 - 34. The Hornets (20 - 23) got a gem of a performance from Kemba Walker, as he led the way with 33 points, four rebounds, five assists and two steals. Jeremy Lamb accrued 19 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Marvin Williams totaled 11 points, five rebounds and three assists while Tony Parker led the bench with eight points, three rebounds and four assists. The Spurs (25 - 20) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he tallied 28 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. DeMar DeRozan accumulated 14 points, five rebounds and five assists. Derrick White amassed 18 points, four rebounds and seven assists while Patty Mills led the bench with 14 points and two boards. On deck for San Antonio is a road matchup versus the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. As for Charlotte, they return to action on Thursday when they play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 103 - 95, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. The Clippers (25 - 21) were looking to snap a five - game losing streak in a tough environment Sunday, so a fast start was certainly important. It was mission accomplished for Los Angeles after 12 minutes, as they built a 38 - 26 first - quarter lead. The Spurs (27 - 21) cut some into their deficit in the second quarter, but they were never able to catch up to the visitors the rest of the way. The Clippers enjoyed a strong effort from their starting five, which featured four double - digit scorers. That included Montrezl Harrell, who entered the first unit for the sidelined Danilo Gallinari (back) and posted 18 points, four rebounds and one steal. Tobias Harris paced the Clippers with 27 points, adding nine rebounds, nine assists, three steals and one block. Patrick Beverley generated an 18 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, four steals and one block. Avery Bradley managed 15 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. Johnathan Motley furnished 10 points, four rebounds and one steal. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 30 points and 14 rebounds, adding two assists and two blocks. Rudy Gay delivered 19 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one block. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Washington Wizards 132 - 119, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. Despite missing DeMar DeRozan (knee), the Spurs got out to a great start at home, with a 36 - 26 lead after one quarter. The Wizards answered back in the second, where they outscored the Spurs by nine, to make it a one - point game by halftime. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 30 points on 12 - of - 21 shooting, nine rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal, in 32 minutes. Davis Bertans followed up with 21 points, three rebounds and two assists, while Bryn Forbes and Derrick White added 16 points each. The Spurs shot 57 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 34 from long range. Tomas Satoransky tallied 21 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and one steal, while Thomas Bryant finished with 15 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. The Spurs (29 - 22) play host to the Suns on Tuesday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 126 - 124, at AT & T Center on Tuesday. It's rare to see a team shoot 60 percent from the field and lose but that was the case here for the Suns. It stayed close throughout though, as there were 15 ties and seven lead changes in total, with neither team leading by more than 12 points. In fact, Rudy Gay played the hero, as he broke a tied game with a mid - range jumper at the buzzer to capture a win for the Spurs. San Antonio simply had more chances than Phoenix, as they took 20 more shots than them. Much of that can be attributed to the offensive rebounding, with the Spurs winning that battle, 14 - 3. The assist - to - turnover differential also played a factor in that, with the Spurs recording 30 assists to 11 turnovers and the Suns committing 18 turnovers to 26 assists. The Suns (11 - 42) were led by Devin Booker, as he tallied 38 points, five rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Mikal Bridges totaled 17 points, six rebounds, three assists and four steals. Josh Jackson accrued 14 points, six rebounds and five assists while Jamal Crawford led the bench with 22 points and seven assists. The Spurs (30 - 22) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he accumulated 29 points, 14 rebounds and four assists. Davis Bertans amassed 18 points, five assists and four steals. Rudy Gay finished with 16 points, five rebounds and five assists. Derrick White generated 15 points, seven rebounds and three assists while Marco Belinelli led the bench with 17 points and five assists. On deck for San Antonio is a home matchup versus the surging Brooklyn Nets on Thursday. As for Phoenix, they're off until Saturday when they play host to the Atlanta Hawks.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 117 - 114, at AT & T Center on Thursday. Over the course of the second and third quarters, the Spurs looked to be losing control of Thursday's contest and ended up facing a deficit as large as seven in the final period. It was at that point that San Antonio managed to go on a bit of a run, and the team was ultimately able to hold off Shabazz Napier from hitting a second three in the closing seconds that would have tied the game. Derrick White was sensational in the outing, scoring a game - high 26 points to go along with six assists in just 25 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge was close behind with yet another double - double of 20 points and 13 rebounds despite struggling from the field (5 - of - 13). DeMar DeRozan also struggled shooting the ball in his first game back after a three - game absence due to knee soreness. The swingman shot just 5 - of - 16 from the field and finished with just 15 points, but he did grab 10 rebounds. As for the Nets, they missed out on what would have been a prime opportunity for a statement when, but they were just unable to hold on in the closing moments. They actually outshot the Spurs, but what really hurt them was the amount of points they left at the free throw line, going 19 - of - 29 from the charity stripe. D'Angelo Russell scored a team - high 25 points but did so on a fairly inefficient 10 - of - 26 shooting. He also added nine assists and five rebounds in the outing. Joe Harris, on the other hand, was very efficient in his shooting performance, going 7 - of - 10 from the field overall and 3 - of - 5 from three en route to scoring 18 points. DeMarre Carroll also came up with a solid outing off the bench, scoring 18 points in 27 minutes as a reserve.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 113 - 108, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The Spurs (32 - 22) set an early tone by building an 11 - point first quarter lead, and they ultimately entered the final period with a 16 - point advantage. Although the Pelicans (23 - 30) were able to get as close as 111 - 108 with 38 seconds remaining, a pair of DeMar DeRozan free throws with 3 seconds remaining sealed the win for San Antonio. The hosts enjoyed a particularly sizable advantage on the boards, as they won the rebounding battle by a 50 - 42 margin. Frank Jackson led the way for the Pelicans with 25 points, adding two rebounds and two assists. Jrue Holiday and Ian Clark posted matching 15 - point contributions, with Holiday notably adding seven rebounds and dishing out four assists. Cheick Diallo furnished 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Kenrich Williams delivered 12 points, eight boards and three assists. Darius Miller netted 11 points and two rebounds, one assist and one steal. LaMarcus Aldridge paced the Spurs with 25 points while also pulling down 14 rebounds, dishing out two assists and recording one steal. Rudy Gay pitched in 17 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal. Marco Belinelli matched Gay's scoring total off the bench. DeRozan shot just 3 - for - 10 overall but finished with 13 points, six rebounds, five assists and one block. Patty Mills and Bryn Forbes had matching 12 - point tallies. The Pelicans head back home to face the Indiana Pacers on Monday night, while the Spurs pay a visit to the Sacramento Kings on Monday evening as well.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 105 - 93, at AT & T Arena on Wednesday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with a few lead changes in the first quarter, before the Spurs emerged with a 32 - 27 lead entering the second. The Spurs pushed their lead to 10 during the second, but the Pistons rallied back to take a one - point lead, before the Spurs regained the edge, with a three - point lead by halftime. The Spurs came out strong in the third and outscored the visitors by eight in the quarter, to take a 78 - 67 lead into the final frame. The Pistons kept fighting and made it a two - point game with just five minutes to go, but the Spurs were able to stay on top and close out the much - needed win, ending a three - game slide. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 24 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks, in 38 minutes. DeMar DeRozan followed up with 17 points, 13 rebounds, eight assists and two steals, while Marco Belinelli added 17 points and five rebounds off the bench. The Spurs shot 52 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 17 from deep. Meanwhile, Reggie Jackson led the Pistons with 22 points on 8 - of - 18 shooting, in 29 minutes. Blake Griffin tallied 17 points, seven rebounds and seven assists, while Andre Drummond finished with 10 points, 17 rebounds, four steals, one block and one assist. The Pistons shot 36 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 38 from long range. The Pistons (29 - 31) will look to bounce back as they take on the Cavs in Cleveland on Saturday. The Spurs (34 - 29) play host to the Thunder on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 116 - 102, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The Spurs got out to a great start at home, with a 38 - 25 lead after one quarter. The Thunder picked it up in the second, but could only knock the deficit down by four points, as they trailed by nine at halftime. The contest slowed down in the third, as both teams combined for only 35 points, however, it was the Spurs who played with the edge, as they outscored the visitors by five, to push their lead to 14, entering the final frame. The Thunder kept fighting through the fourth but could not gain any ground, as the Spurs held on for their second straight win. The Thunder dropped their second in a row with out Paul George (shoulder) in the lineup, and their fourth straight overall. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs, with 27 points, 10 rebounds, one assist, one steal and a block, in 34 minutes. Rudy Gay followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, one assists and one steal, in 26 minutes off the bench, while DeMar DeRozan added 18 points, seven assists and six rebounds. The Spurs shot 50 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 19 from long range. Meanwhile, Russell Westbrook led the Thunder with 19 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Dennis Schroder followed up with 18 points, five rebounds, three assists and one steal, while Steven Adams added 17 points, 13 rebounds, two steals and a block. The Thunder shot 46 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 29 from deep. The Thunder (38 - 24) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Grizzlies on Sunday. The Spurs (35 - 29) play host to the Nuggets on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Denver Nuggets, 104 - 103, at AT & T Center on Monday evening. The Spurs (36 - 29) came out of the gates with uncommon ferocity, building a 36 - 17 first - quarter lead over the overwhelmed Nuggets (42 - 21). While Denver recovered enough to put a nine - point dent into their deficit in the second, San Antonio still entered the fourth quarter with a 16 - point advantage, but the visitors fought back to finish on a 34 - 17 run over the final 10:51. Jamal Murray's 28 - foot step back jumper with 50 seconds left got the Nuggets to within one, but Murray would subsequently miss two other attempts and Gary Harris would misfire on one as well over the remaining time to leave them just short of a successful comeback. jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 25 points, adding eight assists, two rebounds and one steal. Nikola Jokic generated a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included six assists. Malik Beasley furnished 15 points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Will Barton delivered 12 points, six rebounds, one assist and one block. Gary Harris totaled eight points, two rebounds and one assist. Paul Millsap mustered just five points but also pulled down 11 rebounds, dished out two assists and recorded one steal. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 24 points, supplementing them with seven assists, six rebounds, three steals and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge compiled 22 points, nine rebounds and two assists. Rudy Gay generated a near double - double of 14 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal. Derrick White finished with 11 points, nine assists, four rebounds, three blocks and one steal. Patty Mills and Marco Belinelli poured in eight points apiece, while Bryn Forbes supplied seven points and three boards. The Nuggets remain on the road and take on the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night, while the Spurs travel to Atlanta and face the Hawks on the Wednesday evening as well.

The San Antonio Spurs took down the Milwaukee Bucks, 121 - 114, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. San Antonio (38 - 29) picked up its fifth straight win in impressive fashion on Sunday, besting the league - leading Bucks (50 - 17). Milwaukee initially seemed poised to win in a blowout, hopping out to a 15 - point lead in the first quarter. However, the Spurs rallied back and had cut the deficit to only six points by halftime. In an unusual turn of events, San Antonio was given another chance to regroup in the third quarter after the game was temporarily delayed by a bat flying around the court. The Spurs were able to take the lead by the end of the third quarter, thanks largely to strong play from DeMar DeRozan. San Antonio sealed the win with a quick run at the beginning of the fourth in which it extended the lead to double digits. LaMarcus Aldridge was the leading scorer for the Spurs with 29 points. The veteran All-Star added 15 rebounds, two steals, and two blocks in the win. DeRozan, meanwhile, finished with 28 points and dished out a team - high six assists. Sunday's win moved the Spurs into a tie for sixth in the Western Conference. For Milwaukee, MVP hopeful Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 27 points and 13 rebounds to lead the team. Eric Bledsoe scored another 21 points, while Brook Lopez chipped in an 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. With the loss, the Bucks have now dropped three straight games on the road. The Bucks will continue their road trip with a visit to New Orleans on Tuesday. The Spurs, meanwhile, will take a trip to Dallas to take on the Mavericks.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks, 109 - 83, at AT & T Center on Friday night. The Knicks (13 - 56) had been playing more competitively in recent games, but they knew they'd be short - handed Friday due to a lower back injury sidelined Dennis Smith, Jr. for the contest. New York looked offensively challenged without their recent trade acquisition, scoring only 41 points during the first half and falling behind by 15 points at intermission. The visitors managed to put together a 28 - point third period, but they fell apart in the final period by scoring just 14 points. Dewayne Dotson paced the Knicks with 21 points and added two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Kadeem Allen followed with 16 points and also supplied three rebounds, two assists and three steals. Emmanuel Mudiay collected 14 points, four rebounds and two assists. DeAndre Jordan generated an 11 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included nine assists. Kevin Knox delivered seven points, one assist and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 18 points and 11 rebounds. DeMar DeRozan finished with 13 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Bryn Forbes matched DeRozan's scoring total and added one rebound. Jakob Poeltl managed 12 points, nine rebounds, two assists, five blocks and two steals. Rudy Gay and Marco Belinelli turned in matching 12 - point tallies off the bench. The Knicks head back home to take on the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday afternoon, while the Spurs remain home and take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 108 - 103, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the Spurs holding a two - point lead after a back - and - forth first quarter. The Spurs picked it up to start the second, as they built a double - digit lead, however, the Trail Blazers rallied back to take a 50 - 48 lead by halftime. It stayed competitive, as the teams were never more than a couple possessions apart in the third, with the Trail Blazers taking a four - point lead into the fourth. The Spurs came out strong in the fourth and took control by the halfway point in the quarter. They held the lead down the stretch to secure their eighth straight win. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 21 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes. Rudy Gay added 13 points, seven rebounds and one block, while LaMarcus Aldridge tallied 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, three blocks and a steal. The Spurs shot 47 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 17 from deep. Meanwhile, Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 34 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 37 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic followed up with 24 points, 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block, while Rodney Hood chipped in 13 points and three rebounds, off the bench. The Trail Blazers shot 42 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from long range. The Trail Blazers (42 - 27) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pacers on Monday. The Spurs (41 - 29) play host to the Warriors on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Golden State Warriors, 111 - 105, at AT & T Center on Monday. The Spurs (42 - 29) continue to roll, as despite playing their third game in four nights, the team managed to post a wire - to - wire victory over the NBA's best team. DeMar DeRozan led the way with a terrific all - around performance, recording a game - high 26 points, nine rebounds and eight assists across 38 minutes. His 25th and 26th points were the most important, as they came on a heavily contested jumper over Klay Thompson with just over a minute left that put the Spurs up six, and up for good. LaMarcus Aldridge was close behind with a double - double of 23 points and 13 rebounds on 8 - of - 12 shooting, while Rudy Gay came off the bench to score 17 points. As for the Warriors (47 - 22), it was a night to forget for their star backcourt, with Steph Curry and Thompson going a combined 14 - of - 43 from the field Monday night. Curry still managed to finish with a team - high 25 points thanks to making six threes, and he added seven rebounds, eight assists and three steals. Meanwhile, Thompson still hit four threes and finished with 14 points in 38 minutes. Kevin Durant didn't hit a single shot from behind the arc, going 0 - of - 4, but he still went 9 - of - 18 from the field and finished with 24 points. As a team, the Warriors shot a respectable 47 percent from the floor, but their lack of aggression resulted in few trips to the free throw line, and that may have cost them the victory, as they were just 10 - of - 12 from the stripe while the Spurs were 19 - of - 22.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 113 - 106, at AT & T Center on Sunday. It took 25 lead changes to determine a winner in this game, as neither club ever led by more than 12 points. The key for Sacramento was a 90 run to start the fourth quarter, as that gave them a game - high 12 - point lead. Three-point shooting was huge, with the Kings hitting 11 - of - 25 and the Spurs connecting on just 8 - of - 27. Free-throw shooting was also decisive, with Sacramento connecting on 24 - of - 28 and the Spurs hitting just 10 - of - 14. Sacramento also won the defensive rebounding battle, 35 - 27 The Kings (38 - 39) were led by Buddy Hield, as he tallied 26 points, five rebounds and three assists. Willie Cauley-Stein accrued 17 points, six rebounds and two steals. Harrison Barnes finished with 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. De'Aaron Fox collected 12 points, four rebounds and five assists. Bogdan Bogdanovic led the bench with 15 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. The Spurs (44 - 33) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he accumulated 27 points, 18 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Rudy Gay started and finished with 18 points, nine rebounds and three assists. DeMar DeRozan amassed 16 points, two rebounds, seven assists and three steals while Marco Belinelli led the bench with 14 points. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with San Antonio playing host to the Atlanta Hawks and Sacramento welcoming the Houston Rockets to Golden 1 Center.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 117 - 111, at AT & T Center on Tuesday night. The Spurs (45 - 33) came into the contest with a playoff spot locked up, but looking to sharpen their collective knife prior to the postseason. San Antonio knew they'd be in for a challenge against the spoiler - minded Hawks (28 - 50), which gave them all they could handle in the first half. The home squad held a slim two - point lead at intermission, but Atlanta impressively wiped that out in third and entered the final period with a four - point advantage. However, a 17 - 12 run by the Spurs over the first 7:25 of the fourth quarter gave them a lead that they wouldn't relinquish the rest of the way. Kent Bazemore led the way for the Hawks with 26 points, adding four rebounds, two assists and three steals. Alex Len contributed 21 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Trae Young produced 15 points, six assists, one rebound and one steal. Kyle Huerter poured in 13 points. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 29 points, complementing them with seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Derrick White supplied 23 points, four rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Bryn Forbes netted 19 points, while LaMarcus Aldridge contributed a 16 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks. Patty Mills led the bench with 14 points. The Hawks head back home to face the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday evening, while the Spurs pay a visit to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday night as well.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 105 - 94, on Wednesday at AT & T. For both these teams, it was the final game of the regular season, but most importantly, it was the final game for NBA legend Dirk Nowitzki. While he and the Mavericks came up well short of the Spurs on Wednesday night, Nowitzki did get plenty of shots up and managed to lead the team in scoring with 20 points on top of 10 rebounds. It was his only double - double of his final season. Nowitzki was only outdone by LaMarcus Aldridge, who put the finishing touches on a terrific, potentially All-NBA, 2018 - 19 season. Aldridge posted a game - high 34 points on 15 - of - 21 shooting from the floor to go along with 16 rebounds to lead the way for the Spurs in their 48th victory of the season. DeMar DeRozan added 19 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals, while point guard Derrick White scored 14 points of his own. As a team, San Antonio shot a decent 47 percent from the field. It was a strong close to the season for the Spurs, who won three games in a row and are now locked into the No. 7 seed in the Western Conference standings, finishing one game behind the Thunder. They are expected to play the Nuggets in the first round.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Phoenix Suns 131 - 113 at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. The Lakers found their first win of the season against one of the leagues youngest teams in the Suns. LeBron James quickly put behind him the free throw woes that resulted in a brutal OT loss to the Spurs earlier in the week and bounced back to lead Los Angeles (1 - 3) to their first win. A close first quarter that saw the Lakers end with a two point lead was overshadowed by an explosive 44 points in the second quarter. Javale McGree was at the heart of the action in that period, as he finished dunks (unlike his failed dunk in the first quarter, quickly shared on social media) and got to the free throw line in the twenty point rout to end the half. Phoenix (1 - 3) played from behind for the majority of the game, however, they saw a strong outing from their No. 1 overall pick DeAndre Ayton. LeBron James finished with 19 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and three steals, while Lance Stephenson led all scorers with 23 points on 10 - of - 14 shooting off the bench. All five Lakers starters finished in double figures, including Josh Hart, who started in place of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Ayton finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds on 11 - of - 14 shooting and Devin Booker added 23 points, seven rebounds and seven assists in the loss. The Lakers will play the second game of a back - to - back at home against the Nuggets on Thursday, while the Suns will head to Memphis to play the Grizzlies on Saturday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 107 - 98, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Suns had their leading scorer, Devin Booker, back in the lineup, after he missed three games with an hamstring issue. The Suns came out strong in the first and managed to take a 26 - 23 lead by the end of the first quarter. They held a slight edge for most of the second quarter, while the Raptors stole a one - point lead for a few seconds, the Suns got back on top, 52 - 48, by halftime. The Raptors flipped the narrative in the third, as they quickly took over with a small advantage, before pulling away to take a 77 - 71 lead into the fourth. The Raptors pushed their lead to 17, mid way through the quarter, and held on to earn their second straight win. This marked the seventh straight loss for Phoenix. Kawhi Leonard led Toronto with 19 points, six rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, in 29 minutes. Jonas Valanciunas finished with 16 points, seven rebounds, four blocks, one steal and one assist, while Kyle Lowry tallied 11 points, 12 assists, six rebounds and two steals. The Raptors shot 49 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Isaiah Canaan led the way for the Suns, with 19 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting. Deandre Ayton finished with 17 points, 18 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, while Devin Booker tallied 18 points, six assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. The Suns shot 44 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 26 from long range. The Suns (1 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Grizzlies on Sunday. The Raptors (8 - 1) take on the Lakers in Los Angeles on Sunday.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 102 - 100, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Sunday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a good start on the road, holding the edge for most of the first quarter, to take a 28 - 21 lead heading into the second quarter. They stayed on top and pushed their lead to 10, with three minutes left in the second, however, the Suns made a push to end the half, and cut the deficit to just four by halftime. The third quarter started out very close, until the Grizz managed to pull ahead by 10, with five minutes to go. Again, the Suns closed the quarter with a run and made it a four - point game, heading into the final frame. The Grizzlies stayed in control though, as they built yet another 10 - point lead, early in the fourth. The Suns kept chipping away, and had it at a two - point game with just under five minutes remaining. It was a close finish, but Devin Booker led Phoenix in clutch, to outscore the Grizzlies 9 - 5 in the final few minutes, to walk away with the home win, and also end an ugly seven - game losing streak. Devin Booker led the Suns with 25 points on 7 - of - 17 shooting, and seven assists, in 34 minutes. Trevor Ariza followed up with 16 points, nine rebounds, five assists and two steals, while Mikal Bridges chipped in 14 points, in 25 minutes off the bench. The Suns shot 52 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Shelvin Mack was the high - point man for Memphis, with 21 points on 7 - of - 10 shooting, in 27 minutes off the bench. Dillon Brooks tallied 17 points on 7 - of - 10 shooting, in 29 minutes off the bench, while Mike Conley and Marc Gasol both had quiet nights. The Grizzlies shot 47 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 24 from deep. The Grizzlies (5 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Warriors on Monday. The Suns (2 - 7) play host to the Nets on Tuesday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Phoenix Suns in overtime, 116 - 109, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday evening. Matters looked grim for the Celtics (7 - 4) for the majority of the night, as they surprisingly fell behind, 32 - 13, after one quarter. Although they were able to cut into their sizable deficit during the middle periods while outscoring the Suns (2 - 9) by 52 - 48 margin, they still entered the final 12 minutes trailing by 15. However, a 17 - 4 run by Boston over a 3:23 period late in the fourth quarter left them within one point of Phoenix. Following a pair of clutch T.J. Warren free throws, the Celtics were able to get the ball into the hands of Marcus Morris, who burned one of his old franchises with a three - pointer with 1 seconds on the clock. The visitors then took control in overtime, snapping a 109 - 109 tie with a 70 run over the final 2:5 of the extra period. Kyrie Irving keyed the Celtics with 39 points, a total he supplemented with seven rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block. He also provided the assist on Morris' game - tying three. Jaylen Brown and Morris each provided 17 points overall. They also hauled in six and eight rebounds, respectively. Terry Rozier provided 10 points, six boards and one assist off the bench. Gordon Hayward (eight points), Al Horford (seven points) and Jayson Tatum (four points) all had underwhelming performances. Devin Booker enjoyed another productive night versus the Celtics, leading the Suns with 38 points and adding nine assists, three rebounds and three steals. Warren supplied 29 points, seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Deandre Ayton posted a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Trevor Ariza filled out the stat sheet with 11 points, nine rebounds, six assists and one block. The Celtics remain on their road trip and pay a visit to the Utah Jazz on Friday night, while the Suns hit the road as well and face the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday evening.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 110 - 100, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. Both teams started out strong, as the first quarter featured many lead changes and ties, however, the Thunder came out on top, with a 30 - 25 lead after one. Things quieted down in the second, as the Thunder and the Suns both had trouble scoring the ball. They matched each other for 17 points each in the quarter, resulting in a, 47 - 42, Thunder lead at the half. The Thunder pulled away in the third, as they pushed their lead to 12, just three and a half minutes into the quarter. They outscored the Suns, 32 - 23, in the quarter, to take a 79 - 65 lead into the final frame. The Suns put up a fight in the fourth, but ultimately could hardly make a dent in the deficit, as the Thunder cruised to their third straight win. Paul George led the Thunder with 32 points, 11 rebounds, three steals, three blocks and two assists, in 39 minutes. Steven Adams followed up with 26 points, 10 rebounds and one steal, while Dennis Schroder tallied 15 points, seven assists, five rebounds and four steals. The Thunder shot 45 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 24 from deep. Meanwhile, T.J. Warren led the Suns with 23 points, five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block, in 40 minutes. Devin Booker had a solid night, with 18 points, 11 assists and four rebounds, while Deandre Ayton tallied 19 points, nine rebounds, an assist and a steal. The Suns shot 45 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 29 from long range. The Suns (3 - 12) will look to bounce back as they visit Philadelphia to take on the 76ers on Monday. The Thunder (10 - 5) head to Sacramento to face the Kings on Monday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 99 - 85, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Suns got out to a good start at home, as they emerged with a, 25 - 21, lead after a competitive first quarter. The Magic picked it up in the second quarter, as they pulled ahead after just a few minutes and went on to outscore the home team, 30 - 23, in the quarter, to take a, 51 - 48, lead by halftime. The Magic pushed their lead to seven early in the third quarter. The Suns hung around and managed to keep it close, in part thanks to a last - second jumper from Jamal Crawford to cut the deficit to just four points by end of the quarter. The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 107 - 99, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday. The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 118 - 102, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 122 - 118, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 132 - 109, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday evening. The Warriors took the early advantage, with a 31 - 27 lead after one quarter. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 132 - 127, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday evening. The Sixers got out to a great start on the road, as they poured in 44 points in the first quarter and took a 44 - 32 lead into the second. The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 121 - 111, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday. The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 115 - 111, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 102 - 93, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Minnesota Timberwolves cruised past the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 91, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. The Wolves quickly changed that, though, as 10 points in the quarter from Karl-Anthony Towns helped spark a run that gave Minnesota a 15 - point lead by halftime. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 120 - 106, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday evening. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 24 points, three rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 29 minutes. C.J. McCollum added 20 points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Jake Layman finished with 20 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 118 - 112, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Hawks got out to a solid start on the road, as they managed to take a 33 - 30 lead through one quarter.
