Dario Saric totaled 13 points, six rebounds and three assists. Derrick Rose was huge off the bench, providing 29 points, three rebounds and three assists. Taj Gibson recorded a 15 - point, 13 - rebound double - double off the bench as well. Minnesota will return to action on Sunday, as they play host to the struggling New York Knicks. As for Washington, they welcome the Sacramento Kings to the nation's capital on Monday for their next outing.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 103 - 92, at Target Center on Sunday evening. Despite missing Andrew Wiggins (thigh) and Karl-Anthony Towns (knee), the Timberwolves rallied together for an impressive win. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the Timberwolves took a 23 - 22 lead after the first quarter. The Knicks made a run to take a lead early in the second, but the Timberwolves went on to outscore them by nine in the quarter, to push their lead to 10 by halftime. They carried the momentum into the third, where they pushed their lead to 15 by the halfway mark. The Knicks kept fighting, but Minnesota managed to hold a 15 - point lead at the start of the fourth. The Timberwolves stayed in control through the fourth, not letting the Knicks even within 10 points, as they cruised to their second straight win. Taj Gibson led the Timberwolves with 25 points, eight rebounds, two steals, a block and an assist, in 30 minutes. Jeff Teague also came up large, with 20 points, 10 assists, three rebounds, two blocks and a steal, while Keita Bates-Diop tallied 18 points, six rebounds, two steals, two blocks and one assist. The Timberwolves shot 45 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 30 from deep. Meanwhile, Damyean Dotson led the Knicks with 26 points, six rebounds, six assists and two steals, in 40 minutes. Dennis Smith Jr. finished with 13 points, four assists and two rebounds, while Alonzo Trier chipped in 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Knicks shot 43 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 25 from long range. The Knicks (13 - 54) will look to bounce back as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Tuesday. The Timberwolves (32 - 35) head to Denver to take on the Nuggets on Tuesday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 111, at Target Center on Tuesday evening. The Clippers (45 - 30) deployed one of the best strategies for winning on the road - - they got out to a sizable lead early. Los Angeles forged a 42 - 23 lead through the first 12 minutes and held a 75 - 55 halftime advantage. The Timberwolves (33 - 41) did manage to put a nine - point dent in their deficit overall during the second half, but that wasn't nearly enough to overtake Los Angeles. As their final point tally implies, the visitors shot extremely well, draining 54 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent from three - point range. Danilo Gallinari paced the Clippers with a 25 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal. Lou Williams followed with 20 points, seven assists and four rebounds. Montrezl Harrell delivered 18 points, five rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Garrett Temple supplied 15 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Patrick Beverley and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander contributed 11 and 10 points, respectively. Karl-Anthony Towns led the Timberwolves with a 24 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two steals. Andrew Wiggins poured in 22 points and added three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Dario Saric furnished 18 points, five rebounds, one assist and one steal. Tyus Jones managed 13 points, eight assists and two rebounds. Josh Okogie and Jerryd Bayless managed nine points apiece. The Clippers remain on the road and next visit the Milwaukee Bucks on Thursday evening, while the Timberwolves remain home to tangle with the Golden State Warriors on Friday night.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors in overtime 131 - 130, at Target Center on Friday. This game was full of swings, as it wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Stephen Curry hit a game - tying three with 0 seconds left in OT but they fouled Minnesota on the inbound in the following possession. That allowed Karl-Anthony Towns to nail the game - winning free - throw, who then missed the second free - throw intentionally to run out the clock. There were nine ties and 12 lead changes in total, as Minnesota never trailed in the OT. Rebounding was the clear - cut difference, with the Timberwolves outrebounding the Warriors, 59 - 45. Their bench also came up big, outscoring Golden State's bench, 52 - 25. The Warriors (51 - 24) were led by Stephen Curry, as he went 11 - of - 19 from long range to tally 37 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. Kevin Durant finished with 23 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists and two blocks. Klay Thompson amassed 20 points, two rebounds and five assists. DeMarcus Cousins accrued 16 points and nine boards. The Timberwolves (34 - 41) were led by Andrew Wiggins, as he accumulated 24 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Josh Okogie amassed 21 points, five rebounds and four steals. Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 15 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists. Gorgui Dieng was huge off the bench, providing 14 points and 10 boards. Minnesota suits up again on Saturday, as they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers. As for Golden State, they return to action on Sunday against the Charlotte Hornets.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Minnesota Timberwolves, 118 - 109, at Target Center on Saturday evening. The Sixers got out to a great start on the road, as they took a 38 - 20 lead after one quarter. The 76ers stayed control through the second, but the Timberwolves managed to trim it to a 13 - point deficit by halftime. The Sixers stayed on top through third the Timberwolves trimmed it to an 11 - point game entering the fourth. They kept pushing and cut it to a three - point game, just three minutes into the quarter. However, the Sixers regained control and held on for their second straight win. Tobias Harris led the 76ers with 25 points, seven rebounds and four assists, in 39 minutes. The 76ers shot 47 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 31 from long range. Andrew Wiggins led the Timberwolves with 24 points, six rebounds, five assists and two blocks, in 36 minutes. Karl-Anthony Towns followed up with 21 points, seven rebounds, two assists and a block, while Gorgui Dieng chipped in 13 points and three rebounds. The Timberwolves shot 45 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 26 from deep. The Timberwolves (34 - 42) play host to the Trail Blazers on Monday. The 76ers (49 - 27) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 132 - 122, at Target Center on Monday night. The Trail Blazers (49 - 28) got the early jump on the hometown Timberwolves (34 - 43), forging a 38 - 23 lead through one quarter. Rodney Hood drew the start and led the way for the Trail Blazers with 21 points, adding four rebounds, one assist and two steals. The Trail Blazers head back home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday night, while the Timberwolves pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday evening as well.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Miami Heat, 111 - 109, at Target Center on Friday night The Timberwolves (36 - 43) knew they'd have the opportunity to play spoiler against the Heat (38 - 41), which were in desperate need of a win to have an opportunity to vault back into the eighth seed they'd recently relinquished. Miami appeared to have a solid chance of securing a crucial victory after taking a 69 - 61 halftime lead, but they apparently left their offense in the locker room coming out of intermission. Minnesota would hold the visitors to just 40 second - half points, and they clinched the win when Dwyane Wade missed a 25 - foot three - point jumper at the buzzer. Wade paced the Heat with 24 points, adding three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dion Waiters turned in 22 points. Goran Dragic and James Johnson generated matching 15 - point tallies, with Dragic also dishing out nine assists, pulling down seven rebounds and recording four steals. Karl-Anthony Towns contributed a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal, although he also committed a game - high 11 turnovers. Tyus Jones filled out the stat sheet with 12 points, six rebounds, four assists and two steals. The Heat next visit the Toronto Raptors on Sunday afternoon, while the Timberwolves remain home to face the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday afternoon as well.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 132 - 126, at Target Center on Sunday afternoon. The Thunder (47 - 33) came into the game looking to build some positive momentum ahead of the postseason after a recent extended stretch of sub - par play. Russell Westbrook and Paul George co - led the Thunder with 27 points, with Westbrook also dishing out 15 assists and pulling down 10 rebounds. Dario Saric managed 23 points, three rebounds, one assist and one block. Tyus Jones generated a 10 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds. Gorgui Dieng matched Jones' scoring total and posted four rebounds. The Thunder head back home to tangle with the Houston Rockets on Tuesday night, while the Timberwolves remain home to take on the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday evening as well.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Minnesota Timberwolves, 120 - 100, at Target Center on Tuesday. While there were seven lead changes in the first 15 minutes, Toronto dominated after that. In fact, the Raptors rode a 43 - 19 second quarter to victory, holding a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Defensive rebounding was key for Toronto, as they won that battle, 47 - 30. The Raptors ended up shooting 52 percent from the field and 43 percent from three - point range while holding the Timberwolves to 42 percent from the field and 31 percent from long range. The Raptors (58 - 24) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 20 points and six rebounds. Fred VanVleet got another start and amassed 16 points, two rebounds, four assists and three steals. Chris Boucher was huge off the bench, providing 15 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Pascal Siakam accrued 10 points, four rebounds and two assists. Dario Saric totaled 15 points and nine boards while Tyus Jones generated 11 points and 10 assists. No other player reached double figures in scoring. While that marked the season finale for the Raptors, the Timberwolves have to play again on Wednesday when they travel to face the Denver Nuggets.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 121 - 108, at Moda Center on Saturday evening. The hard - fought contest fittingly began with a 22 - 22 deadlock over the first 12 minutes. However, the Trail Blazers (20) outscored the Spurs (1 - 1) by a 75 - 60 margin over the second and third quarters to gain distance, and they then held serve over the final 12 minutes to post the double - digit victory. Shooting was a key to the win, with Portland draining an impressive 54 percent of their attempts and San Antonio managing a 42 percent success rate from the field. As customary, a significant portion of the Blazers offense flowed through their backcourt, as the star duo of Damian Lillard and C.J. McCollum combining for 53 points on identical 9 - for - 15 shooting efforts. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 28 points, a total he supplemented with nine assists, three rebounds and two steals. Bryn Forbes was a distant second with 17 points and added three assists and two rebounds. LaMarcus Aldridge and Rudy Gay contributed matching 12 - point tallies, with the veteran duo also hauling in eight and seven rebounds, respectively. Davis Bertans (11 points) and Paul Gasol (10 points) were productive off the bench. Lillard's 29 points led the Trail Blazers, and he also contributed nine assists and two rebounds. McCollum followed with 24 points and a pair of assists and rebounds apiece. Jusuf Nurkic offered 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Al-Farouq Aminu went for 10 points, six rebounds, one assist and one block. Zach Collins led the bench with 11 points. The Spurs remain on their West Coast swing and next face the Lakers on Monday night, while the Trail Blazers remain home and tangle with the Washington Wizards on Monday evening as well.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 132 - 119, at Moda Center on Thursday. A well - rested Trail Blazers team managed to take advantage of a tired and banged up Pelicans squad Thursday, as the visiting team was playing its fifth game in seven nights and was without superstar Anthony Davis (elbow). Portland did, however, let the undermanned Pelicans hang around for three quarters before New Orleans grew too tired to keep pace over the last 12 minutes. Damian Lillard led the way for the Blazers, scoring a team - high 26 points to go along with seven rebounds and six assists in 31 minutes, while big man Jusuf Nurkic provided 20 points and nine rebounds of his own in just 28 minutes. The surprise performance of the night came from Al-Farouq Aminu, who posted a double - double of 17 points and 10 rebounds in 33 minutes. The driving force behind Portland's victory Thursday night was their terrific shooting from long range, as they went 18 - of - 35 (51 percent) from behind the arc. As for the Pelicans, they needed someone to step up in the absence of Anthony Davis, and Julius Randle was happy to do so, pouring in a game - high 29 points on 9 - of - 16 shooting in just 26 minutes off the bench. Randle, however, did most of his damage in the first half before eventually running out of gas down the stretch. Nikola Mirotic struggled shooting from the field, going 1 - of - 6 from behind the arc and 6 - of - 20 overall, but he still finished with yet another double - double of 18 points and 13 rebounds. The Pelicans as a team struggled mightily shooting the basketball, as they shot a miserable 8 - of - 29 (28 percent) from three and were just unable to keep pace with the Blazers on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 114 - 110, at Moda Center on Saturday night. The Trail Blazers (6 - 3) came into the contest on an impressive run, having rattled off four straight wins, with three of those having come on the road. Portland was a slight favorite on their home floor against the inconsistent Lakers (4 - 5), yet Los Angeles essentially matched them basket for basket in the first half. The Blazers came out of the halftime locker room holding on to a slim one - point lead, but the visitors would flip the game on its proverbial head in the third period by doubling up their hosts, 32 - 16. That allowed them to withstand a 25 - 15 run by Portland over the final 6:53. The Lakers primarily got it done with pinpoint accuracy from the field, shooting 52 percent while limiting the Blazers to a 42 percent success rate. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 28 points and added seven assists, five rebounds and two blocks. Rajon Rondo followed with 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and three steals. JaVale McGee supplied 12 points, nine rebounds, one assist, six blocks and one steal. Kyle Kuzma matched McGee's scoring total and also registered six boards and a block. Josh Hart posted 11 points. Damian Lillard and C.J. McCollum paced the Blazers with matching 30 - point efforts. Lillard added four rebounds, four assists and three steals, while McCollum hauled in five boards and dished out four assists. Jusuf Nurkic generated a 14 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two blocks and one steal. Evan Turner managed 11 points, three rebounds and three assists. Zach Collins added 10 points off the second unit. The Lakers head home and take on the Toronto Raptors in a Sunday night showdown, while the Trail Blazers remain home to face the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday evening as well.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 111 - 81, at Moda Center on Sunday. This was as about lopsided as it gets in the NBA, as Portland won all four individual quarters. They did most of their damage in the middle quarters, outscoring Minnesota, 62 - 37. The Trail Blazers played their best defense of the season, holding the Timberwolves to 31 percent from the field and 23 percent from three - point range. Rebounding was also decisive, with Portland outrebounding Minnesota, 66 - 38. The Trail Blazers took advantage of a friendly whistle, connecting on 28 - of - 32 from the free - throw line. The Timberwolves (4 - 6) had to play this game without Jimmy Butler (rest) and his ordeal really seems to be hurting this team. Karl-Anthony Towns did all he could, as he led the T'Wolves with 23 points, five rebounds and three assists. Andrew Wiggins was the only other player in double figures, as he amassed 17 points and three steals. The Trail Blazers (7 - 3) got a double - double out of Jusuf Nurkic, as he tallied 19 points, 12 rebounds and two assists on 8 - of - 11 shooting. Damian Lillard accrued 18 points, five rebounds and five assists. C.J. McCollum totaled 16 points, three boards and two steals. Meyers Leonard led the bench with 15 points, 12 rebounds and two assists. Minnesota will have to play again on Monday, as they travel to face the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Portland, they play host to the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday for their next outing.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks, 118 - 103, at Moda Center on Tuesday evening. The Trail Blazers got out to a good start and held the lead early on. The Bucks tied it up at 21 late in the first quarter, but Portland squeezed back in front, to take a 33 - 31 lead into the second. The contest got out to a competitive start as the Pistons and Trail Blazers traded the lead through the first quarter, with the Blazers taking a 32 - 28 lead into the second. The Trail Blazers pushed their lead to 12 late in the second, before the Pistons made a run to cut it to a three - point game by halftime. The Blazers came out strong in the third, but the Pistons stayed with it and managed to take a lead late in the quarter, carry a three - point lead into the fourth. The Pistons kept the momentum and led 108 - 103, with 4:28 left in the game. However, the home team caught fire at the right time, outscoring the visitors by 10 the rest of the way, to secure their third straight win. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 28 points, nine assists and six rebounds, in 37 minutes. Al-Farouq Aminu followed up with 22 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Jusuf Nurkic added 15 points, six rebounds, three assists and two blocks. The Trail Blazers shot 54 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 26 from long range. Meanwhile, Blake Griffin led the Pistons with 27 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 35 minutes. Reggie Jackson followed up with 24 points, two rebounds, an assist and a steal, while Andre Drummond added 19 points, 11 rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block. The Pistons shot 50 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 34 from long range. The Pistons (37 - 35) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors on Sunday. The Trail Blazers (45 - 27) play host to the Nets on Monday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Brooklyn Nets, 148 - 144, in double overtime at Moda Center on Monday evening. Portland's (46 - 27) dramatic win was overshadowed by a gruesome injury to star big man Jusuf Nurkic in double overtime. Nurkic went down with a serious lower leg injury with just over two minutes remaining in the period. He was carted off by Portland's medical staff. Nurkic exited the game with a team - high 32 points, 16 rebounds, and four blocks. Despite the horrific injury, the Trail Blazers were able to pull out the tough win. Portland had the chance to go up with 4 seconds remaining in regulation after the Nets' (38 - 37) D'Angelo Russell committed a turnover that led to Seth Curry drawing a foul on the other end. However, Curry went just 1 - of - 2 on his pair of free - throws to force the first overtime. After a back - and - forth throughout the first OT, Portland saw five points from Rodney Hood to help pull ahead and earn the win. On top of Nurkic's strong performance, Damian Lillard had 31 points for the Trail Blazers. Curry added another 20 off the bench for Portland, while Enes Kanter notched a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. For Brooklyn, Russell had a team - high 39 points to go with nine rebounds and eight assists. Caris LeVert had 16 points and seven assists off the bench, while Spencer Dinwiddie added another 22. Next on the agenda for the Trail Blazers is a trip to Chicago on Wednesday. Brooklyn, meanwhile, will visit Philadelphia on Thursday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Memphis Grizzlies, 116 - 89, at Moda Center on Wednesday evening. Portland (50 - 28) delivered a dominant third quarter to secure its 50th win of the season. The Trail Blazers held Memphis (31 - 47) to only 10 points in the third, holding the team to under 35 percent shooting in the second half. Portland coupled its strong defensive play with a well - rounded offensive attack, shooting over 51 percent from the field and seeing five double - digit scoring performances. The win keeps Portland within half a game of third place in the Western Conference. Evan Turner delivered a triple - double off the bench for the Trail Blazers, scoring 13 points to go with 12 rebounds and 11 assists. Enes Kanter had team highs in both points and rebounds with 21 and 15, respectively. Finally, Damian Lillard continued his All-Star season with a double - double, scoring 20 points and dishing out 10 assists. Memphis was led by 16 points off the bench by veteran Chandler Parsons. Former first - round pick Bruno Caboclo added three blocks and 11 points off the bench, while Ivan Rabb finished with 13 points and 10 rebounds for a double - double. Both teams hit the road on Friday, with the Grizzlies visiting Dallas and the Trail Blazers heading to Denver.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Washington Wizards 144 - 122 at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. It was the Stephen Curry show right out the gate for the Warriors after a significant night for the two time MVP. Curry passed Jamal Crawford for fifth all time on the three point field goals made list and did it by pouring in 21 points first quarter. Golden State's point guard went on to score 51 points in 32 minutes. Add Kevin Durant's 30 points on 13 - of - 18 shooting and the game became far too much for the Wizards to handle as the game became a blowout early in the second quarter. Washington (1 - 3) attempted to go three - for - three during the first quarter and posted a respectable 37 points, however, the Warriors 46 points in front of their home crowd proved daunting. Bradley Beal poured in 23 points on 10 - of - 15 shooting, but the rest of the starters were unable to match the high pace and efficiency that the Warriors (4 - 1) were playing at. Curry's finished with 51 points, three assists and four rebounds on 15 - of - 24 shooting and 11 - of - 15 from behind the arc. John Wall, Marcus Morris and Otto Porter Jr. also finished in double figures scoring to aid Beal. Golden State finished 58 percent from the floor, redefining lights out even for Oracle Arena's standard. Both teams play on Friday, as the Warriors visit Madison Square Garden to take on the New York Knicks, while the Wizards continue their west coast road trip and meet the Sacramento Kings.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 131 - 121, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. The Warriors (8 - 1) managed to survive a track meet in the Bay Area on Wednesday, and they earned their sixth straight victory in the process. Steph Curry was, yet again, sensational, scoring a game - high 37 points on 7 - of - 11 shooting from behind the arc and 12 - of - 20 shooting overall. He also dished out a game - high nine assists, barely edging out teammates Kevin Durant and Draymond Green, who each recorded eight. Durant finished with 24 points, while Green posted a very impressive stat line of 16 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists in 34 minutes. As a team, the Warriors consistently found ways to get open looks from three, and it paid off, as they shot 16 - of - 32 (50 percent) from long range. As for the Pelicans (4 - 3), they put up a good fight, but were unable to close the gap over the course of the second half. Jrue Holiday was the driving force behind the team's offense Wednesday night, as he scored a team - high 28 points to go along with nine assists in 42 minutes. It was a rough night, however, for superstar Anthony Davis, who didn't appear to be 100 percent healthy after missing the previous game with an elbow injury. Davis had just 17 points on 6 - of - 16 shooting and 12 rebounds in 41 minutes. Nikola Mirotic and E'Twaun Moore did an adequate job picking up the slack, scoring 26 and 21 points respectively. Up next, the Warriors will remain home to play the Timberwolves on Friday, while the Pelicans will head to Portland on Thursday to take on the Trail Blazers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 116 - 99, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Warriors jumped out to a good start at home, as they built a 21 - 11 lead halfway through the first quarter, and held on to lead 36 - 32 heading into the second. They stayed in front to start the second quarter, but the'Wolves battled back to take a two - point lead halfway thought the quarter. Things stayed tight until halftime, but it was the Warriors who emerged with a 61 - 58 lead at the break. The Timberwolves were not done yet, as they reclaimed the lead four minutes into the third quarter and held on to take a 87 - 83 lead into the final frame. However, the Warriors turned it on in the fourth. Led by eight straight points from Klay Thompson, they went on to outscore the Timberwolves 33 - 12 in the quarter, to cruise to their seventh straight win. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with 33 points, 13 rebounds, three assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 28 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and two blocks, while Klay Thompson added 22 points, on 9 - of - 17 shooting. The Warriors shot 49 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Andre Wiggins led the Timberwolves with 22 points on 9 - of - 23 shooting, in 36 minutes. Jimmy Butler followed up with 21 points, five assists and three rebounds, in 35 minutes, while Karl-Anthony Towns tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds, one assist, two steals and a block. The Timberwolves shot 38 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 45 from long range. The Timberwolves (4 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Sunday. The Warriors (9 - 1) play host to the Grizzlies on Monday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 117 - 101, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a good start on the road, as they emerged with a 31 - 29 lead after a hard - fought first quarter. They stayed strong in the second, and held the lead for almost the entire quarter. However, the Warriors were hot on their tail and had it tied it up at 58, by halftime. The third quarter started out similarly, but by the halfway point, was a whole different game, as the Warriors mounted a 23 - 8 run, to take a 92 - 73 lead into the final frame. They quickly pushed their lead to 20, and beyond, as they cruised to their eighth straight win, and moved to 60 at home this season. Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 27 points on 11 - of - 21 shooting, three assists, two rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 22 points, six rebounds, six assists, and one steal, in 31 minutes, while Stephen Curry added 19 points, seven assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. The Warriors shot 51 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 23 from long range. Meanwhile, Dillon Brooks led the Grizzlies with 18 points on 6 - of - 13 shooting, in 23 minutes off the bench. Shelvin Mack and Jaren Jackson Jr. chipped in 15 points each, while Marc Gasol added eight points, 10 rebounds, nine assists, in 28 minutes. The Grizzlies shot 46 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 27 from long range. The Grizzlies (5 - 4) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nuggets on Wednesday. The Warriors (10 - 1) play host to the Bucks on Thursday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 134 - 111, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Bucks got out to a great start on the road, as they kept it close, before managing to pull ahead in the final minutes of the first quarter, and take a 32 - 29 lead into the second. The Bucks kept their foot on the gas through the second, as they did not allow the Warriors to catch up, constantly pulled another step ahead, as they outscored the home team, 32 - 22, in the quarter, to take a 64 - 51 lead into halftime. The Bucks iced the game in the third, where they took to a 20 - 5 run to pull ahead by 26 late in the third quarter. Stephen Curry was forced to leave the game in the third, as he suffered a strained groin. The Bucks went on to cruise to their third road win, while the Warriors saw their eight - game winning streak come to an end. Draymond Green (toe) did not suit up in the contest. Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 26 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 26 minutes. Giannis Antetokounmpo followed up with 24 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks, in 26 minutes, while Malcolm Brogdon finished with 20 points, three rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Bucks shot 52 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 35 from long range. Meanwhile, Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 24 points, three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal, in 33 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 17 points, nine assists, five rebounds and one block, while Damian Jones tallied 12 points, four rebounds, one assist and a block. The Warriors shot 48 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 28 from deep. The Warriors (10 - 2) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Saturday. The Bucks (9 - 2) take on the Clippers in Los Angeles on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 116 - 100, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Warriors (11 - 2) came into the contest missing both Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe), and they were facing a clearly improved team in the Nets (6 - 7). However, Golden State didn't spend any time mulling over who wasn't suiting up, as they built a 36 - 30 first - quarter lead that they'd expanded to 65 - 53 by intermission. Not satisfied with that advantage, the home squad expanded their lead by another eight points in the third period to essentially cruise to victory. Both teams shot well, but the Warriors were especially sharp. They drained 55 percent of their attempts, including 44 percent of their tries from distance. Joe Harris paced the Nets with 24 points, a total he supplemented with two assists, one rebound and one steal. Shabazz Napier and Spencer Dinwiddie generated matching 14 - point tallies off the bench. D'Angelo Russell provided 12 points, five assists, three rebounds and two steals. Two young pieces that had been key to Brooklyn's early success, Jarrett Allen and Caris LeVert, underwhelmed with six and four points, respectively. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with a 28 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds, three steals and one block. Quinn Cook drew the start for Curry and totaled 27 points, five assists, four rebounds and one steal. Klay Thompson poured in 24 points and added one rebound, one assist, two steals and one block. Damian Jones and Jonas Jerebko each pitched in eight points. The Nets continue on the road and pay a visit to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday night, while the Warriors make the short trip to Los Angeles and tangle with the Clippers on Monday evening as well.

The Oklahoma City Thunder took down the Golden State Warriors, 123 - 95, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday evening. Basketball action ground to a halt in the fourth quarter, as OKC's Hamidou Diallo went down with a gruesome knee and leg injury. Diallo sustained the injury while battling for a rebound. The rookie shooting guard left the floor on a stretcher; it is unclear yet what the exact nature of his injury is. Diallo's injury came in the middle of a dominant fourth quarter for OKC (11 - 6). The Thunder outscored Golden State 36 - 16 in the final quarter, thanks in large part to a stifling defensive effort. OKC already boasted the fourth - best defensive rating in the NBA. On Wednesday, they improved upon it by holding the league - best Golden State (12 - 7) offense to 95. The Warriors were limited to 43 percent shooting from the field and just 24 percent shooting from beyond the arc. The loss brings Golden State's losing streak to four games, making this the first four - game losing streak for the franchise in over four years. Dennis Schroder led the way for OKC with 32 points in the win. Schroder shot 12 - of - 19, including five three - pointers, and committed only one turnover on the night. Former MVP Russell Westbrook notched a triple - double, finishing with 11 points, 12 rebounds, and 13 assists. Paul George added an additional 25 points. Steph Curry (groin) missed his fourth straight game in Wednesday's loss. In his absence, Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson scored 27 points apiece. Durant also had 14 rebounds and three blocked shots. On Friday, OKC will host the Charlotte Hornets while Golden State will see the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 117 - 116, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Kings got out to a great start on the road, as they outscored the Warriors, 29 - 28, in the first quarter. The Kings kept up their ferocity, as they outscored the Warriors, 35 - 32, in the second, to take a, 64 - 60, lead into half time. The Warriors turned the tables in the third, as they pulled ahead by five early in the quarter. They went on to outscore the Kings by six in the quarter, to take a, 95 - 93, lead into the fourth. The Kings did not back down, as they continued to trade the lead with the Warriors throughout the fourth, but Golden State was able to hang down the stretch. Kevin Durant led the way for the Warriors with 44 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists and two blocks, in 40 minutes. Klay Thompson followed up with 31 points on 12 - of - 26 shooting, and four rebounds, while Damian Jones added 13 points, six rebounds and one assist, in 21 minutes. The Warriors shot 51 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Buddy Hield led the Kings with 28 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes. Marvin Bagley III had a big night, with 20 points, 17 rebounds and two assists, in 33 minutes off the bench. Iman Shumpert chipped in 14 points, four rebounds and one steal. The Kings shot 44 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 27 from deep. The Kings (10 - 9) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Jazz on Sunday. The Warriors (14 - 7) play host to the Magic on Monday.

The Golden State Warriors took down the visiting Orlando Magic, 116 - 110, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. Led by a whopping 49 points from All-Star forward Kevin Durant, the Warriors (15 - 7) were able to pull out a narrow win late in the game. With the Magic (10 - 11) up three with 1:45 remaining, Klay Thompson buried a three - pointer to tie the game up. Golden State went on to stifle Orlando on the defensive end, while Durant sealed the win by knocking down a three - point shot to go up by four with 21 seconds remaining. The win puts Golden State in first place in the Western Conference standings. Durant added nine assists, two steals, and two blocks to his incredible scoring outburst. Klay Thompson scored an additional 29 points in the win. Durant and Thompson were the only two Warriors to score in double digits in the win, but that did not seem to make a difference. The team still managed to shoot 49 percent from the field and hit 13 three - pointers. The Magic saw a stellar shooting night of its own, going 14 - of - 28 from three - point territory. Nikola Vucevic led the team with 30 points, 12 rebounds, and six assists. Veteran wing Terrance Ross added another 28 points. Unfortunately for Orlando, neither performance was enough to help the team get its record over .500. The Magic will visit Portland on Wednesday, while the Warriors travel to Toronto to face the Raptors on Thursday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 120 - 116, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Mavs got out to a strong start on the road and managed to hang on to a three - point advantage after one quarter. They kept it tight through the second as they matched the Warriors with 30 points a piece in the quarter, to take a three - point lead at halftime. The Warriors turned the tables in the third, however, as they outscored the visitors by 10, to take a seven - point lead heading into the final frame. Despite a rally from the Mavericks in the final minutes, the Warriors were able to hang on for their 14th home win of the season, while the Mavs dropped their fifth game in a row. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with 29 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 22 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals, in 39 minutes. Draymond Green finished with 14 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and two block, while Klay Thompson chipped in 14 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block. Meanwhile, Wesley Matthews led the Mavericks with 25 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 35 minutes. DeAndre Jordan tallied 12 points, 23 rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, while Luka Doncic added 19 points, five assists, three rebounds, a steal and a block. The Mavs (15 - 16) will look to avoid a sixth straight loss as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Sunday. The Warriors (22 - 11) play host to the Clippers on Sunday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 129 - 127, at Oracle Arena on Sunday. There were 20 ties and 13 lead changes in this game, as it wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Avery Bradley recorded a dunk with 10 seconds left to tie the game but Stephen Curry countered that by hitting one of his patented lay - ups with 0 seconds left to win the game. Los Angeles lost this game despite having the best three - point shooting game of the season, as they connected on 18 - of - 23 from long range. The key for the Warriors was free - throw shooting, as they hit 31 - of - 36 while the Clippers connected on 23 - of - 29. Defense was also critical, with Golden State picking up nine steals and eight blocks while Los Angeles had just one apiece. Offensive rebounding was also decisive, with the Warriors winning that battle, 15 - 5. The Clippers (19 - 14) were led by Tobias Harris, as he tallied 32 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Danilo Gallinari amassed 25 points, 11 rebounds and three assists. Lou Williams was huge off the bench, as he provided 25 points, two rebounds and nine assists. Montrezl Harrell also played well off the bench, amassing 13 points, three rebounds and two assists. The Warriors (23 - 11) were led by Stephen Curry, as he collected 42 points, six rebounds and two assists. Kevin Durant accumulated 35 points, 12 rebounds, five assists and three blocks. Draymond Green finished with 14 points, four rebounds, six assists and five steals. Kevon Looney led their bench with 10 points and seven boards. On deck for Golden State is a Christmas Day showdown against the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday. As for the Clippers, they return to action on Wednesday when they play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 135 - 134, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Warriors got out to a great start at home with a 34 - 22 lead after one quarter and expanded their lead to 70 - 53 by halftime. The Rockets turned it up in the third quarter and outscored the Warriors by 11, to cut the deficit to six at the start of the fourth. They kept the pressure on through the fourth and managed to tie the game in the final second of regulation thanks to pure heroics from James Harden. The Rockets scored the first points in OT, but the Warriors battled back and held a two - point lead with five seconds remaining. However, Harden had more magic left in his bag, as he drilled a seemingly impossible game - winning three - pointer over two Warriors defenders to steal the win on the road. Harden led the Rockets with 44 points, 15 assists, 10 rebounds, two blocks and one steal, in 44 minutes. Clint Capela followed up with 29 points, 21 rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, while Austin Rivers added 18 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Rockets shot 46 percent from the field, including 21 - of - 54 from long range. Meanwhile, Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 35 points, six assists and three rebounds, in 40 minutes. Kevin Durant finished with 26 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one block, while Klay Thompson tallied 26 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. The Warriors shot 38 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 37 from long range. The Warriors (25 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Kings in Sacramento on Saturday. The Rockets (22 - 15) will look for their eighth straight win as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 146 - 109, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Warriors got down to business right off the jump, as they poured in 43 points in the first quarter, while holding the Bulls to just 17 points. The Bulls picked it up in the second quarter and outscored the Warriors by five, but still trailed by 21 at halftime. The Warriors got back to domination mode in the third, where they outscored the visitors 40 - 21 in the quarter, to take a 116 - 76 lead into the final frame. They were able to cruise to their third straight win, and 17th home win of the season, while the Bulls took their sixth straight loss. Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 30 points on 10 - of - 18 shooting, two rebounds, two steals and one assist, in 25 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 28 points, eight assists and five rebounds, while Kevin Durant tallied 22 points, five assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block, in 28 minutes. The Warriors shot 58 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 39 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 29 points on 10 - of - 16 shooting and four rebounds, in 26 minutes. Bobby Portis followed up with 16 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting, four rebounds, two steals and one assist, in 16 minutes off the bench, while Antonio Blakeney tallied 12 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting off the bench. The Bulls (10 - 32) will look to bounce back as they take on the Jazz in Utah on Saturday. The Warriors (28 - 14) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Sunday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 147 - 140, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. On the second game of a back - to - back, the Warriors (31 - 14) came out sluggish and seemed to be a bit hungover from their throttling of the Nuggets on Tuesday night. They fell behind early to the visiting, and surging, Pelicans (21 - 24), who opened up a lead as large as 16 points in the third quarter and appeared to be pulling away. Then, Steph Curry happened. The two - time MVP hit seven threes in the third period on his way to scoring 23 points and leading a furious comeback that had the Warriors miraculously up by one point heading into the final 12 minutes. From there, while the Pelicans kept fighting, it was business as usual for the defending champions, as Curry and company weren't going to let it slip away at that point. Curry finished with a game - high 41 points while shooting 9 - of - 17 from three, while Kevin Durant added 30 points and 15 assists. As a team, Golden State shot a ridiculous 24 - of - 49 (49 percent) from three in the winning effort. The Pelicans, on the other hand, were even more impressive with their arial assault, as they shot a scorching 19 - of - 37 (51 percent) from the field, but it wouldn't be enough. Anthony Davis led the way as usual with 30 points, 18 rebounds and seven assists in 41 minutes, while Nikola Mirotic was close behind with 29 points in 29 minutes off the bench. New Orleans' third frontcourt star, Julius Randle, shot just 6 - of - 8 from the field, but still managed to finish with 23 points in 22 minutes.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Golden State Warriors, 113 - 104, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Warriors got out to a good start at home, with a 35 - 30 lead after one quarter. The Sixers rallied ahead early in the second and kept it close through the quarter, but the Warriors regained control and brought a 60 - 53 lead into halftime. The 76ers came out on fire in the third and outscored the Warriors 42 - 26 in the quarter, to take a 95 - 86 lead into the final frame. Things slowed down in the fourth, as the teams matched each other with 18 points, while the 76ers managed to hover around a double - digit lead, en route to their second straight win. This marks the end of an 11 - game winning streak for the Warriors. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 26 points, 20 rebounds, five assists, and two steals, in 33 minutes. Ben Simmons tallied 26 points, eight rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block, while J.J. Redick added 15 points, three assists and two rebounds. The 76ers shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 41 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 38 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 25 points on 11 - of - 24 shooting, four rebounds, four assists and two steals, in 37 minutes, while Kevon Looney added 14 points, five rebounds, two steals and two blocks. The Warriors shot 47 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 38 from long range. The Warriors (36 - 15) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Lakers on Saturday. The 76ers (34 - 18) take on the Kings in Sacramento on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 101, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. While Los Angeles was competitive throughout this game, Golden State ultimately prevailed thanks to a 27 - 15 fourth quarter. In fact, the Lakers actually led for the majority of the third quarter, as the Warriors finished the game on a 27 - 12 run. The free - throw shooting was the difference in the game, with Golden State hitting 18 - of - 19 and Los Angeles connecting on 10 - of - 17. Ball movement was also critical, with the Warriors recording 31 assists to 10 turnovers while the Lakers picked up 23 assists to 15 turnovers. The Lakers (26 - 26) played this game without LeBron James (rest), as Brandon Ingram led the way with 20 points, four rebounds and three assists. Rajon Rondo collected 12 points, eight rebounds and 11 assists. Kyle Kuzma amassed 13 points, four rebounds and two assists while Lance Stephenson led the bench with 10 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Warriors (37 - 15) were led by Klay Thompson, as he totaled 28 points, five rebounds and two assists. Kevin Durant accumulated 21 points, five rebounds and 11 assists. DeMarcus Cousins tallied 18 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Andre Iguodala led the bench with 17 points, three rebounds and four assists. On deck for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the Indiana Pacers on Tuesday. As for Golden State, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the San Antonio Spurs.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 141 - 102, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. The Warriors (38 - 15) allowed their visitors to hang around for about a quarter and a half Wednesday night, but thanks to a stretch across the second and third quarters where Golden State went 24 - of - 25 from the field, the home team buried the Spurs with little difficulty. 12 of the Warriors' 13 active players saw double - digit minutes Wednesday, with every single one of them scoring at least two points thanks to the blowout nature of the game. Klay Thompson was on fire for all 29 of his minutes, going 4 - of - 5 from three and 11 - of - 13 from the field overall en route to scoring a game - high 26 points, while Kevin Durant was close behind with 23 points in 29 minutes of his own to go along with eight rebounds, nine assists and three steals. Steph Curry finished with 19 points, five rebounds and seven assists in another 29 minutes. As a team, it was a clinic from the Warriors, shooting 47 percent from behind the arc and 58 percent from the field overall. As for the Spurs (32 - 24), they simply did not have enough talent to keep up with the NBA's best team Wednesday, as they were without both DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge for rest purposes. As a result, Patty Mills came through as the team's top scorer with just 16 points, while Rudy Gay added 15 points of his own. As a team, San Antonio shot decent from behind the arc, going 12 - of - 32 from three, but their overall field goal percentage was just 43 percent and not nearly efficient enough to top Golden State. This dropped the Spurs' record on the road this season to 10 - 17 as they continue to be a very different team away from home.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Utah Jazz, 115 - 108, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday evening. Utah (32 - 25) seemed ready to test the Warriors' (41 - 15) dominance, holding a lead until late in the fourth quarter. The Jazz's top - five defense shined in the loss, limiting Golden State's high - powered offense to 81 points through three quarters. However, Utah was unable to hold onto the game late, as Golden State poured in 34 fourth - quarter points to earn the victory. Steph Curry, who finished with 24 points, helped to seal the win in the final five minutes, knocking down a pull - up three - pointer and an ensuing layup to put Golden State up 10. Kevin Durant was the game's high scorer with 28 points. Durant also tallied seven assists in the win. Klay Thompson scored another 22 points, while DeMarcus Cousins contributed 12 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists. The Warriors shot over 49 percent from the field and knocked down 13 three - pointers. The Jazz were led by 25 points from sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell, who shot a dismal 10 - of - 29 from the field. Outside of Mitchell, Utah was remarkably efficient. The Jazz finished shooting over 47 percent from the field. Rudy Gobert had a double - double, finishing with 13 points and 16 rebounds. The Houston Rockets defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 118 - 112, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. While Golden State came into this game as a monster favorite, Houston led throughout. Tucker collected 18 points, 10 rebounds, four steals and two blocks while Clint Capela amassed eight points and 15 boards. The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 122 - 105, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Phoenix Suns upset the Golden State Warriors, 115 - 111, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. Durant went to the locker room and did not return to the game with what was described as an "ankle contusion. "Booker and the Suns were able to hang onto the lead and close out the win in the final minutes. In addition to his strong scoring output, Booker tallied 11 assists and eight rebounds. Oubre also had a strong scoring night, tallying 22 points in total. Rookie sensation DeAndre Ayton added to his strong first - year campaign, finishing with 18 points, nine rebounds, and four assists while taking down the defending champs. The Warriors will have a chance to get back on track with a visit to Houston on Wednesday. Phoenix, meanwhile, will gear up for a clash with the Utah Jazz.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated host Golden State Warriors, 126 - 91, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. It wouldn't have been surprising to see the Warriors win this game in blowout fashion but the Mavericks turned the tables on them here. The Mavericks (29 - 44) got another triple - double from Luka Doncic, as he led the way with 23 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and three steals. Dirk Nowitzki amassed 21 points, five rebounds and two blocks. Jalen Brunson accrued 11 points, four rebounds and five assists while Maxi Kleber led the bench with 16 points and nine boards. The Warriors (49 - 33) were led by Kevin Durant, as he tallied 25 points, five rebounds and four assists. DeMarcus Cousins amassed 19 points, six rebounds and three assists. Quinn Cook started for Stpehen Curry (rest) and provided seven points, six rebounds and seven assists. Kevon Looney was the only other player in double figures, as he led the bench with 12 points and three boards. Golden State has to play again on Sunday, as they play host to the Detroit Pistons. The Golden State Warriors took down the Detroit Pistons, 121 - 114, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. The Pistons relied heavily on their second unit, which combined for 62 points on the night. Luke Kennard led the bench unit with 20 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting. The Golden State Warriors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 120 - 114, at Oracle Arena on Friday night. The Cavaliers return home to face the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday afternoon, while the Warriors remain home to tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 131 - 104, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start but the Warriors managed to keep a slight edge for almost the entire first quarter, and take a four - point lead into the second. The Clippers shot 48 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 19 from deep. The Clippers (47 - 34) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Jazz on Wednesday. The Warriors (56 - 24) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Tuesday.

The Miami Heat defeated the Washington Wizards, 113 - 112, at Capital One Arena on Thursday. After the Heat (1 - 1) were unable to convert on a potential game - winning possession in their season - opener Wednesday night, they made sure to not make the same mistake two games in a row. With Miami down by one point, a Dwyane Wade fadeaway jumper over John Wall hit the back of the rim, but Kelly Olynyk made sure he was in the right place at the right time. The big man got the rebound and laid it in with ease with just .2 seconds remaining to put the visiting team up one. The Wizards (0 - 1) didn't get a shot off in their final possession, and the Heat earned their first victory of the 2018 - 19 season. Josh Richardson led the way for Miami, scoring a game - high 28 points to go along with five assists and four rebounds in 38 minutes. The team managed to overcome a very rough shooting night, as Miami shot just 39 percent from the field. As for the Wizards, their All-Star backcourt did everything they could to will the team to victory on opening night, with John Wall posting a team - high 26 points and nine assists, while Bradley Beal added 20 points of his own. Jeff Green was also impressive in his Wizards debut, scoring 17 points in 33 minutes off the bench. Washington was without starting center Dwight Howard (back), but the team still somehow managed to block 15 shots.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Washington Wizards, 117 - 113, at Capital One Arena on Saturday evening. Despite missing Kawhi Leonard (rest) the Raptors earned an impressive win in Washington. The Wizards started out well, but the Raptors overtook them late in the quarter to hold a 24 - 22 advantage heading into the second. The second quarter stayed close until Toronto pulled away late to amass a 10 - point. However, the Wizards came right back with an 11 - 4 run, to cut the deficit to just three, heading into halftime. The Wizards continued their push into the third quarter, where they squeezed ahead and held a three - point lead with 5:27 to go in the quarter. The Raptors turned it around again as they closed the quarter on a 20 - 9 run, to take a 90 - 82 advantage into the final frame. The Raptors pushed their lead to 13, midway through the fourth, but the Wizards were not done yet, as they made it a two - point game with just 38 seconds left. However, a clutch shot by Fred VanVleet ensured the Raptors remain undefeated on the season, with their third straight win. Kyle Lowry led the Raptors with 28 points, 12 assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Jonas Valanciunas and Serge Ibaka chipped in 16 points each, as well as provided a combined16 rebounds. Fred VanVleet added 13 points, five assists and four rebounds, in 26 minutes off the bench. The Raptors shot 44 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal had a big night with 32 points, six assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block, while John Wall followed up with 25 points, six assists, four rebounds, four steals and one block. The Wizards (0 - 2) will look to bounce back as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Monday. The Raptors (30) host the Hornets on Monday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Washington Wizards, 134 - 111, at Capital One Arena on Friday. These teams are heading in opposite directions and this 23 - point final spread shows exactly which way they're headed. While Washington led for the majority of the first quarter, a 44 - 20 second quarter in advantage of Oklahoma City was simply too much for the Wizards to overcome. In fact, the Thunder led by at least 19 points for the entirety of the second half. The 34 assists recorded by the Thunder was a huge part of that, as they also won the turnover differential, 18 - 13. The Thunder (4 - 4) were led by Russell Westbrook, as he collected 23 points, three rebounds, 12 assists and four steals on 10 - of - 16 shooting. Jerami Grant finished with 22 points, four rebounds and four assists on 9 - of - 11 from the field. Paul George accrued 17 points, four rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Dennis Schroder led the bench with 16 points, six rebounds and five assists. The Wizards (1 - 7) best player was Bradley Beal, as he amassed 27 points, two rebounds and four assists on 10 - of - 16 shooting. Dwight Howard scored 20 points on 7 - of - 8 from the field in his Washington debut. John Wall accumulated 19 points, two rebounds and nine assists. Kelly Oubre Jr. led the bench with 14 points, four boards and two blocks. On deck for Washington is a home matchup versus the New York Knicks on Sunday. As for Oklahoma City, they're off until Monday when they welcome the New Orleans Pelicans to OKC.

The Washington Wizards defeated the New York Knicks, 108 - 95, at Capital One Arena on Sunday evening. The Wizards (2 - 7) came into Sunday's contest in dire need of a win, as they'd dropped seven of their first eight games. They seemingly had a good opportunity to right their ship against the Knicks (3 - 7), but they needed to up their level of play significantly from what it had been until that point. Washington was able to get off to a strong start by taking a 24 - 17 lead in the first quarter, which allowed them to hold on during the middle periods when New York made a run to narrow their deficit to three points going into the final 12 minutes. Then, Washington was able to turn up their play a notch, outscoring the visitors by a 27 - 17 margin to seal the victory. Enes Kanter paced the Knicks with an 18 - point, 12 - rebound double - double. Trey Burke supplied 13 points, three assists and a steal. Dewayne Dotson tallied 11 points, six rebounds and two assists. Mitchell Robinson offered 10 points, six rebounds and one block. Mario Hezonja matched Robinson's scoring total and added eight boards, three assists and three steals. John Wall spearheaded the Wizards with 26 points, seven assists, two rebounds and five steals. Bradley Beal registered 22 points, eight rebounds, three assists and four blocks. Markieff Morris compiled 16 points, six rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal. Jeff Green followed with a bench - leading 14 points and also managed nine boards and two blocks. Dwight Howard started and generated a 10 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one steal and one block. The Knicks head back home to take on the Chicago Bulls on Monday night, while the Wizards pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Tuesday evening.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 117 - 109, at Capital One Arena on Monday. This eight - point final margin is unfair to the Magic, as it was extremely competitive throughout. In addition, the first three quarters all ended in stalemates, as a 34 - 26 fourth quarter ultimately won Washington the game. Defensive rebounding was huge for the Wizards, as they won that battle, 34 - 26. Getting to the free - throw line was also huge, with Washington connecting on 24 - of - 33 while Orlando hit just 8 - of - 11. The Wizards also won the points in the paint battle, 46 - 38 and won the fastbreak differential, 15 - 5. The Magic's (6 - 8) leading scorer came off the bench, as Terrence Ross provided 21 points, three rebounds and two assists. Evan Fournier led the starters with 20 points, two rebounds and five assists. Aaron Gordon collected 18 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals an two blocks. Nikola Vucevic amassed 17 points, 11 rebounds and three assists. The Wizards (4 - 9) were led by John Wall, as he tallied 25 points, four rebounds and 10 assists. Bradley Beal totaled 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Dwight Howard finished with 17 points and eight boards while Markieff Morris generated 16 points and eight rebounds. Jeff Green led the bench with 18 points, six rebounds and two steals on 6 - of - 7 from the field. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Orlando playing host to the Philadelphia 76ers and Washington remaining home to face the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 119 - 95, at Capitol One Arena on Wednesday evening. The Wizards (5 - 9) came into the contest showing some signs of life after a dreadful start, as they'd notched consecutive wins against the Heat and Magic in their prior two games. However, Cavaliers (2 - 12) were feeling good in their own right, having surprised the Charlotte Hornets by a 113 - 89 margin Tuesday. The possibility for a letdown therefore existed, and the first quarter indicated that's exactly what was in the cards. Washington forged a 41 - 29 lead after 12 minutes that they'd expanded to 73 - 52 by halftime. That essentially allowed the home squad to tread water in the second half and still finish with a comfortable victory. Although the Wizards were guilty of 17 turnovers on the night, they forced 23 from the Cleveland while also holding them to a 19 percent success rate from three - point range. Rookie Collin Sexton paced the Cavaliers with 24 points and added three rebounds and two assists. David Nwaba followed with 11 points off the bench, which he partly supplemented with seven rebounds. Larry Nance, Jr. and Rodney Hood generated matching 10 - point tallies on the starting five. Nance also had six rebounds, five assists, four steals and two blocks, while Hood had a pair of rebounds and assists each. Andrew Harrison supplied 10 points on the second unit as well, while Tristan Thompson registered nine points, eight boards, two assists, two steals and one block. Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 20 points while also recording three rebounds, three assists and three steals. Otto Porter, Jr. provided 15 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Austin Rivers poured in 12 points off the bench. Markieff Morris and Dwight Howard had 11 and 10 points, respectively, with Howard also grabbing seven boards. John Wall mustered eight points, nine assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block in just 21 minutes. The Cavaliers are off until next Monday, when they'll take on the Detroit Pistons in Motown. The Wizards remain home and await a visit from the Brooklyn Nets on Friday evening.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Washington Wizards, 115 - 104, at Capital One Arena on Friday evening. The Wizards got out to a good start on the road, with an early 10 - 4 lead, an held on to take a 30 - 26 lead into the second. They managed to stay on top to begin the quarter, but the Nets picked up the pace and pulled ahead to take a 56 - 54 lead into halftime. The Nets picked up where they left off in the third quarter, as they pushed their way to a 10 - point lead, five minutes into the quarter, and went on to outscore Washington by 10 in the quarter, to take a 91 - 79 lead into the final frame. The Wizards had no answer, as the Nets held a 15 - point lead halfway through the quarter, and went on to end a three - game losing streak, while the Wizards saw their three - game winning streak come to an end. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 25 points, eight assists, four rebounds and three steals, in 31 minutes off the bench. The Wizards shot 42 percent from the field, including 3 - of - 18 from deep. The Wizards (5 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Sunday. The Nets (7 - 9) play host to the Clippers on Saturday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Washington Wizards, 119 - 109, at Capital One Arena on Sunday evening. The win snapped a two - game losing streak for Portland (11 - 5), who had dropped back - to - back contests heading into Sunday's matchup. Washington (5 - 11), on the contrary, has now dropped two straight after what seemed like a revitalizing three - game win streak last week. It was tough to question Portland's dominance in Sunday's win, though, as the team quickly jumped out to a double - digit lead in the first quarter. The game was all but sealed by the stifling defense the Blazers exhibited in the second quarter. Washington was held to just 16 points on under 40 percent shooting from the field in the period. Damian Lillard bounced back from a rather pedestrian 16 - point outing on Friday to score a game - high 40 points in the win. Though he shot just 12 - of - 29 from the floor, Lillard made up for it with a 13 - of - 15 performance at the free - throw line. C.J. McCollum added another 25 points, while big man Jusuf Nurkic flirted with a triple - double, tallying 13 points, 14 rebounds, and eight assists on the night. For the Wizards, meanwhile, John Wall led the way with 24 points. Kelly Oubre, Jr. led the bench unit with 19 points in 29 minutes of action on the floor. The team, however, struggled to make the best use of its opportunities at the free - throw line, effectively playing itself out of the game at the stripe. Washington went just 10 - of - 21 from the free - throw line. Portland will continue its road trip with a visit to Madison Square Garden to take on the Knicks this Tuesday. Washington, meanwhile, will play host to the LA Clippers.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 125 - 118, at Capital One Arena on Tuesday evening. The Wizards (6 - 11) came into the contest with controversy swirling around them, given recent rumors that no current player is untouchable in a trade and plenty of rumblings about infighting among some of the team's stars. Therefore, when the Clippers (11 - 6) opened up a 40 - 21 first - quarter lead, it wasn't likely to much of anyone's surprise and normally would have set the tone for a blowout win for the visitors. That wasn't to be Tuesday, however, as Washington clawed back by outscoring Los Angeles, 65 - 55, in the middle periods. That allowed them to enter the final 12 minutes with a 95 - 86 lead, one that they'd preserve by showing some impressive killer instinct while outpacing their visitors by a 39 - 23 fourth - quarter margin. Tobias Harris led the way for the Clippers with 29 points, a total he supplemented with nine rebounds and one assist. Montrezl Harrell managed 20 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Lou Williams each provided 17 points. Marcin Gortat posted nine points and seven rebounds against his old Wizards teammates. John Wall paced the Wizards with 30 points and added eight assists, four rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Bradley Beal generated 27 points, seven assists, three rebounds and one block. Jeff Green followed with a bench - leading 20 points and complemented them with seven boards, three assists, one steal and one block. Tomas Satoransky turned in 13 points, seven rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Markieff Morris poured in 12 points and added five rebounds and a pair of assists off the bench. The Clippers return home to take on the Grizzlies on Friday afternoon, while the Wizards remain home and tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Friday night.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 124 - 114, at Capital One Arena on Saturday. There were 14 ties and 20 lead changes in this tightly - contested battle, as it wasn't decided until the final quarter.
